metadata.title: Visual Findings Library — Main Database Topic Index
metadata.description: The single disease list of the Visual Findings Library, grouped by specialty. Every topic is a disease or syndrome with published images in the library; a topic with no images is removed. General non-visual diseases and single manifestations are excluded.

curation_policy.inclusion_criteria: Disease- or syndrome-level topic with clinical images: patient photographs, endoscopic or fundus photographs, dermoscopy, or a disease-specific radiologic sign, plus pathology where that is how the disease is recognized.
curation_policy.exclusion_criteria: General non-visual conditions (hypothyroidism, uncomplicated diabetes mellitus, essential hypertension, coronary artery disease, asthma, GERD). Single manifestations, complications, and imaging-only anatomic variants (malar rash, digital ulcer, Eisenmenger physiology, retinal vein occlusion, papillary necrosis, Horner syndrome). Umbrella infections without one phenotype (osteomyelitis, septic arthritis).
curation_policy.topic_grain: One disease or syndrome. Sites and complications stay inside that topic and are not separate topics.

Cardiology.name: Acute Aortic Dissection
synonyms: Stanford Type A / Type B dissection
clinical_manifestations: Sudden, catastrophic, tearing, ripping, or sharp chest/interscapular back pain
Asymmetric peripheral pulses (radial, femoral) with pulse deficit between arms (>20 mmHg)
Marfanoid habitus in younger patients (arachnodactyly, high-arched palate, pectus excavatum)
Horner syndrome (miosis, ptosis, anhidrosis from compression of sympathetic ganglion)
Acute murmur of aortic regurgitation and shock (cardiac tamponade)
radiological_manifestations: CT Angiography of Chest and Abdomen (Imaging Gold Standard): Pathognomonic intimal flap dividing the aorta into a true lumen and false lumen; differentiation between Stanford Type A (ascending aorta) and Type B (distal to left subclavian); identification of branch vessel compromise, hemopericardium, and intramural hematoma
Transesophageal Echocardiography (TEE): Mobile intimal flap in the ascending aorta, acute severe aortic regurgitation jet, pericardial tamponade
Chest Radiography: Widened superior mediastinum (>8 cm), obliteration of aortic knob, calcium sign (inward displacement of intimal calcification >10 mm from outer soft-tissue border)
pathology_manifestations: Surgical aortic resection: Cystic medial necrosis with fragmentation and loss of elastic fibers, basophilic pooling of ground substance (proteoglycans) within the media, cleavage plane within the outer third of the aortic media filled with fresh hematoma
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Emergency vascular catastrophe with unmistakable physical exam pulse deficits, Marfan habitus, and Horner sign, diagnosed by the pathognomonic intimal flap separating true/false lumens on CTA.

Cardiology.name: Anomalous Left Coronary Artery from the Pulmonary Artery
synonyms: Anomalous origin of left coronary artery from pulmonary trunk
clinical_manifestations: Infantile feeding angina ('episodic screaming'): Classic presentation between 4 and 12 weeks of age (coinciding with the physiological decline in pulmonary vascular resistance): recurrent paroxysms of acute irritability, vigorous crying, screaming, pallor, cold diaphoresis, and pulling up of the legs during or immediately following feeding or nursing, representing severe episodic myocardial ischemia / infantile angina pectoris

Severe congestive heart failure in infancy: Rapid development of tachypnea, intercostal grunting, wheezing, coughing, severe poor feeding, profound failure to thrive, listlessness, and cardiogenic shock
Precordial physical examination: Hyperdynamic, laterally and inferiorly displaced apical impulse; precordial heave; prominent third heart sound (S3) gallop

Cardiac auscultation: Harsh, high-pitched holosystolic regurgitant murmur best heard at the cardiac apex and radiating to the left axilla, resulting from ischemic mitral regurgitation due to papillary muscle necrosis/fibrosis and mitral annular dilatation; soft, continuous or mid-diastolic murmur audible over the upper left sternal border caused by extensive intercoronary collateral flow emptying into the pulmonary trunk

Electrocardiographic (ECG) hallmark: Characteristic anterolateral infantile myocardial infarction pattern: deep, wide, abnormal Q waves (> 30 ms and > 0.2 mV) with marked ST-segment elevation or T-wave inversion in leads I, aVL, and V4-V6, accompanied by loss of normal precordial R-wave progression
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE - Primary Diagnostic Modality): Direct anatomical visualization of the left main coronary artery arising anomalously from the posterolateral aspect of the main pulmonary artery trunk rather than the aortic sinus; Color and pulsed Doppler reveals pathognomonic retrograde, reversed flow from the left coronary artery into the pulmonary trunk ('coronary steal phenomenon'); markedly dilated and tortuous right coronary artery (RCA) originating normally from the aorta; extensive intercoronary collateral flow visualized as colorful mosaic color Doppler signals within the interventricular septum; severe left ventricular dilatation with global hypokinesia, depressed ejection fraction, and bright, hyperechogenic, scarred/calcified anterolateral papillary muscles with severe ischemic mitral regurgitation

Multidetector CT Angiography (MDCTA - Gold Standard 3D Vascular Mapping): Definitive non-invasive 3D volumetric depiction demonstrating the exact anomalous ostium of the left main coronary artery originating from the pulmonary artery, tracing the course of the dilated, tortuous RCA, mapping coronary collateral pathways, and providing preoperative anatomical roadmaps for surgical coronary transfer / aortic reimplantation

Cardiac MRI (CMR): Evaluates left ventricular volumes and systolic impairment; Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE) definitively delineates extensive subendocardial or transmural myocardial infarction involving the anterolateral LV free wall and papillary muscles; phase-contrast velocity mapping quantifies retrograde left coronary shunt volume
Chest Radiography: Marked, globular cardiomegaly with pronounced left ventricular configuration and prominent pulmonary venous congestion / interstitial pulmonary edema

Coronary Angiography (Catheterization): Aortic root or selective right coronary artery injection reveals an ectatic, giant RCA that retrogradely opacifies a dense network of septal and epicardial collaterals, which fill the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries retrogradely, finally emptying into the main pulmonary trunk
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical & Autopsy Pathology: Left main coronary artery takes its origin from the left or posterior sinus of the main pulmonary artery; the right coronary artery is massively dilated, elongated, and serpentine; the left ventricle is severely dilated and hypertrophied, showing dense, pearly-white endocardial fibroelastosis along the endocardium; anterolateral and posteromedial papillary muscles and adjacent left ventricular anterolateral wall show thinned, scarred, yellowish-white fibrous or calcified replacement tissue indicative of remote myocardial infarction

Histopathology: Extensive subendocardial and transmural ischemic necrosis, loss of cardiomyocytes, and dense replacement collagen fibrosis in the left ventricular anterolateral wall and papillary muscles; marked chronic ischemic vacuolization (hydropic swelling) of surviving subendocardial myocytes; dense fibroelastic tissue expansion (fibroelastosis) of the mural endocardium; medial hypertrophy and cystic medial degeneration of the compensatory right coronary artery and collateral vessels
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening congenital coronary steal syndrome characterized by classic infantile feeding angina and deep Q waves on ECG, verified by direct echocardiographic/CTA visualization of the LMCA arising from the pulmonary artery with retrograde Doppler flow, and pathognomonic papillary muscle necrosis with fibroelastosis.

Cardiology.name: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC / Naxos Disease)
synonyms: Cardiomyopathy with woolly hair and keratoderma
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic cutaneous triad of Naxos disease / Carvajal syndrome: diffuse, non-epidermolytic, yellowish palmoplantar keratoderma with erythematous borders; distinctive, tightly curled, wiry, kinky 'woolly hair'; and early-onset right ventricular cardiomyopathy
Arrhythmogenic bedside emergencies: palpitations, recurrent syncope during athletic exertion, and sudden cardiac death in young athletes and adolescents
Right ventricular failure signs: elevated jugular venous pressure with prominent v waves, hepatomegaly with systolic pulsations, peripheral pitting edema, and tricuspid regurgitant murmur

Electrocardiographic physical trace signs: epsilon wave (reproducible small-amplitude notch/spike at the end of the QRS complex in leads V1-V3 in up to 30% of patients), localized prolonged QRS duration (>110 ms in V1-V3), and T-wave inversion in right precordial leads (V1-V3)
radiological_manifestations: Cardiac MRI (CMR - Imaging Modality of Reference): Regional right ventricular wall motion abnormalities (akinesia, dyskinesia, or dyssynchrony); right ventricular dilatation with elevated RV end-diastolic volume index (>=110 mL/m2 in males, >=100 mL/m2 in females) or reduced RV ejection fraction (<=40%); pathognomonic focal outpouchings/aneurysms of the RV free wall located within the 'triangle of dysplasia' (RV inflow tract, apex, and infundibulum/RVOT); late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) depicting hyperintense fibrous replacement of the thin RV free wall; 'accordion sign' (focal crinkling/wrinkling of the RV wall during systole)

Echocardiography (TTE): Severe dilation of the RV outflow tract (parasternal long-axis RVOT >=32 mm, parasternal short-axis RVOT >=36 mm); localized RV aneurysms and sacculations; hyperreflective, trabeculated RV endocardium with reduced fractional area change (FAC <=33%)
Right Ventriculography: Regional akinesia, scalloping, and bulges in the subtricuspid region and RV apex ('pile of plates' or corrugated appearance)
pathology_manifestations: Gross Cardiac Pathology: Striking localized or diffuse thinning of the right ventricular free wall (translucent, 'parchment-like' appearance), especially in the triangle of dysplasia; marked chamber dilation with saccular outpouchings; endocardial fibroelastosis

Histopathology: Transmural fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricular myocardium (progressing from epicardium toward endocardium), with residual islands of degenerate cardiomyocytes entrapped within adipose tissue and dense fibrous collagen; patchy mononuclear inflammatory infiltrates (T lymphocytes) indicating ongoing inflammatory myocyte necrosis; desmosomal defects (plakoglobin, desmoplakin, plakophilin-2)
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict multimodal criteria: pathognomonic photographic dermatologic signs (woolly hair, palmoplantar keratoderma in Naxos/Carvajal syndrome) alongside the iconic CMR 'triangle of dysplasia' aneurysms, fibrofatty replacement, and translucent gross pathology.

Cardiology.name: Bicuspid Aortic Valve with Ascending Aortopathy
synonyms: Bicuspid aortic valve with ascending aortic aneurysm
clinical_manifestations: Syndromic physical phenotypes: phenotypic stigmata of Turner syndrome (short stature, webbed neck [pterygium colli], low posterior hairline, shield chest with widely spaced nipples, cubitus valgus) or Loeys-Dietz/Marfan habitus (arachnodactyly, pectus deformities, high-arched palate)

Auscultatory physical signs: early, sharp, high-pitched systolic ejection click heard loudest at the apex and left lower sternal border (originating from abrupt opening doming of the pliable, congenitally fused valve leaflets, remaining constant in intensity with respiration, unlike pulmonary clicks); harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating to the carotids

Peripheral vascular pulse signs of severe aortic regurgitation (when present): water-hammer / Corrigan pulse (rapid, bounding carotid upstroke with abrupt collapse), de Musset sign (rhythmic systolic head bobbing), Quincke sign (visible capillary pulsations in nail beds), and wide pulse pressure with low diastolic blood pressure

Vascular bedside findings of associated aortic coarctation: radio-femoral pulse delay with diminished or absent lower extremity femoral/pedal pulses and systolic blood pressure gradient (>20 mmHg) between upper and lower limbs

Clinical emergency signs of acute type A aortic dissection: sudden-onset agonizing, tearing substernal/anterior chest pain radiating between the shoulder blades, asymmetric bilateral radial pulses, and profound hypotensive syncope
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic & Transesophageal Echocardiography (TTE/TEE - Primary Imaging Hallmark): Pathognomonic short-axis visual demonstration during systole of only two functional cusps with an elliptical 'fish-mouth' systolic orifice (rather than the normal triangular trifoliate opening); diastolic closure line demonstrating eccentric cusp coaptation and often a pseudoraphe (congenital fibrous seam at the fusion line between right and left coronary cusps [Type 1, 70–80%] or right and non-coronary cusps [Type 2, 20–25%]); parasternal long-axis systolic doming of the fused leaflet

Electrocardiogram-Gated Multidetector CT Angiography (CTA): High-resolution volumetric 3D reconstruction visualizing asymmetric dilation of the tubular ascending aorta and aortic root (effacement of the sinotubular junction, ascending aorta diameter >40–45 mm), demonstrating root-phenotype vs. ascending aorta-phenotype aneurysm; rules out or confirms aortic dissection flap, intramural hematoma, and concomitant coarctation

Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance (CMR): Phase-contrast 4D-flow CMR visualizes abnormal, highly eccentric helical and vortex systolic transvalvular jet flow impinging directly on the right anterolateral wall of the ascending aorta, causing elevated wall shear stress; quantifies precise aortic root, sinotubular junction, and mid-ascending aortic diameters without ionizing radiation

Chest Radiography (CXR): Prominent right superior mediastinal convexity formed by the dilated ascending aorta, prominent aortic knob, left ventricular enlargement, and occasional rib notching ('3' sign) if concomitant coarctation is present
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical Pathology: Resected aortic valve shows two unequal or equal-sized cusps with thickened, fibrotic margins, heavy coarse calcific nodules clustered within the raphe and cusp base, causing rigid immobility; resected ascending aortic wall shows marked thinning, loss of normal elasticity, smooth intima with pearly atheromatous plaques, and dilated caliber

Aortic Wall Histopathology (Cystic Medial Degeneration / Aortopathy): Profound disruption, fragmentation, and depletion of medial elastic lamellae; apoptosis and loss of vascular smooth muscle cells; large pools and lacunae of alcian blue-positive basophilic extracellular ground substance (mucopolysaccharides / glycosaminoglycans); decreased fibrillin-1 microfibrillar content; adventitial microvascular remodeling

Valvular Histopathology: Severe fibrocalcific remodeling of the aortic valve fibrosa layer with dystrophic calcification, neovascularization, and disorganized extracellular matrix architecture, driven by altered NOTCH1 and eNOS signaling
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Flawlessly meets multimodal criteria by combining phenotypic bedside signs (Turner syndromic stigmata, early systolic ejection click, Corrigan bounding pulse, radio-femoral delay) with pathognomonic echocardiographic systolic 'fish-mouth' orifice and 4D-flow CMR showing eccentric transvalvular jet and ascending aortic aneurysm, matched with gross raphe calcification and cystic medial necrosis histology.

Cardiology.name: Cardiac Amyloidosis
clinical_manifestations: Macroglossia: massive enlargement of the tongue with scalloped lateral indentations from teeth (pathognomonic in AL amyloidosis)
Periorbital ecchymoses: 'raccoon eyes' or 'pinch purpura' triggered by minor pressure or coughing (fragility of cutaneous microvessels in AL amyloidosis)
Subcutaneous amyloid nodules and waxy facial purpuric papules
Carpal tunnel syndrome (often bilateral, preceding cardiac symptoms by years)
Severe right heart failure with massive peripheral edema and hepatomegaly
radiological_manifestations: Echocardiography: Concentric, symmetrical ventricular wall thickening with normal or small left ventricular cavity; granular, sparkling myocardial texture ('ground-glass' appearance); biatrial enlargement; pathognomonic apical sparing pattern on 2D speckle-tracking strain ('cherry on top' bull's-eye map)

Cardiac MRI: Pathognomonic global, subendocardial or transmural late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) that does not conform to any coronary artery territory; difficulty nulling the myocardium; marked elevation of native T1 and extracellular volume (ECV >40%)
99mTc-Pyrophosphate (PYP) / DPD Bone Scintigraphy: Intense myocardial radiotracer uptake (Grade 2 or 3 > rib uptake) definitively diagnostic for ATTR amyloidosis without biopsy
pathology_manifestations: Endomyocardial / abdominal fat pad biopsy: Interstitial expansion by extracellular amorphous, eosinophilic, hyaline substance; pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy after Congo red staining; confirmation of amyloid subtype (AL vs ATTR) by mass spectrometry or immunohistochemistry
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Vivid clinical signs (macroglossia, periorbital 'raccoon eyes' pinch purpura) combined with landmark cardiac imaging: 'cherry on top' strain echo, non-coronary transmural LGE on MRI, and PYP scintigraphy.

Cardiology.name: Cardiac Angiosarcoma
clinical_manifestations: Superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome physical signs: severe facial, periorbital, and neck edema, florid suffusion/erythema of the face and upper thorax, prominent non-pulsatile distension of superficial jugular, thoracic, and arm collateral veins, and positive Pemberton sign (worsening facial cyanosis and stridor upon elevating both arms)

Rapidly progressive right-sided heart failure signs: massive pitting lower extremity edema, rapid-onset refractory ascites ('cardiac cirrhosis'), tender hepatomegaly with positive hepatojugular reflux, and gross jugular venous distension with prominent 'v' wave

Auscultatory and bedside hemodynamic signs of cardiac tamponade (Beck triad): marked hypotension with narrowed pulse pressure, muffled/distant heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure; pulsus paradoxus (>10–12 mmHg drop in systolic pressure during spontaneous inspiration)

Systemic constitutional and cutaneous signs: cachexia, anorexia, involuntary weight loss, intermittent pyrexia, pallor from microangiopathic hemolytic anemia or intra-tumoral hemorrhage, and hemorrhagic skin or scalp metastases in advanced disseminated disease
Respiratory stigmata: dyspnea at rest, hemoptysis, and pleuritic chest pain secondary to malignant pulmonary microvascular embolization or hemorrhagic pulmonary parenchymal metastases
radiological_manifestations: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR - Modality of Choice): Massive (typically >5–10 cm), broad-based, lobulated, ill-defined infiltrative mass centered in the right atrium with aggressive transmural invasion into the right atrial free wall, interatrial septum, tricuspid annulus, superior/inferior vena cava, and epicardial adipose tissue; marked signal heterogeneity on T1- and T2-weighted images with high T1 hyperintense foci representing subacute hemorrhage ('cauliflower' or 'sunburst' appearance); vivid, nodular, heterogeneous peripheral enhancement on first-pass perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) reflecting marked hypervascularity and intra-tumoral necrosis

Contrast-Enhanced Cardiac CT: Large, hypodense, heterogeneously enhancing infiltrative mass in the right atrium causing luminal narrowing or complete SVC/IVC occlusion; direct demonstration of transmural pericardial invasion with irregular nodular pericardial thickening and high-attenuation hemorrhagic pericardial effusion; detection of multiple hypervascular bilateral pulmonary metastases ('cannonball' or hemorrhagic halo lesions)

Transthoracic & Transesophageal Echocardiography (TTE/TEE): Rapid visualization of a broad-based, sessile, non-mobile, highly irregular and echogenic infiltrative right atrial mass obliterating the right atrial cavity; right ventricular inflow obstruction; large circumferential pericardial effusion with features of tamponade (diastolic collapse of the right atrium and right ventricle, plethoric IVC without inspiratory collapse)

18F-FDG PET-CT: Intense, heterogeneous, highly hypermetabolic FDG uptake (SUVmax often >8–15) within the primary right atrial mass and hypermetabolic nodal, pulmonary, or hepatic metastases, distinguishing malignant sarcoma from benign cardiac tumors
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical / Autopsy Pathology: Bulky, dark red-to-violaceous, spongy, fleshy, extensively hemorrhagic and necrotic infiltrative mass arising from the right atrial free wall; lacks a discrete capsule, extensively effacing normal myocardium, ulcerating through the epicardium into the pericardial space, and often encasing coronary vessels and cavoatrial junctions

Histopathology: Markedly pleomorphic, hyperchromatic, atypical malignant endothelial cells lining irregular, anastomosing, slit-like or sinusoidal vascular channels; papillary tufts, solid sheets of spindle and epithelioid cells with brisk atypical mitotic figures and extensive geographic areas of coagulative necrosis and hemorrhage

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong positivity for endothelial vascular markers including CD31 (PECAM-1), ERG (ETS-related gene, highly sensitive and specific), CD34, Factor VIII-related antigen (von Willebrand factor), and VEGF; negative for cytokeratins, S100, desmin, and calretinin (distinguishing from mesothelioma, melanoma, and synovial sarcoma)
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Exemplifies strict criteria by linking dramatic bedside signs (SVC syndrome facial edema/suffusion, rapidly progressive refractory right heart failure, Beck triad of tamponade) with pathognomonic CMR imaging (heterogeneous, hypervascular 'sunburst' infiltrative right atrial mass invading the pericardium) and hallmark angiosarcomatous histology demonstrating CD31/ERG-positive anastomosing malignant vascular channels.

Cardiology.name: Cardiac Fibroma (Gorlin-Goltz Syndrome)
synonyms: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome cardiac fibroma
clinical_manifestations: Phenotypic hallmarks of Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin-Goltz Syndrome, PTCH1 mutation): multiple cutaneous basal cell carcinomas appearing at an early age, palmar and plantar punctate pits (small 1–3 mm discrete dermal depressions), macrocephaly with frontal and parietal bossing, coarse facial features, hypertelorism, and mandibular odontogenic keratocysts
Skeletal and thoracic stigmata of Gorlin syndrome: bifid, splayed, or fused ribs, kyphoscoliosis, and pectus excavatum/carinatum

Cardiovascular hemodynamic presentations: progressive dyspnea, exercise intolerance, fatigue, and low cardiac output heart failure signs (cool extremities, weak pulses, hepatomegaly) resulting from massive rigid replacement of the ventricular wall or mechanical cavity obstruction

Bedside arrhythmogenic manifestations: recurrent syncopal episodes, palpitations, and high risk of sudden cardiac death in children and young adults from sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia or complete heart block (due to direct compression/interruption of the conduction bundle by the calcified septal mass)
Cardiovascular physical examination: prominent systolic murmurs at the left sternal border mimicking hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or aortic stenosis; paradoxical S2 splitting or prominent S4 gallop
radiological_manifestations: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR - Definitive Non-Invasive Diagnostic Tool): Solitary, massive (often 3–10 cm), intramural, sharply demarcated non-contractile mass characteristically embedded within the anterior left ventricular free wall or interventricular septum; pathognomonic signal characteristics: homogeneous isointense signal on T1-weighted images, marked and striking HYPOINTENSITY ('dark' signal) on T2-weighted images (due to dense, paucicellular, packed collagen and lack of free water content); prominent, diffuse, and homogeneous late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on delayed imaging caused by expansion of the extracellular collagenous space and slow contrast clearance

Contrast-Enhanced Cardiac CT: Densely attenuating, well-circumscribed intramyocardial mass; pathognomonic visual demonstration of coarse, central, punctate or curvilinear stippled calcifications (present in >50–60% of cases, virtually excluding other benign pediatric tumors like rhabdomyoma or myxoma); precise spatial delineation of adjacent coronary artery course (LAD or PDA) compressed or draped over the mass

Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE): Large, solitary, highly echogenic, non-mobile intramural mass embedded in the ventricular septum or LV wall; shows bright acoustic shadows from calcific foci; regional ventricular dyskinesia and dynamic outflow tract obstruction without spontaneous regression on serial exams
Chest Radiography (CXR): Striking abnormal calcified cardiac silhouette with cardiomegaly, along with incidental visualization of bifid ribs or vertebral segmentation anomalies of Gorlin syndrome
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical Pathology: Resected specimen reveals a solitary, firm to rock-hard, unencapsulated but sharply circumscribed, glistening gray-white, whorled intramural mass that grates against the scalpel during sectioning due to central calcification; expands the ventricular septum or free wall, sharply demarcated from adjacent red-brown myocardium

Histopathology: Abundant, dense, hyalinized collagenous fibrous tissue arranged in whorls, interlacing bundles, or fascicles; populated by bland, monomorphic, elongated spindle-shaped fibroblasts without cytological atypia, hyperchromasia, or mitoses; central areas of dense dystrophic calcification, ossification, and elastosis; infiltrates and traps surrounding isolated degenerating cardiac myocytes at the outer margins without true encapsulation

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for vimentin and variable smooth muscle actin (SMA); negative for desmin, myogenin, S100, CD31, and CD34; low Ki-67 proliferation index (<1%)
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict multimodal criteria through striking photographic syndromic stigmata (Gorlin syndrome palmar pits, multiple early basal cell carcinomas, frontal bossing) paired with pathognomonic CMR imaging (extreme T2 hypointensity with bright diffuse delayed enhancement and CT central calcification) and gross whorled, rock-hard fibrous histology with bland collagenous bundles.

Cardiology.name: Cardiac Myxoma and Carney Complex
synonyms: NAME syndrome (Nevi, Atrial myxoma, Myxoid neurofibromas, Ephelides)
LAMB syndrome (Lentigines, Atrial myxoma, Mucocutaneous myxomas, Blue nevi)
clinical_manifestations: Spotty mucocutaneous pigmentation and lentigines: heavily pigmented brown-to-black macules concentrated on the vermilion border of the lips, eyelids, conjunctiva, vulva/glans penis, and nasal mucosa
Cutaneous and mucosal myxomas: discrete, asymptomatic, flesh-colored, opalescent or sessile subcutaneous papules and nodules on the face, eyelids, ears, and nipples
Blue nevi: dome-shaped bluish-black dermal nodules and pigmented schwannomas
Constitutional signs: low-grade fever, involuntary weight loss, malaise, Raynaud phenomenon, and arthralgias induced by tumor interleukin-6 (IL-6) secretion

Peripheral embolic signs: splinter hemorrhages, digital petechiae, acute retinal artery occlusion (amaurosis fugax), and painful digital ischemia / blue toe syndrome from fragmented tumor embolization

Auscultatory physical sign: low-pitched early diastolic 'tumor plop' heard shortly after S2 (caused by sudden deceleration of the mobile pedunculated mass as it strikes the endocardial wall or wedges into the mitral orifice), accompanied by a positional murmur that changes with body posture
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic & Transesophageal Echocardiography (TTE/TEE - Modality of Choice): Mobile, heterogeneously echogenic, smooth or villous pedunculated intracardiac mass typically arising from the fossa ovalis border of the interatrial septum (>75% left atrium, 15-20% right atrium); classic real-time visual demonstration of diastolic prolapse through the mitral orifice into the left ventricular inflow tract causing intermittent functional mitral stenosis, and systolic retreat back into the atrium

Cardiac MRI (CMR): Well-circumscribed, lobulated intracavitary mass exhibiting low-to-isointense signal on T1-weighted images, hyperintense heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted and steady-state free precession (SSFP) cine sequences due to high extracellular water and mucopolysaccharide content; variable, patchy, non-uniform enhancement on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging distinguishing it from avascular cardiac thrombi

Contrast-Enhanced Cardiac CT: Smoothly contoured, lobulated, hypoattenuating intracardiac filling defect attached by a narrow stalk to the fossa ovalis; demonstrates mobility between systole and diastole and absence of deep myocardial wall invasion
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical Pathology: Gelatinous, sessile or pedunculated, friable, glistening, semi-translucent, greenish-yellow to dark red/brown polypoid mass with superficial thrombi, hemorrhages, and gelatinous mucoid substance

Histopathology: Abundant, pale, alcian blue-positive acidic mucopolysaccharide-rich myxoid stroma containing stellate, globular, or spindle-shaped 'myxoma cells' (lepidic cells) arranged singly, in cords, syncytial rings, or perivascular pseudorosettes surrounding capillary-like vascular channels; calretinin, CD31, and CD34 positive
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Exemplifies strict multimodal visual criteria: striking photographic cutaneous signs (Carney complex facial lentiginosis, blue nevi, cutaneous myxomas, splinter emboli) combined with pathognomonic real-time echocardiographic diastolic mitral prolapse ('tumor plop') and distinctive alcian blue-rich myxoid histology.

Cardiology.name: Cardiac Rhabdomyoma (Tuberous Sclerosis Complex)
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous photographic hallmarks of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC1/TSC2): hypomelanotic macules ('ash-leaf' spots, best visualized under Wood lamp), shagreen patches (leathery, pebbled plaques on the lumbosacral region), facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum, reddish papules in butterfly distribution across malar and nasal areas), and periungual/subungual fibromas (Koenen tumors)

Neonatal and infantile cardiovascular distress: severe heart failure signs with diaphoresis during feeds, poor weight gain, tachypnea, subcostal retractions, hepatomegaly, and central cyanosis from intracardiac blood flow obstruction
Auscultatory physical findings: harsh systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border (outflow tract obstruction) or holosystolic regurgitant murmurs across AV valves; gallop rhythm (S3/S4)

Arrhythmogenic bedside presentations: life-threatening neonatal tachyarrhythmias (supraventricular tachycardia, Wolff-Parkinson-White [WPW] pre-excitation with delta waves on ECG, ventricular tachycardia) or severe sinus bradycardia/heart block from conduction system involvement
Neurological stigmata of TSC: infantile spasms (West syndrome with hypsarrhythmia), focal motor seizures, and developmental delay
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE - Primary Diagnostic Modality): Multiple (in >70–90% of TSC cases) or solitary, well-demarcated, homogeneously hyper-echogenic, rounded or lobulated intramyocardial masses embedded within the ventricular septum, left ventricular apex, or right ventricular free wall, often protruding into ventricular outflow tracts (causing left or right ventricular outflow tract obstruction [LVOTO/RVOTO]); dynamic serial echocardiograms demonstrate pathognomonic progressive spontaneous tumor regression over the first 2–4 years of life

Fetal Echocardiography: High-resolution prenatal detection of solitary or multiple discrete echogenic cardiac tumors in the ventricular myocardium during the second or third trimester (often the very first phenotypic manifestation prompting parental genetic screening for TSC)

Cardiac MRI (CMR): Well-defined, non-invasive homogeneous masses embedded in myocardium; characteristically isointense to slightly hyperintense to normal myocardium on T1-weighted images, homogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images (due to high intracellular glycogen content); demonstrates lack of late gadolinium enhancement (or minimal peripheral rim enhancement) and absence of myocardial infiltration or tissue destruction

Brain MRI (Concurrent Diagnostic Neuroimaging): Demonstration of pathognomonic subependymal nodules (SENs), subependymal giant cell astrocytomas (SEGAs) near the foramen of Monro, and cortical/subcortical tubers
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical / Autopsy Pathology: Well-circumscribed, solid, non-encapsulated, fleshy, white-to-yellow-tan nodular masses embedded within the myocardium, bulging into the ventricular cavities; cut surface is homogeneous, smooth, and glistening without hemorrhage, calcification, or cyst formation

Histopathology (Pathognomonic 'Spider Cells'): Voluminous, markedly enlarged, rounded or polygonal glycogenic cells with clear, vacuolated cytoplasm containing abundant glycogen (deeply PAS-positive, diastase-sensitive); slender cytoplasmic strands radiate from the centrally or eccentrically placed nucleus through empty-appearing vacuolated spaces to the cell membrane, forming classic, unmistakable 'spider cells' (cellules araignées)

Immunohistochemistry: Positive for muscle and intermediate filament markers including desmin, myoglobin, vimentin, and muscle-specific actin (HHF-35); positive for hamartin (TSC1) / tuberin (TSC2) pathway alterations; low/absent Ki-67 proliferation index confirming benign hamartomatous nature
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets multimodal criteria through classic dermatologic photography (ash-leaf spots under Wood lamp, facial angiofibromas, shagreen patches) combined with distinctive neonatal echocardiography showing multiple homogeneous intramyocardial masses that undergo spontaneous involution, and pathognomonic 'spider cell' histology packed with PAS-positive glycogen.

Cardiology.name: Coarctation of the Aorta
clinical_manifestations: Upper extremity arterial hypertension with differential blood pressure gradient (>20 mmHg higher in arms than legs)
Radiofemoral delay: noticeable lag and palpable diminution or complete absence of femoral pulses relative to simultaneous radial or brachial pulses
Underdeveloped, slender, cold lower extremities with intermittent claudication during exertion, contrasting with robust, well-muscled upper torso and arms

Visibly dilated, tortuous, pulsating collateral intercostal and periscapular arteries palpated or seen over the posterior thoracic wall, infrascapular region, and axillae (accentuated when bending forward)

Continuous or late systolic bruit heard best over the left interscapular region, thoracic spine, and back; association with Turner syndrome (webbed neck, low posterior hairline, shield chest with widely spaced nipples, short stature)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography: Pathognomonic 'figure-of-3' sign on the left mediastinal contour formed by pre-stenotic aortic arch dilatation, the waist-like coarctation indentation, and post-stenotic descending aortic dilatation; pathognomonic inferior rib notching (Roesler sign) affecting the 3rd to 8th ribs bilaterally (due to erosion of the inferior costal grooves by dilated, tortuous, pulsating intercostal collateral arteries; typically spares ribs 1-2); 'reversed figure-3' or 'E-sign' on barium esophagogram

CT Angiography (CTA) / MR Angiography (MRA) of the Aorta (Imaging Gold Standard): Exquisite 3D anatomical visualization of the focal shelf-like posterior aortic infolding and narrowing at the aortic isthmus near the ligamentum arteriosum; extensive 3D mapping of hypertrophied, winding collateral vascular networks (internal mammary arteries, intercostal arteries, scapular circumflex vessels); detection of associated bicuspid aortic valve and ascending aortic aneurysm

Transthoracic Suprasternal Echocardiography: High-velocity systolic and continuous diastolic forward turbulent flow across the narrowing ('sawtooth' or 'diastolic runoff' Doppler pattern); direct 2D imaging of the narrowed aortic isthmus
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical Pathology: Discrete, shelf-like, eccentric medial ridge protruding inward from the posterolateral wall of the aorta toward the ostium of the ductus arteriosus / ligamentum arteriosum, severely compromising the aortic lumen; localized post-stenotic dilatation with intimal thinning ('jet lesion')

Histopathology: Localized hypertrophy and medial thickening with abnormal circumferential extension of ductal-like smooth muscle and fragmented elastic fibers into the aortic wall; prominent intimal fibroelastosis overlying the stenotic shelf
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria: striking physical bedside findings (radiofemoral delay, upper vs. lower limb disparity, visible pulsating scapular collaterals, Turner phenotype) paired with pathognomonic radiological signs ('figure-of-3' sign, Roesler inferior rib notching, and CTA aortic shelf narrowing).

Cardiology.name: Complete Atrioventricular Septal Defect
synonyms: Ostium primum defect with common AV valve
clinical_manifestations: Striking syndromic physical phenotype: Strong, classic association with Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome, present in >60% of cases): characteristic dysmorphic facies (upslanting palpebral fissures, prominent epicanthal folds, flat nasal bridge, macroglossia, low-set ears), Brushfield spots on the iris, generalized muscular hypotonia, and a single transverse palmar crease (simian crease)

Infantile heart failure presentation: Onset of progressive, high-output congestive heart failure between 4 and 8 weeks of life (as pulmonary vascular resistance falls): tachypnea, diaphoresis during feeding, prolonged feeding times with poor caloric intake, failure to thrive, and recurrent lower respiratory tract infections due to massive left-to-right shunting and early pulmonary vascular engorgement

Precordial physical examination: Hyperdynamic precordium with prominent left parasternal lift and palpable apical impulse; precordial bulge; wide and fixed splitting of S2 with a markedly accentuated pulmonary closure sound (loud P2) reflecting pulmonary hypertension

Cardiac auscultation: Harsh holosystolic regurgitant murmur best heard at the apex and radiating to the left axilla (mitral component of common AV valve regurgitation), accompanied by a mid-systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border (increased flow across the pulmonary valve) and a mid-diastolic rumble at the lower left sternal border

Electrocardiographic (ECG) pathognomonic sign: Superior QRS axis with extreme left-axis deviation (-30° to -150°), counterclockwise frontal QRS loop, prolonged PR interval (first-degree AV block), and biventricular hypertrophy with prominent biphasic R and S waves across mid-precordial leads (Katz-Wachtel phenomenon)
radiological_manifestations: Cineangiography & Left Ventriculography (Historical & Interventional Gold Standard): Classic pathognomonic 'gooseneck deformity' of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) demonstrated in the right anterior oblique (RAO) and elongated hepatoclavicular views, caused by deficiency of the inlet muscular ventricular septum, unwedging and anterior displacement of the aortic root, and the elongated, scalloped, narrowed LVOT bordered by the anterior bridging leaflet of the common AV valve

Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE - Diagnostic Modality of Choice): Pathognomonic loss of the normal apical offset of the tricuspid valve relative to the mitral valve (the two atrioventricular valve rings lie in the exact same horizontal plane); large ostium primum atrial septal defect extending directly to the AV valve junction; confluent, large inlet ventricular septal defect with a scooped-out crest of the muscular ventricular septum; single, unpartitioned common atrioventricular valve with anterior and posterior bridging leaflets spanning across both ventricles (Rastelli classification Type A, B, or C depending on anterior leaflet chordal attachments to the crest of the septum or anterior papillary muscle); Color Doppler assesses the degree of common AV valve regurgitation (predominantly originating from the zone of apposition / 'cleft' between the left anterior and posterior bridging leaflets) and evaluates right and left ventricular chamber balance (balanced vs. unbalanced AVSD)

Cardiac MRI (CMR): High-resolution cine SSFP and 4D flow MR imaging provide precise 3D delineation of the common valve morphology, accurately quantify regurgitant fractions, assess the extent of anterior bridging leaflet tethering, and calculate exact ventricular volumes to guide univentricular versus biventricular surgical repair pathways

Chest Radiography: Marked biventricular and right atrial cardiomegaly, prominent main pulmonary artery segment, and extensive pulmonary plethora (increased pulmonary vascular markings) with rapid development of pulmonary arterial remodeling
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical & Autopsy Pathology: Complete failure of embryonic fusion of the superior and inferior endocardial cushions, creating a large, confluent central cardiac defect involving the inferior portion of the atrial septum (ostium primum defect) and the inlet portion of the ventricular septum (scooped-out, crescentic inlet VSD); a single common five-leaflet atrioventricular valve (anterior bridging leaflet, posterior bridging leaflet, right lateral leaflet, left lateral leaflet, and right anterior leaflet); unwedged, anteriorly displaced aortic valve leading to an elongated, narrowed left ventricular outflow tract; complete developmental absence of the atrioventricular septum

Histopathology: Mesenchymal hypocellularity or myxoid dysmorphic connective tissue matrix within the common atrioventricular valve leaflets, with disordered collagen and fragmented elastic fibers; abnormal displacement and hypoplasia of the cardiac conduction system (the AV node is displaced postero-inferiorly toward the coronary sinus ostium, and the bundle of His travels along the lower fibrous rim of the inlet VSD, creating susceptibility to surgical and congenital AV block); progressive medial hypertrophy and intimal proliferation of muscular pulmonary arteries (Heath-Edwards Grade I-IV changes) if uncorrected
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive endocardial cushion embryopathy featuring classic bedside syndromic markers (Down syndrome facies, Brushfield spots, simian crease) and superior ECG axis, pathognomonic 'gooseneck' sign on angiography/ventriculography, echocardiographic single common AV valve with primum ASD/inlet VSD, and diagnostic developmental absence of the AV septum on pathology.

Cardiology.name: Constrictive Pericarditis
clinical_manifestations: Marked elevation of jugular venous pressure with rapid 'y' descent (Friedreich sign)
Kussmaul sign: paradoxical rise in jugular venous pressure during inspiration
Pericardial knock (high-pitched, early diastolic sound following S2)
Massive abdominal ascites ('cardiac cirrhosis') out of proportion to dependent lower extremity edema
Cachexia, jaundice, and facial fullness/plethora
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT / Cardiac MRI: Dense, circumferential, thick pericardial calcification encircling the cardiac ventricles; thickened pericardium (>4 mm); tubular or conical ventricular deformity, marked dilatation of inferior vena cava and hepatic veins

Echocardiography (Doppler): Ventricular septal bounce / 'shiver' in early diastole; marked respiratory variation in mitral inflow velocity (>25%) and tricuspid inflow velocity (>40%); hepatic vein expiratory diastolic flow reversal; preserved/elevated tissue Doppler mitral annular e' velocity (annulus reversus)
pathology_manifestations: Pericardiectomy surgical specimen: Dense, hyalinized, hypocellular fibrotic thickening of the parietal and visceral pericardium with extensive dystrophic calcification and chronic non-specific mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Striking bedside hemodynamic signs (Kussmaul sign, elevated JVP, massive ascites) matched with the pathognomonic dense pericardial calcification on chest CT and septal bounce on echo.

Cardiology.name: D-Transposition of the Great Arteries
synonyms: Complete transposition of the great arteries
clinical_manifestations: Immediate neonatal cyanosis: Deep, generalized, intense cyanosis manifesting within the first hours to days of life, refractory to 100% supplemental oxygen (negative hyperoxia test with arterial PaO2 characteristically < 35-40 mmHg), as the systemic and pulmonary circulations function as two parallel, independent closed circuits rather than in series

Reverse differential cyanosis: Pathognomonic bedside finding in cases with coexisting pulmonary hypertension and a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA): the upper extremities are noticeably MORE cyanotic than the lower extremities (pre-ductal desaturated blood from the transposed aorta supplies the head and arms, whereas post-ductal oxygenated blood from the pulmonary artery shunts right-to-left through the PDA into the descending aorta supplying the lower extremities)

Respiratory physical sign: 'Comfortable tachypnea' — infants exhibit rapid breathing without prominent chest wall retractions or severe respiratory distress in early hours, contrasting with the profound hypoxemia

Cardiac auscultation: Single, loud, accentuated second heart sound (S2) heard prominently at the left upper sternal border, caused by anterior displacement of the aortic valve bringing aortic closure close to the chest wall, while pulmonary valve closure is muffled posteriorly; cardiac murmurs are often surprisingly soft or absent unless accompanied by a significant ventricular septal defect or left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
Hyperdynamic precordium: Markedly increased right ventricular impulse and parasternal lift, reflecting the morphological right ventricle operating under systemic afterload

Acute hemodynamic collapse: Rapid, life-threatening clinical decompensation with severe metabolic acidosis, shock, and death upon spontaneous closure of the ductus arteriosus and foramen ovale, requiring emergency prostaglandin E1 (alprostadil) infusion and urgent balloon atrial septostomy (Rashkind procedure)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Classic Neonatal Sign): Pathognomonic 'egg-on-a-string' (or 'egg-shaped') cardiac silhouette, characterized by an enlarged, oval/globular heart silhouette resting on the diaphragm with a markedly narrow superior mediastinal shadow (caused by the superimposition of the anteriorly positioned aorta directly in front of the pulmonary artery, combined with stress-induced thymic atrophy), accompanied by increased pulmonary vascular markings (pulmonary plethora)

Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE - Diagnostic Gold Standard): Ventriculoarterial discordance with atrioventricular concordance: Morphological right ventricle (identified by coarse apical trabeculations, moderator band, and tricuspid valve with septal leaflet attachment) gives rise anteriorly to the aorta (identified by arch vessels and coronary ostia); Morphological left ventricle (identified by smooth septal surface, two discrete papillary muscles, and mitral valve) gives rise posteriorly to the main pulmonary artery (identified by immediate bifurcation into left and right branch pulmonary arteries); Parasternal short-axis view demonstrates parallel, non-crossing great vessels ('double-barrel' or 'two circles' appearance) rather than the normal perpendicular crossing orientation; Doppler interrogation evaluates the size and direction of intercirculatory mixing at the ASD/PFO, VSD, and PDA

Cardiac MRI (CMR): 3D cine SSFP and magnetic resonance angiography provide exquisite definition of ventriculoarterial discordance, quantify systemic RV function, delineate great vessel spatial geometry, and map coronary artery branching patterns (e.g., circumflex arising from RCA) critical for arterial switch (Jatene) surgical planning
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical & Autopsy Pathology: Complete ventriculoarterial discordance with concordant atrioventricular connections; the aorta arises entirely from the anterior, morphological right ventricle and lies anterior and to the right of the pulmonary trunk (D-looping); the main pulmonary trunk arises from the posterior, morphological left ventricle and lies posterior and to the left; well-developed subaortic muscular infundibulum (conus arteriosus) produces fibrous discontinuity between the aortic valve and the tricuspid valve, whereas subpulmonary muscular conus is absent, maintaining fibrous continuity between the pulmonary valve and the anterior mitral leaflet; progressive, massive concentric hypertrophy of the systemic right ventricle

Histopathology: Transition from normal neonatal myocardium to severe concentric muscular hypertrophy and interstitial collagen fibrosis of the right ventricle; rapid development of severe pulmonary vascular remodeling with medial hypertrophy and intimal proliferation of muscular pulmonary arteries if excessive pulmonary blood flow is left uncorrected
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic parallel-circulation cyanotic congenital heart disease with striking bedside refractory cyanosis and single loud S2, diagnosed by the pathognomonic 'egg-on-a-string' CXR sign and ventriculoarterial discordance with parallel great vessels on echocardiography, verified by conal anatomy discordance at pathology.

Cardiology.name: Ebstein Anomaly
synonyms: Ebstein's malformation of the tricuspid valve
clinical_manifestations: Variable central and peripheral cyanosis, deepening during crying, exercise, or in the presence of an associated atrial septal defect (ASD) or patent foramen ovale (PFO)
Striking digital clubbing in adolescents and adults with chronic right-to-left shunting

Bedside signs of severe right-sided heart failure: prominent jugular venous distention with large regurgitant v waves or rapid y descents; gross, tender hepatomegaly with palpable systolic liver pulsations; marked ascites and peripheral edema
Facial plethora and dusky complexion; precordial asymmetry with left parasternal bulge

Auscultatory 'cadence murmur': widely split S1 with loud, delayed, snapping tricuspid closure sound ('sail sound'), third and fourth heart sounds creating a characteristic triple or quadruple gallop rhythm, and holosystolic regurgitant murmur at the lower left sternal border; Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) pre-excitation delta waves on ECG in up to 25% of cases
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Iconic Hallmark): Massive, globular, 'wall-to-wall' or 'box-shaped' cardiomegaly filling the entire right hemithorax (cardiac silhouette often spanning from left to right ribs with cardiothoracic ratio >0.65-0.80); extremely sharp, prominent right heart border formed by the enormous right atrium; narrow superior mediastinal vascular pedicle; pulmonary oligemia from reduced pulmonary blood flow

Transthoracic & Transesophageal Echocardiography (TTE/TEE - Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic apical displacement of the hinge point of the septal and posterior tricuspid valve leaflets by >= 8 mm/m2 body surface area (or >20 mm in adults) relative to the anterior mitral leaflet; division of the right ventricle into two distinct compartments: a thinned, dilated, hypocontractile 'atrialized right ventricle' (aRV) continuous with the true right atrium, and a small, functional apical right ventricle (fRV); gigantic, redundant, elongated, 'sail-like' anterior tricuspid valve leaflet exhibiting whipping motion; severe, low-velocity tricuspid regurgitation jet; Celermajer severity index (ratio of aRA + aRV area to fRV + LA + LV area > 1.0 indicating severe disease)

Cardiac MRI (CMR): Precise volumetric quantification of functional RV vs. atrialized RV volumes; late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) demonstrating fibrosis in the thinned atrialized RV free wall; accurate 3D assessment of tricuspid regurgitation volume
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology: Marked failure of delamination of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve from the underlying ventricular myocardium, adhering them downwards toward the apex; marked thinning and dilation of the inlet portion of the RV free wall (atrialized RV), which functions hemodynamically as an extension of the right atrium; huge, sail-like anterior leaflet with tethered, anomalous chordae tendineae attached directly to the ventricular free wall

Histopathology: Extreme thinning of the atrialized right ventricular myocardium with attenuation or near-complete loss of myocytes, replaced by fibrofatty tissue; endocardial fibroelastosis of the true right atrium and atrialized ventricle; dysplastic tricuspid valve leaflets with disrupted fibrosa and spongy collagen
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria: striking physical bedside manifestations (cyanosis, clubbing, pulsatile liver, quadruple gallop) combined with iconic 'wall-to-wall / box-shaped heart' on chest radiograph, pathognomonic apical displacement of tricuspid leaflets on echo, and gross atrialized RV pathology.

Cardiology.name: Endomyocardial Fibrosis (Davies Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Severe cachexia, muscle wasting, and stunted growth in endemic tropical populations ('Davies habitus')

Massive, refractory abdominal ascites ('cardiac cirrhosis') with gross abdominal distension, out of proportion to mild or absent lower extremity edema (due to preferential right ventricular involvement)
Central and peripheral cyanosis, cold extremities, and striking digital clubbing of the fingers and toes
Facial periorbital puffiness, exophthalmos, parotid gland enlargement, and central/peripheral jaundice
Grossly elevated jugular venous pressure with steep 'y' descent and positive Kussmaul sign; tricuspid/mitral regurgitation murmurs
radiological_manifestations: Echocardiography (TTE/TEE - Diagnostic Hallmark): Pathognomonic endocardial thickening and dense fibrous obliteration of the left and/or right ventricular apex, creating an 'apical amputated' appearance; retraction and apical tethering of the posterior atrioventricular valve leaflets (mitral and/or tricuspid), causing severe valve regurgitation; extreme biatrial enlargement ('giant atria') with normal or small ventricular cavities; restrictive ventricular filling pattern on Doppler with high E wave, low A wave (E/A > 2.0), and shortened deceleration time (<140 ms)

Cardiac MRI (CMR): Pathognomonic 'V'-shaped apex with continuous, thick subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) lining the ventricular apices and inflow tracts; overlying apical intraventricular thrombus that shows no gadolinium uptake; precise identification of three layers at the apex (normal myocardium, thick enhancing fibrotic endocardium, and non-enhancing cavitary thrombus)

Chest Radiography: Massive cardiomegaly dominated by extreme right or bilateral atrial enlargement; curvilinear apical endocardial calcification outlining the ventricular apex; pulmonary venous congestion in left-sided disease
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology: Thick, porcelain-white, cartilaginous-like endocardial plaque lining the ventricular apices and extending along the inflow tract up to the papillary muscles and atrioventricular valve leaflets, rigidly anchoring and retracting the posterior leaflet into the ventricular wall; ventricular apical obliteration by dense collagenous tissue with organized overlying mural thrombi

Histopathology: Thickened endocardium composed of dense, hyalinized collagen bundles and proliferating fibroblasts with loss of subendocardial elastic fibers; underlying subendocardial myocardium shows progressive vacuolar degeneration, replacement fibrosis, and chronic mononuclear infiltrate; in Löffler variant, prominent eosinophilic infiltration, degranulation, and Charcot-Leyden crystals
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Satisfies strict multimodal visual criteria: hallmark physical signs (cachectic habitus, massive ascites, central cyanosis, digital clubbing) paired with pathognomonic echocardiographic and CMR visual signs of apical obliteration ('amputated apex') and porcelain-white endocardial fibrous thickening.

Cardiology.name: Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy
clinical_manifestations: Dynamic auscultatory hallmark: Harsh, crescendo-decrescendo mid-systolic ejection murmur best heard along the lower left sternal border and cardiac apex, radiating toward the axilla but characteristically NOT to the carotid arteries (distinguishing from aortic stenosis)

Murmur provocation dynamics: Murmur dramatically INCREASES in intensity with maneuvers that reduce left ventricular end-diastolic volume/preload or reduce afterload (Valsalva strain phase, abrupt standing, amyl nitrate inhalation, nitroglycerin administration); murmur characteristically DECREASES in intensity with maneuvers that increase preload or afterload (squatting, passive leg elevation, sustained isometric handgrip)

Arterial pulse sign: Pulsus bisferiens ('spike-and-dome' carotid arterial pulse), exhibiting a brisk, jerky initial percussion wave resulting from rapid early systolic LV ejection, followed by a mid-systolic dip caused by acute LVOT obstruction, and a secondary slower tidal wave

Precordial palpation: Sustained, forceful, double or triple apical impulse (a prominent presystolic impulse due to vigorous left atrial contraction against a stiff noncompliant LV, followed by a sustained systolic lift and late-systolic thrust)
Jugular venous examination: Exaggerated 'a' wave reflecting forceful right atrial contraction against a hypertrophied, noncompliant right ventricle (Bernheim effect)

Clinical presentation: Exertional dyspnea, angina pectoris in the setting of angiographically normal epicardial coronary arteries (caused by microvascular ischemia and oxygen supply-demand mismatch), exertional presyncope or syncope, and tragic sudden cardiac death (SCD) triggered by ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation during intense athletic exertion in young asymptomatic individuals
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic & Transesophageal Echocardiography (TTE/TEE - Primary Diagnostic Standard): Marked asymmetric septal hypertrophy (ASH) with an interventricular septum to left ventricular posterior wall thickness ratio (IVS/PW) > 1.3 in normotensives (or > 1.5 in hypertensives), with absolute septal thickness typically >= 15 mm (>= 13 mm in patients with positive family history); Systolic Anterior Motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet striking the hypertrophied septum in mid-to-late systole, producing dynamic Left Ventricular Outflow Tract (LVOT) obstruction and an eccentric, posteriorly directed mitral regurgitation jet; Continuous-wave Doppler pathognomonic late-peaking, 'dagger-shaped' (saber-shaped) high-velocity systolic jet across the LVOT, with peak resting or provoked gradient >= 30 mmHg defining obstruction (>= 50 mmHg defining hemodynamically severe obstruction)

Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CMR - Modality of Choice for Phenotypic Characterization & Risk Stratification): Cine steady-state free precession (SSFP) sequences provide superior tomographic quantification of maximal wall thickness, detection of focal or apical variants (Yamaguchi phenotype), structural anterior mitral leaflet elongation, and anomalous papillary muscle architecture (accessory heads or direct insertion into the anterior leaflet); Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE) characteristically demonstrates patchy, non-ischemic mid-wall enhancement preferentially localized at the junctional anterior and posterior right-to-left ventricular insertion points and areas of maximal myocardial hypertrophy, serving as a validated substrate marker for ventricular arrhythmogenesis and sudden cardiac death risk

Electrocardiography (ECG): High-voltage criteria for severe left ventricular hypertrophy (Sokolow-Lyon, Cornell); narrow, deep, dagger-like pseudo-infarct Q waves in inferolateral leads (II, III, aVF, V4-V6) resulting from initial septal depolarization of the hypertrophied anterior septum; giant negative symmetric T-wave inversions in anterolateral or precordial leads (> 10 mm in apical variant)

Chest Radiography: Mild-to-moderate left ventricular prominence with normal or widened aortic root, left atrial enlargement secondary to elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure and chronic mitral regurgitation, without classic post-stenotic aortic dilatation
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical & Autopsy Pathology: Massive asymmetrical myocardial hypertrophy predominantly involving the basal anterior and subaortic interventricular septum bulging convexly into the left ventricular outflow tract; narrowed, compressed, slit-like or banana-shaped left ventricular cavity; thickened, elongated anterior mitral valve leaflet with a prominent, well-demarcated fibrous endocardial friction plaque on the opposing septal surface caused by recurrent systolic anterior motion collisions

Histopathology: Pathognomonic myocardial disarray (loss of normal parallel myofiber architecture, replaced by complex branching, herringbone, pinwheel, or whorled patterns of hypertrophied myocytes interweaving at bizarre oblique and perpendicular angles); marked myocyte hypertrophy with nuclear pleomorphism and hyperchromatic 'boxcar' nuclei; extensive interstitial and perimysial replacement collagen fibrosis; prominent medial hypertrophy and intimal hyperplasia of intramural coronary arterioles (small-vessel arteriolar dysplasia) producing localized microvascular ischemia
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic structural genetic cardiomyopathy with unmistakable physical examination findings (dynamic murmur intensifying with Valsalva, bisferiens carotid pulse) coupled with pathognomonic echocardiographic systolic anterior motion (SAM), dagger-shaped Doppler envelope, and gold-standard histological myofiber disarray.

Cardiology.name: Kawasaki Disease
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral non-exudative bulbar conjunctival injection with perilimbal sparing
Strawberry tongue: bright red tongue with prominent, enlarged fungiform papillae
Erythema, dryness, cracking, fissuring, and bleeding of the vermilion border of the lips
Polymorphous cutaneous exanthem (erythematous morbilliform, maculopapular rash)
Indurated, non-pitting edema and erythema of the palms and soles
Subacute periungual sheet-like desquamation (peeling of skin around fingers and toes)
Acute cervical lymphadenopathy (typically unilateral, >1.5 cm)
radiological_manifestations: Echocardiography (Pediatric Cardiac Echo): Rapid, serialized detection of coronary artery ectasia, saccular and fusiform coronary artery aneurysms (LAD, RCA), giant coronary aneurysms (internal diameter >=8 mm or Z-score >=10), intraluminal thrombi, pericardial effusion, decreased left ventricular contractility
CT Coronary Angiography (CTCA): High-resolution 3D mapping of coronary aneurysm remodeling, calcification, and occlusive stenosis in convalescent/adolescent Kawasaki disease
pathology_manifestations: Coronary artery biopsy/autopsy: Systemic vasculitis of medium-sized muscular arteries with three sequential phases: acute necrotizing arteritis (neutrophilic infiltration destroying internal elastic lamina), subacute/chronic vasculitis (lymphocytic, plasma cell infiltration), and luminal myofibroblastic proliferation causing progressive coronary stenosis
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria: striking clinical physical findings (strawberry tongue, cracked lips, periungual peeling, conjunctivitis) coupled with life-saving echocardiographic coronary artery aneurysms.

Cardiology.name: Rheumatic Heart Disease and Acute Rheumatic Carditis
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous photographic hallmarks of Acute Rheumatic Fever (Jones Criteria): Erythema marginatum (transient, non-pruritic, pink-to-red serpiginous or annular macules and patches with sharp, raised advancing borders and central clearing, predominantly on the trunk and proximal extremities, sparing the face) and Subcutaneous nodules (firm, painless, freely movable nodules ranging from 0.5–2 cm over bony prominences and extensor tendons of the elbows, wrists, knees, and ankles)

Neurological motor physical signs: Sydenham chorea (St. Vitus dance: involuntary, purposeless, non-rhythmic choreiform jerks of the face, tongue, and limbs, 'milkmaid grip' [rhythmic squeezing and releasing of examiner's hand], 'choreic tongue' [darting tongue], and spooning of the hands)

Auscultatory physical examination in acute carditis: Carey Coombs murmur (short, soft, mid-diastolic apical murmur without presystolic accentuation, caused by active mitral valvulitis) and apical holosystolic regurgitant murmur; pericardial friction rub (three-component scratchy sound)

Auscultatory physical examination in chronic rheumatic mitral stenosis: loud first heart sound (S1), high-pitched early diastolic opening snap (OS) followed by a low-pitched, rumbling mid-diastolic murmur with presystolic accentuation heard best at the apex in the left lateral decubitus position

Physical exam stigmata of chronic mitral stenosis: 'facies mitralis' (malar flush with violaceous, dusky erythema over the cheeks), gross signs of right heart failure (severe jugular venous distension, hepatomegaly, ascites), and irregularly irregular pulse indicating atrial fibrillation
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic & Transesophageal Echocardiography (TTE/TEE - Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic rheumatic mitral valve morphology: diastolic anterior leaflet doming producing the classic 'hockey-stick' or 'dog-leg' deformity on parasternal long-axis view; thickening and retraction of leaflet tips with commissural fusion; severe subvalvular thickening, shortening, and fusion of chordae tendineae; short-axis view demonstrates the pathognomonic rigid, stenotic 'fish-mouth' (buttonhole) mitral orifice; continuous wave Doppler demonstrates elevated transmitral mean pressure gradient and prolonged pressure half-time (PHT) used to calculate stenotic valve area

Electrocardiogram-Gated Multidetector CT / Fluoroscopy: Dense, heavy calcification along the fused mitral commissures, leaflet margins, and subvalvular chordal apparatus; accurate assessment of mitral valve calcification score prior to percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy (PMBC); severe left atrial enlargement with mural calcification ('porcelain left atrium')

Chest Radiography (CXR): Classic 'mitral heart' configuration: prominent left atrial appendage straightening the left cardiac border, double-density right heart border (enlarged left atrium projecting behind right atrium), splaying of the carina (>90 degrees), upward displacement of the left mainstem bronchus, and pulmonary venous hypertension with cephalization and Kerley B lines

Cardiac MRI (CMR): Assesses transvalvular peak velocities and planar mitral valve area; identifies chronic left atrial chamber remodeling and intra-atrial appendage thrombus; late gadolinium enhancement demonstrates myocardial replacement fibrosis in chronic rheumatic cardiomyopathy
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical / Autopsy Pathology: Fibrous thickening, contracture, and fusion of the valve leaflets; commissural fusion transforming the mitral valve into a rigid, funnel-shaped or 'fish-mouth' / 'buttonhole' orifice; markedly thickened, fused, and shortened chordae tendineae ('tree-trunk' chordae); pathognomonic MacCallum patch (corrugated, map-like, irregular thickened endocardial plaque in the posterior wall of the left atrium above the posterior mitral leaflet); small, sterile, translucent verrucae (1–2 mm) along the contact margins of valve closure in acute phase

Histopathology (Hallmark Pathognomonic Aschoff Bodies): Distinctive interstitial myocardial and subendocardial granulomatous nodules featuring a central focus of eosinophilic fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by a cuff of T lymphocytes, plasma cells, and pathognomonic Anitschkow cells ('caterpillar cells': specialized cardiac histiocytes with abundant amphophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei containing a central slender, wavy ribbon of chromatin with serrated margins); multinucleated Aschoff giant cells with up to 4–5 overlapping nuclei
Chronic Histopathology: Dense, hyalinized collagenous vascularized scar tissue obliterating normal trilaminar valve architecture, with neovascular capillary proliferation and dystrophic calcification
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria by uniting historic, visually striking bedside stigmata (erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules, Sydenham chorea, facies mitralis) with pathognomonic echocardiography showing 'hockey-stick' anterior mitral doming and 'fish-mouth' stenotic orifice, corroborated by pathognomonic Aschoff body and Anitschkow 'caterpillar cell' histopathology.

Cardiology.name: Syphilitic Aortitis (Cardiovascular Syphilis)
clinical_manifestations: Peripheral hyperdynamic circulatory signs of severe aortic regurgitation: 'water-hammer' or Corrigan pulse (rapid, forceful pulse upstroke with abrupt collapse); wide pulse pressure (>100 mmHg differential)
de Musset sign: rhythmic, involuntary head nodding synchronous with arterial pulsation
Müller sign: systolic pulsation of the uvula and soft palate
Quincke sign: alternating blanching and flushing of the nailbed capillary bed when gentle pressure is applied

Traube sign: booming 'pistol-shot' sounds heard over the femoral arteries during systole; Duroziez sign: systolic murmur over the femoral artery upon proximal compression and diastolic murmur upon distal compression

Cutaneous and neurological tertiary syphilitic stigmas: syphilitic gummas (noduloulcerative, punched-out cutaneous or palatal destructive ulcers), Argyll Robertson pupils (small, irregular pupils that accommodate to near vision but do not react to bright light; 'prostitute's pupils'), tabetic Charcot joints, and tabetic sensory ataxia
Suprasternal pulsatile mass, tracheal tug (Oliver sign), and hoarseness (Ortner syndrome from recurrent laryngeal nerve stretch)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography: Pathognomonic thin, linear, curvilinear calcification outlining the ascending aorta wall ('tree-bark calcification' or eggshell calcification), rarely seen in simple atherosclerosis which predominantly calcifies the aortic arch and descending aorta; massive aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta widening the right mediastinal shadow

Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT / CTA: Extensive circumferential calcification and thickening of the ascending aorta wall; large saccular or fusiform ascending aortic aneurysm (often >6-8 cm) with potential erosion into the sternum, ribs, or superior vena cava; severe dilation of the aortic root and annulus with non-coapting aortic valve cusps; coronary ostial stenosis from periaortic ostial cicatrization

Transthoracic & Transesophageal Echocardiography: Marked dilation of the aortic root and ascending aorta with severe central aortic regurgitation jet; thickened, rolled aortic leaflet margins with preserved cusp architecture
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical / Autopsy Pathology: Pathognomonic 'tree-bark' appearance of the aortic intima characterized by wrinkled, irregular, pearly-white fibrous plaques, scarred depressions, and longitudinal corrugations resulting from underlying medial destruction; dilation of the aortic annulus with separation and widening of the aortic valve commissures ('commissural separation')

Histopathology: Obliterative endarteritis of the vasa vasorum in the aortic adventitia with dense perivascular cuffing by plasma cells and lymphocytes; extensive ischemic necrosis and elastolysis of the aortic media with replacement fibrosis (mesa-like scars) and destruction of the elastic lamina; Warthin-Starry silver stain or Treponema pallidum immunohistochemistry may show rare spirochetes in early gummatous lesions
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria: historic, dramatic bedside photographic/physical findings (Corrigan pulse, de Musset sign, Quincke pulse, Argyll Robertson pupils, cutaneopalatal gummas) coupled with pathognomonic ascending aortic eggshell calcification and gross 'tree-bark' intimal scarring.

Cardiology.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
synonyms: Cyanotic congenital heart disease - Tetralogy of Fallot
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark central cyanosis: slate-blue or dusky violet discoloration of the lips, tongue, mucous membranes, conjunctivae, and nail beds ('blue baby' syndrome)
Hypercyanotic 'tet spells': acute, paroxysmal episodes of intense cyanosis, hyperpnea, irritability, syncope, or seizures triggered by crying, feeding, or agitation due to acute infundibular spasm

Characteristic squatting posture: children spontaneously assume a squatting position during exertion or after a hypercyanotic spell to acutely increase systemic vascular resistance, thereby reversing the right-to-left shunt and improving pulmonary blood flow
Prominent digital clubbing: bulbous, drumstick-like enlargement of the distal fingertips and toes with increased nail curvature (watch-glass nails)
Stunted physical growth, poor weight gain, and single loud second heart sound (S2) with harsh systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Iconic Hallmark): Pathognomonic 'boot-shaped heart' (coeur en sabot) characterized by an upturned, rounded cardiac apex (produced by marked concentric right ventricular hypertrophy) and a deep concavity in the mid-left mediastinal contour where the main pulmonary artery segment is normally located (due to hypoplasia of the pulmonary trunk); marked pulmonary oligemia (clear, black lung fields with sparse vascular markings); right-sided aortic arch seen in 25% of cases

Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE - Definitive Bedside Imaging): Visual identification of the four structural cardinal anomalies: (1) large, non-restrictive subaortic malalignment ventricular septal defect (VSD); (2) overriding aorta (aortic root displaced anteriorly over the VSD, straddling both ventricles by up to 50%); (3) right ventricular outflow tract obstruction (RVOTO) with infundibular narrowing, dysplastic/hypoplastic pulmonary valve, and high-velocity continuous wave Doppler jet; (4) concentric right ventricular wall hypertrophy with wall thickness equaling or exceeding the left ventricle

Cardiac CT Angiography / Cardiac MRI: Precise 3D reconstruction of the pulmonary arterial tree, measuring branch pulmonary artery diameters (Nakata and McGoon indices), and mapping major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (MAPCAs)
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical / Autopsy Pathology: Anterior and cephalad deviation of the infundibular (outlet) ventricular septum resulting in a large perimembranous/subaortic VSD; concentric hypertrophy of the RV parietal and septal muscle bands forming a fibromuscular infundibular stenotic channel; small, bicuspid or domed pulmonary valve; dextroposition of the aorta; massively thickened right ventricular myocardium matching or exceeding the left ventricular wall thickness

Histopathology: Severe concentric hypertrophy and disarray of right ventricular cardiomyocytes; dense fibrosis of the subvalvular and infundibular endocardium; dysplastic myxoid changes with disorganized elastin fibers in the stenotic pulmonary valve leaflets
Cardiology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria: archetypal photographic pediatric cyanosis, digital clubbing, and squatting posture paired with the timeless 'boot-shaped heart' (coeur en sabot) on radiography and 4-feature anatomical demonstration on echo/CMR.

Cardiology.name: Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return
clinical_manifestations: Obstructive neonatal emergency (predominantly Type III Infracardiac): Severe, profound, dusky cyanosis developing within hours of life, accompanied by severe tachypnea, grunting, deep intercostal retractions, pink frothy pulmonary secretions, marked metabolic acidosis, and rapid progression to cardiogenic shock and death

Non-obstructive presentation (Type I Supracardiac, Type II Cardiac): Mild-to-moderate central cyanosis, tachypnea, poor feeding, diaphoresis during feeds, recurrent wheezing and pulmonary infections, failure to thrive, and progressive right-sided heart failure in early infancy

Precordial physical examination: Hyperdynamic right ventricular lift / parasternal heave, palpable pulmonary artery pulsation along the left upper sternal border, and marked hepatomegaly with firm, tender liver edge

Cardiac auscultation: Widely split, fixed second heart sound (S2) with a markedly accentuated, booming pulmonary closure sound (loud P2); soft mid-systolic ejection murmur at the left second intercostal space (increased pulmonary flow); low-pitched mid-diastolic tricuspid inflow rumble along the lower left sternal border; pathognomonic continuous venous hum audible over the site of anomalous connection (e.g., upper left sternal border in supracardiac vertical vein drainage)

Obligate right-to-left interatrial shunt: Total dependence of systemic cardiac output on right-to-left shunting across a patent foramen ovale or atrial septal defect; restriction at this level results in rapid low-cardiac-output shock
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography: Pathognomonic 'snowman sign' or 'figure-of-8 sign' in non-obstructed supracardiac TAPVR (the dilated vertical vein on the left, dilated left brachiocephalic/innominate vein superiorly, and dilated right SVC form the rounded upper body/head of the snowman, while the enlarged right atrium and ventricle form the bulbous lower body); In obstructed infracardiac TAPVR, the radiograph characteristically reveals a normal-sized or small cardiac silhouette ('small heart') with diffuse, dense, hazy reticular interstitial opacities, Kerley B lines, and pulmonary edema ('white-out lungs'), frequently misdiagnosed as neonatal respiratory distress syndrome
