Dermatology.name: Generalized Pustular Psoriasis (von Zumbusch)
clinical_manifestations: Abrupt, fulminant eruption of innumerable pinpoint-to-millimeter-sized, sterile, creamy-yellow pustules arising on diffuse, fiery erythematous, exquisitely painful and burning skin

Coalescence of discrete pustules over hours to days into extensive, glistening sheets of purulent fluid termed 'lakes of pus' (nappes pusztuleuses), followed by sheet-like desquamation and erythroderma
Severe systemic toxicity with high spiking fevers, chills, tachycardia, profound malaise, anorexia, and marked peripheral leukocytosis with neutrophilia (>20,000/µL)
Characteristic cyclic or episodic waves of pustular eruptions recurring at intervals of days to weeks

Extracutaneous complications: geographic tongue (annulus migrans), acute sterile polyarthritis, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), high-output heart failure, severe hypoalbuminemia, and hypocalcemia

Often triggered by rapid withdrawal of systemic corticosteroids, high-dose potent topical steroids, infections, hypocalcemia, or pregnancy (impetigo herpetiformis); familial forms linked to loss-of-function mutations in IL36RN (DITRA), CARD14, or AP1S3
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz): Thickened, hyperechoic epidermal layer punctuated by multiple, well-circumscribed anechoic to hypoechoic subcorneal cavities (spongiform pustules of Kogoj); intensely hypoechoic upper dermis indicating acute dermal edema; power Doppler demonstrates turbulent, marked hypervascular flow in dermal papillae

Whole-Body Skeletal MRI / Radiographs: Used to detect associated Chronic Recurrent Multifocal Osteomyelitis (CRMO), SAPHO syndrome (Synovitis, Acne, Pustulosis, Hyperostosis, Osteitis), or aseptic osteolytic lesions in children and young adults with IL36RN mutations, revealing bone marrow edema on STIR sequences, hyperostosis of anterior chest wall/clavicle, and sacroiliitis

Chest Radiography and CT: Evaluates for acute non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema / ARDS induced by cytokine storm (IL-1, IL-36, TNF-alpha), revealing diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities and alveolar consolidations

Transthoracic Echocardiography: Hyperdynamic circulation, left ventricular volume overload, and evaluation for high-output cardiac failure resulting from widespread cutaneous erythroderma and cutaneous arteriovenous shunting
pathology_manifestations: Epidermal Spongiform Pustules of Kogoj: Pathognomonic accumulation of mature neutrophils within the upper stratum spinosum and beneath the stratum corneum; neutrophils migrate into intercellular spaces of degenerate, necrotic spinous keratinocytes forming a spongy, multilocular network
Macropustules of Kogoj: Enlargement and coalescence of spongiform pustules into large, unilocular, intraepidermal and subcorneal pustules packed with viable and karyorrhectic neutrophils

Epidermal Changes: Prominent confluent parakeratosis containing pyknotic neutrophilic aggregates (Munro microabscesses), complete loss of the granular layer directly beneath pustules, and marked psoriasiform acanthosis with regular elongation and clubbing of rete ridges

Dermal Infiltrate: Marked dermal papillary edema; intensely tortuous, elongated, and congested capillary loops within dermal papillae; superficial perivascular and interstitial infiltrate consisting of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and histiocytes
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening acute pustular dermatosis characterized by sheets of sterile 'lakes of pus' and systemic toxicity, diagnosed on skin ultrasound by subcorneal hypoechoic cavities and Doppler hyperperfusion, monitored via chest CT/echo for ARDS and high-output heart failure, imaged via MSK MRI for associated CRMO/SAPHO, and pathologically defined by the classic spongiform pustules of Kogoj.

Dermatology.name: Gorlin Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Development of multiple (often dozens to hundreds) cutaneous basal cell carcinomas (BCCs) across the face, neck, and upper trunk, appearing at an unusually young age (often adolescence or early adulthood)
Pathognomonic palmar and plantar pits (pinpoint to 3-mm shallow, punched-out, reddish or flesh-colored depressions in the dermal epidermal ridges of the palms and soles)
Macrocephaly with prominent frontal bossing, hypertelorism, broad nasal root, and coarse facial contours
Musculoskeletal anomalies including pectus excavatum, pectus carinatum, sprengel deformity, and kyphoscoliosis
Multiple benign facial epidermoid cysts, milia, and lipomas
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic Dental Radiography (Orthopantomogram) / Maxillofacial CT: Multiple well-demarcated, unilocular or multilocular expansile radiolucent cystic lesions (odontogenic keratocysts [OKCs]) of the mandible (angle and ramus) and maxilla causing root resorption and tooth displacement

Skull Radiography / Non-Contrast Head CT: Pathognomonic early, extensive, heavy bilamellar calcification of the falx cerebri, tentorium cerebelli, and petroclinoid ligaments present in childhood or adolescence
Chest Radiography: Congenital rib malformations, particularly bifid ribs, splayed, missing, or fused ribs (most commonly ribs 3, 4, or 5), and hemivertebrae
Brain MRI: Screening and identification of desmoplastic medulloblastoma (typically in children under 3 years old) and intracranial meningiomas
Pelvic Ultrasound / MRI: Bilateral, lobulated, calcified ovarian fibromas in young females
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous Basal Cell Carcinoma Biopsy: Distinct nests of uniform basaloid keratinocytes showing peripheral nuclear palisading, haphazard central nuclear orientation, stromal retraction artifact (mucin-rich clefts separating tumors from stroma), and variable mitotic figures

Odontogenic Keratocyst (OKC) Histology: Fibrous cyst wall lined by a uniform, thin (6-8 cells thick) parakeratinized stratified squamous epithelium with a wavy, corrugated surface, prominent palisaded columnar/cuboidal basal layer with hyperchromatic 'tombstone' nuclei, and an absence of rete ridges
Palmar Pit Biopsy: Localized hypokeratosis with sharply circumscribed depression of the stratum corneum and underlying focal proliferations of basaloid buds extending into the papillary dermis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal multi-system cancer predisposition syndrome uniting dozens of early-onset BCCs and palmar pits with hallmark panoramic radiographic jaw odontogenic keratocysts, bilamellar falx calcification, and bifid ribs.

Dermatology.name: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent, spontaneous, often severe epistaxis starting in childhood or adolescence as the primary presenting symptom

Characteristic punctate, macular, spider-like, and arborizing mucocutaneous telangiectasias (1-3 mm blanching ruby-red macules) clustered on the lips, vermilion border, tongue, buccal mucosa, hard palate, fingertips, palms, nailbeds, and face
Chronic iron deficiency anemia resulting from recurrent nosebleeds and occult gastrointestinal telangiectatic bleeding
Digital clubbing, cyanosis, and exertional dyspnea in patients with substantial right-to-left pulmonary arteriovenous shunts
Hepatic bruits, thrill, high-output heart failure, or portal hypertension secondary to large intrahepatic vascular shunting
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT Angiography (CTA): Direct visualization of pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs) demonstrating a dilated feeding pulmonary artery, aneurysmal vascular sac, and enlarged draining pulmonary vein; transthoracic contrast echocardiography (bubble study) showing delayed (>3-4 cardiac cycles) microbubble appearance in the left heart chambers

Triphasic Hepatic Contrast CT / MRI: Extensive intrahepatic vascular malformations, marked hepatic artery tortuosity and dilatation, early contrast filling of hepatic or portal veins (arterioportal/arteriovenous shunts), and nodular regenerative hyperplasia ('pseudocirrhosis')

Brain Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) / Conventional Cerebral Angiography: Intracranial arteriovenous malformations (AVMs), pial arteriovenous fistulas, and cavernous malformations; cerebral infarcts and ring-enhancing brain abscesses resulting from paradoxical septic emboli bypassing pulmonary capillary filtration
CT / MR Enterography: Mucosal telangiectasias and angiodysplasias visible along the stomach, duodenum, and proximal jejunum
pathology_manifestations: Mucocutaneous Punch Biopsy of Telangiectasia: Markedly dilated, ectatic, thin-walled postcapillary venules and capillaries occupying the superficial papillary dermis, lined by a single layer of mature endothelial cells; direct pathological arteriovenous communications without intervening normal capillary beds; loss of elastic tissue and perivascular smooth muscle in the vascular walls
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield vascular syndrome defined by landmark mucocutaneous telangiectasias of the lips/fingertips and epistaxis, linked with pulmonary AVMs on chest CTA, hepatic vascular shunting on triphasic abdominal CT, and cerebral AVMs on MRI.

Dermatology.name: Hidradenitis Suppurativa
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent painful, deep-seated, inflamed nodules and boils in apocrine gland-rich intertriginous areas (axillae, inguinal, perianal, inframammary)
Double-ended and multi-headed open comedones ('tombstone comedones')
Fluctuant subcutaneous abscesses draining foul-smelling, purulent, serosanguinous discharge
Interconnecting subcutaneous draining sinus tracts and fistulae
Extensive, hypertrophic rope-like and bridgelike fibrotic scarring
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Ultrasound (HFUS) of Dermis/Subcutis: Fluid-filled dermal and subcutaneous interconnected tunnel tracts, pseudocysts, widened hair follicles, loss of normal dermal architecture, power Doppler hyperemia

Pelvic / Perineal MRI: Extensive fluid-filled draining sinus tracts with intense T2/STIR hyperintensity, rim enhancement, deep pelvic fistulae, ischioanal and gluteal fascial phlegmon or abscesses (Hurley stage III)
pathology_manifestations: Excision/biopsy: Follicular hyperkeratosis and occlusion with infundibular dilation; follicular rupture releasing keratin and bacteria into dermis; dense suppurative mixed inflammatory infiltrate, foreign body granulomas, and extensive dermal sinus tract lined by stratified squamous epithelium
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic debilitating cutaneous disorder with bridged scars and draining sinuses matching high-frequency ultrasound tunnels and deep pelvic/perineal MRI fistulous anatomy.

Dermatology.name: Incontinentia Pigmenti
clinical_manifestations: Four dynamic evolutionary cutaneous stages distributed strictly along the lines of Blaschko: Stage 1 (vesicular stage: linear erythematous streaks of inflammatory vesicles and bullae on extremities and trunk present at birth or within the first 2-4 weeks of life)
Stage 2 (verrucous stage: linear hyperkeratotic, warty, verrucous papules and crusts predominantly on distal extremities between 2 and 6 months of age)

Stage 3 (hyperpigmented stage: striking, bizarre, whorled, marbled, reticulated slate-gray to chocolate-brown hyperpigmentation distributed along Blaschko's lines across the trunk, flanks, and thighs, developing in late infancy and persisting into adolescence)
Stage 4 (atrophic/hypopigmented stage: faint, pale, hairless, hypohidrotic atrophic streaks and patches, most evident on the posterior calves and flexures in adult life)
Dental anomalies present in over 80% of patients: delayed dentition, hypodontia/anodontia, and distinctive crowned conical or peg-shaped incisors and canines
Ophthalmologic and neurologic abnormalities including cicatricial alopecia of the crown, retinal detachment, seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delay
radiological_manifestations: Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) & Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI): Acute neonatal/infantile cytotoxic cerebral edema, multifocal ischemic cortical and subcortical white matter infarctions, cystic periventricular leukomalacia, corpus callosum hypoplasia, and progressive hemispheric cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Orthopantomogram (Panoramic Dental Radiograph): Delayed dental eruption, missing permanent tooth buds (oligodontia), and small, pointed, peg-shaped/conical dental crowns
Fluorescein Retinal Angiography: Severe peripheral retinal vascular non-perfusion and avascularity, arteriovenous shunts, neovascularization, vitreous hemorrhages, and tractional retinal detachment
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Stage-Dependent Evolution):
Stage 1: Intraepidermal spongiotic vesicles packed with abundant eosinophils (eosinophilic spongiosis) and dyskeratotic apoptotic keratinocytes in the spinous layer
Stage 2: Prominent epidermal hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, papillomatosis, and dyskeratotic, brightly eosinophilic corps ronds throughout the epidermis

Stage 3: Hallmark pigmentary incontinence characterized by extensive melanin loss from basal keratinocytes with abundant coarse melanin granules engulfed within large melanophages throughout the papillary dermis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential X-linked dominant genodermatosis with pathognomonic 4-stage Blaschkoid cutaneous lesions and conical teeth, matched with ischemic brain injury on neonatal MRI and retinal avascularity on fluorescein angiography.

Dermatology.name: Kaposi Sarcoma
clinical_manifestations: Multiple discrete or confluent violaceous, purple, pink, or red-brown macules, plaques, and exophytic nodules
Characteristic distribution along skin cleavage lines; predilection for lower extremities, face, trunk, and genitalia
Oral mucosal lesions (hard palate, gingiva, tongue: purple exophytic vascular masses)
Marked brawny, non-pitting lymphedema of the lower extremities and external genitalia
Epidemic (HIV-associated), classic (Mediterranean), endemic (African), and iatrogenic immunosuppressive forms
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT: Pathognomonic 'flame-shaped' or ill-defined peribronchovascular consolidations and nodules, thickening of interlobular septa, bilateral pleural effusions, hilar/mediastinal adenopathy
Abdominal / Gastrointestinal CT: Multifocal mucosal and submucosal nodular thickening of the stomach, duodenum, and colon; hypervascular retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy; hepatosplenomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Skin/mucosal biopsy: Proliferation of atypical spindle cells forming slit-like vascular channels containing extravasated erythrocytes, hemosiderin pigment, and hyaline globules; strong nuclear positivity for Human Herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8 / LANA-1) by immunohistochemistry; CD31, CD34, and D2-40 positivity
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: High-impact visual cutaneous tumor with vibrant violaceous plaques and mucosal nodules matched with diagnostic peribronchovascular 'flame-shaped' consolidations on chest CT.

Dermatology.name: Kimura Disease
clinical_manifestations: Painless, slowly enlarging, firm subcutaneous soft tissue nodules or masses predominantly localized to the head and neck region, especially the preauricular, parotid, submandibular, cheek, and periorbital regions
Overlying cutaneous surface is typically flesh-colored, erythematous, or hyperpigmented, occasionally pruritic; soft-to-elastic on palpation
Prominent regional cervical and preauricular lymphadenopathy in over 70% of cases
Epidemiological predilection for young Asian males (male-to-female ratio ~3-6:1, peak onset 2nd to 3rd decade)
Marked peripheral blood eosinophilia (often >15-50% of total white blood count) and extraordinarily high serum IgE levels (frequently >1,000-10,000 IU/mL)
Concurrent renal disease in up to 20-60% of patients, presenting with heavy proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome, most commonly membranous nephropathy or minimal change disease
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Head and Neck CT: Poorly circumscribed or well-defined, variable attenuation soft tissue masses within subcutaneous fat and major salivary glands (parotid and submandibular glands), exhibiting moderate to intense, homogeneous enhancement post-contrast; prominent enlargement of multiple regional cervical lymph nodes with preserved fatty hilum

Head and Neck MRI (T1, T2, STIR, T1+C): Subcutaneous and salivary gland masses are isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and markedly, uniformly hyperintense on T2/STIR images; avid, homogeneous enhancement post-gadolinium with distinct feeding and draining vessels; diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) shows high signal with variable ADC values reflecting high lymphoid cellularity

Color Doppler Ultrasound: Hypoechoic, well-vascularized soft tissue masses within or adjacent to salivary glands showing prominent internal arterial vascularity with low resistance index; associated multiple enlarged, oval lymph nodes with thick cortex and preserved hilum
Renal Ultrasound: Evaluates parenchymal echogenicity and renal cortical thickness in patients presenting with concurrent nephrotic syndrome and proteinuria
pathology_manifestations: Follicular Lymphoid Hyperplasia: Dense, nodular lymphoid infiltrate organized into abundant, prominent secondary lymphoid follicles with active, hyperplastic germinal centers and intact mantle zones
Eosinophilic Infiltration: Heavy, extensive interfollicular infiltration of mature eosinophils, frequently coalescing into eosinophilic microabscesses with eosinophil degranulation and necrosis

Vascular Proliferation: Florid proliferation of post-capillary venules and small blood vessels lined by plump, cuboidal endothelial cells without cellular atypia, cytologic vacuolation, or 'tombstone' hobnail morphology (essential distinction from angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia [ALHE])
Stromal Changes: Variable degrees of post-inflammatory interfollicular collagenous fibrosis and sclerosis; occasional polykaryocytes (Warthin-Finkeldey-like multinucleated giant cells)
Immunopathology: Striking reticular meshwork of IgE deposition decorating the germinal centers; negative for clonality on B-cell and T-cell gene rearrangement studies
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Chronic allergic-inflammatory subcutaneous disease characterized by head/neck nodules, salivary gland enlargement, and eosinophilia, imaged by head/neck MRI/CT showing avidly enhancing subcutaneous/parotid masses and regional lymphadenopathy, and pathologically verified by florid lymphoid follicular hyperplasia with eosinophilic microabscesses and vascular proliferation.

Dermatology.name: Lipoid Proteinosis
synonyms: lipoid proteinosis of Urbach and Wiethe
clinical_manifestations: Early-onset, persistent, hoarse, weak, or rasping cry and progressive severe dysphonia beginning in infancy due to early vocal cord hyaline infiltration
Moniliform blepharosis: pathognomonic pearl-like, beaded row of yellowish-white waxy papules lining the upper and lower eyelid margins
Yellowish, waxy, infiltrated papules, plaques, and nodules on the face, lips, tongue, oral mucosa, axillae, and scrotum
Firm, thickened, immobile tongue ('woody tongue') with shortened lingual frenulum causing ankyloglossia, impaired swallowing, and restricted articulation
Prominent acneiform, varioliform (pockmark-like) atrophic scars appearing on the face, neck, and extensor extremities following minor trauma or transient vesiculopustules
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Head CT / Plain Skull Radiography: Pathognomonic bilateral, symmetric, comma-shaped, bean-shaped, or hook-like dense calcifications in the medial temporal lobes, localized selectively within the amygdala and hippocampal uncus, with sparing of surrounding cerebral neocortex

Brain MRI: Dense signal voids and blooming artifacts on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) within both amygdaloid nuclei corresponding to calcifications, accompanied by surrounding regional gliosis on T2/FLAIR

Laryngoscopy / Videostroboscopy: Extensive yellowish mucosal thickening, nodularity, and hyaline plaques infiltrating the true and false vocal cords, aryepiglottic folds, and interarytenoid area with glottic aperture restriction
pathology_manifestations: Skin and Oral Mucosa Punch Biopsy: Extensive dermal and submucosal extracellular deposition of pale, homogeneous, amorphous eosinophilic hyaline material; pathognomonic strong Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS) positivity that is diastase-resistant; striking concentric mantles of PAS-positive basement membrane-like material surrounding dermal capillaries ('onion-skin' perivascular cuffing) and encasing eccrine sweat gland coils with progressive adnexal atrophy
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive infiltrative ECM1 genodermatosis with infant hoarseness, beaded eyelid papules (moniliform blepharosis), and pockmark scars, alongside pathognomonic bilateral amygdala comma-shaped calcifications on head CT and onion-skin PAS-positive dermal hyalinosis.

Dermatology.name: Livedoid Vasculopathy (Atrophie Blanche)
synonyms: Painful purpuric ulcers with reticular pattern of lower extremities (PURPLE)
clinical_manifestations: Exquisitely painful, recurrent, punctate, branching or retiform purpuric macules and plaques localized to the lower legs, perimalleolar regions, and dorsal feet
Rapid progression of purpuric areas to punched-out, irregular, angulated, painful necrotic cutaneous ulcers with jagged violaceous borders
Healing of ulcers leaves pathognomonic stellate, porcelain-white or ivory atrophic scars with prominent peripheral punctate telangiectasias and surrounding hyperpigmentation ('atrophie blanche')
Underlying livedo racemosa (violaceous, non-blanching, broken/irregular reticular rings) exacerbated by cold, dependent positioning, or summer heat ('livedo reticularis with summer ulcerations')
Chronic, episodic, highly debilitating course with marked hyperalgesia and nocturnal pain out of proportion to exam findings

Strong association with hypercoagulable and thrombophilic states (factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A mutation, protein C/S deficiency, antithrombin III deficiency, antiphospholipid antibodies, elevated lipoprotein(a))
radiological_manifestations: Lower Extremity Arterial and Venous Duplex Ultrasound: Excludes deep vein thrombosis, macrovascular superficial venous reflux/chronic venous insufficiency, and peripheral artery occlusive disease, establishing that the ulceration is primarily microvascular rather than stasis or large-vessel ischemic

High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz): Shows focal dermal thickening during acute thrombotic phases, progressing to striking dermal atrophy and thinning at sites of porcelain-white atrophic scars, with complete loss of normal dermal collagen echo-density; absence of subcutaneous fat necrosis

Laser Doppler / Laser Speckle Contrast Imaging: Pathognomonic profound focal microcirculatory ischemia ('cold spots') localized to active retiform purpura and ulcers, contrasted with peripheral hyperperfusion halo
Plain Radiography of Ankle and Foot: Demonstrates absence of underlying cortical bone erosion, periostitis, or osteomyelitis beneath chronic ulcers, and rules out dystrophic calcinosis cutis
pathology_manifestations: Occlusive Microvascular Vasculopathy: Striking, extensive deposition of intraluminal fibrin thrombi within dilated, post-capillary venules and small arterioles of the upper and mid reticular dermis
Subendothelial Fibrinoid Deposition: Vessel walls show marked hyalinization and dense subendothelial eosinophilic fibrinoid material with plump, reactive endothelial cells

Absence of True Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis: Notably devoid of significant transmural neutrophilic infiltration, true fibrinoid necrosis of the media, or dense leukocytoclasia (nuclear dust), differentiating it from true small-vessel vasculitis
Perivascular Changes: Scant perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate, extravasated erythrocytes, and extensive perivascular hemosiderin deposition
Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Intense, uniform, granular or homogeneous deposition of fibrinogen/fibrin, IgM, and C3 within dermal vessel walls
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Painful thrombo-occlusive microvascular dermatosis defined by retiform purpura ulcerating into pathognomonic porcelain-white stellate atrophie blanche scars, evaluated by vascular duplex ultrasound excluding macrovascular disease and Doppler demonstrating focal microvascular arrest, and pathologically characterized by intraluminal fibrin thrombi and vessel hyalinization without true vasculitis.

Dermatology.name: Malignant Atrophic Papulosis (Degos Disease)
synonyms: Lethal cutaneous and systemic atrophic papulosis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic cutaneous lesions: small (2-5 mm), dome-shaped, pink-red inflammatory papules that undergo central necrosis over days to weeks, yielding characteristic porcelain-white, ivory-white, or mother-of-pearl atrophic scars with a depressed center and an elevated, hyperemic, telangiectatic violaceous rim
Widespread distribution of cutaneous lesions across trunk and extremities, notably sparing the face, palms, and soles
Systemic / Malignant Degos form (>60% of patients): devastating, recurrent ischemic infarctions involving the gastrointestinal tract and central nervous system
Gastrointestinal crisis: severe episodic colicky abdominal pain, intestinal ischemia, and fatal transmural bowel perforation with peritonitis ('gastrointestinal disaster')
Neurological involvement: ischemic and hemorrhagic strokes, transverse myelitis, seizures, radiculopathies, cranial nerve palsies, and progressive fatal encephalopathy
Other systemic targets: pleural and pericardial effusions, constrictive pericarditis, ophthalmologic ischemic lesions, and renal microinfarcts
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal and Pelvic CT: Multiple segmental areas of bowel wall thickening, target sign (submucosal edema), focal pneumatosis intestinalis, mesenteric ischemic stranding, avascular wedge-shaped bowel infarcts, and pneumoperitoneum (free intraperitoneal air indicating bowel perforation)

Brain MRI (DWI, FLAIR, T1+C, T2*): Multiple punctate and wedge-shaped subcortical and cortical ischemic microinfarcts with diffusion restriction on DWI; focal leptomeningeal enhancement; cerebral microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI); magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) reveals peripheral intracranial arterial caliber irregularity, stenosis, and branch occlusions

High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS): Inverted cone-shaped or wedge-shaped hypoechoic area spanning the epidermis and reticular dermis with central epidermal atrophy, corresponding precisely to the localized microvascular ischemic infarct

CT Angiography of Abdomen / Mesenteric Angiography: Obliterative endarteritis with focal tapering and occlusion of distal small-to-medium mesenteric and jejunal/ileal arterial branches without aneurysm formation
Chest CT & Echocardiography: Pleural thickening, pericardial effusion, fibrinous pericarditis, or constrictive physiology from avascular serosal fibroelastosis
pathology_manifestations: Pathognomonic Wedge-Shaped Dermal Infarct: Distinctive inverted pyramid or cone-shaped zone of complete dermal ischemia and collagen necrosis, with the apex pointing toward an occluded small artery/arteriole in the deep reticular dermis or subcutis
Epidermal Pathology: Marked epidermal atrophy directly overlying the ischemic zone with flattened rete ridges, basal vacuolization, and prominent hyperkeratosis

Obliterative Arteriolitis / Endovasculitis: Small-to-medium arteries and arterioles exhibit marked subendothelial intimal fibrointimal proliferation, cellular edema, endothelial swelling, and secondary intraluminal platelet-fibrin thrombosis leading to complete vascular lumen occlusion

Paucicellular Necrosis: Absence of significant transmural neutrophilic infiltration, leukocytoclasia, or true necrotizing vasculitis; the necrotic dermis displays abundant interstitial colloidal iron/alcian blue-positive stromal mucin (hyaluronic acid)
Late lesions: Dermal collagen becomes completely hyalinized and sclerotic, giving the clinical porcelain-white atrophic plaque appearance
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Lethal vaso-occlusive multisystem disorder defined by pathognomonic porcelain-white atrophic papules with telangiectatic rims, radiologically identified by abdominal CT showing bowel ischemia and pneumoperitoneum, brain MRI showing wedge-shaped infarctions, and pathologically characterized by inverted cone-shaped paucicellular dermal infarcts with obliterative arteriolitis.

Dermatology.name: Morphea and Linear Scleroderma
clinical_manifestations: Plaque morphea: indurated, shiny, ivory-white or porcelain-colored sclerotic plaques surrounded by an active violaceous or lilac inflammatory border
Linear scleroderma: band-like induration extending along an extremity, causing joint contractures and limb atrophy
En coup de sabre: linear, depressed, indurated furrow on the frontoparietal forehead and scalp resembling a sabre strike, often with cicatricial alopecia
Parry-Romberg syndrome (progressive hemifacial atrophy of subcutaneous tissue, muscle, and underlying facial bone)
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Craniofacial MRI/CT (in En coup de sabre and Parry-Romberg): Thinning and depression of the underlying frontal bone, ipsilateral cerebral hemiatrophy, white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, intracranial cortical calcifications, leptomeningeal enhancement
Musculoskeletal MRI / Plain X-ray (Linear Morphea): Deep fascial and muscular involvement, soft-tissue atrophy, limb length discrepancy, periosteal bone changes
pathology_manifestations: Full-thickness skin/subcutis biopsy: Dense, hyalinized collagen bundles in the reticular dermis replacing the subcutaneous fat ('trapped eccrine glands'), perivascular and interstitial lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate in active borders
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Presents unmistakable ivory plaques with lilac borders and cranial 'en coup de sabre' furrows, accompanied by underlying craniofacial bone erosion and cerebral white matter changes on brain MRI/CT.

Dermatology.name: Muir-Torre Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark eruptive cutaneous sebaceous neoplasms: solitary or multiple yellowish, umbilicated, firm papules, nodules, or plaques on the face, scalp, and torso representing sebaceous adenomas, sebaceomas (sebaceous epitheliomas), and sebaceous carcinomas (particularly aggressive on the eyelids arising from meibomian glands or glands of Zeis)
Multiple keratoacanthomas, frequently exhibiting distinctive sebaceous differentiation on histopathology, occurring at an unusually early age
Cystic sebaceous tumors and basal cell carcinomas with sebaceous differentiation

High lifetime risk of early-onset, multiple, synchronous or metachronous visceral malignancies, most notably colorectal adenocarcinoma (typically proximal to the splenic flexure / right-sided colon, mean age of onset <50 years) and genitourinary cancers (transitional cell carcinoma of the renal pelvis, ureters, or bladder; endometrial and ovarian carcinoma in females)
Skin lesions often serve as the presenting herald sign of internal malignancy in over 40% of cases or arise concurrently with visceral neoplasms
radiological_manifestations: Optical Colonoscopy and CT Colonography: Visualizes early-onset, flat, sessile, or polypoid colorectal adenomas and advanced right-sided (cecum, ascending colon) mucinous or poorly differentiated colorectal adenocarcinomas; demonstrates synchronous or metachronous colonic neoplasms

Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography (CECT) of Abdomen and Pelvis: Evaluates primary gastrointestinal tumor depth, colonic wall thickening, mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, hepatic metastases, and genitourinary tumors (e.g., filling defects in renal pelvis or hydronephrosis)

Computed Tomography Urography (CTU) / Retrograde Pyelography: Detects irregular polypoid filling defects, mucosal thickening, or obstruction within the renal pelvicalyceal system, ureter, or bladder indicative of upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC)

Pelvic Ultrasound and Dynamic Pelvic MRI: Identifies thickened endometrial stripe (>4 mm in postmenopausal women) and heterogeneously enhancing uterine masses diagnostic of early-stage paraneoplastic endometrial adenocarcinoma
pathology_manifestations: Sebaceous Adenoma Biopsy: Sharply circumscribed, well-demarcated dermal lobules composed of two distinct cell populations: an outer peripheral rim of small, dark basaloid germinative cells and an expanded central zone of mature, multivacuolated, lipid-rich sebocytes with distinct foamy ('bubbly') cytoplasm and indented, star-shaped nuclei

Sebaceous Carcinoma Biopsy: Asymmetric, infiltrative sheets and cords of atypical, pleomorphic cells with prominent hyperchromasia, high nucleocytoplasmic ratio, frequent atypical mitotic figures, comedo necrosis, and pagetoid intraepithelial spread (particularly in eyelid conjunctiva)

Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for Mismatch Repair (MMR) Proteins: Loss of nuclear expression of one or more DNA mismatch repair proteins: MSH2 (loss in >80-90% of MTS cases), MSH6, MLH1, or PMS2 in both cutaneous sebaceous neoplasms and visceral tumors

Molecular Genetics: Demonstrates high-frequency microsatellite instability (MSI-H) by PCR/NGS and confirms germline pathogenic mutations in MSH2, MLH1, or MSH6 (classic Lynch syndrome autosomal dominant transmission)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic genodermatosis and paraneoplastic cancer syndrome pairing herald facial/eyelid sebaceous neoplasms with colonoscopy and CT/MRI detection of Lynch-associated right-sided colorectal and urothelial malignancies and MMR protein loss.

Dermatology.name: Necrobiosis Lipoidica
clinical_manifestations: Well-circumscribed, asymptomatic or tender, oval to irregular plaques located on the bilateral pretibial surfaces of the lower legs (shins in >85% of cases)

Characteristic tripartite clinical morphology: active, raised, firm, violaceous-to-erythematous borders; central yellowish, waxy, sclerotic atrophic depression; and prominent overlying arborizing telangiectatic vessels that are clearly visible through the parchment-like thinned epidermis
Extreme skin fragility with frequent, recalcitrant, exquisitely painful central ulcerations developing following minor mechanical trauma in up to 30% of patients
Long-standing plaques may undergo hypopigmentation, anesthesia, hair loss, and rarely malignant transformation (squamous cell carcinoma) in chronic non-healing ulcers

Historically associated with diabetes mellitus (~65-75% of patients have diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance), though occurring in non-diabetics; associated with thyroiditis and autoimmune diseases
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz): Marked thinning and effacement of the dermal layer; pathognomonic broad, horizontal, band-like hypoechoic zone extending throughout the mid and reticular dermis with loss of normal echogenic dermal collagen bundles; preservation of the epidermal entrance echo; sublesional subcutaneous fat layer shows hyperechoic septal thickening

Color Doppler & Laser Speckle Contrast Imaging: Displays severe central microvascular attenuation/avascularity within the atrophic plaque core, surrounded by an active peripheral hypervascular halo matching the clinically erythematous border

Plain Radiography of Lower Extremities: Soft-tissue thinning overlying the anterior tibial cortex; exclusion of underlying tibial periostitis, cortical erosion, or dystrophic soft-tissue calcification in chronic ulcerated plaques

Lower Extremity Arterial Duplex Ultrasound: Assesses distal micro- and macro-arterial patency, excluding severe peripheral artery disease (tibial/peroneal arterial calcification) in diabetic patients presenting with ulcerated lesions
pathology_manifestations: Classic 'Layer-Cake' (Tiered) Architecture: Full-thickness dermal and subcutaneous septal granulomatous inflammation arranged in broad, horizontal, alternating parallel bands of collagen necrobiosis and histiocytic inflammatory infiltrates

Collagen Necrobiosis: Zones of pale, smudged, eosinophilic degenerate collagen bundles with loss of normal fibrillar architecture and marked diminution/loss of dermal elastic fibers (demonstrated on Verhoeff-van Gieson stain)

Granulomatous Infiltrate: Interstitial and palisaded histiocytes, lymphocytes, multinucleated giant cells (both foreign-body and Langhans types), and abundant plasma cells (the presence of plasma cells is a key histological feature distinguishing NL from granuloma annulare)

Vascular Alterations: Marked endothelial cell swelling, proliferation, and endarteritis obliterans with vessel wall hyalinization and luminal narrowing in deep dermis and subcutaneous septa, without true leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Lipid Deposition: Extracellular lipid and cholesterol droplets within degenerate collagen bands demonstrated on oil red O or Sudan stains on frozen tissue
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Hallmark pretibial granulomatous necrobiotic dermatosis presenting as waxy yellowish plaques with prominent arborizing telangiectasias, evaluated radiologically by high-frequency ultrasound demonstrating dermal thinning with horizontal hypoechoic bands, microvascular Doppler showing central hypoperfusion, and pathologically confirmed by the distinctive tiered 'layer-cake' granulomas with plasma cells and necrobiotic collagen.

Dermatology.name: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma (NXG)
clinical_manifestations: Indurated, yellowish, red-orange to violaceous papules, plaques, and nodules that slowly enlarge, exhibiting a central atrophic, waxy yellowish depression with prominent arborizing telangiectasias, scar-like changes, and frequent painful, non-healing ulcerations

Pathognomonic periorbital predilection (>80% of patients): bilateral, symmetric yellowish plaques on upper and lower eyelids and periorbital skin, leading to severe ocular complications including cicatricial ectropion, ptosis, proptosis, lagophthalmos, scleritis, keratitis, and blindness
Extra-orbital involvement: trunk, extremities, and neck

Nearly universal association (>80-90% of cases) with monoclonal gammopathy, overwhelmingly an IgG kappa or lambda paraproteinemia; high risk of progression to multiple myeloma, smoldering myeloma, Waldenström macroglobulinemia, or lymphoproliferative disorders
Systemic internal organ xanthogranulomatous infiltrations: myocardium, pericardium, lungs, spleen, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system
radiological_manifestations: Orbital and Facial MRI / CT (High-Resolution T1, T2, T1+C): Extensive, bilateral, infiltrating, non-calcified soft tissue masses centered in the anterior and retrobulbar orbital spaces; masses are isointense to muscle on T1, heterogeneously hypointense to isointense on T2 (due to dense fibrosis and lipid), exhibiting avid, homogeneous post-contrast enhancement; frequently infiltrates extraocular muscles, lacrimal glands, and encases the optic nerve sheath without osseous destruction

Contrast-Enhanced Chest and Abdominal CT: Identifies systemic internal visceral lesions including solitary or multiple pulmonary nodules, pericardial thickening/effusion, myocardial xanthomatous masses, and retroperitoneal/mesenteric soft tissue infiltration

Skeletal Radiographic Survey / Low-Dose Whole-Body CT: Evaluates for osteolytic 'punched-out' bone lesions, severe osteoporosis, or pathologic fractures associated with underlying IgG monoclonal gammopathy and multiple myeloma
Cardiac MRI / Echocardiography: Detects myocardial nodular xanthogranulomas, pericardial infiltration, or restrictive cardiomyopathy secondary to systemic disease
pathology_manifestations: Massive Dermal and Subcutaneous Granulomatous Infiltrate: Broad, expansive granulomatous infiltrate replacing the entire reticular dermis and extending deep into the subcutaneous adipose tissue and skeletal muscle

Extensive Collagen Necrobiosis: Vast, irregular, geographic zones of degenerate, hypereosinophilic collagen necrobiosis with abundant cholesterol clefts (slit-like spaces where cholesterol crystals dissolved during processing)

Bizarre Multinucleated Giant Cells: Striking population of both classic Touton giant cells (wreath of nuclei with foamy periphery) and pathognomonic, enormous, bizarre foreign-body-type giant cells containing dozens to over a hundred hyperchromatic nuclei arranged irregularly or in florets
Infiltrate Components: Abundant lipid-laden foamy histiocytes, lymphocytes, plasma cells, and dense lymphoid aggregates with germinal centers
Immunohistochemistry: Histiocytes are intensely CD68+ and CD163+; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Destructive paraproteinemia-associated granulomatous dermatosis characterized by periorbital xanthomatous plaques with ectropion, imaged on orbital MRI/CT by infiltrating retrobulbar masses, on skeletal CT by osteolytic myeloma lesions, and pathologically proven by extensive collagen necrobiosis with cholesterol clefts and bizarre Touton/foreign-body giant cells.

Dermatology.name: Paraneoplastic Pemphigus
clinical_manifestations: Severe, intractable, excruciatingly painful mucosal ulcerations and hemorrhagic crusting involving the vermilion lip borders, tongue, buccal mucosa, palate, and oropharynx (stomatitis is the universal, earliest, and most recalcitrant clinical sign)
Severe bilateral erosive or pseudomembranous conjunctivitis, symblepharon formation, and progressive cicatricial ocular scarring that can lead to permanent visual impairment

Polymorphous cutaneous eruption displaying a spectrum of features: flaccid or tense bullae, necrotic erosions, targetoid erythema-multiforme-like lesions, dusky erythematous plaques, and lichenoid papules
Striking and excruciating palmoplantar sloughing, erosions, and painful erythema mimicking toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) or severe Stevens-Johnson syndrome

Life-threatening pulmonary involvement: progressive exertional dyspnea, non-productive cough, and severe hypoxemia secondary to acantholysis of bronchial and bronchiolar respiratory epithelium, progressing to irreversible, fatal bronchiolitis obliterans
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography (CECT) of Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis: High-yield identification of occult lymphoproliferative neoplasms or hematologic malignancies; pathognomonic detection of Castleman disease (unicentric hyaline-vascular type presenting as a sharply demarcated, hypervascular retroperitoneal, pelvic, or mediastinal mass with avid homogeneous arterial enhancement and branching central calcifications), follicular non-Hodgkin lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), or thymoma

High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of Chest: In patients with respiratory symptoms, HRCT demonstrates hallmark findings of bronchiolitis obliterans: geographic mosaic attenuation with low-attenuation areas of air trapping accentuated on dynamic expiratory scans, central and peripheral bronchial wall thickening, peribronchial cuffing, and cylindrical bronchiectasis in the absence of mucous plugging
18F-FDG PET/CT: Differentiates indolent Castleman disease from aggressive transformed lymphomas, accurately staging occult disease and guiding percutaneous or surgical core needle biopsy
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous and Mucosal Histopathology: Hallmark combination of intraepidermal suprabasal acantholysis (forming intraepidermal clefts, blisters, and tombstone-pattern basal layer retention) coexisting with interface dermatitis (vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer, apoptotic necrotic keratinocytes throughout the epidermis, and a lichenoid band-like mononuclear dermal infiltrate)

Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Demonstrates both cell surface (intercellular) IgG and/or C3 deposition within the epidermis ('fish-net' pattern) AND continuous granular or linear deposition of IgG and C3 along the epidermal basement membrane zone (BMZ)

Indirect Immunofluorescence (IIF) on Rat Bladder Epithelium: Highly specific (approaching 100% specificity for PNP), exhibiting intense intercellular IgG staining on transitional epithelium (which expresses high levels of plakin proteins but lacks desmoglein 1/3, thus distinguishing PNP from classical pemphigus vulgaris)

Immunoprecipitation and Immunoblotting: Demonstrates circulating autoantibodies targeting a complex of plakin family proteins: envoplakin (210 kDa), periplakin (190 kDa), desmoplakin I (250 kDa) and II (210 kDa), plectin (500 kDa), BP230, desmoglein 1 and 3, and alpha-2-macroglobulin-like-1 (A2ML1)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Landmark paraneoplastic autoimmune syndrome uniting intractable hemorrhagic stomatitis, polymorphous bullae, and fatal bronchiolitis obliterans with CT detection of occult retroperitoneal Castleman disease or lymphoma and rat-bladder IIF plakin autoimmunity.

Dermatology.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris
clinical_manifestations: Painful, extensive, persistent oral mucosal ulcerations and erosions (buccal mucosa, palate, gingiva)
Flaccid, thin-walled, clear-fluid cutaneous bullae arising on normal or erythematous skin that rupture easily
Raw, painful, denuded, weeping erosions that bleed easily and fail to heal without therapy
Positive Nikolsky sign (detachment of superficial epidermis upon light rubbing of peri-lesional skin)
Scalp, face, neck, axillae, groin, and perineum predilection
radiological_manifestations: Barium Esophagram / Endoscopy / CT: Esophagitis dissecans superficialis (severe sloughing and peeling of the esophageal squamous epithelium, 'cast' formation)
Chest CT: Aspiration pneumonia secondary to severe dysphagia and pharyngeal denudation
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Intraepidermal suprabasal acantholysis with blister formation; 'row of tombstones' appearance of basal keratinocytes attached to the basement membrane
Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in a net-like or 'fishnet' / chicken-wire pattern throughout the epidermis (targeting desmoglein 3 and 1)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic intraepidermal bullous disease with flaccid blisters, Nikolsky sign, and oral mucosal sloughing, alongside esophagrams demonstrating esophageal lining detachment (esophagitis dissecans superficialis).

Dermatology.name: Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Striking, pathognomonic mucocutaneous pigmented macules (lentigines): discrete, flat, dark brown to black round or oval macules (1-5 mm) densely clustered around the vermilion border of the lips, perioral cutaneous margins, buccal mucosa, hard palate, tongue, nostrils, perianal skin, and volar fingertips
Pigmented macules typically appear in infancy or early childhood; mucosal macules characteristically persist throughout life, whereas facial cutaneous macules may fade in adulthood
Recurrent episodes of severe colicky abdominal pain, small bowel mechanical obstruction, and rectal bleeding/melena
Gynecomastia, accelerated bone age, and sexual precocity in prepubertal boys (due to estrogen-secreting testicular tumors)
radiological_manifestations: CT Enterography / MR Enterography: Multiple discrete, lobulated, pedunculated or sessile polyps throughout the gastrointestinal tract (predominantly jejunum, ileum, and duodenum); hallmark visualization of acute transient or fixed small bowel intussusceptions demonstrating classic 'target sign', 'donut sign', or sausage-shaped soft-tissue mass with lead-point polyps on ultrasound and CT
Pelvic Ultrasound / MRI: Sex cord tumors with annular tubules (SCTAT) of the ovary presenting as bilateral small, solid, calcified ovarian masses in females; adenoma malignum of the cervix
Scrotal Ultrasound: Bilateral, multifocal, bright intratesticular calcifications with acoustic shadowing diagnostic of Large Cell Calcifying Sertoli Cell Tumors (LCCSCT)
pathology_manifestations: Gastrointestinal Hamartomatous Polyp Histopathology: Pathognomonic architectural structure consisting of an extensive, arborizing, branching tree-like network of well-developed smooth muscle bundles (derived from the muscularis mucosae) that forms a structural core supporting hyperplastic, mature glandular mucosa with normal cellular differentiation

Mucocutaneous Macule Punch Biopsy: Marked increase in melanin pigmentation concentrated within keratinocytes of the epidermal basal layer and abundant melanophages nestled in the upper papillary dermis, without atypical melanocytic proliferation or significant increase in melanocyte numbers
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Signature hamartomatous polyposis syndrome with pathognomonic perioral/mucosal melanocytic lentigines, matched with CT enterographic lead-point intussusceptions ('target sign'), testicular/ovarian sex-cord calcifications on ultrasound, and arborizing smooth muscle polyps on histology.

Dermatology.name: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda
clinical_manifestations: Marked mechanical cutaneous fragility and photodistributed skin vulnerability confined to sun-exposed regions, most prominently the dorsal hands, extensor forearms, neck, and face
Tense subepidermal bullae and vesicles developing after trivial mechanical friction or sun exposure, rapidly rupturing into painful crusted erosions
Healing with characteristic tiny, firm, white inclusion cysts (milia), superficial atrophic scarring, and irregular mottled postinflammatory hyperpigmentation
Facial hypertrichosis featuring fine, dark, lanugo-like hairs developing over the malar prominences, temples, and periorbital margins
Sclerodermoid (morphea-like) induration with waxy yellowish thickened plaques on the chest, back, and face in longstanding disease
Dark reddish-brown or tea-colored urine exhibiting striking, brilliant coral-pink to red fluorescence under Wood's lamp examination (365 nm UVA)
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal MRI with Quantitative Iron Relaxometry (T2* / R2* Mapping): Marked diffuse loss of hepatic parenchymal signal intensity on T2-weighted and T2*-weighted gradient-echo sequences, directly quantifying hepatic iron overload (hemosiderosis) and guiding therapeutic phlebotomy

Multiphasic Liver CT / MRI: Assessment of underlying hepatic architectural changes (cirrhotic nodular surface, splenomegaly, ascites) and mandatory surveillance detection of hypervascular arterial-enhancing nodular lesions diagnostic of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
Abdominal Ultrasound: Diffuse coarse increase in hepatic parenchymal echogenicity secondary to hepatic steatosis, iron deposition, and progressive portal fibrosis
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy of Fresh Blister: Cell-poor, pauci-inflammatory subepidermal bulla with preserved, intact dermal papillae protruding upward into the blister lumen in an undulating, undulating pattern ('festooning of dermal papillae'); prominent eosinophilic PAS-positive, diastase-resistant hyaline cuffs encasing the superficial dermal microvasculature; intraepidermal eosinophilic globoid 'caterpillar bodies' representing degraded basement membrane components within the blister roof
Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Broad, homogeneous linear deposition of IgG and C3 (and to a lesser extent IgM) encircling upper dermal capillary walls and lining the dermo-epidermal junction

Liver Core Biopsy: Marked hemosiderin deposition primarily within periportal hepatocytes and Kupffer cells (confirmed with Perls' Prussian blue stain), accompanied by variable steatohepatitis; frozen unfixed liver tissue demonstrates needle-shaped birefringent uroporphyrin crystals showing bright red autofluorescence under fluorescence microscopy
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential photo-induced metabolic dermatosis combining dorsal hand mechanical blistering, milia, and facial hypertrichosis with tea-colored fluorescent urine, hepatic T2* MRI iron overload quantification, and festooned cell-poor subepidermal histology.

Dermatology.name: Pseudoxanthoma Elasticum
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic yellowish, cobblestone-like or 'plucked-chicken skin' papules and confluent plaques primarily on the lateral neck and flexural folds (axillae, antecubital fossae, groin)
Progressive redundancy and laxity of skin in flexural creases forming prominent hanging folds

Angioid streaks on fundoscopic examination (breaks in calcified Bruch membrane radiating outward from the optic disc) with 'peau d'orange' mottling and subretinal choroidal neovascularization leading to retinal hemorrhages and central vision loss
Mucosal involvement with discrete yellowish submucosal papules on the inner aspect of the lower lip and buccal mucosa
Accelerated peripheral vascular insufficiency manifested by diminished or absent peripheral pulses, early-onset intermittent claudication, and cold extremities
Recurrent upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage from friable, calcified submucosal gastric vessels
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography of Extremities: Extensive, symmetric, fine linear 'tram-track' arterial wall calcifications along medium-sized muscular arteries (femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial, and radial arteries) in young adult patients

Non-Contrast Computed Tomography (CT): Extensive calcification of peripheral, visceral (mesenteric, renal), and cerebral arteries (particularly internal carotid siphon and vertebrobasilar arteries); premature coronary artery calcification on cardiac CT calcium scoring

Scrotal and Abdominal Ultrasound: Diffuse, fine, non-shadowing testicular microlithiasis ('snowstorm' pattern in bilateral testes); medullary nephrocalcinosis and acoustic shadowing along splenic and intrahepatic arterial branches
Screening Mammography: Distinctive linear and punctate microcalcifications tracing intramammary arterial walls with high specificity

Fundus Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) & Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): Angioid streaks appearing as irregular hyperfluorescent radial cracks, subretinal fluid, retinal pigment epithelium detachment, and choroidal neovascular membranes (CNVM)
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Mid-to-Deep Reticular Dermis): Clumped, curled, fragmented, and swollen basophilic elastic fibers displaying a distinct 'ravelled wool' or 'ant-eaten' appearance on routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)

Special Histochemical Stains: von Kossa and Alizarin Red stains demonstrate dense calcium phosphate mineralization coating and encrusting the fragmented elastic fibers; Verhoeff-van Gieson (VVG) stain highlights irregular, fragmented, shortened black/blue elastic fibers

Arterial Wall Histology: Massive fragmentation and dense calcification concentrated within the internal elastic lamina of medium- and small-caliber muscular arteries, accompanied by secondary luminal narrowing and reactive intimal fibroplasia
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic heritable elastic tissue disorder marrying hallmark flexural 'plucked-chicken skin' and fundoscopic angioid streaks with striking peripheral 'tram-track' arterial calcifications on plain radiography/CT and von Kossa-positive fragmented dermal elastic fibers.

Dermatology.name: Psoriasis
Dermatology.summary: Chronic inflammatory skin disease with well-demarcated scaly plaques and nail changes.
clinical_manifestations: Well-demarcated, erythematous plaques covered by thick, silvery-white micaceous scales (extensor elbows, knees, scalp, lumbosacral)
Auspitz sign: punctate bleeding points upon removal of scales
Koebner phenomenon (isomorphic response to epidermal trauma)
Psoriatic nail changes (pitting, oil-drop discoloration, subungual hyperkeratosis)
Guttate, inverse (intertriginous flexural), and generalized pustular (von Zumbusch) variants
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Ultrasound (HFUS) of Skin: Epidermal thickening, subepidermal hypoechoic band (dermal edema), hypervascularity on power Doppler
Joint and Entheseal Ultrasound: Subclinical enthesopathy (Achilles, plantar fascia) in cutaneous psoriasis patients
Plain Radiography / MRI (screening for concomitant PsA): Asymmetric periostitis and entheseal new bone formation
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Marked regular epidermal hyperplasia (acanthosis) with elongation of rete ridges ('test tubes in a rack'), hyperkeratosis with confluent parakeratosis, hypogranulosis, Munro microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum), spongiform pustules of Kogoj, tortuous dilated capillary loops in dermal papillae
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Core skin disease with unmistakable clinical plaques and nail changes paired with cutaneous high-frequency ultrasound and musculoskeletal imaging of concomitant enthesitis.

Dermatology.name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly progressive, agonizingly painful ulceration starting as an inflammatory pustule or furuncle
Pathognomonic undermined, violaceous, gunmetal-blue borders
Purulent, cribriform (sieve-like) necrotic ulcer base with foul exudate
Marked pathergy (ulcer enlargement or new lesion development following minor trauma, debridement, or venipuncture)
Heals with characteristic cribriform or 'cigarette paper' atrophic scarring
Peristomal pyoderma gangrenosum (around stomas in patients with inflammatory bowel disease)
radiological_manifestations: Soft Tissue Ultrasound / MRI: Marked subcutaneous edema, absence of necrotizing fascial fluid or gas (differentiating from necrotizing fasciitis)
CT / MR Enterography: Underlying inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease with transmural bowel thickening or Ulcerative Colitis)
Skeletal Radiography / CT: Underlying associated arthritis or hematologic malignancy (myelodysplastic syndrome bone marrow changes)
pathology_manifestations: Skin ulcer edge biopsy: Massive, dense, suppurative neutrophilic infiltration of the dermis with leukocytoclasia, tissue necrosis, and secondary endothelial swelling; lack of true primary vasculitis or infectious pathogens
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential neutrophilic ulcer with signature undermined violaceous borders and cribriform base, paired with abdominal CT enterography of associated IBD and soft-tissue MRI to rule out deep fascial infection.

Dermatology.name: Reactive Perforating Collagenosis
clinical_manifestations: Eruption of multiple, intensely pruritic, discrete, umbilicated, dome-shaped erythematous to hyperpigmented papules and nodules (2 to 10 mm in diameter)
Pathognomonic firmly adherent, central, hard, dark brown-to-black hyperkeratotic crust or keratinous plug lodged in a central cup-shaped crater

Classic distribution over extensor surfaces of limbs (forearms, shins, thighs) and trunk, prominently demonstrating the Koebner phenomenon (linear arrays of eruptive papules induced by scratching or minor trauma)

Highly prevalent acquired association (>10% of patients with end-stage renal disease [ESRD] undergoing chronic hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis and patients with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus with microvascular complications)
Removal of the central plug causes pinpoint hemorrhage and is rapidly followed by reformation of the keratinous crater
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasound: Demonstrates bilateral, symmetrically small, shrunken, hyper-echogenic kidneys with severe cortical thinning (<1 cm) and loss of normal corticomedullary differentiation indicative of end-stage renal parenchymal disease (diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis); may show acquired cystic disease of uremia with multiple bilateral simple or complex cysts

Plain Radiography of Extremities: Extensive, symmetric, continuous 'pipe-stem' arterial wall calcifications along the femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial, and dorsalis pedis arteries characteristic of Mönckeberg medial calcific sclerosis; reveals severe renal osteodystrophy (subperiosteal cortical bone resorption along radial aspects of middle phalanges, terminal tuft acro-osteolysis, and 'salt-and-pepper' skull)

Plain Radiographs of Spine: Demonstrates pathognomonic 'rugger-jersey spine' (dense, sclerotic bands across the superior and inferior vertebral endplates with central lucency) reflecting secondary hyperparathyroidism in ESRD
Dermoscopy: Central yellow-brown to dark keratotic core surrounded by a structureless white or pink halo and a peripheral rim of dotted and hairpin vessels
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous Biopsy (Including Central Crater and Underlying Dermis): Cup-shaped or saucer-shaped epidermal invagination filled with a massive, compact plug of parakeratin, orthokeratin, degenerated basophilic nuclear debris, and inflammatory cells

Transepidermal Elimination: Disruption and perforation of the epidermal basement membrane at the base of the invagination with vertically oriented, altered, degenerated basophilic collagen bundles streaming upward from the papillary dermis directly into the epidermal crater
Masson Trichrome Special Stain: Vividly stains the perforating degenerated collagen bundles blue/green, highlighting their vertical extrusion through the epidermal cleft
Verhoeff-van Gieson (VVG) Special Stain: Demonstrates that elastic fibers are fragmented and remain excluded from the crater, distinguishing RPC from elastosis perforans serpiginosa
von Kossa / Alizarin Red Stains: Negative for calcium deposits within the plug or collagen, differentiating from perforating calcinosis cutis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic perforating dermatosis coupling hallmark umbilicated papules with central keratinous plugs in dialysis-dependent renal failure with renal ultrasound of shrunken kidneys, Mönckeberg calcifications, and Masson trichrome collagen elimination.

Dermatology.name: Scleredema Adultorum of Buschke
clinical_manifestations: Insidious, symmetric, non-pitting, woody, indurated thickening and tightening of the skin characteristically beginning on the nape and lateral aspects of the neck and posterior upper back
Progressive spread over the shoulders, upper arms, chest wall, and occasionally the face, resulting in a mask-like facial appearance and restricted neck and shoulder range of motion
Characteristic 'peau d'orange' (orange peel) skin surface texture with prominent follicular ostia and complete loss of normal skin folds; skin cannot be pinched or wrinkled
Pathognomonic sparing of the hands and feet (absence of sclerodactyly, Raynaud phenomenon, or telangiectasias, cleanly distinguishing scleredema from systemic sclerosis/scleroderma)

Three recognized distinct clinical subsets: (1) Type 1: Post-infectious acute scleredema (typically preceded by streptococcal pharyngitis or viral infection in young females, often self-limiting); (2) Type 2: Paraproteinemia-associated chronic progressive scleredema (associated with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance [MGUS], multiple myeloma, or amyloidosis); (3) Type 3: Scleredema diabeticorum (occurring in middle-aged, obese individuals with longstanding, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus with severe insulin resistance and microvascular disease)
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz) of Dermis: Demonstrates profound, diffuse thickening of the reticular dermis (often measuring 3 to 5 times thicker than unaffected skin) with marked hypoechogenicity reflecting abundant interstitial mucin and edema; demonstrates a sharply demarcated, intact dermal-subcutaneous boundary with complete sparing of subcutaneous fat and deep fascia

Soft Tissue Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of Neck and Upper Torso: Demonstrates marked diffuse thickening of the cutaneous and dermal layer; the expanded dermis is isointense to hypointense on T1-weighted images and markedly hyperintense on T2-weighted, STIR, and fat-suppressed sequences owing to high mucin (acid glycosaminoglycan) and free water content; crucially confirms normal appearance, signal, and absence of thickening or enhancement of the deep muscular fascia and skeletal muscle (distinguishing scleredema from eosinophilic fasciitis and dermatomyositis)

Whole-Body Low-Dose CT (WBLDCT) or Skeletal Survey: Evaluates patients with Type 2 scleredema for punched-out lytic bone lesions, osteosclerosis, or diffuse osteopenia indicative of underlying multiple myeloma or systemic plasma cell dyscrasias
Transthoracic Echocardiography: Assesses for diastolic dysfunction and restrictive cardiomyopathy in patients with paraproteinemia-associated deposition disease
pathology_manifestations: Full-Thickness Skin Incisional / Punch Biopsy (Extending into Subcutis): Demonstrates striking, massive thickening of the reticular dermis (up to 300-400% of normal dermal depth) characterized by markedly swollen, thickened, broad collagen bundles separated by wide, clear fenestrations and spaces (interstitial edema and mucin)

Preservation of Surrounding Structures: Unremarkable overlying epidermis, normal pilosebaceous and sweat gland adnexa, and absence of inflammatory infiltrate, cellular atypia, or vasculitis; subcutaneous fat lobules are normal, with broad collagen bands occasionally extending between fat cells

Alcian Blue (pH 2.5) & Colloidal Iron Special Stains: Strongly stain the clear fenestrations between collagen bundles bright turquoise/blue, confirming extensive extracellular deposition of non-sulfated acid mucopolysaccharides (hyaluronic acid)
Hyaluronidase Digestion: Completely abolishes the Alcian blue and colloidal iron staining, confirming hyaluronic acid as the principal accumulating glycosaminoglycan
Masson Trichrome & Verhoeff-van Gieson (VVG): Normal collagen and normal or slightly diminished elastic fibers without dermal fibrosis or elastorrhexis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Landmark deposition dermatosis characterized by woody neck/back induration with hand-sparing, where high-frequency ultrasound and soft-tissue MRI prove isolated dermal mucin thickening while sparing muscular fascia, and Alcian blue confirms hyaluronidase-sensitive mucin.

Dermatology.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
clinical_manifestations: Dusky, purpuric, atypical targetoid macules rapidly coalescing across the face, trunk, and extremities
Extensive flaccid epidermal bullae and sheet-like full-thickness sloughing of epidermis leaving raw, weeping, denuded dermis ('scalded skin')
Positive Nikolsky sign (shearing of epidermis upon gentle lateral digital pressure)
Positive Asboe-Hansen sign (lateral extension of bulla upon direct pressure)
Severe mucositis of >=2 surfaces: hemorrhagic crusting of vermilion lips, oral stomatitis, severe purulent conjunctivitis, pseudomembranes, genital/urethral erosions
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / CT: Acute pulmonary complications: tracheobronchial mucosal sloughing, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, diffuse ground-glass infiltrates, chemical pneumonitis, bacterial superinfection
pathology_manifestations: Frozen section / Formalin-fixed biopsy: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis and detachment, subepidermal separation, extensive keratinocyte apoptosis, satellite cell necrosis, minimal superficial dermal perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Dramatic dermatologic emergency featuring full-thickness sheet sloughing and severe mucositis with chest imaging demonstrating tracheobronchial sloughing and ARDS.

Dermatology.name: Subcorneal Pustular Dermatosis (Sneddon-Wilkinson Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, recurrent eruption of sterile, flaccid, pea-sized pustules grouped in annular, circinate, polycyclic, or serpiginous patterns

Pathognomonic 'Half-and-Half' Pustule Sign: pustules characteristically settle under the influence of gravity, such that purulent cellular debris forms a horizontal sediment in the lower half of the blister while clear serous fluid fills the upper half
Predilection for flexural aspects of the trunk and extremities: axillae, groins, submammary folds, inframammary regions, and lower abdomen; face, palms, and soles are characteristically spared

Pustules are extremely fragile and rupture rapidly within hours to days, leaving superficial circular or annular erythematous erosions with fine, collarette-like scaling and residual brown hyperpigmentation without scarring

Strong clinical association with monoclonal gammopathy, overwhelmingly an IgA paraproteinemia, which may herald or accompany multiple myeloma, smoldering myeloma, pyoderma gangrenosum, or inflammatory bowel disease
Remarkable and rapid clinical response to oral dapsone therapy, often within 48 to 72 hours
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz): Identifies very superficial, subcorneal, anechoic to hypoechoic lenticular fluid pockets strictly localized to the uppermost stratum corneum and intraepidermal interface, with a thin roof and acoustic transmission; underlying dermis shows minimal, mild perivascular edema without deep subcutaneous expansion

Skeletal Radiographic Survey / Low-Dose Whole-Body CT: Essential screening for associated IgA multiple myeloma, identifying 'punched-out' osteolytic bone lesions of the calvarium, pelvis, spine, and long bones, or vertebral compression fractures
Chest CT and Abdominal CT: Evaluates for underlying systemic plasma cell neoplasms, solitary plasmacytomas, or occult lymphoproliferative disorders
Abdominal Ultrasound / Colonoscopy Imaging: Evaluates for concurrent inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis) in patients presenting with relapsing flexural pustulosis
pathology_manifestations: Subcorneal Cleavage: Large, unilocular pustules located directly beneath the stratum corneum, resting directly on the underlying stratum spinosum
Neutrophilic Content: The pustular cavity is filled overwhelmingly with mature, well-preserved polymorphonuclear neutrophils, with occasional eosinophils, and complete absence of acantholytic cells

Underlying Epidermis: The underlying spinous epidermis remains essentially intact, exhibiting minimal to mild intercellular edema (spongiosis) without acantholysis or significant spongiform pustule formation (distinguishing it from generalized pustular psoriasis)
Dermal Infiltrate: Superficial perivascular inflammatory infiltrate composed of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and histiocytes in the upper papillary dermis

Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Strictly negative for intercellular or basement membrane zone antibodies (negative for IgG, IgA, IgM, and C3), which is the essential diagnostic criteria ruling out subcorneal IgA pemphigus
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Relapsing sterile pustular dermatosis with the pathognomonic 'half-and-half' gravity sign and IgA paraproteinemia association, monitored by high-frequency skin ultrasound showing superficial subcorneal fluid cavities, screened by skeletal radiography/CT for osteolytic myeloma lesions, and pathologically confirmed by subcorneal neutrophilic pustules without acantholysis or DIF positivity.

Dermatology.name: Subcutaneous Granuloma Annulare (Deep Granuloma Annulare)
clinical_manifestations: Solitary or multiple, firm, non-tender, immobile or mobile deep dermal and subcutaneous nodules measuring 0.5 to 5 cm in diameter
Predominantly affects young children (peak age 2 to 6 years) who are otherwise healthy and lack systemic symptoms
Characteristic anatomic distribution: lower extremities (especially the anterior pretibial shins), dorsal hands and feet, fingers, buttocks, and scalp
Overlying skin typically appears completely normal, slightly violaceous, or flesh-colored, without epidermal scaling, ulceration, or ring-like surface morphology
Rapid initial growth over weeks often alarms clinicians and parents, raising concern for deep soft tissue sarcoma (epithelioid sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma) or rheumatoid nodules
Spontaneous regression occurs over months to several years without scar formation; recurrent lesions may develop at identical or distant sites
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal MRI (Extremity / Soft Tissue): Infiltrative or well-demarcated nodular mass centered within the deep subcutaneous fat directly abutting or tracking along the deep muscular fascia; isointense to hypointense to muscle on T1-weighted images; heterogeneously hyperintense or target-like on T2-weighted and STIR images; demonstrates marked, avid, heterogeneous or thick peripheral nodular enhancement following intravenous gadolinium; absence of bone invasion or cortical breach

High-Frequency Soft Tissue Ultrasound: Well-defined or lobulated, uniformly hypoechoic subcutaneous mass abutting the underlying muscular fascia or periosteum without bony erosion; color Doppler shows minimal to moderate peripheral vascularity without high-velocity internal arteriovenous shunting (distinguishing it from vascular malformations or aggressive sarcomas)
Plain Radiography: Soft tissue nodular prominence without internal calcification (excluding phleboliths, calcinosis, or tumoral calcinosis) and completely normal underlying bone architecture
pathology_manifestations: Deep Subcutaneous Palisading Granulomas: Large, discrete or confluent granulomatous foci centered within the deep reticular dermis and extending broadly into subcutaneous adipose septa and lobules
Necrobiotic Core: Central expansive zones of pale, basophilic necrobiosis (altered, smudged collagen) containing abundant interstitial mucin (hyaluronic acid)

Colloidal Iron / Alcian Blue Stains: Intense, bright blue staining within the necrobiotic centers confirming abundant hyaluronic acid mucin, a key histological hallmark distinguishing SGA from rheumatoid nodules
Palisading Border: Palisade of activated CD68+ histiocytes, epithelioid macrophages, and multinucleated giant cells surrounding the necrobiotic mucinous cores

Differential Exclusions: Complete absence of neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells (differentiating from necrobiosis lipoidica); absence of central fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by CD3+ T-cells (differentiating from classic rheumatoid nodules); negative fungal and mycobacterial stains
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Deep granulomatous condition of childhood presenting as firm non-tender subcutaneous nodules mimicking soft tissue sarcoma, characterized on extremity MRI by fascial-abutting hyperintense avidly enhancing masses, and pathologically defined by palisading granulomas surrounding mucin-rich (alcian blue+) necrobiotic collagen.

Dermatology.name: Sweet Syndrome (Acute Febrile Neutrophilic Dermatosis)
clinical_manifestations: Sudden onset of painful, tender, sharply demarcated erythematous to violaceous succulent papules, plaques, and nodules with a characteristic mammillated or pseudovesicular/pustular surface caused by intense upper dermal edema
High spiking fevers (often >38.5°C) accompanying the eruption and dramatic peripheral neutrophilic leukocytosis (>10,000/µL with left shift)
Predilection for the upper extremities (dorsum of hands, forearms), head, neck, and upper trunk; lesions often exhibit an annular or arciform configuration with central clearing
Extracutaneous manifestations including severe arthralgias/arthritis (knees, wrists), ocular inflammation (conjunctivitis, episcleritis, iridocyclitis), and oral aphthous-like ulcerations

Association with hematologic neoplasms (acute myeloid leukemia, myelodysplastic syndrome in up to 20%), inflammatory bowel disease, infections, and medications (especially granulocyte colony-stimulating factor [G-CSF], all-trans retinoic acid [ATRA])
Rapid and dramatic therapeutic response to systemic corticosteroids (prompt defervescence within 48-72 hours)
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz): Marked, pathognomonic hypoechoic band in the upper papillary dermis directly subjacent to an intact epidermis representing massive papillary dermal edema; absence of true fluid collections or abscess cavities (confirming pseudovesicular nature); increased dermal Doppler vascularity during acute flares

Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT: Multiple bilateral pulmonary opacities representing aseptic pulmonary Sweet syndrome / neutrophilic alveolitis, presenting as patchy peribronchovascular consolidations, ground-glass opacities, pleural effusions, and mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy that rapidly clear under systemic steroids

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal and Pelvic CT: Splenomegaly and multiple ill-defined, low-attenuation sterile splenic or hepatic lesions (neutrophilic microabscesses) that fail antibiotic therapy but resolve with steroids; mesenteric lymphadenopathy and screening for occult visceral malignancy or pelvic tumors

18F-FDG PET/CT: Intense focal hypermetabolism corresponding to active cutaneous plaques, splenic lesions, pulmonary infiltrates, and evaluation of underlying hematologic marrow involvement (diffuse hypermetabolism in AML/MDS transformation)
Musculoskeletal MRI: Periarticular soft tissue edema, joint effusion, and sterile tenosynovitis in symptomatic joints without underlying cortical erosions
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (H&E): Striking, massive papillary dermal edema causing separation of collagen bundles and the clinical appearance of pseudovesicles, without intraepidermal blister formation

Dermal Infiltrate: Dense, band-like or nodular inflammatory infiltrate in the papillary and upper-to-mid reticular dermis composed overwhelmingly of mature, morphologically intact neutrophils with prominent leukocytoclasia (nuclear dust / karyorrhexis)

Absence of Primary Vasculitis: True leukocytoclastic vasculitis is absent (no primary fibrinoid necrosis of post-capillary venule walls, no erythrocyte extravasation into vessel walls); any minor vessel alteration is strictly secondary to bystander cytokine injury

Histiocytoid Sweet Syndrome Variant: Infiltrate composed predominantly of immature, myeloid-lineage mononuclear cells with histiocytoid reniform nuclei expressing myeloperoxidase (MPO), CD68, and CD43
Special Stains: Gram, PAS, and Fite/Grocott silver stains are strictly negative for bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial microorganisms; negative direct immunofluorescence (DIF)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic acute neutrophilic dermatosis characterized clinically by tender succulent pseudovesicular plaques and high fever, diagnostically evaluated radiologically by high-frequency skin ultrasound showing massive papillary dermal edema and chest/abdominal CT revealing aseptic pulmonary consolidations and splenic microabscesses, and pathologically confirmed by dense dermal neutrophilia with striking papillary edema without primary vasculitis.

Dermatology.name: Wells Syndrome (Eosinophilic Cellulitis)
clinical_manifestations: Sudden, recurrent eruption of intensely itchy, stinging, or burning erythematous and edematous plaques that rapidly expand over 2-3 days to involve large cutaneous areas, clinically masquerading as severe bacterial cellulitis or erysipelas
Eruption frequently preceded by prodromal tingling, burning, or paresthesias; fails multiple courses of systemic antibacterial therapy
Evolution over several days into distinctive, indurated, firm, morphea-like or woody plaques with violaceous, dusky, or slate-blue/slate-gray advancing borders and central involution
Frequent formation of tense bullae, vesicles, or petechiae overlying the edematous plaques
Predilection for extremities, trunk, and face; resolves without scarring over 2-8 weeks, leaving temporary hyperpigmentation

Prominent peripheral blood eosinophilia (>50-60% of patients) during acute flares, accompanied by elevated serum eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) and total IgE; triggered by arthropod bites, viral/parasitic infections, medications, or hematologic disorders
