radiological_manifestations: Soft Tissue MRI (T1, T2, STIR, T1+C): Extensive, diffuse cutaneous thickening and marked hyperintensity of the subcutaneous fat and superficial fascia on T2-weighted and STIR sequences (representing profound inflammatory edema); diffuse reticular enhancement post-contrast; crucial absence of discrete loculated fluid collections, drainable abscess cavities, intramuscular fluid, or soft tissue gas, radiologically excluding bacterial necrotizing fasciitis/cellulitis

High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS): Marked hypoechoic expansion of the dermis with a characteristic 'cobblestone' pattern in the subcutaneous tissue due to fluid tracking along fat lobules and septa; absence of hypoechoic liquefactive abscess pockets; power Doppler reveals diffuse hyperemia in acute phases
Plain Radiography: Excludes subcutaneous gas, radiopaque foreign bodies, or adjacent periosteal reaction
pathology_manifestations: Dynamic Triphasic Histological Evolution: Striking, diagnostic progression through acute, subacute, and resolution phases

Acute Phase: Massive dermal edema with an intense, diffuse inflammatory infiltrate dominated by mature eosinophils spreading through the reticular dermis and tracking along subcutaneous fibrous septa, without vasculitis

Subacute Phase (Pathognomonic): Formation of classic, diagnostic 'flame figures' (figures en flamme), composed of degenerate dermal collagen bundles coated with brightly eosinophilic granules of degranulated eosinophil major basic protein (MBP), surrounded by a palisade of CD68+ histiocytes and multinucleated foreign-body giant cells
Resolution Phase: Gradual phagocytosis of flame figures by histiocytic giant cells, disappearance of eosinophils, and mild dermal interstitial fibrosis
Immunohistochemistry: Extracellular granular deposition of eosinophil major basic protein (MBP) and eosinophil-derived neurotoxin (EDN) decorating the flame figures
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Recurrent inflammatory dermatosis masquerading as severe bacterial cellulitis, imaged on soft tissue MRI and ultrasound by diffuse subcutaneous/fascial edema lacking drainable abscess or gas, and pathologically characterized by dramatic eosinophilic infiltrates with pathognomonic flame figures encrusted with eosinophil major basic protein.

Dermatology.name: Xanthoma Disseminatum
synonyms: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis, xanthoma disseminatum type
clinical_manifestations: Eruption of hundreds to thousands of discrete, round, smooth, yellowish-red, orange-brown, or reddish-brown waxy papules and nodules (1-5 mm) that frequently coalesce into indurated, verrucous plaques

Characteristic pathognomonic flexural and intertriginous predilection: axillae, antecubital and popliteal fossae, groin, perineum, neck folds, and antecubital creases, as well as periorbital and perioral facial skin

Extensive mucosal involvement (40-60% of cases): xanthomatous papules and plaques infiltrating the upper aerodigestive tract (oral cavity, tongue, pharynx, epiglottis, larynx, vocal cords, trachea, bronchi), leading to progressive hoarseness, dysphonia, dysphagia, stridor, and potentially fatal upper airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy

Pituitary-hypothalamic axis involvement (~40% of cases): transient or permanent central diabetes insipidus resulting in polyuria and polydipsia, forming the classic Montgomery triad (flexural xanthomas, mucosal lesions, and diabetes insipidus)
Ocular involvement: xanthomatous infiltration of conjunctiva, cornea, sclera, and orbits causing visual impairment
Normal serum lipid and cholesterol profile (normolipemic xanthomatosis), distinguishing it from hyperlipidemic xanthomatosis
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Pituitary MRI (High-Resolution T1, T2, T1+C): Nodular thickening and avid, homogeneous gadolinium enhancement of the pituitary stalk (infundibulum) and hypothalamus; absence of the normal hyperintense 'bright spot' of the posterior pituitary on unenhanced T1-weighted images (hallmark of central diabetes insipidus); meningeal thickening and xanthomatous dural plaques

CT of Neck and Soft Tissues / Virtual Endoscopy: Extensive irregular nodular soft tissue mucosal thickening causing luminal narrowing of the glottis, subglottis, pyriform sinuses, and upper trachea without destruction of underlying laryngeal cartilage
Chest CT: Nodular xanthomatous deposits along tracheobronchial tree, pulmonary interstitial infiltrates, and subpleural micronodules
Orbital MRI / CT: Well-defined, non-calcified soft tissue masses within the epibulbar space, cornea, and retrobulbar orbit with variable T2 hypointensity and contrast enhancement

Skeletal Radiography / Whole-Body Low-Dose CT: Complete absence of osteolytic skeletal bone lesions, which is crucial for distinguishing xanthoma disseminatum from Langerhans cell histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester disease
pathology_manifestations: Non-Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis: Dense, sheets-like, nodular inflammatory infiltrate occupying the upper and mid dermis without extending into the epidermis (clear Grenz zone)

Cellular Composition: Predominance of large, lipid-laden foamy histiocytes (xanthoma cells) admixed with pathognomonic Touton-type multinucleated giant cells (characterized by a central wreath of nuclei surrounded by a rim of foamy, lipid-rich cytoplasm)
Admixed Infiltrate: Interspersed mature lymphocytes, plasma cells, neutrophils, and eosinophils; older lesions show progressive storiform interstitial fibrosis

Immunohistochemistry (IHC): Histiocytes are strongly positive for CD68, CD163, and Factor XIIIa; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207) (ruling out Langerhans cell histiocytosis); S100 protein is typically negative or only weakly and focally positive
Electron Microscopy: Absence of Birbeck granules (pentalaminar tennis-racket organelles), confirming non-Langerhans lineage
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive normolipemic non-Langerhans cell histiocytic dermatosis characterized by widespread flexural xanthomas and upper airway lesions, imaged on brain MRI by infundibular stalk thickening with loss of the posterior pituitary T1 bright spot, on neck CT by laryngeal/tracheal airway narrowing, and confirmed histologically by CD68+/CD1a- foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells.

Dermatology.name: Mycosis Fungoides
clinical_manifestations: Patch stage: bathing-suit distribution of scaly, atrophic, wrinkled patches
Plaque and tumor stage: infiltrated arcuate plaques and ulcerated nodules
Poikiloderma and a wrinkled epidermis in long-standing patches
radiological_manifestations: CT or PET only when staging nodes or viscera; the diagnostic images are clinical and histologic
pathology_manifestations: Epidermotropic atypical CD4 lymphocytes, Pautrier microabscesses, and a band-like dermal infiltrate
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Cutaneous lymphoma whose stage photographs and skin biopsy are the image library, not a single rash type.

Dermatology.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Pearly rolled-border papule with telangiectasias on sun-exposed skin
Ulcerated rodent ulcer and the scar-like morpheaform plaque
Pigmented and superficial variants on dermoscopy
radiological_manifestations: Imaging is reserved for neglected perineural or orbital invasion and is not required for the usual gallery
pathology_manifestations: Basaloid tumor islands with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The most photographed cutaneous malignancy, with clinical, dermoscopic, and histologic images.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma
synonyms: Marjolin ulcer when arising in a scar
clinical_manifestations: Hyperkeratotic, crateriform nodule on sun-damaged skin
Marjolin ulcer in a burn scar or chronic osteomyelitis sinus
Keratoacanthoma-like dome with a central keratin plug
radiological_manifestations: Regional nodal ultrasound or CT when a high-risk tumor is staged
pathology_manifestations: Invasive atypical keratinocytes, keratin pearls, and solar elastosis in the adjacent dermis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Keratinocyte cancer with ulcer and keratosis photographs plus a standard histologic image.

Dermatology.name: Darier Disease
clinical_manifestations: Greasy hyperkeratotic papules in seborrheic areas, coalescing into plaques
Nail dystrophy with red and white longitudinal bands and V-shaped nicks
Palmar pits and cobblestone oral papules
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific radiology; nail and oral photographs carry the non-skin sites
pathology_manifestations: Acantholytic dyskeratosis with corps ronds and grains
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Genodermatosis identified by the seborrheic papules, pathognomonic nails, and acantholytic histology.

Dermatology.name: Hailey-Hailey Disease
clinical_manifestations: Macerated, fissured plaques in the neck, axillae, and groin with a soggy scale crust
Flare photographs after friction, heat, or secondary infection
radiological_manifestations: No radiology; intertriginous photographs and histology define the topic
pathology_manifestations: Dilapidated brick wall full-thickness acantholysis, distinguishing it from pemphigus vulgaris
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Inherited blistering disease with a recognizable intertriginous photograph and a named histologic pattern.

Dermatology.name: Lamellar Ichthyosis
clinical_manifestations: Collodion membrane in the newborn, then large plate-like brown scales
Ectropion and eclabium photographs
Palmoplantar keratoderma
radiological_manifestations: No diagnostic radiology; the neonatal and scale photographs are the gallery
pathology_manifestations: Compact orthohyperkeratosis without the epidermolytic change of epidermolytic ichthyosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Congenital ichthyosis with unmistakable neonatal and plate-scale photographs, distinct from epidermolytic ichthyosis already indexed.

Dermatology.name: Xeroderma Pigmentosum
clinical_manifestations: Lentigines and poikiloderma on sun-exposed skin of a child
Multiple basal and squamous cell carcinomas and melanoma on the face
Photophobia and conjunctival injection or ocular surface tumors
radiological_manifestations: Neuroimaging only in the De Sanctis-Cacchione neurologic subset
pathology_manifestations: Early keratinocyte atypia and the specific skin cancers that arise in the poikiloderma
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: DNA-repair genodermatosis whose childhood pigmentary photographs and skin cancers are the image set.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Mastocytosis
clinical_manifestations: Red-brown macules and papules on the trunk of a child
Darier sign: wheal and flare photographed after stroking a lesion
Mastocytoma: a solitary yellow-orange plaque that blisters when rubbed
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey or abdominal imaging only if systemic mastocytosis is being separated from the cutaneous disease
pathology_manifestations: Dermal mast-cell aggregates highlighted by tryptase and CD117
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Mast-cell skin disease with a photographable Darier sign, kept separate from systemic mastocytosis.

Dermatology.name: Lichen Planus
clinical_manifestations: Flat-topped violaceous polygonal papules with Wickham striae on the wrists and ankles
Lacy white buccal network
Nail pterygium and scarring alopecia in lichen planopilaris, filed as sites of the same disease rather than separate topics
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Band-like lymphocytic interface dermatitis, sawtooth acanthosis, and cytoid bodies
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Interface dermatosis with skin, mouth, and nail photographs plus a standard biopsy image.

Dermatology.name: Vitiligo
clinical_manifestations: Depigmented macules with convex borders on the face, hands, and genitals
Wood lamp accentuation of chalk-white patches
Segmental vitiligo stopping at the midline
radiological_manifestations: No radiology; Wood lamp is the imaging adjunct
pathology_manifestations: Absent melanocytes on melan-A or Fontana stain, distinguishing vitiligo from post-inflammatory hypopigmentation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Pigmentary disease whose clinical and Wood-lamp photographs are the library. It is a disease, not a manifestation of another indexed topic.

Dermatology.name: Lichen Sclerosus
clinical_manifestations: Ivory-white atrophic figure-of-eight plaques on the vulva or a sclerotic prepuce
Purpura, fissures, and architectural loss in chronic anogenital disease
Extragenital crinkled porcelain papules on the trunk
radiological_manifestations: No radiology unless urethral stricture is imaged in male disease
pathology_manifestations: Homogenized papillary dermal collagen, follicular plugging, and a lichenoid lymphocytic band
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Sclerotic dermatosis with characteristic anogenital photographs and histology.

Dermatology.name: Infantile Hemangioma
clinical_manifestations: Precursor pallor or telangiectatic patch, then a bright red lobulated plaque in infancy
Deep bluish subcutaneous component and later gray involution
Beard distribution and segmental facial lesions that prompt airway or PHACE evaluation, without making those complications separate topics
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound of a deep component; MRI when a segmental facial lesion is assessed for PHACE
pathology_manifestations: GLUT1-positive capillary lobules, distinguishing infantile hemangioma from vascular malformations
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Infantile vascular tumor with a predictable photographic life cycle and a confirming immunostain.

Dermatology.name: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Blue rubbery compressible skin blebs, including palms and soles
Endoscopy: similar venous malformations that bleed
radiological_manifestations: No required radiology unless a deep lesion is mapped with MRI
pathology_manifestations: Venous malformations, unlike GLUT1-positive infantile hemangioma
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Venous malformation syndrome with skin and endoscopic photographs.

Dermatology.name: Acrodermatitis Enteropathica
clinical_manifestations: Erosive, scaly plaques around the mouth, anus, and acral sites in a weanling infant
Alopecia and diarrhea
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Pale upper epidermis; low serum zinc and SLC39A4 confirm
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Zinc dermatosis with a periorificial photograph. Ordinary nutritional deficiency without this pattern stays out.

Dermatology.name: Pellagra
clinical_manifestations: Casal necklace and a photosensitive dermatitis on the hands and feet
Beefy red tongue
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: No specific biopsy; the distribution photograph is the diagnosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Niacin deficiency with a named photosensitive photograph. Included as a visual deficiency disease, not as generic malnutrition.

Dermatology.name: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: A rapidly growing red-violet nodule on sun-exposed skin of an older adult
radiological_manifestations: Regional nodal ultrasound or PET when staging
pathology_manifestations: Trabecular neuroendocrine tumor, CK20 perinuclear dot, Merkel-cell polyomavirus in most
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma with a nodule photograph and a CK20 immunostain.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
clinical_manifestations: Discoid plaques with follicular plugging, scarring, and pigment change
Polycyclic photosensitive plaques of subacute disease
Malar erythema of acute disease is a site of lupus, and systemic lupus remains the systemic topic
radiological_manifestations: No routine radiology
pathology_manifestations: Interface dermatitis, basement-membrane thickening, and a lupus band on immunofluorescence
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Skin-limited lupus phenotypes with scar and annular photographs. Systemic lupus stays the systemic topic; a malar rash alone is not a topic.

Dermatology.name: Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly spreading confluent salmon-colored or orange-red erythroderma displaying pathognomonic sharply demarcated islands of completely normal, uninvolved skin ("islands of sparing")

Follicular hyperkeratotic papules topped by central horny plugs distributed on the dorsal aspects of the fingers (proximal phalanges), hands, wrists, and elbows, imparting a coarse "nutmeg-grater" texture on palpation
Distinctive thick, waxy, orange-yellow palmoplantar keratoderma extending onto the lateral margins of the hands and feet ("PRP sandals" and "PRP gloves") with deep painful fissures
Facial erythema with thick branny scale, severe ectropion, conjunctival injection, and thick yellow-brown subungual hyperkeratosis with longitudinal nail splintering
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound: Diffuse hyperechoic thickening of the stratum corneum and epidermal acoustic shadow corresponding to hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis
Chest Radiography / CT: Utilized in atypical erythroderma workup to exclude underlying solid-organ malignancies or paraneoplastic triggers
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Histology): Alternating orthokeratosis and parakeratosis oriented both vertically and horizontally across the stratum corneum, creating a characteristic "checkerboard pattern"

Folliculotropic features: Follicular infundibular plugging with shoulder parakeratosis surrounding hair follicular ostia; broad suprapapillary plates and thick hypergranulosis without significant epidermotropism
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual papulosquamous disease entity featuring unmistakable clinical images (orange-red erythroderma with islands of normal skin, nutmeg-grater dorsal finger papules, and waxy palmoplantar keratoderma) confirmed by checkerboard parakeratosis on histology.

Dermatology.name: Erythema Multiforme Major
clinical_manifestations: Abrupt onset of pathognomonic symmetric three-concentric-zone "target" or "iris" lesions: dark dusky purpuric or vesicular center, surrounding pale edematous intermediate zone, and an outer sharply defined erythematous halo
Acral and extensor predilection: initial appearance on the dorsa of hands, feet, palms, soles, forearms, and shins, spreading centripetally to limbs and trunk

Severe painful mucosal erosions involving at least one mucosal site (most commonly vermilion border of the lips and oral labial mucosa) with hemorrhagic lip crusting, shallow oral aphthoid erosions, and pseudomembrane formation

Ocular and genital mucosal involvement: bilateral non-purulent conjunctival injection, chemosis, and painful genital erosions (frequently triggered by recurrent Herpes simplex virus infection or Mycoplasma pneumoniae)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution Chest CT: Indicated when triggered by Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection, demonstrating patchy reticular-nodular interstitial opacities or ground-glass bronchointerstitial infiltrates
Slit Lamp Biomicroscopy: Direct visualization of tarsal and bulbar conjunctival erosions, pseudomembranes, and punctate corneal epithelial erosions
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy: Prototypic cytotoxic cell-mediated interface dermatitis characterized by hydropic degenerating basal keratinocytes and necrotic apoptotic individual keratinocytes (Civatte bodies) throughout the stratum spinosum

Subepidermal separation: Dermal-epidermal detachment leading to subepidermal clefting with papillary dermal edema and dense perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate; direct immunofluorescence is negative for intercellular or basement membrane immune complexes
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield dermatologic disease defined by unmistakable physical clinical photographs of concentric three-zone target iris lesions on the palms and soles and bloody crusted lip erosions.

Dermatology.name: Epidermodysplasia Verruciformis
clinical_manifestations: Lifelong genetic vulnerability to beta-human papillomavirus (beta-HPV, especially types 5 and 8) presenting in early childhood with widespread, polymorphic verrucous and lichenoid cutaneous eruptions
Multiple flat, smooth-topped, flesh-colored, pink, or light-brown papules resembling flat warts (verruca plana) on the dorsa of hands, fingers, forehead, neck, and forearms
Large confluent reddish-brown, pink, or hypopigmented macules and plaques with fine scale resembling tinea versicolor (pityriasis versicolor-like lesions) on the trunk, abdomen, and limbs

Extremely high malignant transformation rate: 30-60% of patients develop multiple primary actinic keratoses, Bowenoid carcinoma in situ, and invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas (cutaneous SCC) starting in the third to fourth decade, strictly concentrated on sun-exposed head, neck, and hands
radiological_manifestations: Cutaneous High-Resolution Ultrasound: Measurement of tumor thickness, depth of invasion, and dermal penetration of transformation lesions into subcutaneous fat
Head and Neck CT / MRI: Staging of metastatic or deeply invasive squamous cell carcinomas, delineating cortical bone erosion of the calvarium or facial skeleton and cervical nodal metastasis
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Cytopathic Effect): Marked epidermal acanthosis with swollen, enlarged keratinocytes in the granular and upper spinous layers possessing pathognomonic pale blue-gray or slate-colored cytoplasm and clear perinuclear halos

Nuclear alterations: Large, round, hyperchromatic or pyknotic nuclei with clumped chromatin; electron microscopy and in situ hybridization confirm intranuclear crystalline arrays of beta-HPV viral particles

Molecular Genetics: Inactivating biallelic mutations in EVER1 (TMC6) or EVER2 (TMC8) genes leading to impaired intracellular zinc homeostasis and selective inability of cutaneous keratinocytes to restrict beta-papillomaviruses
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic genodermatosis with indelible clinical photographs of extensive flat-wart plaques, pityriasis-like trunk macules, and hyperkeratotic cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas, verified by pathognomonic swollen blue-gray keratinocytes on biopsy.

Dermatology.name: Granuloma Faciale
clinical_manifestations: Solitary or multiple smooth, soft-to-firm, asymptomatic, well-circumscribed plaques, nodules, or macules measuring 1 to 5 cm, localized almost exclusively to the face (bridge of the nose, malar eminences, cheeks, and forehead)
Distinctive coloration ranging from reddish-brown to violaceous, purplish, or bronze, often with an oily or glistening sheen
Accentuated, prominent, gaping follicular orifices giving the surface an "orange-peel" (peau d'orange) appearance, studded with fine arborizing superficial telangiectasias
Absence of ulceration or epidermal atrophy; lesions run a chronic, persistent, relapsing course without spontaneous involution
radiological_manifestations: Facial Soft-Tissue MRI / Ultrasound: Well-demarcated dermal soft-tissue thickening confined strictly to the cutaneous compartment, without invasion into underlying facial musculature, cartilaginous nasal framework, or periosteum
Dermoscopy: Pinkish-red homogeneous background with prominent linear branching vessels and conspicuous white follicular circles surrounded by halo-like follicular sparing
pathology_manifestations: Skin Biopsy (Pathognomonic Grenz Zone): Unmistakable subepidermal "Grenz zone"—a distinct band of uninvolved, completely normal collagen in the upper papillary dermis separating the flattened epidermis from the dense inflammatory infiltrate beneath

Dense polymorphous dermal infiltrate: Massive infiltration of the mid and deep reticular dermis composed of an intimate mixture of abundant eosinophils, neutrophils with prominent leukocytoclasia (nuclear dust), lymphocytes, histiocytes, and plasma cells

Periadnexal sparing: The dense infiltrate completely surrounds but spares hair follicles and eccrine sweat ducts; vascular endothelial swelling with extravasated erythrocytes and hemosiderin deposition without true fibrinoid necrosis of blood vessel walls
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Visually classic facial dermatologic disease featuring soft violaceous plaques with accentuated follicular openings (peau d'orange) on the nose and cheeks, diagnosed by the pathognomonic subepidermal Grenz zone and eosinophil-rich infiltrate on biopsy.

Dermatology.name: Pityriasis Lichenoides et Varioliformis Acuta
clinical_manifestations: Abrupt, recurrent crops of polymorphic cutaneous lesions erupting in symmetric waves over the trunk, flexural extremities, and proximal limbs
Rapid morphological evolution of lesions: initial discrete erythematous macules and edematous papules evolving into central vesicles, hemorrhagic pustules, and dark necrotic crusted ulcers
Pathognomonic healing phase: lesions resolve leaving depressed, varioliform ("chickenpox-like") pitted atrophic scars accompanied by post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation

Constitutional symptoms: low-grade fever, malaise, burning or pruritus; severe cases can progress to febrile ulceronecrotic Mucha-Habermann disease (FUMHD) with confluent necrotizing ulcers and septic-like systemic collapse
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Skin Ultrasound: Acoustic demarcation of epidermal necrosis, intraepidermal fluid collections, and dermal edema beneath active necrotic eschars
Abdominal / Chest CT (in severe FUMHD variant): Evaluation of hepatosplenomegaly, interstitial pneumonitis, and systemic lymphadenopathy
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Wedge-Shaped Infiltrate): Dense, wedge-shaped (V-shaped) perivascular and interstitial lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with the base at the dermal-epidermal junction and apex in the deep reticular dermis
Epidermal Necrosis & Interface Changes: Extensive vacuolar interface alteration with prominent confluent keratinocyte necrosis, dyskeratosis, and ballooning degeneration

Vascular and RBC findings: Extensive extravasation of red blood cells throughout the dermis and extending up into the necrotic stratum corneum; CD8+ T-cell predominant clonal infiltrate with endothelial swelling without true necrotizing vasculitis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield distinct clinical disease with unmistakable polymorphic photographs (crops of papulonecrotic lesions, black hemorrhagic crusts, and varioliform pox-like scars) and pathognomonic wedge-shaped lymphocytic histology.

Dermatology.name: Keratoacanthoma
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly growing, solitary, symmetric, dome-shaped cutaneous nodule appearing on sun-exposed skin (face, nose, cheeks, dorsum of hands, and forearms) in middle-aged and elderly individuals

Pathognomonic crateriform "volcano-like" silhouette: elevated, smooth, firm, flesh-colored to erythematous rolled border surrounding a prominent central crater packed with a hard, dark-brown or yellow, hyperkeratotic horn plug

Distinct triphasic biological progression: rapid growth phase over 4 to 8 weeks, static plateau phase lasting 2 to 8 weeks, followed in classic cases by spontaneous involution over 6 months leaving a depressed puckered scar (or persistent aggressive malignant behavior)
Clinical differentiation from nodular BCC/SCC: explosive growth velocity (growing from a tiny macule to 1-2.5 cm within weeks) and absence of central bleeding or ulcerated floor
radiological_manifestations: Dermoscopy: Central amorphous yellowish-white or brownish keratin mass surrounded by a peripheral white collar and radial, linear-irregular "hairpin" or "crown" vessels
High-Resolution Cutaneous Ultrasound: Well-circumscribed hypoechoic dermal nodule with a central hyperreflective crateriform cone corresponding to the dense keratin plug
Soft-Tissue MRI: Used for large or giant keratoacanthomas of the central face (nose, lip) to exclude infiltration of facial cartilage or deep muscle compartments
pathology_manifestations: Excisional Biopsy Silhouette (Low-Power Hallmark): Exo-endophytic, symmetric, cup-shaped or crateriform architectural configuration filled with an enormous plug of lamellar parakeratotic and orthokeratotic keratin
Epidermal 'Lip' / Shoulder: Lateral margins of normal epidermis form a distinctive overhanging "lip" or "collar" capping the peripheral borders of the crater

Cytology: Proliferating islands and sheets of highly differentiated squamous epithelium composed of voluminous, glassy, eosinophilic keratinocytes with minimal nuclear pleomorphism, sharp borders, and prominent neutrophil-containing intraepithelial microabscesses
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual cutaneous neoplasm featuring a pathognomonic volcano-shaped clinical photograph (central hyperkeratotic keratin horn plug and rolled border) and a classic cup-shaped low-power histological silhouette.

Dermatology.name: Pemphigus Foliaceus
clinical_manifestations: Superficial autoimmune blistering disease characterized by extremely fragile, superficial, flaccid bullae that rupture almost immediately upon formation, rarely seen intact by examiners
Striking clinical picture of widespread, shallow, erythematous erosions covered by greasy, scaly, cornflake-like adherent crusts ("cornflake sign")

Predilection for seborrheic anatomical zones: initial appearance on the face (often in a malar "butterfly" distribution), scalp, upper chest, and interscapular back, progressing to generalized exfoliative erythroderma
Positive Nikolsky sign: gentle lateral shearing friction on perilesional normal skin induces instant superficial epidermal detachment

Strict absence of mucosal lesions: oral cavity, pharynx, and genital mucosal membranes are completely spared (unlike Pemphigus vulgaris), reflecting tissue distribution of desmoglein 1 versus desmoglein 3
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound: Subcorneal micro-cleavages and intraepidermal acoustic disorganization confined to the superficial upper third of the epidermis, contrasting with deep suprabasal detachment in pemphigus vulgaris
Dermoscopy: Yellowish greasy scales, circular white scaling collarettes, and linear-irregular vessels on an erythematous base
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Clefting Level): Subcorneal or intragranular acantholysis resulting in a cleft situated immediately beneath the stratum corneum or within the granular cell layer; individual detached rounded acantholytic keratinocytes float within the subcorneal space

Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF - Diagnostic Standard): Deposition of IgG (specifically IgG4 subclass) and complement C3 in an intercellular, honeycomb, or "chicken-wire" net pattern restricted strictly to the upper superficial spinous and granular layers of the epidermis
Serology (ELISA): High circulating titers of autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 (anti-Dsg1 IgG), with negative anti-desmoglein 3 (anti-Dsg3) titers
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic autoimmune bullous disease presenting with unique physical examination images (greasy cornflake-like crusts on seborrheic areas with complete mucosal sparing) and pathognomonic subcorneal acantholysis on DIF.

Dermatology.name: Erythema Annulare Centrifugum
clinical_manifestations: Prototypic reactive figurate erythema presenting with slowly expanding annular, arcuate, polycyclic, or circinate erythematous plaques that advance outward at 2 to 5 mm per day with central clearing
Pathognomonic "trailing scale" (in the superficial form): a fine, delicate collarette of scale situated along the inner margin of the advancing indurated erythematous border, behind the leading edge
Deep variant presentation: firm, non-scaly, cord-like elevated erythematous border with a smooth surface and central hyperpigmentation or clearing
Predilection for the trunk, buttocks, hips, and thighs, typically sparing the face, palms, and soles; lesions can coalesce into vast intricate polycyclic, festooned, or "wood-grain" patterns
Chronic relapsing course triggered by dermatophyte infections (tinea pedis), candidiasis, arthropod bites, medications, or occult hematologic/solid malignancies
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / Abdominal Ultrasound: Used as part of the systemic clinical workup to exclude occult pulmonary infections, sarcoidosis, or intra-abdominal neoplasms in refractory elderly presentations
Dermoscopy: Delicate inner collarette of white scale clinging to the internal border of the erythematous ring with dotted or linear irregular vessels
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic "Coat-Sleeve" Pattern): Tight, dense, sharply demarcated lymphohistiocytic infiltrate concentrated around blood vessels in the upper and middle dermis, producing a classic "coat-sleeve" perivascular cuffing appearance
Epidermal alterations (Superficial Form): Focal spongiosis, parakeratosis coinciding with the trailing scale, and mild basilar vacuolization without significant individual necrotic keratinocytes
Absence of true vasculitis: Vascular lumens remain patent, and there is an absence of fibrinoid necrosis, leukocytoclasia, or vascular thrombosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic figurate dermatologic disease displaying unmistakable clinical photographs (expanding polycyclic rings with a pathognomonic trailing scale) and distinctive 'coat-sleeve' perivascular lymphocytic cuffs on histology.

Dermatology.name: Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma / Tufted Angioma
clinical_manifestations: Indurated, bruise-like violaceous cutaneous-subcutaneous plaque, often retroperitoneal or truncal, in an infant
Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon: profound thrombocytopenic consumptive coagulopathy over the lesion
Tufted angioma is the smaller superficial counterpart on the same spectrum
radiological_manifestations: MRI: infiltrative T2-hyperintense enhancing mass crossing tissue planes with cutaneous thickening and stranding
pathology_manifestations: Spindle-cell nodules with slit-like vessels and platelet microthrombi; D2-40/LYVE-1 lymphatic markers positive; GLUT1 negative (unlike infantile hemangioma)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Photographable vascular tumor biologically distinct from covered infantile hemangioma and defined by Kasabach-Merritt coagulopathy.

Dermatology.name: PHACE Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Large (>5 cm) segmental, plaque-like infantile hemangioma of the face (S1-S4 dermatomal zones)
Sternal defect or supraumbilical raphe
Posterior-fossa malformations, arterial cerebrovascular anomalies, cardiac anomalies/coarctation, and eye anomalies complete the acronym
radiological_manifestations: MR angiography of head and neck: arterial agenesis, hypoplasia, or anomalous course supplying the hemangioma region; brain MRI: Dandy-Walker-type posterior fossa anomalies; echocardiography: coarctation
pathology_manifestations: GLUT1-positive segmental infantile hemangioma with extracutaneous regional anomalies; postzygotic developmental field defect
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The infantile-hemangioma topic references PHACE workup but does not cover this multisystem syndrome-level entity.

Dermatology.name: Harlequin Ichthyosis
clinical_manifestations: Armor-plate large polygonal scales separated by deep red fissures at birth
Severe ectropion, eclabium, rudimentary ear/nose development, and flexion contractures
Highest mortality of the congenital ichthyoses; survivors have severe persistent ichthyosis
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; the neonatal external phenotype is the image
pathology_manifestations: Massively thickened compact stratum corneum; ABCA12 mutations (lamellar granule lipid-transport defect)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct severe ABCA12 phenotype kept as its own topic per open question - the armor-plate neonatal image is unmistakable.

Dermatology.name: Netherton Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Ichthyosis linearis circumflexa: polycyclic erythematous plaques with a characteristic double-edged scale
Trichorrhexis invaginata ('bamboo hair') on hair-shaft microscopy - pathognomonic
Brittle sparse hair, high IgE, and atopic diathesis
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Loss of LEKTI (SPINK5) causing unrestricted epidermal protease activity and premature corneodesmosome degradation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Bamboo-hair microscopy is a pathognomonic sign; the circumflexa phenotype is distinct from covered ichthyoses.

Dermatology.name: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
clinical_manifestations: Periorificial exuberant granulation-tissue plaques around nose, lips, and ears - a hallmark
Nail shedding and dystrophy, dental enamel hypoplasia, and laryngeal stridor
Nonhealing erosions healing with atrophy but without the milia of dystrophic EB
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Cleavage within the lamina lucida; mutations in laminin-332 chains (LAMA3/B3/C2), type XVII collagen, or integrins; absent staining on IF mapping
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct cleavage plane and periorificial granulation phenotype versus covered dystrophic EB.

Dermatology.name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
clinical_manifestations: Trauma-induced superficial blisters and erosions that heal without scarring or milia
Herpetiform (Dowling-Meara) variant: grouped vesicles on the trunk with marked palmoplantar involvement
Worsening with heat and sweating; onset at birth or early childhood
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Intraepidermal basal-cell cytolysis; mutations in KRT5/KRT14 (clumped keratin tonofilaments in Dowling-Meara on EM)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Basal-layer split distinct from the covered dystrophic form; trauma-induced non-scarring acral blistering.

Dermatology.name: Kindler Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Acral blistering in infancy that improves with age
Progressive diffuse poikiloderma with skin atrophy and photosensitivity
Gingival fragility and mucosal involvement
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: FERMT1 (kindlin-1) loss; unique among EBs for multiple simultaneous cleavage planes (intraepidermal, junctional, subepidermal) and reduplicated lamina densa
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Only EB with mixed cleavage planes plus the unusual blister-to-poikiloderma evolution.

Dermatology.name: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
clinical_manifestations: Annular and arciform plaques with peripheral vesicles arranged as 'string of pearls' or 'crown of jewels'
Childhood-onset form affects lower trunk and genital/perineal skin; adult form is polymorphic
Mucosal involvement including conjunctival in some cases
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Direct immunofluorescence: linear IgA deposition along the basement membrane zone (LABD97/LAD-1 antigen)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The string-of-pearl blister arrangement plus linear-IgA DIF is disease-specific.

Dermatology.name: Rothmund-Thomson Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Infantile poikiloderma starting on cheeks and spreading to extensor limbs and buttocks
Sparse hair, small stature, and radial-ray (thumb/radius) defects
Osteosarcoma predisposition and juvenile cataracts
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: radial-ray hypoplasia and osteopenia; plain films for osteosarcoma surveillance
pathology_manifestations: RECQL4 helicase mutation; poikiloderma histology (atrophy, telangiectasia, pigment incontinence)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Fills the poikiloderma/DNA-repair gap with distinct infantile poikiloderma plus radial defects.

Dermatology.name: Hypohidrotic Ectodermal Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Frontal bossing, depressed (saddle) nasal bridge, everted lips, and periorbital wrinkling/hyperpigmentation
Sparse fine blonde hair, absent sweating (hypohidrosis) with heat intolerance
Hypodontia with conical 'peg' teeth on examination
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic dental film: multiple missing teeth and peg-shaped incisors - diagnostic composite with the facies
pathology_manifestations: EDA/EDAR/EDARADD pathway mutation; absent or hypoplastic eccrine glands on skin biopsy
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic composite facies plus pathognomonic dental film findings.

Dermatology.name: Piebaldism
clinical_manifestations: White forelock (poliosis) present from birth
Symmetric leukoderma of forehead, anterior trunk, and limbs with characteristic islands of normal or hyperpigmented skin within depigmented areas
Stable lifelong patches without progression
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: KIT proto-oncogene mutation; absence of melanocytes in depigmented skin (vs. autoimmune destruction in vitiligo)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: White forelock plus leukoderma-with-islands is an instantly recognizable hereditary pigmentary phenotype.

Dermatology.name: Oculocutaneous Albinism
clinical_manifestations: Diffuse skin, hair, and iris hypopigmentation ranging from white (OCA1A) to sandy-brown (OCA2)
Iris transillumination, nystagmus, and reduced acuity
Increased skin-cancer susceptibility
radiological_manifestations: Fundus/OCT: hypopigmented fundus with absent foveal pigmentation and foveal hypoplasia on OCT - a diagnostic combination
pathology_manifestations: Tyrosinase-pathway mutations (TYR, OCA2, TYRP1, SLC45A2, and others); reduced/absent melanin in melanocytes
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Full-body hypopigmentation photographs plus iris transillumination and foveal hypoplasia imagery; Hermansky-Pudlak is a covered subtype but OCA itself is absent.

Dermatology.name: Brooke-Spiegler Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Multiple dome-shaped scalp cylindromas that can coalesce into a 'turban tumor'
Trichoepitheliomas clustering in the nasolabial folds
Spiradenomas adding painful nodules to the phenotype
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Cylindroma histology: dermal tumor islands fitting together in a 'jigsaw-puzzle' pattern with hyaline sheaths; CYLD tumor-suppressor mutation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Turban-tumor scalp photographs plus pathognomonic jigsaw-puzzle histology.

Dermatology.name: Pachyonychia Congenita
clinical_manifestations: Massive wedge-shaped subungual hyperkeratosis of all twenty nails - pathognomonic
Focal palmoplantar keratoderma that can be crippling
Oral leukokeratosis and follicular keratosis in subtypes
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Keratin mutations (KRT6A/B, KRT16, KRT17) disrupting nail-matrix cytoskeleton; pilonidal cysts in some subtypes
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The 20-nail wedge-shaped hypertrophy photograph is unmistakable.

Dermatology.name: Erythropoietic Protoporphyria
clinical_manifestations: Immediate painful burning photosensitivity without blistering (non-scarring vs. PCT)
Waxy thickened lichenified skin over knuckles and nose with pitted 'pseudo-rhagades' scars
Gallstones and occasional liver disease from protoporphyrin accumulation
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; hepatic imaging when indicated
pathology_manifestations: FECH deficiency accumulating protoporphyrin IX; Maltese-cross birefringence of RBC protoporphyrin on polarized microscopy; perivascular hyaline deposits in skin
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct painful-nonblistering photosensitivity with waxy knuckle scars; separate disease from covered PCT.

Dermatology.name: Bloom Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Photosensitive telangiectatic malar erythema in a butterfly distribution
Proportionate severe short stature with dolichocephaly and prominent ears/nose
Café-au-lait spots and predisposition to early cancers
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: BLM helicase mutation; dramatically elevated sister-chromatid exchange rate on cytogenetic assay (pathognomonic laboratory image)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: RECQ-defect telangiectatic malar erythema alongside covered XP and Cockayne.

Dermatology.name: Focal Dermal Hypoplasia (Goltz Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Blaschko-linear atrophic streaks and cribriform atrophy with soft yellow fat-herniation nodules
Periorificial and genital papillomas
Digital anomalies: syndactyly, lobster-claw deformity, absent rays; eye colobomas
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal radiographs: osteopathia striata - parallel longitudinal bony striations pathognomonic in this context
pathology_manifestations: X-linked dominant PORCN mutation (Wnt-signaling defect); dermis almost absent in streaks with fat herniating to the epidermis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Streaky atrophy plus fat-herniation photos and pathognomonic osteopathia striata.

Dermatology.name: Papillon-Lefèvre Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Sharply demarcated transgradient palmoplantar keratoderma spreading onto dorsal surfaces
Aggressive premature periodontitis destroying deciduous then permanent dentition
Hyperhidrosis and recurrent cutaneous infections
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic dental radiograph: severe alveolar bone loss producing 'floating teeth' appearance
pathology_manifestations: Cathepsin C (CTSC) loss-of-function; periodontal pathogens trigger unchecked inflammation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The floating-teeth radiograph plus transgradient PPK is a classic composite.

Dermatology.name: Vohwinkel Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Diffuse honeycomb-pattern palmoplantar keratoderma
Starfish-shaped hyperkeratoses on dorsal hands, elbows, and knees
Pseudoainhum constricting bands auto-amputating digits; associated sensorineural deafness
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: GJB2 (connexin-26) mutation in the classic variant; loricrin mutation in variant II with ichthyosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Honeycomb PPK plus starfish keratoses and auto-amputating bands are iconic photographs.

Dermatology.name: KID Syndrome (Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness)
clinical_manifestations: Erythematous, leather-grain or stippled hyperkeratotic plaques on face, scalp, palms, and soles
Progressive vascularizing keratitis causing photophobia and vision loss
Congenital profound sensorineural deafness; alopecia and nail dystrophy
radiological_manifestations: Slit-lamp: corneal neovascularization and keratitis over ichthyotic lid skin
pathology_manifestations: GJB2 (connexin-26) gain-of-function mutation; risk of squamous-cell carcinoma in keratotic plaques
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The keratitis-plus-plaque-plus-deafness triad is a distinct photographable genodermatosis.

Dermatology.name: Conradi-Hünermann-Happle Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Blaschko-linear ichthyosiform erythroderma in a newborn resolving into follicular atrophoderma (pitted 'orange-peel' scars)
Cicatricial alopecia and coarse lusterless hair
Asymmetric limb shortening and congenital cataracts
radiological_manifestations: Neonatal skeletal survey: stippled epiphyseal calcification (chondrodysplasia punctata); sectorial cataract on slit-lamp
pathology_manifestations: X-linked dominant EBP (sterol-8-isomerase) mutation; elevated 8(9)-cholestenol; males usually lethal
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Blaschko-linear ichthyosis evolving to atrophoderma plus stippled epiphyses - dual signature.

Dermatology.name: Trichothiodystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Brittle, sparse, easily broken hair of the scalp, eyebrows, and lashes
Photosensitivity in the nucleotide-excision-repair forms; ichthyosis in subsets
Recumbent-I phenotypes (PIBIDS): photosensitivity, ichthyosis, brittle hair, impaired intelligence, decreased fertility, short stature
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Polarized microscopy of the hair shaft: alternating light-dark 'tiger-tail' banding - pathognomonic; XPD/XPB/TTDA helicase defects reduce hair-sulfur content
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Tiger-tail polarized hair banding is a pathognomonic microscopic image.

Dermatology.name: Sjögren-Larsson Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Ichthyosis with characteristic sparing of the central face, giving a 'clean-face' look
Spastic diplegia and mild-moderate intellectual disability
Glistening white dots around the fovea on fundoscopy - a pathognomonic retinal sign
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: periventricular white-matter signal and delayed myelination; fundus photograph shows the glistening foveal dots
pathology_manifestations: Fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH3A2) deficiency; accumulation of fatty alcohols in skin and CNS
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The glistening foveal-dot fundus plus clean-face ichthyosis is a distinctive composite.

Dermatology.name: Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome (Schimmelpenning)
clinical_manifestations: Linear or whorled yellow-orange sebaceous nevus on scalp or face along Blaschko lines
Alopecic verrucous plaque that thickens at puberty
Ocular colobomas, lid tags, and seizures with hemimegalencephaly in syndromic form
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: hemimegalencephaly or other CNS malformations in Schimmelpenning syndrome
pathology_manifestations: Postzygotic mosaic HRAS/KRAS RASopathy; sebaceous-gland hyperplasia; secondary tumors (trichoblastoma, syringocystadenoma papilliferum) can arise within
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Linear sebaceous nevus plus ocular/CNS anomalies - the RASopathy mosaic neurocutaneous syndrome.

Dermatology.name: Pemphigoid Gestationis
clinical_manifestations: Periumbilical urticarial papules and plaques in the second or third trimester
Tense bullae spreading to trunk and extremities
Frequent postpartum flare
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Direct immunofluorescence: linear C3 (and often IgG) along the basement membrane zone; anti-BP180 (BPAG2) autoantibodies
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Defined pregnancy dermatosis with periumbilical onset and linear-C3 DIF.

Dermatology.name: Porokeratosis
clinical_manifestations: Annular plaques with a sharply raised, hyperkeratotic peripheral ridge (cornoid lamella) and atrophic center
Variants: plaque of Mibelli (large solitary), DSAP (multiple small photoexposed), linear (Blaschko)
Small squamous-cell-carcinoma risk within plaques
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Histology: cornoid lamella - a column of parakeratosis over a shallow epidermal depression with absent granular layer; dermoscopy shows the 'volcanic' ridge
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Cornoid-lamella ridge is pathognomonic on both histology and dermoscopy.

Dermatology.name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
clinical_manifestations: Trauma-induced blisters on extensor hands, knuckles, elbows, and knees healing with scarring and milia (mechanobullous type, mimicking dystrophic EB)
Inflammatory variant resembling bullous pemphigoid
Nail dystrophy and mucosal erosions
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: IgG antibodies to type VII collagen; salt-split skin DIF localizes IgG to the dermal (floor) side, distinguishing it from BP (roof)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Acquired mechanobullous disease with disease-specific salt-split-skin immunofluorescence.

Dermatology.name: X-Linked Recessive Ichthyosis
clinical_manifestations: Large, dark-brown 'dirty' scales of the trunk and neck characteristically sparing the flexures
Comma-shaped corneal deposits on slit-lamp (asymptomatic) in carriers and patients
Prolonged maternal labor from placental sulfatase deficiency; cryptorchidism association
radiological_manifestations: Slit-lamp: comma-shaped deep stromal corneal opacities - the disease-specific ocular sign
pathology_manifestations: STS gene deletion/mutation; stratum-corneum retention from cholesterol-sulfate accumulation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Dark-scaling with flexure sparing plus pathognomonic comma corneal deposits.

Dermatology.name: HLRCC Syndrome (Reed Syndrome)
synonyms: hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer
clinical_manifestations: Multiple firm, often painful cutaneous piloleiomyomas in clustered or segmental distribution
Early-onset uterine fibroids (women) and aggressive type-2 papillary renal-cell carcinoma predisposition
Cold and touch-induced pain over lesions is typical
radiological_manifestations: Renal imaging (CT/MRI) for associated papillary renal-cell carcinoma surveillance
pathology_manifestations: Fumarate hydratase (FH) mutation; leiomyomas with eosinophilic nucleoli; SDHB-negative papillary renal tumors
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Painful piloleiomyoma photographs define a distinct hereditary tumor-predisposition dermatosis.

Dermatology.name: Olmsted Syndrome
synonyms: mutilating palmoplantar keratoderma with periorificial plaques
clinical_manifestations: Progressive mutilating transgradient palmoplantar keratoderma causing flexion contractures and digital auto-amputation
Symmetric periorificial (mouth, nose, perianal) hyperkeratotic plaques
Nail dystrophy, alopecia, and joint laxity
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: TRPV3 gain-of-function (commonest) or TP63 mutation; massive orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The mutilating PPK-plus-periorificial-plaque phenotype is uniquely photographable.

Dermatology.name: AEC Syndrome (Hay-Wells Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Ankyloblepharon filiforme: fine strands of tissue connecting upper and lower eyelids
Severe chronic erosive scalp dermatitis and granulation tissue
Cleft lip/palate plus ectodermal defects (sparse wiry hair, nail dystrophy, hypodontia, hypohidrosis)
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: TP63 (sterile-alpha-motif domain) mutations distinct from EEC mutations; ectodermal-layer developmental disruption
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Ankyloblepharon strands plus erosive scalp dermatitis are pathognomonic photographs.

Dermatology.name: Hidrotic Ectodermal Dysplasia (Clouston Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma over pressure points
Thickened, brittle, discolored nails often partially lost
Sparse, brittle hair that may progress to near-total alopecia; normal sweating (unlike HED)
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: GJB6 (connexin-30) mutation; sweat-gland function preserved - the 'hidrotic' distinction from HED
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Nail dystrophy plus PPK plus sparse hair with preserved sweating is a distinct ED composite.

Dermatology.name: Griscelli Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Silvery metallic sheen to the hair with pale skin
Pigment clumps visible as irregular melanin aggregates on hair-shaft microscopy
Neurologic (type 1, MYO5A) or immunodeficiency/hemophagocytic (type 2, RAB27A) features depending on subtype
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Hair-shaft microscopy: large irregular melanin clumps (vs. small even distribution of Chédiak-Higashi); melanosome-transport GTPase defects
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Silvery-hair photograph plus pathognomonic shaft pigment clumping - distinct from covered Chédiak-Higashi.

Dermatology.name: Dowling-Degos Disease
clinical_manifestations: Reticulate (net-like) hyperpigmentation of the axillae, groin, and other flexures
Pitted perioral scars and comedo-like lesions on the face
Hyperpigmented macules that slowly enlarge in adulthood
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: KRT5/POGLUT1/POFUT1 mutations; elongated branched rete ridges with melanin incontinence
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct flexural reticulate pigmentary genodermatosis.

Dermatology.name: Cutis Marmorata Telangiectatica Congenita
clinical_manifestations: Persistent reticulate violaceous livedo present at birth that does not fully resolve with warming
Localized ulceration, atrophy, or telangiectasia over the mottled skin
Possible limb asymmetry and associated glaucoma or macrocephaly-capillary-malformation overlap
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Dilated capillaries and venules in the reticular dermis; sporadic developmental vascular defect
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Persistent congenital livedo with ulceration is a distinct neonatal photographic entity.

Dermatology.name: Juvenile Xanthogranuloma
clinical_manifestations: Firm yellow-orange to red-brown papules/nodules on the head, neck, and upper trunk of infants
Iris lesions causing spontaneous hyphema and glaucoma in the ocular form
Spontaneous regression over several years leaving atrophy
radiological_manifestations: Ocular ultrasound/UBM for iris masses; no external radiologic signature
pathology_manifestations: Non-Langerhans-cell histiocytes with pathognomonic Touton giant cells (ring of nuclei with foamy rim); CD68+, CD1a-
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Touton-giant-cell histology plus classic yellow-orange infantile nodules.

Dermatology.name: Steatocystoma Multiplex
clinical_manifestations: Multiple small, movable dermal cysts on the trunk and proximal limbs that exude oily fluid when incised
Eruptive onset at puberty
Occasionally associated with pachyonychia-congenita-type nail changes in the KRT17 family
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Dermal cysts with folded keratinizing lining incorporating sebaceous lobules; KRT17 mutation in familial cases
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct eruptive dermal-cyst phenotype on clinical photography.

Dermatology.name: Primary Cutaneous Amyloidosis (Lichen and Macular)
clinical_manifestations: Intensely pruritic grouped hyperkeratotic papules on the shins (lichen amyloidosis)
Rippled 'salt-and-pepper' hyperpigmented macules on the upper back and arms (macular amyloidosis)
Notalgia-paresthetica-associated variants
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Amyloid (cytokeratin-derived, AA-negative) deposits in the papillary dermis showing Congo-red apple-green birefringence
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Rippled flexural hyperpigmentation and pruritic papules with amyloid histology - not captured by covered cardiac amyloidosis.

Dermatology.name: Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans
clinical_manifestations: Indurated, slow-growing violaceous plaque that eventually forms protuberant nodules, typically on the trunk or shoulders
Pseudopod-like infiltration that belies the deceptively small surface
Pigmented Bednar variant
radiological_manifestations: MRI for deep-infiltration extent when planning excision; no pathognomonic imaging
pathology_manifestations: Monomorphic spindle-cell storiform infiltrate honeycombing subcutaneous fat; CD34 strongly positive; COL1A1-PDGFB fusion
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct protuberant sarcoma entity with characteristic photographic and histologic features.

Dermatology.name: Angiolymphoid Hyperplasia with Eosinophilia
clinical_manifestations: Dusky-red, pruritic or pulsatile nodules on the scalp and periauricular skin
Peripheral eosinophilia in a subset
Recurrent after treatment
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Vascular proliferation lined by plump 'hobnail' epithelioid endothelium with dense eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct photographic scalp/ear nodule entity with characteristic eosinophil-rich histology.

Dermatology.name: Dissecting Cellulitis of the Scalp
clinical_manifestations: Interconnecting boggy abscesses and sinus tracts of the scalp that drain seropurulent fluid on pressure
Patchy cicatricial alopecia and keloidal scarring
Part of the follicular-occlusion tetrad (with hidradenitis, acne conglobata, pilonidal disease)
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Neutrophilic follicular destruction with sinus-tract formation; culture is secondary - a primary scarring disorder
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct interconnecting-abscess scalp phenotype photographically recognizable.

Dermatology.name: Paget Disease of the Breast and Extramammary Paget Disease
clinical_manifestations: Sharply demarcated eczematous, scaling or crusted plaque of the nipple-areola (mammary Paget)
Analogous 'eczema' that resists steroid treatment in vulvar or perianal skin (extramammary Paget)
Underlying ductal carcinoma in mammary disease
radiological_manifestations: Mammography/MRI for the underlying ductal carcinoma; no skin-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Paget cells - large clear adenocarcinoma cells with mucin - infiltrating the epidermis in pagetoid spread; CK7+/GCDFP-15+
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic eczematous nipple/perineal plaques plus pagetoid-cell histology.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Angiosarcoma
clinical_manifestations: Bruise-like, infiltrative violaceous plaques and nodules on the scalp and face of elderly patients
Stewart-Treves variant: angiosarcoma arising in chronic lymphedema (post-mastectomy arm)
Rapid centrifugal spread and hemorrhagic nodules
radiological_manifestations: MRI: enhancing infiltrative scalp/soft-tissue mass; chest CT for early pulmonary metastases
pathology_manifestations: Anastomosing atypical vascular channels infiltrating collagen; CD31+/ERG+; MYC amplification in radiation-associated cases
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Bruise-like scalp plaques in the elderly are pathognomonic photography; Stewart-Treves folded in as synonym.

Dermatology.name: Acne Vulgaris
clinical_manifestations: Open and closed comedones with inflammatory papules, pustules, and nodules on the face, chest, and back
Postinflammatory hyperpigmentation and scarring sequelae
Grading from comedonal to nodulocystic on photography
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Follicular plugging with Cutibacterium acnes proliferation and perifollicular inflammation; ruptured comedones incite foreign-body granulomas
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Highest-prevalence photographic dermatosis; the catalog includes other common diseases (lichen planus, vitiligo, psoriasis).

Dermatology.name: Rosacea
clinical_manifestations: Centrofacial flushing and fixed erythema with telangiectasia
Papules and pustules without comedones distinguishing it from acne
Rhinophyma (bulbous sebaceous nasal enlargement) and ocular rosacea blepharitis
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with dilated vessels; Demodex density elevated; rhinophyma shows sebaceous hyperplasia and fibrosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Commonest photographic facial dermatosis after acne; composite erythema-telangiectasia-rhinophyma imagery.

Dermatology.name: Pityriasis Rosea
clinical_manifestations: Solitary herald patch: a larger annular scaly plaque preceding the eruption
Secondary eruption of oval salmon-pink patches aligned along skin cleavage in a 'Christmas-tree' pattern on the back
Collarette (inward-facing) scale on each lesion
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Nonspecific spongiotic dermatitis; probable HHV-6/7 association; syphilis serology when atypical
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Herald patch plus Christmas-tree distribution is a classic named dermatosis photograph.

Dermatology.name: Alopecia Areata
clinical_manifestations: Well-circumscribed round patches of sudden nonscarring hair loss
Exclamation-point hairs (short tapering proximal shafts) at patch margins
Nail pitting and trachyonychia in a subset; ophiasis band pattern at margins
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Peribulbar lymphocytic 'swarm-of-bees' infiltrate attacking anagen follicles; increased catagen/telogen follicles
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Patchy exclamation-point alopecia is a disease-level photographic dermatosis.

Dermatology.name: Seborrheic Dermatitis
clinical_manifestations: Greasy yellow-scale patches on the scalp, eyebrows, nasolabial folds, and ears
Honey-colored cradle cap in infants
Intertriginous and presternal involvement; worse in Parkinson disease and HIV
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Mild spongiotic dermatitis; Malassezia yeast association but not a direct infection
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distribution-limited greasy-scale photographs define a common disease-level dermatosis.

Dermatology.name: Pyogenic Granuloma (Lobular Capillary Hemangioma)
clinical_manifestations: Friable bright-red pedunculated nodule that bleeds on minimal contact
Rapid eruption over days at sites of minor trauma; gingival form in pregnancy (pregnancy tumor)
Band of hyperkeratotic epidermis at the stalk base
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Lobular aggregates of capillaries in an edematous stroma with ulceration; not infectious despite the name
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The bleeding red nodule photograph is instantly recognizable.

Dermatology.name: Epidermal Inclusion Cyst
clinical_manifestations: Firm, skin-colored, freely movable dermal nodule often with a central punctum
Cheesy keratin discharge when expressed or ruptured
Inflamed cysts become tender erythematous swellings
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: well-defined hypoechoic cystic structure with posterior enhancement
pathology_manifestations: Stratified-squamous epithelial cyst wall filled with laminated keratin; foreign-body giant-cell reaction if ruptured
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The punctum-bearing nodule is a classic photographic skin lesion.

Dermatology.name: Dermatofibroma
clinical_manifestations: Firm hyperpigmented papule on legs that dimples inward with lateral pressure (dimple/Fitzpatrick sign)
Fixed to the overlying skin but movable on deeper tissues
Often multiple; post-traumatic or insect-bite origin
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Dermal spindle-cell proliferation overlying epidermal hyperplasia with basal hyperpigmentation; peripheral collagen entrapment
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The dimple-sign lesion is a classic photographic dermatosis.

Dermatology.name: Keloid
clinical_manifestations: Firm, shiny, raised scar tissue that extends beyond the original wound margins (unlike hypertrophic scar)
Predilection for earlobes, shoulders, chest, and jawline in darker skin
Pruritic or painful progressive growth
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Thick, glassy hyalinized collagen ('keloidal collagen') haphazardly arranged in the dermis; fibroblast hyperactivity
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Beyond-the-wound-margin overgrowth is a pathognomonic photographable phenotype.

Dermatology.name: Seborrheic Keratosis
clinical_manifestations: Waxy, 'stuck-on' pigmented papule or plaque with a greasy surface and horn cysts
Multiple lesions on trunk and face in older adults
Sudden eruptive onset (Leser-Trélat) signals internal malignancy
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Acanthotic proliferation of basaloid keratinocytes with intraepidermal horn cysts and pseudo-horn cysts
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The stuck-on waxy plaque is one of the most photographed skin lesions.

Dermatology.name: Spitz Nevus
clinical_manifestations: Dome-shaped, pink to red-brown papule on the face or legs of a child
Rapid growth phase followed by stability
Dermoscopy: starburst (pigmented spindle-cell) or reticular patterns
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Large spindle and epithelioid melanocytes with epidermal clefting; Kamino bodies; low mitotic activity vs. melanoma
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct benign tumor entity photographically and histologically characteristic.

Dermatology.name: Acquired Melanocytic Nevus (Common Mole)
clinical_manifestations: Small symmetric uniform tan-to-brown macules (junctional) or raised papules (compound/intradermal)
Evolution from flat to raised lesions with loss of pigment in intradermal type
Halo depigmentation in halo-nevus variant
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Nests of nevomelanocytes at the dermoepidermal junction (junctional), in dermis (intradermal), or both; benign maturation pattern
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive photographic skin lesion; the commonest pigmented skin entity.

Dermatology.name: Pilomatricoma
clinical_manifestations: Firm, deep-seated dermal nodule on the face, neck, or upper extremities of a child
'Tent sign': faceted surface when stretched; blue-purple tinge over calcified lesions
Sudden inflammation episodes
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: hypoechoic solid-cystic lesion with internal calcification and peripheral rim - characteristic sonographic sign
pathology_manifestations: Basaloid cells differentiating toward hair matrix with 'shadow' (ghost) cells and calcification; beta-catenin mutations
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Calcifying Malherbe nodule is a classic pediatric photographic and sonographic diagnosis.

Dermatology.name: Androgenetic Alopecia
clinical_manifestations: Frontotemporal recession progressing to vertex baldness in the male pattern (Norwood scale)
Diffuse central thinning with preserved frontal hairline in the female pattern (Ludwig scale)
Miniaturized vellus follicles on dermoscopy
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Progressive follicular miniaturization under androgen influence; increased vellus-to-terminal ratio
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Pattern-hair-loss photographs define a highly prevalent disease entity.

Dermatology.name: Keratosis Pilaris
clinical_manifestations: Rough keratotic follicular papules on extensor upper arms, thighs, and buttocks ('chicken skin' texture)
Perifollicular erythema in the rubra variant
Worse in winter and with atopy
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Keratin plugging of follicular openings with mild perifollicular inflammation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Common follicular dermatosis recognizable on extensor-surface photographs.

Dermatology.name: Lichen Simplex Chronicus
clinical_manifestations: Well-demarcated, intensely itchy lichenified plaque with exaggerated skin lines
Classic sites: nape, ankles, forearms, scrotum, vulva
Hyperpigmented and excoriated chronic lesions
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Compact hyperkeratosis and acanthosis with markedly thickened papillary dermal collagen (lichenification)
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The lichenified plaque photograph is a classic itch-scratch-cycle entity.

Dermatology.name: Periorificial Dermatitis
clinical_manifestations: Grouped erythematous papules and pustules clustered around the mouth, nose, and eyes
Characteristic sparing of the skin immediately adjacent to the vermilion border
Flares with topical corticosteroid use and cosmetic application
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Perifollicular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with spongiosis; not an acneiform eruption despite the appearance
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Vermilion-sparing periorificial papule pattern is a recognizable photographic entity.

Dermatology.name: Dyshidrotic Eczema (Pompholyx)
clinical_manifestations: Deep-seated 'tapioca-like' intensely itchy vesicles on palms, soles, and lateral fingers
Recurrent crops followed by desquamation
No primary follicular involvement unlike palmoplantar pustulosis
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Spongiotic intraepidermal vesicles with lymphocytic exocytosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Tapioca-vesicle palmoplantar photographs define a named eczematous entity.

Dermatology.name: Syringoma
clinical_manifestations: Multiple small (1-3 mm) skin-colored to yellowish papules clustered on the lower eyelids
Eruptive form involves trunk and extremities
Predominantly in women; often symmetric
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Comma-shaped epithelial cords ('tadpoles') and small ducts embedded in a sclerotic dermal stroma
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Lower-eyelid papule cluster is a recognizable photographic entity.

Dermatology.name: Lipoma
clinical_manifestations: Soft, doughy, freely movable subcutaneous nodule with normal overlying skin
'Slippage sign' on palpation
Single or multiple; any site but commonest on trunk and limbs
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: well-encapsulated isoechoic/hyperechoic fatty mass; MRI: fat-signal lesion suppressing on fat-sat sequences
pathology_manifestations: Encapsulated mature adipocytes indistinguishable from normal fat; angiolipoma variant has microthrombi and is painful
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The doughy slip-sign subcutaneous nodule is a classic clinical lesion.

Dermatology.name: Trichilemmal (Pilar) Cyst
clinical_manifestations: Firm smooth dome-shaped nodule on the scalp without a punctum
Mobile scalp nodules that shell out at excision
Multiple lesions in familial cases
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: well-defined hypoechoic scalp cyst, often calcified
pathology_manifestations: Trichilemmal keratinization: abrupt keratinization without a granular layer; compact keratin fill with frequent calcification
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Scalp punctum-free cyst is a distinct common photographic lesion.

Dermatology.name: Lymphomatoid Papulosis
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent self-healing crops of papulonecrotic papules and nodules in different stages simultaneously
Lesions erupt, ulcerate, and resolve with varioliform scars over weeks
Indolent chronic course despite malignant cytology
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Wedge-shaped infiltrate with large atypical CD30+ T-cells; histologic types A-E including type-B MF-like infiltrate
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Instantly recognizable mixed-stage papulonecrotic photographs; a defined CD30+ lymphoproliferative disease.

Dermatology.name: Primary Cutaneous B-Cell Lymphoma
clinical_manifestations: Leg-type: rapidly enlarging red-brown tumors on the legs of elderly women
Indolent marginal-zone/follicle-center types: papulonodules on head/neck and trunk
Solitary or clustered violaceous tumors without epidermal change
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; staging imaging for systemic exclusion
pathology_manifestations: Dense dermal infiltrate of B-cells; CD20/BCL6/BCL2 patterns distinguish leg-type from indolent types
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct photographic B-cell tumors separate from covered T-cell lymphomas; umbrella caveat noted.

Dermatology.name: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
clinical_manifestations: 'Bruise-like' solitary or multiple violaceous nodules and plaques as the first presentation (skin in ~85%)
Rapid dissemination to marrow, nodes, and CNS
Elderly patients typically
radiological_manifestations: Staging PET/CT for marrow and nodal involvement
pathology_manifestations: Dermal infiltrate of medium blasts without epidermotropism; CD123+/CD4+/CD56+/TCL1+ signature
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Bruise-like violaceous nodule presentation is a distinctive photographic entity.

Dermatology.name: Hydroa Vacciniforme-Like Lymphoproliferative Disorder
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent vesiculonecrotic facial eruptions healing to vacciniform (smallpox-like) scars in children
Facial swelling and systemic symptoms in severe cases
Photosensitive distribution
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: EBV-infected T/NK-cell infiltration with necrotizing ulcers; clonality distinguishes it from benign HV
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Varioliform-scar facial eruption is a recognized EBV-driven entity; paired with proposed benign HV.

Dermatology.name: Diffuse Normolipemic Plane Xanthoma
clinical_manifestations: Extensive symmetric yellow-orange flat plaques on the neck, upper trunk, and flexures
Periocular, cervical, and flexural predominance
Normal lipid levels (unlike lipid-driven xanthomas)
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Dermal foamy histiocytes; strongly associated with MGUS and multiple myeloma - a paraneoplastic marker
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Same paraneoplastic-dermatosis class as covered necrobiotic xanthogranuloma and scleromyxedema.

Dermatology.name: Infantile Myofibromatosis
clinical_manifestations: Firm, rubbery, violaceous skin and subcutaneous nodules in a neonate
Single or multicentric lesions; systemic (visceral) involvement in severe cases
Spontaneous regression of cutaneous lesions
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: lytic metaphyseal long-bone lesions in multicentric cases; ultrasound of nodules
pathology_manifestations: Myofibroblastic proliferation with biphasic hemangiopericytoma-like areas; PDGFRB mutations in some
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Violaceous neonatal nodules plus lytic metaphyses is a distinct fibromatosis.

Dermatology.name: Juvenile Hyaline Fibromatosis / Infantile Systemic Hyalinosis
clinical_manifestations: Pearly perianal, perinasal, and postauricular papules and nodules
Massive gingival hyperplasia and joint contractures
Systemic form adds infections and early death
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: osteolytic lesions and cortical thinning in the systemic form
pathology_manifestations: ANTXR2 (CMG2) mutation; abundant amorphous hyaline material with fibroblasts in skin and gingiva
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Pearly papules plus gingival overgrowth plus contractures is a named hyalinosis entity.

Dermatology.name: Glomuvenous Malformation
clinical_manifestations: Cobblestone, blue-purple, plaque-like segmental vascular lesions
Tender on palpation unlike venous malformations
Worsens with hormonal changes
radiological_manifestations: MRI: T2-hyperintense plaque-like lesion; ultrasound distinguishes it from hemangioma
pathology_manifestations: Glomus cells lining irregular vascular channels; PLXNA1 mutation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct cobblestone tender blue-purple plaques versus covered BRBNS and infantile hemangioma.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Polyarteritis Nodosa
clinical_manifestations: Livedo racemosa with tender subcutaneous nodules on the legs
Ulcers and digital gangrene in severe cases
Absence of visceral involvement distinguishes it from systemic PAN
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; systemic workup negative by definition
pathology_manifestations: Medium-vessel necrotizing arteritis in the deep dermis/subcutis; fibrinoid necrosis like systemic PAN but skin-limited
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Limited cutaneous entity photographically distinct from covered systemic PAN.

Dermatology.name: Chronic Arsenic Poisoning (Arsenicosis)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic triad: 'raindrop' depigmentation, palmoplantar arsenical keratoses, and Mees white transverse nail lines
Diffuse bronzed hyperpigmentation with hypopigmented spots
