clinical_manifestations: Acute Angioinvasive Aspergillosis (Neutropenic, Leukemia, or Transplant Patients): Refractory high fevers despite broad-spectrum antibacterial coverage, sharp pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea, dry cough, and acute hemoptysis

Chronic Cavitary Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Aspergilloma: Recurrent, often massive and life-threatening hemoptysis (from erosion into bronchial arterioles), chronic productive cough, low-grade fevers, night sweats, and severe progressive cachexia

Disseminated Extrapulmonary Manifestations: Necrotic cutaneous papules evolving into ulcerated plaques with central black necrotic eschar; epistaxis and necrotic black palatal/turbinate eschars in sinonasal extension
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT) - Angioinvasive Stage: Pathognomonic 'CT Halo Sign' (macronodule >1 cm or mass surrounded by a perimeter of ground-glass attenuation corresponding to alveolar hemorrhage secondary to fungal angioinvasion and infarction); 'Hypoattenuating Center Sign' on contrast CT; and 'Vessel Cutoff Sign' on CT angiography

HRCT - Cavitation / Neutrophil Recovery Stage: Pathognomonic 'Air Crescent Sign' (crescent-shaped collection of gas appearing within or along the margin of a necrotic pulmonary nodule as the infarcted lung sequestrum separates from viable parenchyma)

Aspergilloma (Simple Fungus Ball): Well-defined pre-existing cavity containing a mobile, gravity-dependent, rounded, heterogeneously attenuating mass ('Monod Sign') that shifts position between supine and prone CT acquisitions, separated from the cavity wall by a crescent of air
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology of Lung Biopsy: Extensive coagulative ischemic necrosis, hemorrhagic infarction, and prominent vascular angioinvasion; fungal hyphae actively penetrating through elastica and endothelial walls of pulmonary arteries and arterioles, inducing intravascular thrombosis and localized tissue death

Fungal Hyphal Morphology: Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stains reveal uniform, slender, parallel-walled, septate hyphae (3-6 um in diameter) that branch characteristically at acute, progressive 45-degree dichotomous angles (V-shaped branching)

Aspergilloma Histopathology: Intertwined, dense, felt-like matted mass of degenerative fungal hyphae, conidiophores with biseriate sterigmata (in aerobic cavities), fibrin, degenerating erythrocytes, and cellular debris without tissue invasion of the surrounding thick fibrous cavity wall
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening opportunistic mycosis defined by pathognomonic imaging signs on chest CT ('CT halo sign', 'air crescent sign', and mobile 'Monod sign' for aspergilloma), alongside hallmark acute-angle 45-degree branching septate hyphae with angioinvasion on histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Leprosy
clinical_manifestations: Hypopigmented or erythematous anesthetic skin macules and plaques with loss of pain, temperature, and touch sensation
Leonine facies: diffuse facial skin thickening, infiltrated nodules, deep furrowing, and complete loss of eyebrows and eyelashes (madarosis)
Saddle nose deformity from destruction of nasal cartilage
Palpable, thickened, tender peripheral nerves (greater auricular, ulnar at elbow, common peroneal at fibular neck)
Neuropathic trophic claw hand, wrist drop, foot drop, and perforating plantar ulcers
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Nerve Ultrasound / MRI: Marked fusiform enlargement and thickening of peripheral nerves, loss of normal fascicular architecture, intraneural power Doppler hyperemia during lepra reactions

Hand and Foot Radiographs: Severe neurotrophic acro-osteolysis, concentric bone resorption leading to 'licked candy stick' or 'penciling' appearance of phalanges and metatarsals, neuropathic joint destruction (Charcot foot)
pathology_manifestations: Skin and nerve biopsy: In lepromatous leprosy: dermis packed with sheets of foamy, lipid-laden macrophages (Virchow cells / lepra cells) loaded with clumps and globi of acid-fast bacilli highlighted by Fite-Faraco stain; in tuberculoid leprosy: well-defined epithelioid granulomas invading dermal nerves
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Legendary visual disease with unmistakable leonine facies, madarosis, and anesthetic skin plaques, coupled with high-resolution nerve ultrasound thickening and 'licked candy stick' acro-osteolysis on plain X-rays.

Infectious Diseases.name: Loiasis (Loa Loa Filariasis)
clinical_manifestations: Calabar Swellings (Fugitive Swellings): Pathognomonic transient, localized, non-pitting, migratory angioedema (typically 5-20 cm in diameter) occurring predominantly on extremities (wrist, dorsal hand, forearm, ankle), warm and pruritic, occasionally mildly painful, resolving spontaneously over 3 to 7 days before recurring elsewhere

Subconjunctival Worm Migration (Eyeworm): Spectacular, unmistakable bedside finding of an adult female or male worm (Loa loa, 30-70 mm in length) actively crawling across the bulbar subconjunctiva of the eye, producing foreign body sensation, extreme pruritus, lacrimation, photophobia, and periocular edema
Generalized pruritus, urticaria, maculopapular exanthem, fatigue, and myalgias

Post-treatment Encephalopathy: Acute severe neurological deterioration, coma, and retinal microhemorrhages triggered by mass microfilarial death following diethylcarbamazine (DEC) or ivermectin therapy in individuals with high microfilarial loads (>30,000 mf/mL)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Ocular and Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Real-time dynamic visualization of a motile, coiled or serpentine, hyperechoic tubular structure measuring ~0.5 mm in diameter actively undulating within the subconjunctival space or subcutaneous tissue layers ('filarial dance sign')
Soft Tissue Radiographs: Fine, curvilinear, thread-like or coiled radio-opaque calcifications corresponding to dead, calcified adult worms in subcutaneous tissues of hands, wrists, or feet

Brain MRI (in Loa loa post-treatment encephalopathy): Multiple small punctate hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR throughout the deep cerebral white matter and basal ganglia, diffuse vasogenic cerebral edema, and microhemorrhages on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) from microvascular obstruction by dying microfilariae
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear Examination: Giemsa or hematoxylin-stained thick blood smear collected during peak diurnal hours (10:00 to 14:00, reflecting diurnal microfilarial periodicity); microfilariae measure 250-300 um by 6-8 um, possess a distinct hyaline sheath, and display somatic nuclei that extend in a continuous column to the absolute, rounded tip of the tail

Adult Worm Surgical Pathology: Intact cylindrical filarial nematode extracted from conjunctiva or skin; cuticle is distinctive, possessing numerous small, rounded, dome-shaped bosses or tubercles scattered over the surface; males measure 30-34 mm with unequal spicules, females measure 50-70 mm with vulva located anteriorly
Tissue Histology: Marked perivascular tissue infiltration with eosinophils, forming eosinophilic granulomas and Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon around degenerating worms in subcutaneous tissues
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Classic neglected filariasis with unforgettable bedside visual findings: the migrating subconjunctival 'eyeworm' and transient Calabar swellings, real-time ultrasound detection of motile worms, and diurnal sheathed microfilariae on blood smear.

Infectious Diseases.name: Ludwig's Angina
synonyms: phlegmon of the floor of the mouth
sublingual and submandibular space gangrenous cellulitis
clinical_manifestations: 'Brawny' or 'woody' bilateral submandibular induration: Rapidly spreading, tense, board-like, extremely tender, non-fluctuant ('brawny') swelling of the bilateral submandibular, sublingual, and submental spaces, obliterating the normal submental fold and jawline ('bull neck' appearance), characteristically without palpable fluctuance or lymphadenopathy in early stages

Elevation and backward protrusion of the tongue: Swelling in the sublingual space forces the tongue superiorly and posteriorly against the hard and soft palates, visible on physical exam as an edematous, protruding tongue that prevents mouth closure and causes inability to swallow secretions (drooling / sialorrhea)

'Hot potato' muffled voice and trismus: Severe pain, trismus (inability to open the mouth due to pterygoid and masseter muscle irritation), and a muffled, guttural voice ('hot potato' speech) caused by hypopharyngeal and lingual displacement

Acute inspiratory stridor and airway compromise: The dreaded hallmark complication, manifesting as air hunger, tachypnea, suprasternal and intercostal retractions, cyanosis, and tripoding posture as the expanding cellulitis rapidly occludes the glottic aperture, posing an immediate threat of asphyxiation and death

Odontogenic source findings: Tenderness to percussion and purulent discharge from the second or third lower mandibular molars (whose roots extend inferior to the insertion of the mylohyoid muscle, providing direct access to the submandibular space)
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Neck CT (Gold Standard): Demonstrates diffuse, extensive, symmetric soft tissue thickening, inflammatory fat stranding, and phlegmonous enlargement of the bilateral sublingual, submandibular, and submental spaces; marked superior and posterior displacement of the tongue; effacement of the vallecullae, pyriform sinuses, and oropharyngeal airway column; small microabscesses or pockets of gas (emphysematous cellulitis); detects caudal extension into the 'danger space' (retrovisceral/retropharyngeal space) and superior mediastinum (mediastinitis)

Portable Bedside Ultrasound: Rapidly detects non-drainable cellulitic phlegmon versus pocketed drainable fluid collections in the submandibular and sublingual spaces, and evaluates airway caliber when the patient cannot lie flat for CT scanning

Soft Tissue Lateral Neck Radiograph: Demonstrates marked prevertebral and submandibular soft tissue swelling, elevation of the floor of the mouth, backward displacement of the base of the tongue, and severe narrowing of the pharyngeal and tracheal air columns
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology and Microbiology: Rapidly progressive, necrotizing cellulitis and fasciitis involving the floor of the mouth and deep cervical fascial compartments; extensive serosanguinous and gelatinous exudate with extensive polymorphonuclear neutrophilic infiltration, widespread microvascular thrombosis, and secondary coagulative necrosis of skeletal muscle fibers; notably characterized by serosanguinous phlegmon rather than large frank collections of thick pus; polymicrobial mixed odontogenic flora dominated by oral viridans group Streptococci (Streptococcus mitis, Streptococcus anginosus group), anaerobic bacteria (Fusobacterium nucleatum, Prevotella melaninogenica, Porphyromonas species), Peptostreptococcus, and occasionally Staphylococcus aureus or Klebsiella pneumoniae (especially in diabetic hosts)
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Critical airway emergency featuring unforgettable bedside findings of woody submandibular induration, a superiorly displaced protruding tongue with drooling, and stridor, diagnosed on contrast neck CT by severe airway column effacement and submandibular phlegmon.

Infectious Diseases.name: Lyme Disease
clinical_manifestations: Erythema migrans: expanding, erythematous, circular or oval annular rash often with central clearing creating a pathognomonic 'bull's-eye' targetoid lesion
Borrelial lymphocytoma: bluish-red, firm, painless nodule on earlobe (children) or nipple (adults)
Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans: late-stage bluish-red discoloration with 'cigarette-paper' skin atrophy and prominent superficial veins (lower limbs)
Bilateral or unilateral lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy)
Large joint chronic oligoarthritis (predominantly the knee) with massive swelling
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Spine MRI (Neuroborreliosis): Intense contrast enhancement of cranial nerves (especially CN VII), leptomeningeal enhancement, multiple focal T2/FLAIR hyperintense subcortical white matter lesions
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound / MRI (Lyme Arthritis): Marked knee joint effusion, prominent popliteal (Baker) cyst formation, thick synovial hypertrophy with marked vascularity, enthesitis
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy of erythema migrans: Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate with occasional eosinophils; spirochetes visualized with Warthin-Starry silver stain or focus-floating immunohistochemistry
Synovial biopsy: Striking villous hyperplasia, dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with lymphoid follicles, marked endarteritis obliterans
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Features textbook cutaneous erythema migrans ('bull's-eye') and earlobe lymphocytoma matched with cranial nerve enhancement on brain MRI and massive synovitis on joint MRI.

Infectious Diseases.name: Lymphatic Filariasis
clinical_manifestations: Chronic Disfiguring Lymphedema (Elephantiasis): Progressive, irreversible, massive swelling of the lower extremities (less commonly upper extremities, breasts, and vulva), initially pitting but rapidly progressing to non-pitting brawny induration
Pachydermia and Mossy Foot: Severely thickened, hyperkeratotic, verrucous skin with deep transverse skin folds, fissuring, mossy papules, and foul-smelling secondary bacterial and fungal intertrigo
Filarial Scrotal Hydrocele: Massive, fluctuating, fluid-filled enlargement of the scrotum (can reach extreme, disabling dimensions), with burying of the penis beneath the edematous scrotal fold
Chyluria: Intermittent or chronic discharge of milky white, lipid-rich urine due to rupture of obstructed retroperitoneal lymphatic varices into the renal pelvicalyceal system

Acute Dermatolymphangioadenitis (ADLA): Recurrent, debilitating episodes of high-spiking fever, chills, and retrograde spreading lymphangitis (erythematous streaks traveling distally from inflamed lymph nodes)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Scrotal / Inguinal Ultrasound: Pathognomonic 'Filarial Dance Sign' (FDS) on B-mode real-time ultrasound and color Doppler - continuous, vigorous, erratic, chaotic undulating movement of live adult worms within dilated, tortuous, anechoic lymphatic vessels in the spermatic cord or peritesticular lymphatics

Lymphoscintigraphy (Gold Standard for Lymphatic Functional Imaging): Demonstrates extensive lymphatic obstruction, dilated tortuous collectors, delayed or absent radiotracer clearance to regional nodes, and prominent dermal backflow into cutaneous collateral networks

Plain Radiography and CT: Small, linear, calcified string-like or coiled opacities representing dead, calcified adult worms within pelvic and retroperitoneal lymphatic chains; gross soft-tissue thickening and trabeculated subcutaneous fluid without deep muscular edema
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear Examination: Giemsa-stained thick blood smear collected during peak nocturnal hours (between 22:00 and 02:00, corresponding to nocturnal microfilarial periodicity); microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti measure 240-300 um in length, are enclosed in a delicate hyaline sheath, and have somatic nuclei that terminate cleanly before the pointed tip, leaving a pathognomonic terminal nuclear-free clear space

Histopathology of Lymph Node or Spermatic Cord: Dilated, tortuous lymphatic channels containing living or necrotic coiled adult nematodes (females 80-100 mm long, males 40 mm long) surrounded by intense eosinophilic endolymphangitis, perilymphatic granulomas, foreign-body giant cells, and extensive concentric fibrotic obliteration of lymphatic lumina
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal disfiguring tropical infection with the visual spectrum of elephantiasis and massive hydrocele, confirmed by the real-time 'filarial dance sign' on high-frequency ultrasound and nocturnal sheathed microfilariae on blood smear.

Infectious Diseases.name: Melioidosis
clinical_manifestations: Primary cutaneous melioidosis: Painful, non-healing necrotic cutaneous pustules, ecthyma-like ulcers with undermined violaceous edges, cellulitis with lymphangitis, and subcutaneous fluctuant abscesses
Suppurative acute parotitis: Painful, tense, unilateral swelling of the parotid gland (classic pediatric presentation in Southeast Asia)
Severe acute septicemic melioidosis: Sudden high spiking fevers, profound septic shock, respiratory failure, and multiple pustular skin lesions scattered across trunk and extremities
Chronic form: Recurrent chronic subcutaneous cold abscesses, osteomyelitis, and fistulous tracts mimicking tuberculosis
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution CT: Hallmark 'Swiss cheese' appearance: multiple nodular airspace consolidations that rapidly progress to coalescent, thick-walled cavitary lesions and multi-loculated lung abscesses, predilection for upper lobes mimicking tuberculosis; pleural effusion/empyema

Abdominal / Pelvic Contrast CT (Diagnostic Hallmark): Multiple, discrete, multiloculated hypodense abscesses in the spleen, liver, and prostate; splenic abscesses classically display a pathognomonic 'honeycomb' or 'necklace' architecture with peripheral radiating internal septations and rim enhancement
Musculoskeletal CT / MRI: Multifocal osteomyelitis with extensive subperiosteal abscesses, cortical erosions, and soft-tissue phlegmon
pathology_manifestations: Gram stain of pus / aspirate: Small, straight or slightly curved, Gram-negative bacilli displaying pathognomonic bipolar staining ('safety-pin appearance' with dark ends and a clear central zone, due to metachromatic volutin granules)

Histopathology of tissue biopsy: Severe acute suppurative and necrotizing inflammation (microabscesses) with marked cellular debris, surrounded by a variable granulomatous reaction composed of epithelioid histiocytes, lymphocytes, and multinucleated foreign body/Langhans giant cells
Culture morphology: Wrinkled, dry, corncob-like, metallic-sheen colonies on Ashdown's selective agar producing a characteristic distinctive earthy/musty odor
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Major tropical bacterial pathogen characterized by acute cutaneous pustules/parotitis, cavitary 'Swiss cheese' pneumonia, pathognomonic 'honeycomb' splenic abscesses on CT, and safety-pin bipolar bacilli on Gram stain.

Infectious Diseases.name: Mycetoma (Eumycetoma and Actinomycetoma)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic classic diagnostic triad: (1) painless, indurated, non-pitting, woody subcutaneous mass/swelling ('mycetoma tumor'), (2) multiple chronic draining sinuses and fistulae opening onto the cutaneous surface, and (3) persistent discharge containing macroscopic, pigmented granules or 'grains' (black, pale/white, red, or yellow depending on causative organism)
Progressive severe deformity, enlargement, and structural destruction of the affected body part (classically the foot, 'Madura foot', or hand/back)
Relative preservation of general systemic well-being and absence of constitutional symptoms until secondary bacterial superinfection or advanced bone invasion occurs
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'dot-in-circle sign' on T2-weighted and STIR images (multiple small, round, hyperintense spherical areas representing granulomas, containing a central hypointense dot representing the fungal or bacterial grain surrounded by a low-signal fibrous ring)

Plain Radiography: 'Madura foot' osteolytic changes featuring multiple round, punched-out bone cavities ('geodes'), periosteal reaction with exuberant spiculation, cortical disruption, and patchy reactive osteosclerosis leading to the 'melting bone' appearance
Ultrasound: Multiple thick-walled, round, hypoechoic granulomas containing distinct hyperreflective central echoes with or without posterior acoustic shadowing corresponding to grains
pathology_manifestations: Macroscopic grain examination and histopathology (GMS, PAS, Gram stains): Characteristic grains/granules embedded within suppurative granulomas: Eumycetoma shows true broad septate hyphae (2-6 um) with chlamydoconidia and cement-like matrix; Actinomycetoma shows delicate tangled branching filamentous Gram-positive rods (<1 um) surrounded by Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon
Tissue reaction: Extensive chronic suppurative and granulomatous panniculitis with dense neutrophil pools around grains, bordered by palisading histiocytes, giant cells, and thick fibrous tissue
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: World Health Organization neglected tropical disease characterized by the classic visual triad of woody foot swelling, draining sinuses with colored grains, the pathognomonic MRI 'dot-in-circle' sign, and distinctive grain histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis
clinical_manifestations: Agonizing pain out of proportion to physical examination findings (early hallmark)
Rapidly advancing dusky, purplish, or bronze erythema with poorly demarcated margins
Large, flaccid, hemorrhagic bullae filled with dark purple/black foul fluid
Palpable subcutaneous crepitus (gas in tissues)
Cutaneous anesthesia (numbness from necrosis of cutaneous nerves)
Frank black eschar skin gangrene and visible 'dishwater' purulent fluid on surgical incision
Fournier gangrene: necrotizing infection of perineum, scrotum, and perianal region
radiological_manifestations: Plain Soft-Tissue Radiography: Extensive tracking soft-tissue gas along deep fascial planes (linear radiolucencies)

Contrast CT: Pathognomonic tracking subcutaneous and deep interfascial gas collections; asymmetrical, non-enhancing, thickened deep fascial layers; fluid tracking along muscular compartments without discrete wall enhancement (differentiating from abscess)
pathology_manifestations: Frozen section / surgical debridement biopsy: Widespread liquefactive necrosis of the deep fascia and subcutaneous fat, extensive microvascular thrombosis of dermal and fascial vessels, dense neutrophilic infiltration, and massive bacterial proliferation with lack of bleeding on surgical cut
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Surgical emergency showing classic hemorrhagic bullae, dusky necrosis, and dishwater fluid paired with extensive tracking deep fascial gas on plain radiography and CT.

Infectious Diseases.name: Neurocysticercosis
clinical_manifestations: Epileptic Seizures: Most common presentation (~70-90% of symptomatic patients) and leading infectious cause of acquired adult-onset epilepsy in endemic regions, presenting with focal seizures with or without secondary generalization

Intracranial Hypertension: Chronic severe throbbing headaches, projectile vomiting, papilledema, and visual obscurations due to obstructive hydrocephalus from intraventricular cysts (Bruns syndrome with episodic positioning headaches) or subarachnoid basal meningitis

Racemose / Giant Subarachnoid Form: Proliferating multilocular lobulated cysts in basal cisterns causing basal arachnoiditis, multiple cranial neuropathies, and stroke-like focal deficits from cerebral vasculitis

Extracranial Physical Signs: Palpable, non-tender, rubbery subcutaneous and intramuscular cystic nodules in soft tissues; subretinal or vitreous cysticercosis visible on ophthalmoscopy as a shimmering translucent cyst with an invaginated white scolex
radiological_manifestations: Brain CT and MRI (Pathognomonic 4 Evolutionary Stages): (1) Vesicular Stage: Well-circumscribed, round, thin-walled cyst with CSF-like fluid, containing an eccentric, hyperdense/T1-hyperintense 1-2 mm nodule representing the scolex ('hole-with-a-dot' sign); (2) Colloidal Vesicular Stage: Thickened cyst wall with ring enhancement, hyperintense fluid on T1/FLAIR, and marked perilesional vasogenic edema; (3) Granular Nodular Stage: Collapsed, shrunken cyst forming a nodular or ring-enhancing granuloma with diminishing edema; (4) Calcified Stage: Shrunken, densely calcified punctate non-enhancing nodule (2-10 mm), brilliantly seen on non-contrast CT ('starry sky' in heavy infection) or SWI/GRE MRI
Soft Tissue Skeletal Radiographs: Elongated, oval, calcified 'rice grain' calcifications (10-15 mm long) oriented strictly parallel to the long axis of skeletal muscle fibers

Constructive Interference in Steady State (CISS) / FIESTA MRI: 3D high-resolution steady-state sequences providing crisp delineation of intraventricular and cistern cyst membranes, internal scolex, and hooklets that are otherwise isointense to CSF
pathology_manifestations: Gross Morphology of Intact Cyst: Spherical, translucent membranous cyst (5-15 mm) filled with clear fluid, containing a single invaginated white mural nodule representing the larval scolex

Microscopic Histopathology: Three-layered cyst wall consisting of an outer anucleate cuticular tegument with microvilli, a middle cellular layer, and an inner reticular fibrillary layer containing smooth muscle bundles and pathognomonic basophilic calcareous corpuscles (spherical calcium concretions, 10-25 um)
Scolar Architecture: Demonstrates four muscular suckers (acetabula) and a retractile apical rostellum armed with a double crown of chitinous, refractile, acid-fast hooklets

Surrounding Host Response: Zonal granulomatous inflammation surrounding the degenerating larva with dense infiltrates of eosinophils, histiocytes, lymphocytes, and multinucleated foreign body giant cells, progressing to fibrous encapsulation and dense dystrophic calcification
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Leading parasitic cause of adult epilepsy globally, defined by the pathognomonic 'hole-with-a-dot' scolex sign across 4 radiographic stages on CT/MRI, rice-grain muscle calcifications, and larval scolex histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Nocardiosis
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous / Subcutaneous nocardiosis (N. brasiliensis): Painful, erythematous, indurated cellulitis, subcutaneous fluctuant 'cold' abscesses, ulcerated nodules, sporotrichoid lymphocutaneous chains, and actinomycetoma with draining sinuses
Pulmonary nocardiosis (N. asteroides complex): Subacute/chronic fever, productive cough with purulent sputum, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and hemoptysis

Disseminated / Central Nervous System nocardiosis: Severe persistent headache, seizures, focal neurological deficits, and altered mental status due to single or multiple cerebral abscesses (marked predilection for brain hematogenous seeding)
radiological_manifestations: Brain Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Multiple or solitary, multilocular, thick-walled ring-enhancing cerebral abscesses with pronounced surrounding vasogenic edema; classic central restricted diffusion (bright hyperintensity on DWI with low ADC signal) and smooth, thin, T2-hypointense capsule

Chest CT: Multifocal subpleural nodular opacities, dense lobar or segmental airspace consolidation with central necrosis and cavitation, thick-walled cavitary masses, pleural effusion, and chest wall invasion/empyema necessitans
Musculoskeletal CT / MRI: Extensive soft-tissue phlegmon, deep interfascial abscesses, and adjacent osteolytic cortical erosion
pathology_manifestations: Modified Kinyoun / Fite-Faraco acid-fast stain: Delicate, beaded, branching, filamentous organisms that are partially/weakly acid-fast positive (staining red against a blue background, in contrast to Actinomyces which is non-acid-fast, and Mycobacterium which is strongly acid-fast on standard Ziehl-Neelsen)
Gram stain / Culture: Gram-positive, thin, beaded, branching filaments; chalky-white to orange-yellow wrinkled colonies with a characteristic earthy/musty odor

Histopathology: Intense, acute suppurative necrosis dominated by dense collections of polymorphonuclear neutrophils (microabscesses) with minimal or absent true granuloma formation, accompanied by prominent peripheral granulation tissue
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Critical opportunistic and cutaneous pathogen presenting with cold subcutaneous abscesses/nodules, multilocular ring-enhancing cerebral abscesses with restricted diffusion on MRI, and pathognomonic partially acid-fast beaded branching filaments on modified Kinyoun stain.

Infectious Diseases.name: Noma (Cancrum Oris)
clinical_manifestations: Necrotizing gingivostomatitis prodrome (Stage 1-2): Rapidly progressive, extremely painful ulceration of the gingiva and buccal mucosal lining with foul-smelling, putrid fetor oris, spontaneous gingival bleeding, loose teeth, and extensive destruction of interdental papillae in severely malnourished children (often post-measles or malaria)

Full-thickness ischemic black necrotic demarcation (Stage 3): Development of a hard, woody, bluish-black ischemic induration of the cheek and facial skin that rapidly undergoes liquefactive necrosis, forming a sharply demarcated, full-thickness blackened gangrenous eschar extending through all tissue planes (mucosa, subcutaneous fat, facial musculature, and overlying skin)

Devastating facial mutilation and bone denudation (Stage 4): Spontaneous sloughing of the necrotic facial plug, leaving a horrific, gaping facial crater exposing denuded, necrotic maxillary and mandibular bone, teeth roots, nasal septum, and orbital floor with loss of lips, nose, or eyelid tissues

Severe cicatricial fibrous ankylosis (Stage 5 / Sequelae): Contraction and dense scarring of healed tissues producing complete fibrous or osseous temporomandibular joint (TMJ) ankylosis, causing permanent lockjaw, inability to feed, speech arrest, and severe facial asymmetry with permanent disfigurement
Profound systemic toxemia and cachexia: High fever, severe protein-energy malnutrition (kwashiorkor or marasmus), marked apathy, profound anemia, and high early mortality (>80-90% if untreated)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution 3D Craniofacial CT (Bone and Soft Tissue Algorithms): Critical imaging modality demonstrating extensive, massive full-thickness facial soft-tissue defects; aggressive cortical erosion, osteonecrosis, and sequestrum formation of the maxilla, mandible, alveolar process, zygoma, and nasal bones; pathognomonic osseous bridges and heterotopic bony fusion causing temporomandibular joint bony ankylosis; intraorbital osseous defects with globe displacement

Craniofacial Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Delineates the exact margins of non-enhancing necrotic muscle and fat planes versus viable tissue; demonstrates perineural spread along trigeminal nerve branches; identifies deep masticator and infratemporal fossa phlegmon or intracranial extension through skull base foramina
Panoramic Radiography (Orthopantomogram / OPG): Shows gross dental dislocation, loss of alveolar crest bone, jagged mandibular osteolytic destruction, and dental impaction within scar tissue
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology and Polymicrobial Synergy: Severe, acute, non-granulomatous, liquefactive and ischemic coagulative necrosis involving skin, skeletal muscle, salivary glands, and bone; extensive thrombophlebitis and obliterative arteriolitis with fibrinoid thrombi in microvascular beds, explaining the rapid, ischemic, sharply demarcated gangrenous progression; abundant bacterial colonization with mixed flora invading the deep muscular tissue ahead of the inflammatory boundary; synergistic polymicrobial infection driven by anaerobic and spirochetal organisms: Fusobacterium necrophorum (elaborating dermonecrotic endotoxin and leukocidin), Prevotella intermedia, Borrelia vincentii, Treponema denticola, and Peptostreptococcus species, thriving in the setting of severe immunosuppression, zinc and micronutrient deficiency, and mucosal breakdown
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Devastating neglected tropical disease characterized by horrifying visual facial gangrene sloughing the cheek and exposing the jaws, documented radiographically by 3D craniofacial CT osseous destruction and TMJ ankylosis, driven by polymicrobial Fusobacterium-spirochete ischemic necrosis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Paracoccidioidomycosis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic 'moriform stomatitis' (stomatite moriforme of Aguiar-Pupo): mulberry-like ulcerated, granular, hemorrhagic mucosal lesions studded with pinpoint petechial bleeding spots on the gingiva, lips, buccal mucosa, tongue, and hard palate
Massive, dramatic cervical and submandibular lymphadenopathy (scrofula-like) that becomes fluctuant and can drain externally through suppurative cutaneous fistulae
'Tapir head' (facies de anta): Disfiguring enlargement and ulcerated infiltration of the upper lip and nose
Laryngeal involvement causing painful hoarseness, stridor, and dysphagia
radiological_manifestations: Chest High-Resolution CT: Symmetric, bilateral, diffuse interstitial and alveolar infiltrates with a classic 'bat-wing' or 'butterfly' distribution predominantly involving the middle and lower pulmonary zones while sparing the apices and bases; combination of ground-glass opacities, centrilobular nodules, interlobular septal thickening, architectural distortion, and thick-walled cavitary lesions; reversed halo sign ('atoll sign')
Abdominal CT / Ultrasound: Marked hepatosplenomegaly, necrotic abdominal and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and bilateral adrenal enlargement with hypodense centers
pathology_manifestations: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) mount / GMS / PAS stain: Large (10-30 um, up to 60 um), round-to-oval parent yeast cells with multiple small, round-to-ovoid, narrow-necked peripheral daughter buds distributed around the entire circumference, producing the pathognomonic 'mariner's wheel', 'ship's wheel', or 'Mickey Mouse head' appearance

Tissue histology: Mixed suppurative and granulomatous reaction featuring dense microabscesses surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells, and extensive interstitial fibrosis
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Major Latin American endemic fungal infection distinguished by pathognomonic mulberry-like moriform stomatitis, facial disfigurement ('tapir head'), bilateral butterfly/bat-wing CT infiltrates, and mariner's-wheel multipolar budding yeasts.

Infectious Diseases.name: Paragonimiasis (Pulmonary Distomiasis / Lung Fluke)
clinical_manifestations: Classic Respiratory Triad: Chronic, productive cough yielding rusty-brown or chocolate-colored sputum resembling anchovy sauce, recurrent bouts of frank endemic hemoptysis, and pleuritic chest pain; clinically indistinguishable from, and frequently misdiagnosed and treated as, multidrug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis
Extrapulmonary / Cerebral Paragonimiasis (Most serious complication): Chronic seizures, visual disturbances, motor deficits, and signs of elevated intracranial pressure from intracranial granulomas
Abdominal and Subcutaneous Migratory Nodules: Painful, firm, mobile subcutaneous nodules on the abdominal wall or extremities ('creeping tumor') caused by aberrant migrating juvenile flukes
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (Diagnostic Imaging Hallmarks): 'Ring Shadow' / 'Worm Cyst' (thick-walled or thin-walled cystic cavities, 1-3 cm, with surrounding ground-glass halos, frequently containing internal fluid or gas, situated in mid-to-lower subpleural lung zones); 'Burrow Track Sign' / 'Worm Track' (linear or tortuous tubular opacities connecting subpleural cystic lesions with the visceral pleura, representing the physical track carved by migrating juvenile flukes through lung parenchyma); and marked pleural thickening with loculated pleural effusions

Brain CT and MRI (in Cerebral Paragonimiasis): Pathognomonic multilocular, grouped, clustered cystic lesions with thick rim-like calcifications resembling a 'soap bubble' or 'grape cluster' in the temporo-parieto-occipital region, surrounded by extensive vasogenic edema
pathology_manifestations: Sputum and Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) Microscopy: Direct identification of pathognomonic Paragonimus eggs in chocolate-colored sputum: large, yellowish-brown, thick-walled, asymmetrically oval, operculated eggs measuring 80-120 um in length by 45-65 um in width, with a flattened operculum bordered by prominent opercular shoulders and a thickened abopercular shell at the opposite pole

Histopathology of Lung Cyst Wall Biopsy: Fibrotic cyst capsule containing a pair of hermaphroditic, leaf-shaped, fleshy adult trematodes (P. westermani, 8-16 mm long) enveloped by an intense chronic inflammatory reaction comprising dense sheets of eosinophils, Charcot-Leyden crystals, foreign-body giant cells, and cholesterol clefts
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Major endemic parasitic pulmonary disease mimicking tuberculosis, characterized by rusty-brown hemoptysis, pathognomonic 'worm tracks' and 'ring shadows' on chest CT, and golden-brown operculated eggs in sputum.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rhino-Orbital-Cerebral Mucormycosis
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly progressing, lethal black necrotic eschar on the hard palate, nasal turbinates, or nasal septum
Marked periorbital edema, dark dusky facial discoloration, and chemosis
Acute complete ophthalmoplegia (cranial nerves III, IV, VI palsies), severe ptosis, proptosis, and loss of vision
Facial anesthesia (trigeminal nerve V1/V2 involvement)
Predominance in diabetic ketoacidosis, uncontrolled diabetes, and severe neutropenia
radiological_manifestations: Facial and Orbital Contrast CT / MRI: Opacification of paranasal sinuses with severe bone destruction (cribriform plate, lamina papyracea, orbital apex); non-enhancing 'black turbinate sign' on contrast MRI (indicating tissue infarction); retro-orbital fat infiltration, proptosis
Brain MRI / MRA: Cavernous sinus thrombosis, cavernous internal carotid artery occlusion or narrowing, cerebritis and fungal abscesses
Chest CT (Pulmonary Mucormycosis): 'Reverse halo sign' (central ground-glass opacity surrounded by a complete ring of consolidation)
pathology_manifestations: Tissue biopsy / KOH mount: Broad (6-30 um), thin-walled, ribbon-like, predominantly non-septate or pauciseptate hyphae with wide-angle (90-degree) irregular branching; marked angioinvasion with fungal hyphae infiltrating vessel walls, causing extensive arterial thrombosis, tissue infarction, and ischemic necrosis
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-urgency visual fungal entity featuring pathognomonic black hard palate eschar and ophthalmoplegia alongside the MRI 'black turbinate sign' and invasive skull base bony destruction.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark exanthem: Erupts 2-4 days into fever as small (1-5 mm), blanching, pink-to-erythematous macules on the wrists, forearms, ankles, palms, and soles; centrifugally and centripetally spreads to the trunk, face, and extremities
Petechial / purpuric evolution: By day 5-6, macules become non-blanching, dark red-to-purple petechiae and coalescent ecchymotic plaques
Acral ischemic necrosis: Microvascular occlusion causing localized gangrene, cyanosis, and full-thickness necrosis of digits, ears, nose tip, and scrotum
Striking periorbital and pretibial non-pitting edema due to systemic vascular leakage; calf muscle tenderness; severe toxic delirium/encephalopathy
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (CNS Vasculitis / Encephalopathy): Pathognomonic 'starry sky' appearance on T2-weighted, FLAIR, and DWI sequences, showing innumerable tiny, punctate, hyperintense microvascular infarctions and petechial microhemorrhages scattered throughout the subcortical white matter, internal capsule, basal ganglia, and cerebellum

Chest CT / Radiography: Diffuse, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, patchy non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, bibasilar airspace consolidations, and small bilateral pleural effusions resulting from pulmonary capillary leak syndrome
Abdominal Ultrasound: Gallbladder wall thickening (acalculous cholecystitis) and splenomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Punch biopsy of petechial skin lesion: Acute, severe, necrotizing vasculitis and perivasculitis: tropism for vascular endothelial cells; endothelial cell necrosis, microvascular thrombosis, dense perivascular cuffing composed of mononuclear histiocytes and lymphocytes with occasional neutrophils, transmural vessel wall necrosis, and extensive erythrocyte extravasation into the dermis

Direct immunofluorescence / Immunohistochemistry: Bright, intracellular granular staining of Rickettsia rickettsii antigens within endothelial cells and smooth muscle cells of dermal arterioles, venules, and capillaries
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening rickettsial vasculitis diagnosed by the classic centripetal petechial palm/sole rash with acral gangrene, the MRI 'starry sky' brain microinfarctions, and pathognomonic endothelial infective vasculitis on biopsy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Schistosomiasis
clinical_manifestations: Acute Phase: 'Swimmer's itch' (pruritic papular cercarial dermatitis at skin penetration site) followed weeks later by Katayama fever (acute immune complex illness with high fever, urticaria, dry cough, severe eosinophilia, and generalized lymphadenopathy)

Urinary Schistosomiasis (Schistosoma haematobium): Painless terminal gross hematuria, dysuria, frequency, and secondary squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder; Female Genital Schistosomiasis (FGS) with pathognomonic grainy, sandy patches on the cervix and vulva, postcoital bleeding, and ectopic pregnancy

Intestinal and Hepatosplenic Schistosomiasis (S. mansoni, S. japonicum): Chronic colicky abdominal pain, bloody mucoid diarrhea; severe presinusoidal portal hypertension presenting with massive splenomegaly, firm non-cirrhotic hepatomegaly, caput medusae, spider angiomas, and catastrophic upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage from ruptured esophageal varices
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound (WHO Protocols): Pathognomonic Symmers Pipe-Stem Periportal Fibrosis (marked hyperechoic fibrous cuffing along portal vein walls >4-6 mm thickness in peripheral branches, >6-8 mm in main trunk with patent lumen); splenomegaly, dilated splenic/portal veins (>12 mm), and portosystemic collateral vessels

Pelvic Plain Radiographs: Pathognomonic curvilinear, circumferential, paper-thin calcification outlining the entire bladder wall, resembling the shape of a fetal head ('fetal head sign'), as well as distal ureteral calcifications
Pelvic and Abdominal CT: Irregular, thickened, nodular bladder wall, obstructive hydroureter, hydronephrosis, pseudopolyps, and secondary bladder wall tumor masses
pathology_manifestations: Parasite Egg Morphology: (1) S. haematobium: Elliptical, transparent eggs (110-170 x 40-70 um) possessing a sharp, terminal spine at the posterior pole; (2) S. mansoni: Large, elongated eggs (115-175 x 45-70 um) featuring a prominent, sharp lateral spine near the posterior pole; (3) S. japonicum: Smaller, oval-to-spherical eggs (70-100 x 50-65 um) with an inconspicuous, rounded lateral knob

Histopathology of Bladder, Rectal, or Liver Biopsy: Concentric granulomatous inflammation centered around miracidium-containing eggs, composed of dense rings of eosinophils, epithelioid histiocytes, lymphocytes, and multinucleated foreign body giant cells; progression to extensive concentric 'onion-skin' collagenous fibrosis without true hepatic lobular architectural distortion (preserving normal hepatic lobules and central veins)
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Major helminthic infection characterized by terminal hematuria, the pathognomonic 'fetal head' calcification of the bladder on radiography, Symmers pipe-stem periportal fibrosis on ultrasound, and definitive terminal/lateral spine egg morphology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Scrub Typhus
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic inoculation eschar ('tache noire'): Begins as a small erythematous papule at the chigger mite bite site, ulcerates, and forms a painless, punched-out ulcer covered by a central dark black necrotic crust surrounded by an erythematous, indurated inflammatory halo (frequently located in intertriginous skin folds: groin, axilla, perineum, under waistband)
Cutaneous rash: Transient, macular or maculopapular, non-pruritic, pink-to-erythematous rash developing around day 5-7, spreading centrifugally from trunk to extremities
Bilateral bulbar conjunctival injection / suffusion without purulent discharge
Painful, tender regional lymphadenopathy draining the eschar site, rapidly evolving into generalized lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates, diffuse ground-glass opacities (GGOs), interlobular septal thickening, bronchial wall thickening, centrilobular nodules, and dependent airspace consolidations; bilateral pleural effusions; signs of acute lung injury / acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
Abdominal Ultrasound / Contrast CT: Hepatosplenomegaly, gallbladder wall thickening with pericholecystic edema, and generalized mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy
Brain Contrast MRI (Scrub Typhus Meningoencephalitis): Leptomeningeal enhancement, multifocal punctate T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in cerebral white matter, and microvascular microbleeds
pathology_manifestations: Skin eschar punch biopsy: Acute, systemic, infective microvascular endothelitis and perivasculitis: swelling and proliferation of vascular endothelial cells, transmural infiltration of mononuclear leukocytes (predominantly CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes and histiocytes), microvascular thrombosis, erythrocyte extravasation, and full-thickness epidermal coagulative necrosis overlying dermal necrosis

Immunohistochemistry (IHC) / PCR: Specific identification of Orientia tsutsugamushi bacterial antigens localized within the cytoplasm of vascular endothelial cells and perivascular mononuclear phagocytes
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential chigger-borne rickettsial illness recognized by the pathognomonic black 'tache noire' inoculation eschar, bilateral ground-glass pneumonitis on chest CT, and systemic endothelial vasculitis on histopathology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Severe Generalized Tetanus
clinical_manifestations: Trismus ('lockjaw'): Severe, painful tonic contraction and involuntary spasm of the masseter and temporalis muscles, preventing the patient from opening the mouth; elicited by the spatula test (touching the posterior pharyngeal wall with a tongue spatula causes reflex spasm of the masseters and biting down, rather than the normal gag reflex)

Risus sardonicus ('sardonic grin'): Pathognomonic grotesque facial grimace caused by continuous, sustained tonic contraction of the facial expression muscles (frontalis, orbicularis oris, and risorius), resulting in sustained elevation of the eyebrows, deep horizontal forehead furrowing, and retraction of the oral commissures exposing clenched teeth

Opisthotonos and board-like abdominal rigidity: Extreme, violent hyper-extension of the entire axial skeleton where the spine, neck, and lower extremities arch backward into a rigid bridge supported only by the back of the head and the heels; accompanied by stony 'board-like' involuntary rigidity of the abdominal wall and chest

Stimulus-induced reflex tetanic spasms: Excruciatingly painful, generalized paroxysmal muscle spasms triggered by minimal auditory, visual, or tactile stimuli (sudden noise, turning on lights, touching the bed, drafts of air), during which the patient remains fully conscious and alert, with flexed fists held tightly against the chest and extended lower limbs

Autonomic storm / sympathetic hyperactivity: Severe cardiovascular instability beginning several days into the illness, characterized by fluctuating malignant hypertension alternating with profound hypotension, persistent resting tachycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, profuse drenching diaphoresis, hyperpyrexia, and peripheral vasoconstriction due to disinhibition of preganglionic sympathetic neurons in the brainstem and spinal cord
radiological_manifestations: Thoracic and Lumbar Spine Plain Radiographs / CT: Classic, pathognomonic mid-thoracic vertebral compression fractures (typically T4-T8) resulting from the violent, unremitting force of paraspinous and paraspinal muscle contractions against the bony skeleton in conscious patients; often accompanied by compression deformities of anterior vertebral bodies

Skeletal Plain Films and CT: Heterotopic ossification of periarticular soft tissues (particularly around hips and elbows) developing secondary to sustained immobility, muscle hypertonicity, and tissue hypoxia; fractures of the femoral neck, humeral head, or avulsion of muscular insertions

Soft Tissue Radiography and Wound CT: Identification of radiopaque foreign bodies (soil, wood splinters, rusted metal fragments) or pockets of gas within devitalized, necrotic soft tissue tracking from the primary inoculation puncture site
pathology_manifestations: Pathophysiology and Toxin Mechanism: Infection of devitalized, anaerobic puncture wounds by spores of Clostridium tetani, which germinate and elaborate tetanospasmin (tetanus neurotoxin, TeNT), a 150-kDa zinc-dependent endopeptidase; TeNT undergoes retrograde intra-axonal transport along peripheral motor neurons to the central nervous system, where it enters inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells) and selectively cleaves synaptobrevin-2 (VAMP-2), abolishing the presynaptic exocytosis of glycine and GABA, producing unchecked motor neuron disinhibition, continuous resting tone, and reflex spasms

Microbiology: Gram stain of wound tissue or debrided exudate demonstrating slender, Gram-positive (or Gram-variable in older cultures) rod with a spherical, terminal spore yielding a pathognomonic 'drumstick' or 'tennis racket' morphology; strict obligate anaerobe; diagnosis is fundamentally clinical as blood cultures are uniformly negative and wound cultures are positive in only ~30% of cases
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Unforgettable neurotoxic disease presenting with unmistakable photographic physical signs—risus sardonicus, trismus, and opisthotonos—sparing consciousness during excruciating reflex spasms, complicated radiologically by thoracic compression fractures from pure muscular force.

Infectious Diseases.name: Severe Leptospirosis (Weil's Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic physical examination sign: Dramatic bilateral conjunctival suffusion (deep ciliary and scleral erythema/vascular injection without purulent discharge or chemosis) appearing within the first 48-72 hours

Severe triad of Weil's syndrome: (1) deep, intense, orange-yellow jaundice / icterus with hepatomegaly, (2) acute oliguric renal failure with azotemia, and (3) generalized hemorrhagic diathesis (petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, epistaxis, pulmonary hemorrhage)
Severe, exquisite muscle tenderness and hyperesthesia, characteristically concentrated in the calves, thighs, and paraspinal/lumbar musculature
Severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome (SPHS): Acute hemoptysis, cyanosis, and catastrophic respiratory arrest
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution CT: Classic diffuse, bilateral, patchy ground-glass opacities, alveolar consolidations, and a coarse 'snowstorm' appearance representing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, predominantly involving the lower and middle lobes; resolution or rapid migration over 24-48 hours

Abdominal Ultrasound: Hepatomegaly with patent bile ducts, acute acalculous cholecystitis (marked gallbladder wall thickening, mucosal striation, pericholecystic fluid halo), and bilaterally enlarged, swollen kidneys with hyperechoic cortex and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
pathology_manifestations: Lung histopathology: Massive intra-alveolar and interstitial hemorrhage, disruption of capillary endothelial basement membranes, extensive fibrin thrombi in alveolar capillaries, without significant inflammatory infiltrate (bystander capillary damage)

Liver and Kidney histology: Liver demonstrates disarray of hepatic cords, marked intracellular and canalicular cholestasis, and Kupffer cell hyperplasia without massive hepatocellular necrosis; kidneys exhibit acute tubular injury, interstitial edema, and dense interstitial mononuclear nephritis

Warthin-Starry / Steiner silver impregnation stain: Slender, tightly coiled, flexible spirochetes (6-20 um long, 0.1 um wide) with characteristic hooked or bent ends (resembling a question mark or umbrella handle) visible within renal tubular lumens, interstitial tissue, and hepatic sinusoids
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Iconic severe spirochetal zoonosis featuring pathognomonic non-purulent conjunctival suffusion, Weil's jaundice-renal failure triad, 'snowstorm' pulmonary hemorrhage on chest CT, and hooked spirochetes on silver stain.

Infectious Diseases.name: Sporotrichosis
clinical_manifestations: Classic lymphocutaneous presentation ('sporotrichoid spread'): Initial painless erythematous subcutaneous nodule at the site of minor skin trauma ('sporotrichotic chancre'), which ulcerates into an indolent violaceous ulcer with a ragged undermined edge

Subsequent eruption of a linear, ascending chain of painless, firm, nodular subcutaneous lesions along proximal draining lymphatics ('sporotrichoid cord'), which progressively soften, fluctuate, ulcerate, and discharge serosanguinous/purulent fluid
Fixed cutaneous form: Solitary, indurated, verrucous, vegetative, or ulcerated plaque without lymphatic dissemination
Extracutaneous osteoarticular sporotrichosis: Chronic asymmetric monoarthritis (knee, wrist) with chronic joint effusion, soft tissue swelling, and periarticular sinus tract formation
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal Radiography / MRI (Osteoarticular Sporotrichosis): Asymmetric periarticular osteopenia, marginal bone erosions, joint space narrowing, and cortical lytic lesions; contrast MRI reveals pronounced synovial hypertrophy, nodular pannus formation, and extensive soft-tissue abscesses tracking along tendon sheaths

Chest CT (Pulmonary Sporotrichosis): Chronic upper-lobe predominant cavitary infiltrates with irregular thick walls, surrounding parenchymal fibrosis, and architectural distortion, frequently mimicking secondary tuberculosis; ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch / synovial biopsy (H&E, GMS, PAS stains): Suppurative granulomatous dermatitis and panniculitis featuring central microabscesses dominated by neutrophils, encircled by a granulomatous mantle of epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells, and dense plasma cells

Microscopic fungal morphology: Pleomorphic, round, oval, and classic elongated 'cigar-shaped' budding yeast cells (2-6 um in length); pathognomonic 'asteroid body' (Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon) displaying a central round basophilic yeast cell encircled by radiating, club-like, brightly eosinophilic spicules
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Definitive prototype of ascending nodular lymphocutaneous infection ('sporotrichoid spread') with classic rose-gardener/feline contact history, tuberculous-like upper lobe cavities on chest CT, and cigar-shaped yeasts with asteroid bodies on pathology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Strongyloidiasis Hyperinfection Syndrome and Disseminated Strongyloidiasis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Larva Currens: Rapidly progressing, pruritic, raised, serpiginous, urticarial linear cutaneous eruption moving at astonishing speed (5 to 10 cm per hour - the fastest migrating parasitic lesion in medicine), predominantly distributed over the buttocks, perianal region, groin, thighs, and trunk

Thumbprint Purpura: Characteristic scattered, purpuric, petechial macules and ecchymoses across the lower periumbilical abdomen and thighs caused by larval extravasation and dermal microvascular rupture

Hyperinfection Gastrointestinal and Pulmonary Syndrome: Severe watery diarrhea, paralytic ileus, severe abdominal distension, intestinal obstruction, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with hemoptysis, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) triggered by immunosuppressive therapy (especially high-dose systemic corticosteroids or HTLV-1 co-infection)

Recurrent Polymicrobial Sepsis and Meningitis: Gram-negative bacteremia (E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus) and bacterial meningitis caused by enteric bacteria carried on the cuticle or in the gut lumen of hyper-migrating filariform larvae piercing the bowel wall
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT: Extensive bilateral ground-glass opacities, focal or confluent consolidations, and interlobular septal thickening representing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema; multifocal patchy infiltrates and 'tree-in-bud' nodular opacities corresponding to larval migration through bronchovascular bundles

Abdominal Plain Radiograph and CT: Marked dilation of small bowel loops with loss of normal mucosal fold architecture ('pipestem' or 'featureless' rigid duodenum and jejunum), severe paralytic ileus, duodenal wall thickening, and pneumatosis intestinalis in transmural necrosis
pathology_manifestations: Direct Sputum, Stool, and Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) Wet Prep: Massive swarms of active, wriggling rhabditiform and infectious filariform larvae; filariform larvae measure 500-600 um in length, have a long esophagus extending half the length of the body, and possess a pathognomonic notched, bifurcated tail (forked tail tip)

Duodenal and Jejunal Biopsy Histopathology: Profound infiltration of the lamina propria with eosinophils and plasma cells, villous blunting, crypt hyperplasia, and cross-sections of adult female worms, rhabditiform larvae, and embryonated eggs directly embedded within mucosal crypts of Lieberkuhn

Extraintestinal Organ Histopathology: In disseminated disease, filariform larvae identified in tissue sections of the lung alveoli, myocardium, kidneys, brain, and skin alongside extravasated erythrocytes and mixed inflammatory cells
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Catastrophic parasitic emergency featuring the lightning-fast migrating 'larva currens' and periumbilical 'thumbprint purpura' on physical exam, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage on chest CT, and notched-tail filariform larvae on sputum/BAL microscopy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Syphilis
clinical_manifestations: Primary: painless, indurated, clean-based ulcer (chancre) with raised borders and painless regional lymphadenopathy

Secondary: symmetrical non-pruritic copper-red ('raw ham') papulosquamous eruption predominantly on palms and soles (syphilitic collarette of Biett); condylomata lata (flat, moist, highly infectious whitish papules in anogenital folds); mucosal mucous patches; moth-eaten alopecia
Tertiary: destructive noduloulcerative gummas (face, palate, extremities), Charcot joints, Argyll Robertson pupils (accommodate but do not react to light)
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT Angiography / MRA: Cardiovascular syphilis: ascending aortic aneurysm with pathognomonic linear calcification of the ascending aorta ('tree-bark calcification'), aortic valve insufficiency, ostial coronary stenosis

Brain MRI: Meningovascular syphilis: basal leptomeningeal enhancement, arteritis with cerebral ischemic strokes; parenchymal syphilitic gummas (ring-enhancing dural-based lesions mimicking meningiomas); tabes dorsalis (dorsal column atrophy and hyperintensity)
Skeletal Radiography: Gummatous osteitis and periostitis with mixed lytic and sclerotic bone remodeling
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy: Dense perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate rich in plasma cells; marked endothelial cell swelling and proliferation leading to obliterative endarteritis ('onion-peel' intimal fibrosis); gummas display central coagulative gummatous necrosis surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes and plasma cells; spirochetes demonstrated by Warthin-Starry stain or Treponema immunohistochemistry
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: 'The Great Imitator' featuring pathognomonic palmoplantar copper collarettes and condylomata lata paired with linear ascending aortic calcification on chest CT and cerebral gummas on brain MRI.

Infectious Diseases.name: Talaromycosis
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark skin manifestation: Generalized, widespread, painless umbilicated papules with central necrotic crusts or ulcerations resembling molluscum contagiosum (predominantly involving the face, ears, neck, chest, and upper extremities)
Infiltrated plaques, pustules, subcutaneous nodules, and necrotic mucosal ulcers of the palate and tongue
High remittent fever, profound constitutional wasting/cachexia, and severe anemia
Marked generalized lymphadenopathy and progressive hepatosplenomegaly (in patients with advanced HIV/CD4 < 100 or non-HIV immunocompromise in Southeast Asia)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution CT: Diffuse, bilateral interstitial reticulonodular opacities; patchy multifocal alveolar consolidations with air bronchograms; thin- and thick-walled cavitary nodules; extensive necrotic mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy; pleural effusions

Abdominal CT / Ultrasound: Marked hepatosplenomegaly with multiple discrete, round, hypodense/hypoechoic microabscesses scattered in the splenic parenchyma; extensive retroperitoneal and mesenteric necrotic lymphadenopathy
Musculoskeletal CT / MRI: Multifocal osteolytic bone lesions involving the ribs, skull, and appendicular skeleton, associated with overlying soft-tissue cold abscesses
pathology_manifestations: Wright-Giemsa / GMS / PAS stains of skin scraping, bone marrow, or lymph node biopsy: Innumerable small (2-8 um), round, oval, or sausage-shaped yeast-like cells situated intracellularly within histiocytes and extracellularly; pathognomonic finding is a distinctive internal transverse cross-wall (binary fission septum) rather than budding, distinguishing it from Histoplasma

Fungal culture morphology: Characteristic thermal dimorphism producing a distinctive water-soluble, diffusible deep-red/wine-colored pigment that stains Sabouraud dextrose agar at 25 deg C, with conversion to a yeast form at 37 deg C
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Key Southeast Asian dimorphic endemic mycosis featuring hallmark molluscum-like umbilicated necrotic facial papules, cavitary bronchopneumonia with necrotic lymphadenopathy on CT, and intracellular fission yeasts on cytology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Trichinellosis (Trichinosis)
clinical_manifestations: Classical Diagnostic Clinical Tetrad: (1) Sudden-onset, symmetrical, non-pitting bilateral periorbital and facial edema (classically accompanied by prominent chemosis, subconjunctival hemorrhages, and photophobia); (2) Severe muscle pain and tenderness (myalgia) with wooden induration exacerbated by muscle contraction, predominantly involving extraocular muscles, masseters (causing trismus and difficulty chewing), diaphragm, intercostals, and proximal limb muscles; (3) High persistent fever (39-40 C) with rigors and profuse diaphoresis; (4) Subungual splinter hemorrhages (characteristic linear, dark reddish-brown hemorrhages beneath fingernails and toenails)

Extreme Laboratory Marker: Striking, profound leukocytosis with marked peripheral eosinophilia (often 30-70%, reaching absolute counts >5,000/uL) and massive serum creatine kinase (CK) and aldolase elevation
Severe Complications: Lethal acute myocarditis (arrhythmias, congestive heart failure) and neurotrichinellosis (encephalopathy, stroke-like focal deficits)
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal MRI: Bilateral, symmetrical, diffuse or patchy areas of high signal intensity on T2-weighted and STIR sequences within affected skeletal muscles (deltoids, biceps, quadriceps, gastrocnemius), accompanied by intense heterogeneous intramuscular contrast enhancement on T1-gadolinium images, reflecting active acute infectious myositis

High-Frequency Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Diffuse hypoechoic thickening and swelling of skeletal muscle bundles with loss of normal fibrillar pennate architecture and localized intramuscular fluid collections

Soft Tissue Plain Radiography: In remote, longstanding cases (years later), fine, minute, punctate or oval calcifications (0.5-1.0 mm) oriented parallel to muscle fibers representing calcified nurse cell-larva complexes
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy (Diagnostic Gold Standard - Deltoid or Gastrocnemius, performed 3-4 weeks post-infection): Fresh muscle crush preparation (compressorium technique) or histopathologic examination: pathognomonic coiled, spiral nematode larva (Trichinella spiralis, measuring ~1 mm long) encysted within an altered skeletal muscle cell known as a 'Nurse Cell'

Nurse Cell Complex Histology: The infected myofiber loses its transverse striations, undergoes basophilic transformation, develops multiple enlarged vesicular nuclei, and becomes enveloped by a thick, eosinophilic collagenous capsule (0.3-0.5 mm) with a surrounding network of newly formed capillaries (hyperangiogenesis)

Surrounding Tissue Reaction: Intense interstitial myositis with a prominent infiltrate composed primarily of eosinophils, histiocytes, lymphocytes, and occasional multinucleated giant cells; late stages demonstrate complete larva necrosis and dystrophic shell-like calcification of the nurse cell complex
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Classic foodborne parasitic myositis presenting with the hallmark bedside tetrad of periorbital edema, trismus/myalgia, high fever, and subungual splinter hemorrhages, symmetrical muscle inflammation on MRI, and pathognomonic coiled larvae in nurse cells on muscle biopsy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tuberculosis
clinical_manifestations: Scrofula (scrofuloderma): massive cervical lymphadenitis forming firm, cold, matted masses that break down into chronic draining sinus tracts with bluish undermined borders
Lupus vulgaris: reddish-brown gelatinous plaques on face/neck demonstrating classic 'apple-jelly' nodules upon glass diascopy
Erythema induratum of Bazin: painful, violaceous nodules on the posterior lower calves that ulcerate
Pott disease physical gibbus deformity (sharp angular kyphosis of the spine due to anterior vertebral collapse)
Miliary TB: choroidal tubercles on fundoscopy
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / CT: Apical and posterior segment upper lobe cavitary lesions with thick irregular walls; 'tree-in-bud' branching centrilobular opacities (endobronchial spread); miliary mottling (1-3 mm diffuse uniform micronodules); Ghon focus and calcified Ranke complex
Spine MRI / CT (Pott Disease): Destruction of adjacent anterior vertebral bodies and intervening intervertebral disc; prevertebral and paraspinal 'cold abscess' with thick peripheral rim enhancement
Brain MRI: Intense basilar meningeal enhancement, tuberculomas (ring-enhancing lesions with central T2 hypointensity), vasculitic infarcts
pathology_manifestations: Histology: Caseating (necrotizing) granulomas with central amorphous eosinophilic caseous necrosis surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells (horseshoe-shaped nuclei), and lymphocytes; positive Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast) or auramine-rhodamine fluorescence staining
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The supreme visual infectious disease with iconic bedside lesions (scrofula, lupus vulgaris, Pott gibbus) and landmark radiology (cavitary upper lobe CT, miliary TB, spinal Pott cold abscesses).

Infectious Diseases.name: Tularemia
clinical_manifestations: Ulceroglandular tularemia (most common clinical form, ~75-85%): Punched-out, painful, indurated cutaneous ulcer with sharply circumscribed, raised, erythematous borders and a deep, necrotic or yellow-slough base at the arthropod bite or animal handling site

Disproportionate, massive, tender regional lymphadenopathy (epitrochlear, axillary, cervical, or inguinal) that rapidly enlarges, becomes fluctuant ('bubo-like'), and may spontaneously suppurate and drain

Oculoglandular tularemia (Parinaud oculoglandular syndrome): Severe, unilateral, painful conjunctivitis with yellowish chemotic granulomatous ulcers on the palpebral conjunctiva, periorbital edema, and massive ipsilateral preauricular/submandibular lymphadenopathy
Oropharyngeal tularemia: Severe membranous pharyngotonsillitis with deep tonsillar ulcers and painful cervical lymphadenopathy
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT / Ultrasound of Lymph Nodes: Markedly enlarged, matted, conglomerate regional lymph node complexes with prominent peripheral rim enhancement and central low-attenuation cystic liquefactive necrosis (suppurative lymphadenitis) with extensive surrounding soft-tissue edema

Chest CT (Pneumonic / Systemic Tularemia): Patchy lobar, segmental, or subsegmental consolidation with air bronchograms, cavitary pulmonary nodules, pleural effusion, and prominent, asymmetric, necrotic hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Abdominal Contrast CT: Multiple small, round, low-attenuation microabscesses or granulomas scattered throughout the spleen and liver parenchyma
pathology_manifestations: Lymph node excision / core biopsy (H&E stain): Classic progression of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation: central confluent caseous-like or coagulative suppurative necrosis surrounded by an inner palisade of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated Langhans giant cells, encased within a dense outer cuff of lymphocytes and plasma cells (closely resembling tuberculosis or cat scratch disease)

Microbiologic staining: Francisella tularensis are extremely tiny (0.2 x 0.7 um), poorly staining, pleomorphic, non-motile Gram-negative coccobacilli; rarely visualized on standard Gram stain; definitive identification by direct immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, or real-time PCR
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-consequence zoonotic pathogen presenting with punched-out inoculation ulcers, massive suppurative regional lymphadenopathy, cavitary bronchopneumonia with necrotic hilar nodes on CT, and stellate necrotizing granulomas on biopsy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-Azar)
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Clinical Pentad: (1) Massive, progressive, non-tender splenomegaly (splenic edge frequently descending below the umbilicus into the right lower quadrant/pelvis); (2) Moderate, smooth, non-tender hepatomegaly; (3) Prolonged, irregular, undulating high fever with double daily peaks (dromedary curve); (4) Profound cachexia, temporal wasting, and severe emaciation contrasting with the protuberant belly; (5) Characteristic gray-black or ashen hyperpigmentation of the face, hands, feet, and abdominal midline ('kala-azar' = black sickness)
Pancytopenia Manifestations: Mucosal bleeding, epistaxis, petechiae, severe pallor from anemia, and secondary bacterial infections (noma/cancrum oris, pneumonia)

Post-Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL): Chronic dermatologic complication arising months to years after successful visceral cure, characterized by hypopigmented macules evolving into erythematous butterfly-distribution facial plaques and nodular granulomas resembling lepromatous leprosy
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound: Massive, homogeneous splenomegaly (frequently >20 cm in craniocaudal dimension) with normal or mildly hypoechoic architecture, occasional focal hypoechoic splenic microabscesses or infarctions, hepatomegaly with smooth contours, and generalized intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy (porta hepatis, retroperitoneum, and mesentery)

Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT: Huge splenomegaly displacing the stomach and left kidney, patent portal and splenic veins without cirrhotic distortion, and retroperitoneal/peripancreatic lymphadenopathy
Chest Radiography: Secondary opportunistic bronchopneumonia and basilar atelectasis from marked diaphragmatic splinting by the enlarged spleen
pathology_manifestations: Bone Marrow, Splenic, or Lymph Node Aspirate: Giemsa- or Leishman-stained smears demonstrate abundant intracellular and extracellular Leishman-Donovan (LD) Bodies (Amastigotes); amastigotes are tiny (2-4 um), round-to-oval organisms lacking a free flagellum, containing a prominent spherical nucleus and a distinct, pathognomonic, rod-shaped or bar-shaped organelle termed the kinetoplast (oriented perpendicularly or obliquely to the nucleus)

Reticuloendothelial Hyperplasia: Marked proliferation of macrophages and histiocytes engorged with hundreds of amastigotes throughout the red pulp of the spleen, hepatic Kupffer cells, and bone marrow cords; marked bone marrow erythroid, myeloid, and megakaryocytic hypoplasia with pronounced reactive polyclonal plasmacytosis

Immunodiagnostics: Recombinant rK39 immunochromatographic rapid strip test positive for anti-leishmanial antibodies; kinetoplast DNA (kDNA) real-time PCR demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Neglected tropical protozoan disease featuring massive splenomegaly, characteristic skin hyperpigmentation ('black fever'), ultrasound documentation of organomegaly, and pathognomonic amastigotes with rod-shaped kinetoplasts on bone marrow/splenic aspirate.

Infectious Diseases.name: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
clinical_manifestations: A chronic crateriform ulcer with a rolled edge on an exposed site
Mucocutaneous disease: destructive nasal and lip ulcers, filed as the mucosal site of the same infection
radiological_manifestations: No routine radiology; facial CT only for destructive mucocutaneous bone loss
pathology_manifestations: Dermal amastigotes in macrophages on Giemsa or biopsy
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Protozoal ulcer with a classic clinical photograph and a visible parasite.

Infectious Diseases.name: Herpes Zoster
clinical_manifestations: Dermatomal vesicles on an erythematous base that do not cross the midline
Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with a Hutchinson sign on the nose
Disseminated zoster in an immunocompromised patient remains the same disease
radiological_manifestations: MRI only for the rare zoster myelitis or vasculopathy complication, which is not a separate topic
pathology_manifestations: Multinucleated keratinocytes and acantholysis; PCR of vesicle fluid confirms VZV
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Reactivation infection with a dermatomal photograph. Postherpetic neuralgia is a symptom and is not a topic.

Infectious Diseases.name: Mpox
clinical_manifestations: Firm deep-seated umbilicated pustules in the same stage across a region
Anogenital and oral mucosal lesions in the 2022 clade pattern
Palmar and plantar pustules
radiological_manifestations: No routine imaging; proctitis MRI is a complication, not the topic
pathology_manifestations: Orthopox viral cytopathic effect; PCR distinguishes mpox from varicella
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Poxvirus whose umbilicated pustule photographs are the diagnostic image.

Infectious Diseases.name: Measles
clinical_manifestations: Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa opposite the molars
Cephalocaudal morbilliform eruption that becomes confluent on the face
Conjunctivitis and a toxic febrile appearance
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph only if pneumonia complicates the illness; the gallery is the spots and rash
pathology_manifestations: Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells in lymphoid tissue when biopsied, which is uncommon
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Viral exanthem with two photographable hallmarks, Koplik spots and the confluent rash.

Infectious Diseases.name: Respiratory Diphtheria
clinical_manifestations: Adherent gray pharyngeal pseudomembrane that bleeds when lifted
Bull neck from cervical edema
Cutaneous diphtheria ulcers are a site of the same infection, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: Neck soft-tissue radiograph or endoscopy images of airway membrane when intubation is considered
pathology_manifestations: Toxin-producing Corynebacterium diphtheriae on culture; the membrane is necrotic epithelium and fibrin
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Toxin disease with a membrane photograph and a bull-neck photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Yaws
clinical_manifestations: Primary mother yaw: a papillomatous raspberry lesion
Secondary disseminated papillomas and palmoplantar keratoderma
Late gangosa nasal destruction and saber tibia, kept as late sites of yaws rather than new topics
radiological_manifestations: Tibial radiograph: periosteal new bone in late osteoperiostitis
pathology_manifestations: Epidermal hyperplasia with treponemes on silver stain; serology crosses with syphilis, so geography and the photograph matter
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Endemic treponematosis with papilloma photographs and a late bone film, distinct from venereal syphilis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Orf
clinical_manifestations: A targetoid nodule on a finger after sheep or goat exposure, evolving through macule, target, weeping nodule, and crust
Usually a single lesion on the hand
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Ballooning keratinocytes and eosinophilic inclusions; parapoxvirus PCR confirms
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Zoonotic poxvirus with a staged hand photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease
clinical_manifestations: Oval gray vesicles on the palms, soles, and buttocks
Painful oral vesicles and shallow ulcers
Onychomadesis weeks later is a sequela, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Reticular degeneration of the epidermis; enterovirus PCR when needed
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Enteroviral illness with a distribution-specific vesicle photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Cutaneous Larva Migrans
clinical_manifestations: Intensely pruritic, erythematous, elevated, serpiginous, winding, snake-like burrowing cutaneous tracks ("creeping eruption") advancing millimeters to centimeters per day

Acral and dependent anatomical distribution: predilection for barefoot-exposed surfaces including the dorsum and soles of the feet, interdigital web spaces, buttocks, thighs, and hands following contact with tropical beach sand or moist soil contaminated with animal feces

Progression of lesions: initial erythematous pruritic papule at the larval penetration site evolving into a tortuous, raised, red or pink linear track (1-3 mm wide) with localized vesicular or bullous formation along the burrow

Excoriation, secondary impetiginization (Staphylococcus aureus / Streptococcus pyogenes superinfection), and severe sleep-disrupting nocturnal pruritus caused by trapped non-human hookworm larvae (Ancylostoma braziliense, Ancylostoma caninum)
radiological_manifestations: Dermoscopy (Epiluminescence Microscopy): Direct non-invasive visualization of the translucent nematode larva within the advancing terminus of the burrow; demonstrates brownish-yellow translucent oval structures with red dots and empty winding tracks with white scales
Reflectance Confocal Microscopy (RCM): In vivo visualization of round-to-oval refractile structures corresponding to hookworm larvae within the stratum spinosum and stratum basale
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology (rarely required for diagnosis): Biopsy of the advancing edge demonstrates an intraepidermal or subepidermal burrow with marked epidermal spongiosis, necrotic keratinocytes, and intraepidermal eosinophilic microabscesses
