Inflammatory infiltrate: Dense dermal perivascular and interstitial infiltrate packed with eosinophils, mast cells, and mononuclear cells; the migrating larva is rarely caught on single sections due to its location 1-2 cm ahead of the visible inflammatory erythema
Peripheral Blood Laboratory: Peripheral eosinophilia (>500 cells/mcL) in 20-30% of extensive or disseminated cases
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield parasitic tropical infection with indelible, pathognomonic clinical photographs of winding, serpiginous creeping eruption tracks across bare feet and buttocks.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rhinoscleroma
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, progressive granulomatous bacterial infection of the upper respiratory tract caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae subsp. rhinoscleromatis
Triphasic clinical evolution: 1) Catarrhal/atrophic phase with persistent purulent rhinorrhea and crusting mimicking ozena; 2) Granulomatous/hypertrophic phase; 3) Cicatricial/sclerotic phase
Granulomatous phase physical findings: progressive development of woody, rock-hard, non-tender, reddish-blue nodular infiltrates in the nasal mucosa and vestibule

Pathognomonic facial deformity: "Hebra nose" or tapir snout deformity—striking widening, bulbous expansion, and woody induration of the lower half of the external nose with complete obliteration of the anterior nares
Extension into upper airway: infiltration and destruction of the nasal septum, hard/soft palate, uvula, and subglottic larynx leading to stridor, airway compromise, and hoarseness
radiological_manifestations: Maxillofacial & Neck CT: Soft-tissue masses with homogeneous or heterogeneous contrast enhancement occupying the nasal cavity, maxillary sinuses, and nasopharynx, with destruction and remodeling of the nasal septum and turbinates without regional lymphadenopathy
Laryngeal & Neck CT: Circumferential subglottic soft-tissue stenosis and concentric tracheal narrowing ("hour-glass" trachea)

Head & Neck MRI: Soft-tissue masses demonstrating intermediate signal on T1-weighted images and markedly hypointense signal on T2-weighted images corresponding to dense fibrosis and hypercellular granulomatous tissue
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy of Nasal Mass (Pathognomonic Histology): Diagnostic "Mikulicz cells"—massively distended, pale, foamy or vacuolated macrophages (20-100 μm) with reticulated cytoplasm and eccentric nuclei
Special Staining: Warthin-Starry silver, Giemsa, and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stains directly reveal intracellular Gram-negative bacilli packed inside the cytoplasm of Mikulicz cells

Plasma Cell Inclusions: Abundant surrounding plasma cells with prominent Russell bodies (eosinophilic globular proteinaceous immunoglobulin inclusions) and dense interlacing collagen fibrosis in the cicatricial stage
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Striking infectious disease featuring unmistakable photographic facial deformities (woody Hebra nose / tapir snout obliterating the nares) and diagnostic Mikulicz cells on histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rhinosporidiosis
clinical_manifestations: Chronic granulomatous mucocutaneous infection caused by the aquatic mesomycetozoan protoctist Rhinosporidium seeberi (acquired from bathing in stagnant pond water in South Asia and tropical regions)

Pathognomonic fleshy mucocutaneous lesions: friable, vascular, sessile or pedunculated, mulberry-like or "strawberry-like" polypoid masses protruding from the nasal cavity (septum, inferior turbinate) or conjunctiva

Characteristic surface appearance: bright red, glistening, vascular masses covered with visible tiny white, yellowish, or greyish pinhead-sized dots representing mature subepithelial sporangia ready to rupture

Ocular presentation (Oculosporidiosis): bright red polypoid vascular mass originating from the palpebral conjunctiva, caruncle, or lacrimal sac with foreign body sensation, bloody epiphora, and eversion of the eyelid
Associated signs: recurrent unilateral epistaxis, partial or total nasal obstruction, serosanguinous discharge, and visible mass hanging from the anterior nares or dangling into the oropharynx
radiological_manifestations: Paranasal Sinus CT: Well-defined, hyperattenuating, polypoid soft-tissue mass filling the nasal cavity with focal remodeling or thinning of adjacent bony sinus walls without frank osseous invasion

Facial MRI: Intensely enhancing lobulated nasal mass showing heterogeneous intermediate T1 signal and hypointense to isointense T2 signal with punctate hyperintense foci corresponding to cystic sporangia
CT Angiography: Conspicuous hypervascularity with rich arterial feeder vessels (typically from sphenopalatine and facial arteries) requiring preoperative consideration of embolization
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy / Surgical Excision (Diagnostic Hallmark): Enormous, thick-walled, globular sporangia (100 to 450 μm in diameter) embedded within hyperplastic, vascularized mucosal stroma
Sporangiospores: Mature sporangia are packed with thousands (up to 12,000) of round, basophilic endospores (6-7 μm), seen in various stages of maturation with an apical operculum / germ pore

Histochemical Stains: Sporangial walls stain intensely with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS), Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), and Mucicarmine; surrounded by a chronic granulomatous reaction with histiocytes, foreign-body giant cells, and vascular granulation tissue
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Visually unmistakable tropical infectious entity featuring classic clinical photographs of friable strawberry-like bleeding nasal polyps studded with white dots, verified by giant mature sporangia on histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Clostridial Myonecrosis
clinical_manifestations: Hyperacute, rapidly fatal necrotizing soft-tissue and deep muscular infection occurring post-trauma, post-surgery, or spontaneously (Clostridium septicum in occult colon cancer)
Excruciating, out-of-proportion, sudden pain at the injury site followed rapidly by systemic toxic shock, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, and mental apathy
Cutaneous physical hallmarks: skin overlying the infected muscle rapidly turns from pale to tense, shiny, bronze or copper-colored, progressing to dark purple, black, and frank cutaneous necrosis
Large, tense hemorrhagic bullae containing thin, dark, reddish-brown, sweet-foul-smelling "dishwater" fluid

Palpable soft-tissue crepitus extending rapidly along anatomical fascial planes; infected muscle exposed at surgery appears pale, edematous, fails to bleed on incision, and does not contract upon electrical stimulation ("cooked meat" appearance)
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography: Pathognomonic feathery, branching, linear lucencies of extensive gas dissecting longitudinally along muscle fibers and fascial planes far beyond the clinical borders of trauma

Computed Tomography (CT of Involved Extremity / Body Region): Extensive intramuscular gas pockets (subcutaneous emphysema and myonecrosis), fascial fluid collections, and absence of muscular contrast enhancement indicating complete muscular devitalization

Emergency Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS): "Cobblestoning" of subcutaneous tissues with bright, hyperechoic foci of gas producing dirty acoustic shadowing and reverberation artifacts within muscle bellies
pathology_manifestations: Emergency Exudate / Muscle Gram Stain (Immediate Diagnostic Clue): Abundant, large, thick, blunt-ended, rectangular Gram-positive bacilli ("boxcar-shaped" rods) accompanied by a dramatic, striking *absence of polymorphonuclear leukocytes* (leukocytes are rapidly lysed by clostridial alpha-toxin and theta-toxin)

Surgical Muscle Histopathology: Extensive coagulative necrosis of skeletal muscle bundles with loss of nuclear staining (ghost myocytes); gas bubbles dissecting myofibrillar architecture; marked intravascular thrombosis and capillary destruction without inflammatory infiltrate
Microbiology: Rapid double zone of beta-hemolysis on anaerobic sheep blood agar produced by Clostridium perfringens
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic emergency surgical infection defined by dramatic bedside physical images (bronze skin discoloration, hemorrhagic dishwater bullae, exposed cooked-meat muscle) and pathognomonic feathery gas patterns on plain radiography and CT.

Infectious Diseases.name: Acute Fulminant Meningococcemia and Purpura Fulminans
clinical_manifestations: Catastrophic, hyperacute invasive bacterial sepsis caused by Neisseria meningitidis with rapid progression from mild febrile illness to septic shock and death within hours
Initial rash: faint, discrete, pink-to-red maculopapular or petechial eruption concentrated on the trunk, lower extremities, and conjunctiva

Rapid evolution to purpura fulminans: explosive coalescence of petechiae into extensive, jagged, angular, stellate ecchymoses and large purpuric plaques with central dusky, gunmetal-gray or black cutaneous ischemic infarction

Symmetrical peripheral gangrene: acute ischemic dry gangrene of the digits, hands, feet, nose, and earlobes resulting from widespread microvascular thrombosis and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)

Endocrine collapse (Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome): acute fulminant adrenal crisis caused by bilateral massive adrenal hemorrhage, manifesting with profound refractory hypotension, hypoglycemia, and vascular collapse
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal CT / Ultrasound (Emergency Diagnostic Clue): Bilaterally enlarged, round or oval adrenal glands demonstrating high-attenuation intraparenchymal hematoma on non-contrast CT and absence of normal post-contrast adrenal enhancement (pathognomonic Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome)
Extremity Doppler Ultrasound: Extensive occlusion of distal peripheral arterial and venous microvasculature with preservation of proximal major conduit vessels
Chest Radiography: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with bilateral confluent fluffy alveolar infiltrates and cardiomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Skin Biopsy / Tzanck-like Slit-Skin Smear: Extensive occlusive microvascular thrombosis of dermal capillaries and arterioles by dense fibrin thrombi; marked extravasation of erythrocytes into the dermis with ischemic necrosis of the overlying epidermis
Pathognomonic Gram Stain of Skin Lesion: Gram-negative coffee-bean-shaped diplococci directly visualized within the cytoplasm of endothelial cells and neutrophils lining thrombosed dermal vessels
Autopsy Pathology: Bilateral hemorrhagic destruction of the adrenal cortex with diffuse petechial hemorrhages into epicardium, pleura, and peritoneum
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield critical care infectious disease featuring undeniable, unforgettable photographs of stellate purpura fulminans lesions and peripheral acral gangrene, paired with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage on CT.

Infectious Diseases.name: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
clinical_manifestations: Systemic bacteremic complication of mucosal Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection (frequently asymptomatic primary urogenital, anorectal, or pharyngeal colonization)
Classic clinical triad of the Arthritis-Dermatitis Syndrome: migratory polyarthralgias, acute tenosynovitis, and distinctive cutaneous pustular lesions
Pathognomonic skin lesions: sparse (typically 2 to 10 lesions total), painless, discrete lesions located on the distal extremities, fingers, palms, toes, and over joints

Morphological progression of cutaneous lesions: initial erythematous or purpuric macules evolving rapidly into tender hemorrhagic vesicles or necrotic, gray-centered, gunmetal-colored pustules on an erythematous base

Acute severe tenosynovitis: simultaneous, dramatic, visible swelling and exquisite tenderness along multiple tendon sheaths (predominantly wrist extensors, dorsum of hands, ankles, and Achilles tendons)
Second phase: localized purulent monoarthritis or oligoarthritis (most frequently the knee, ankle, or wrist) with hot, tense, swollen joint effusion
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Dramatic thickening and distension of tendon sheaths with anechoic/hypoechoic fluid collections, synovial proliferation, and intense hypervascularity on Power Doppler (tenosynovitis of extensor pollicis, extensor digitorum, or tibialis anterior)
Joint MRI: Marked synovial enhancement, joint effusion, and periarticular soft-tissue and tenosynovial contrast enhancement without initial subchondral bony erosions
Plain Radiography of Involved Joints: Soft-tissue swelling and periarticular osteopenia; joint space preservation in acute presentation
pathology_manifestations: Synovial Fluid Analysis: Markedly purulent synovial fluid with leukocytosis (typically 30,000 to 100,000 WBC/mcL, >90% polymorphonuclear neutrophils); low glucose level

Microbiology: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci identified inside polymorphonuclear neutrophils on synovial fluid or skin lesion smear; high diagnostic yield on NAAT (nucleic acid amplification testing) from mucosal and synovial sites; chocolate agar / Thayer-Martin medium culture
Skin Biopsy: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis or microvascular thrombosis in the upper dermis with subepidermal pustule formation packed with neutrophils
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield infectious disease defined by a classic physical exam triad: sparse gunmetal-gray necrotic pustules on the extremities, severe visible wrist/ankle tenosynovitis, and acute purulent arthritis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Human African Trypanosomiasis
clinical_manifestations: Vector-borne protozoan infection transmitted by the bite of the tsetse fly (Glossina species) in sub-Saharan Africa, occurring in West African form (Trypanosoma brucei gambiense) and acute East African form (T. b. rhodesiense)
Primary inoculation lesion (Trypanosomal chancre): painful, indurated, fiery-red nodule or ulcer (2-5 cm) at the bite site appearing within 5-15 days, exuding serous fluid teeming with parasites
Stage 1 (Hemolymphatic stage) hallmark: Winterbottom sign—pathognomonic painless, rubbery, firm, mobile enlargement of the posterior cervical lymph nodes along the posterior triangle of the neck
Systemic signs: undulating recurrent fevers, striking pruritus, transient circinate or annular erythema ("trypanids"), and progressive facial and periorbital edema

Stage 2 (Meningoencephalitic stage): inversion of the circadian sleep-wake cycle (daytime somnolence and nighttime insomnia), progressive choreiform movements, ataxia, tremors, personality deterioration, and terminal coma
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Stage 2 Encephalitic Phase): Bilateral, symmetrical, patchy or confluent T2/FLAIR hyperintensities within the basal ganglia, internal capsules, brainstem tegmentum, and periventricular deep cerebral white matter
Post-Contrast T1 MRI: Punctate or diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement reflecting chronic lymphoplasmacytic meningoencephalitis
Neck Soft-Tissue Ultrasound: Multiple discrete, round, hypoechoic lymph nodes in the posterior cervical chains with prominent central hilar vascularity
pathology_manifestations: Microscopy (Diagnostic Hallmark): Direct microscopic identification of motile, slender, flagellated trypomastigotes (15-30 μm) with an undulating membrane and anterior flagellum in Giemsa-stained thin/thick blood films, lymph node aspirate, or chancre exudate

CSF Examination (Staging Hallmark): Elevated CSF WBC count (>5 WBC/mcL) or direct visualization of trypanosomes; presence of pathognomonic "Mott cells" (morula cells of Mott)—plasma cells distended with multiple spherical Russell-body-like eosinophilic IgM inclusions
Lymph Node Biopsy: Follicular hyperplasia with sinus histiocytosis, marked plasma cell infiltration, and high concentrations of IgM
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual tropical disease featuring unmistakable photographic signs (primary trypanosomal chancre, pathognomonic Winterbottom posterior cervical adenopathy) and diagnostic flagellated trypomastigotes on Giemsa smear.

Infectious Diseases.name: Crusted Scabies
clinical_manifestations: Highly contagious, severe, exuberant hyperinfestation by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis occurring in individuals with impaired cell-mediated immunity (HIV, HTLV-1, organ transplant, systemic corticosteroids) or sensory/neurological deficits (Down syndrome, leprosy, dementia)
Striking physical examination: massive, thick, adherent, chalky white-to-yellow-gray, hyperkeratotic, warty, fissured crusts resembling severe psoriasis, Darier disease, or pachyonychia congenita
Extensive anatomical distribution: predilection for the palms, soles, scalp, face, ears, elbows, knees, and beneath deformed subungual nail beds; can progress to generalized exfoliative erythroderma
Severely deformed, dystrophic, thickened nails with massive subungual hyperkeratotic debris ("oyster-shell" appearance) harboring millions of mites

Paradoxical absence or minimal degree of pruritus despite teeming millions of mites (due to deficient host cell-mediated immune response), contributing to delayed diagnosis and explosive institutional outbreaks
radiological_manifestations: Dermoscopy (Diagnostic Bedside Hallmark): Pathognomonic "delta-wing jet" or "delta-glider" sign—dark, pigmented triangular structure (representing the anterior body, head, and anterior legs of the mite) located at the end of a whitish, tortuous, S-shaped burrow
High-Frequency Skin Ultrasound: Massive hyperechoic thickening of the stratum corneum with multiple acoustic micro-discontinuities corresponding to intra-stratum burrows
pathology_manifestations: Microscopic Examination of Skin Scrapings (Immediate Diagnostic Gold Standard): Direct potassium hydroxide (KOH) or mineral oil mount of superficial crust scrapings reveals an astonishing horde of hundreds to thousands of live, eight-legged adult mites, six-legged larvae, oval translucent eggs, and brownish-black oval fecal pellets (scybala)
Skin Punch Biopsy: Enormous compact hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis of the stratum corneum completely riddled with hundreds of round-to-oval tunnels and cross-sections of Sarcoptes scabiei mites
Dermal changes: Marked epidermal acanthosis, papillomatosis, and a dense mixed dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, histiocytes, and lymphocytes
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield contagious parasitic dermatosis with dramatic, unmistakable clinical photographs (massive hyperkeratotic chalky crusts over palms/soles and oyster-shell dystrophic nails) and millions of mites visible on direct KOH microscopy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Varicella (Chickenpox)
clinical_manifestations: Crops of polymorphous vesicles on erythematous bases ('dewdrop on a rose petal') in simultaneous stages of healing and eruption
Centripetal distribution beginning on scalp, face, and trunk with mucosal involvement
Intensely pruritic lesions progressing macule to vesicle to crust over 3-5 days
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph in varicella pneumonia: diffuse small nodular infiltrates that may calcify as innumerable tiny pulmonary nodules years after infection
pathology_manifestations: Intraepidermal acantholytic vesicle with multinucleated giant cells and steel-gray nuclear inclusions on Tzanck smear
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Primary VZV exanthem with a pathognomonic polymorphous vesicle crop; distinct disease from covered herpes zoster (reactivation).

Infectious Diseases.name: Scarlet Fever
clinical_manifestations: Diffuse finely papular 'sandpaper' scarlatiniform eruption beginning on neck and trunk and accentuated in skin folds (Pastia lines)
Flushed face with circumoral pallor; white-strawberry then beefy-red strawberry tongue
Desquamation of palms and soles, especially fingers, in convalescence
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; suppurative complications (peritonsillar abscess) imaged as needed
pathology_manifestations: Neutrophilic and spongiotic interface dermatitis; diagnosis is clinical with positive streptococcal testing
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Single-agent toxin disease defined by the sandpaper rash, strawberry tongue, Pastia lines, and convalescent desquamation.

Infectious Diseases.name: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Bright-red confluent 'slapped cheek' facial erythema with circumoral sparing
Symmetric lacy reticular maculopapular eruption on extensor arms and trunk, recurring with heat or sun
Prodrome of fever, headache, and coryza 1-2 weeks before the exanthem
radiological_manifestations: In hydrops fetalis from B19 infection: fetal ultrasound shows edema, effusions, and cardiomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Minimal lymphocytic perivascular dermatitis; diagnosis serologic (parvovirus B19 IgM)
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The rash is the disease definition: slapped-cheek erythema plus a lacy reticular exanthem.

Infectious Diseases.name: Mumps
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral or unilateral parotid swelling obliterating the angle of the jaw and elevating the earlobe
Erythema and edema of Stensen duct orifice
Orchitis with testicular swelling in postpubertal males
radiological_manifestations: Salivary ultrasound: enlarged heterogeneous parotid glands with hyperemia and reactive nodes; no pathognomonic sign
pathology_manifestations: Lymphocytic parotitis; diagnosis clinical/serologic
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The parotid swelling that lifts the earlobe off the jaw angle is a classic inspection diagnosis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Periorificial (mouth, nose, eyes) crusting and radial fissuring with tender diffuse erythema
Superficial intraepidermal desquamation with positive Nikolsky sign that conspicuously spares mucous membranes
Flaccid bullae and sheet-like peeling in infants and young children
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Subcorneal granular-layer split caused by exfoliative toxins A/B; minimal inflammatory infiltrate distinguishing it from SJS/TEN full-thickness necrosis
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Toxin-mediated exfoliative disease recognizable by periorificial crusting and mucosa-sparing superficial desquamation.

Infectious Diseases.name: Acute Epiglottitis
clinical_manifestations: Cherry-red, edematous epiglottis at laryngoscopy in a drooling, toxic child
Tripod or sniffing positioning with dysphagia, drooling, and muffled 'hot potato' voice
Abrupt-onset stridor and respiratory distress with little cough
radiological_manifestations: Lateral soft-tissue neck radiograph: 'thumbprint sign' - a thickened epiglottis obliterating the vallecula with loss of the normal epiglottic contour
pathology_manifestations: Supraglottic cellulitis with polymorphonuclear infiltrate; blood and epiglottic cultures may grow Haemophilus influenzae type b or other agents
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Named emergency with a photographic cherry-red epiglottis and the pathognomonic thumbprint sign.

Infectious Diseases.name: Toxic Shock Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Diffuse macular 'sunburn' erythroderma involving palms and soles
Delayed desquamation of palms, soles, and fingertips one to two weeks after onset
Nonpurulent conjunctival and mucosal (oropharyngeal, vaginal) hyperemia with fever and shock
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Superficial perivascular and spongiotic dermatitis; toxin-mediated (TSST-1, streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins)
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Criteria-defined toxin disease with a recognizable erythroderma-plus-desquamation phenotype.

Infectious Diseases.name: Poliomyelitis
clinical_manifestations: Asymmetric flaccid paralysis of proximal limb muscles with preserved sensation
Limb atrophy and shortened hypoplastic limb as late sequela (post-polio residual)
Bubbling respirations and bulbar weakness in bulbospinal disease
radiological_manifestations: MRI spinal cord: bilateral anterior-horn T2 hyperintensity ('owl-eye' anterior horn) in the paralytic phase
pathology_manifestations: Loss and chromatolysis of anterior-horn motor neurons with perivascular inflammation
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Near-eradicated enterovirus disease with iconic asymmetric flaccid paralysis and anterior-horn MRI signature; archival image base.

Infectious Diseases.name: Smallpox (Variola)
clinical_manifestations: Synchronous centrifugal exanthem: firm deep-seated papules evolving through vesicle to umbilicated pustule to crust, all at the same stage
Dense lesions on face, palms, and soles with high fever and severe backache
Survivors bear characteristic depressed 'pock' scars
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Cytoplasmic Guarnieri inclusion bodies in epithelial cells; variola confirmed by electron microscopy/PCR
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Eradicated orthopoxvirus disease with the classic synchronous centrifugal pustular exanthem (dracunculiasis eradicated-disease precedent).

Infectious Diseases.name: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection
clinical_manifestations: 'Blueberry-muffin' dermal erythropoiesis purpuric nodules at birth
Microcephaly, petechiae, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, and sensorineural hearing loss
Periventricular (rather than diffuse) intracranial calcification pattern
radiological_manifestations: Neurosonography/CT: periventricular eggshell-like intracranial calcifications; lenticulostriate vasculopathy; white-matter abnormalities and polymicrogyria on MRI
pathology_manifestations: Cytomegalic 'owl-eye' intranuclear inclusions in affected tissues and placenta; direct fetal/neonatal PCR
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Most common congenital infection; periventricular eggshell calcifications and blueberry-muffin phenotype distinguish it from congenital toxoplasmosis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Classic triad: congenital cataract (cloudy cornea/pupil), sensorineural deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus
'Blueberry-muffin' extramedullary hematopoiesis nodules and purpura
Growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, and thrombocytopenia
radiological_manifestations: Salt-and-pepper retinopathy on fundoscopy (normal vision despite pigmentary changes); cardiac echo: PDA and peripheral pulmonary stenosis; neonatal US/CT for microcephaly and calcifications
pathology_manifestations: Chronic villitis and placental infection; persistent viral shedding demonstrable in infant secretions
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The archetypal teratogenic infection with cataract, cardiac, and salt-and-pepper fundus imagery.

Infectious Diseases.name: Congenital Syphilis
clinical_manifestations: Hutchinson teeth (barrel-shaped, notched incisors) and mulberry molars as late stigmata
Saddle nose, frontal bossing, rhagades (periorificial scars), and saber shins
Snuffles, hepatosplenomegaly, pemphigus syphiliticus (bullous eruption), and condylomata lata in early disease
radiological_manifestations: Long-bone radiographs: Wimberger metaphyseal lucent bands and bony destruction (medial tibial margin), periostitis, and osteochondritis; interstitial keratitis on slit-lamp in late disease
pathology_manifestations: Placental spirochetes on silver stain; dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in lesions
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Distinct congenital phenotype (Hutchinson teeth, saddle nose, Wimberger sign) beyond covered acquired syphilis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
clinical_manifestations: Neonatal triad: chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial calcifications
Hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, and maculopapular exanthem at birth
Bilateral macular-predominant retinochoroiditis scars as the characteristic late finding
radiological_manifestations: Diffuse (rather than periventricular) intracranial calcifications on CT; hydrocephalus on neurosonography/CT; 'white-centered' or focal chorioretinal lesions on fundoscopy
pathology_manifestations: Tachyzoites and Toxoplasma cysts in retina and placenta; confirmed by amniotic-fluid/infant PCR and serology
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Distinct congenital phenotype (diffuse calcifications, macular chorioretinitis) versus covered reactivation ocular toxoplasmosis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Congenital Zika Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Severe microcephaly with a collapsed skull vault and redundant scalp folds
Hypertonia, arthrogryposis, and clenched hands with camptodactyly
Macular chorioretinal scarring and pigment mottling on fundoscopy
radiological_manifestations: Cranial ultrasound/CT/MRI: subcortical and intracranial calcifications, ventriculomegaly, callosal and cortical malformations, and brainstem hypoplasia
pathology_manifestations: Zika virus detection by RT-PCR/immunohistochemistry in placental and fetal tissues
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive collapsed-skull microcephaly, arthrogryposis, and macular imaging produced a large open-access image corpus.

Infectious Diseases.name: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus Infection
clinical_manifestations: Grouped vesicles on erythematous bases on scalp (including fetal scalp-electrode sites), face, and trunk in the skin-eye-mouth form
Oral ulceration and keratoconjunctivitis
Afebrile neonate with seizures or fulminant hepatitis signaling CNS/disseminated disease
radiological_manifestations: Cranial MRI: temporal-predominant restricted diffusion and hemorrhagic encephalitis pattern in neonatal HSV CNS disease
pathology_manifestations: Multinucleated giant cells and Cowdry A inclusions on Tzanck smear; HSV PCR from lesions or CSF
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Recognizable SEM vesicle crops and scalp-electrode-site lesions; temporal neonatal encephalitis is a distinct imaging signature.

Infectious Diseases.name: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)
clinical_manifestations: Barking 'seal-like' cough, inspiratory stridor, and hoarseness in a toddler, worse at night
Low-grade fever and coryza; absence of drooling or toxicity distinguishes it from epiglottitis
radiological_manifestations: Anteroposterior soft-tissue neck radiograph: 'steeple sign' - symmetrical subglottic tracheal narrowing replacing the normal squared shoulders
pathology_manifestations: Parainfluenza (type 1 commonest) subglottic mucosal edema; diagnosis clinical
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Clinically defined viral syndrome with the named pathognomonic steeple sign on neck film.

Infectious Diseases.name: Impetigo
clinical_manifestations: Honey-colored crusts over superficial facial erosions (nonbullous form)
Fragile flaccid bullae leaving collarette scale in the bullous form
Periorificial and perinasal predominance in children
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Staphylococcus aureus (bullous toxin cleaves desmoglein-1) or Streptococcus pyogenes; subcorneal pustule with gram-positive cocci
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Honey-crust photograph is the iconic image of this common single-agent skin infection.

Infectious Diseases.name: Erysipelas and Cellulitis
clinical_manifestations: Erysipelas: bright-red, sharply demarcated, raised plaque with a palpable advancing edge on the leg or face
Cellulitis: deeper spreading erythema, warmth, and edema without a sharp border
Lymphangitic streaking and regional adenopathy in severe disease
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; ultrasound to exclude abscess
pathology_manifestations: Streptococcal (usually group A) dermal/soft-tissue infection; histology nonspecific edema and neutrophilia
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The sharply bordered erysipelas plaque is a classic clinical photograph; a defined infectious disease entity.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tinea Capitis including Kerion
clinical_manifestations: Patches of alopecia with black-dot broken hairs or gray-scaly 'moth-eaten' scaling
Kerion: boggy, tender, purulent inflammatory mass with regional nodes
Cervical/occipital lymphadenopathy; Wood's-lamp fluorescence varies by species
radiological_manifestations: Wood's lamp: blue-green fluorescence in Microsporum canis; absent in Trichophyton tonsurans endothrix
pathology_manifestations: Endothrix or ectothrix hyphal invasion of the hair shaft on KOH microscopy; kerion shows neutrophilic follicular abscesses
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Black-dot alopecia and the boggy kerion are iconic pediatric photographs.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tinea Corporis
clinical_manifestations: Annular erythematous plaque with a raised, scaly, advancing edge and central clearing
Peripheral vesicles or pustules in inflammatory variants
Majocchi granuloma deep follicular variant on legs after shaving
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: KOH prep of scraped scale: septate branching hyphae; PAS-positive hyphae in stratum corneum
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The classic ring-with-clearing lesion is a pathognomonic photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Pityriasis Versicolor
clinical_manifestations: Multiple hypo- or hyperpigmented macules with fine branny scale on trunk and shoulders
Lesions do not tan, giving a mottled 'two-tone' appearance in summer
Slight itch; recurrent in hot humid climates
radiological_manifestations: Wood's lamp: golden or coppery-orange fluorescence of lesions
pathology_manifestations: KOH 'spaghetti and meatballs': clusters of spherical yeasts with short septate hyphae - pathognomonic
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Spaghetti-and-meatballs microscopy plus Wood's fluorescence is disease-specific.

Infectious Diseases.name: Oropharyngeal and Cutaneous Candidiasis
clinical_manifestations: Thrush: removable white plaques on erythematous buccal mucosa and tongue
Intertrigo: beefy-red erosions with satellite pustules at margins in folds
Angular cheilitis and chronic paronychia forms
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: KOH: pseudohyphae with budding yeasts; mucosal scraping or culture confirms Candida albicans and non-albicans species
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Thrushes and satellite-pustule intertrigo are among the most reproduced clinical photographs.

Infectious Diseases.name: Herpes Simplex Virus Infection
clinical_manifestations: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base at the vermilion lip border (labialis) or genital mucosa
Recurrence at the same site triggered by stress, sun, or illness
Herpetic whitlow on fingers and eczema herpeticum as severe AD complication
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Tzanck smear: multinucleated giant cells and molded nuclei with margination; HSV PCR is confirmatory
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The recurrent grouped-vesicle lesion is among the most photographed dermatologic entities.

Infectious Diseases.name: Molluscum Contagiosum
clinical_manifestations: Pearly, dome-shaped, flesh-colored papules with central umbilication
Clusters in skin folds and trunk in children; genital distribution in adults
Giant or widespread molluscum in immunocompromised hosts
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Henderson-Patterson (molluscum) bodies - large eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in keratinocytes; poxvirus PCR
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Umbilicated pearly papule is a pathognomonic photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Verruca (Cutaneous Warts)
clinical_manifestations: Hyperkeratotic papule with thrombosed black dots (capillary tips) and interrupted skin lines on hands
Plantar mosaic warts and painful callus-like lesions
Flat-topped verruca plana on face and shins
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Acanthotic papillomatosis with koilocytosis (perinuclear halos) in the upper epidermis; HPV types 1/2/3/4 and others
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The dotted-acanthotic wart is an iconic photographic entity.

Infectious Diseases.name: Condyloma Acuminatum (Anogenital Warts)
clinical_manifestations: Soft, exophytic cauliflower-like papules and plaques of the anogenital and oral mucosa
Multiple lesions in moist intertriginous areas
Flat and sessile subtypes detectable on acetowhitening
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Koilocytic atypia with papillomatosis; HPV 6/11 in most, high-risk types (16/18) in a minority
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Cauliflower anogenital exophytes are definitive photographs.

Infectious Diseases.name: Pediculosis (Lice Infestation)
clinical_manifestations: Visible crawling lice and cemented nits (eggs) adherent to hair shafts near the scalp
Excoriated papules on the neck and shoulders in pediculosis capitis
'Sky-blue' maculae caeruleae from bites in pediculosis pubis
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Lice are 1-3 mm arthropods visible to the naked eye; nits fluoresce under Wood's lamp
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Nit-on-hair and visible lice photographs are classic teaching images.

Infectious Diseases.name: Onychomycosis
clinical_manifestations: Distal-lateral subungual hyperkeratosis with yellow-brown discoloration and onycholysis
White-superficial and proximal-white subtypes
Thick, brittle, crumbling dystrophic nails
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: KOH/fungal culture: dermatophyte (Trichophyton rubrum commonest), non-dermatophyte molds, or Candida; PAS-positive hyphae in nail plate
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Highly photographed nail disease with disease-specific mycology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Erythrasma
clinical_manifestations: Well-demarcated brown-red finely scaling patches in the groin, axillae, and toe webs
Wood's lamp: pathognomonic coral-red fluorescence from porphyrin production
Asymptomatic or mildly itchy; often mistaken for tinea
radiological_manifestations: Wood's lamp examination is the disease-specific 'imaging' - coral-red fluorescence
pathology_manifestations: Gram-positive filaments of Corynebacterium minutissimum in the superficial stratum corneum
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The coral-red Wood's fluorescence is a named disease-specific sign.

Infectious Diseases.name: Pitted Keratolysis
clinical_manifestations: Crateriform pits and erosions over weight-bearing plantar skin with a punched-out appearance
Strong foot odor and hyperhidrosis
Shallow coalescent pits on the heels and forefoot
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Kytococcus sedentarius / Dermatophilus congolensis producing keratinase pits in the stratum corneum
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Crateriform plantar pits with malodor are a pathognomonic photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Bacillary Angiomatosis
clinical_manifestations: Friable red-violaceous vascular papules and nodules mimicking Kaposi sarcoma in immunocompromised patients
Subcutaneous nodules and peliosis hepatis on the same Bartonella spectrum
Responds dramatically to macrolides
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI: enhancing hepatic/splenic peliosis lesions; osseous lytic lesions in disseminated disease
pathology_manifestations: Warthin-Starry silver stain reveals clumps of Bartonella bacilli; lobular vascular proliferation with neutrophils and leukocytoclasia
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Distinct Bartonella vascular-tumor syndrome separate from covered cat-scratch disease.

Infectious Diseases.name: Plague (Yersinia pestis)
clinical_manifestations: Massive tender buboes - inguinal, axillary, or cervical lymph nodes swollen to several centimeters
Acral gangrene and purpura ('Black Death' necrotic fingers/toes) in septicemic spread
Fulgurant pneumonia in pneumonic form
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph in pneumonic plague: rapidly progressive multilobar consolidation
pathology_manifestations: Gram-negative bipolar 'safety-pin' staining of Yersinia pestis on bubo aspirate; Wayson/Giemsa stain
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Buboes plus acral gangrene are the largest named-disease omission; bipolar staining is pathognomonic.

Infectious Diseases.name: Donovanosis (Granuloma Inguinale)
clinical_manifestations: Painless, beefy-red, friable genital ulcers that bleed on contact
Progressive ulcerative lesions without significant adenopathy
Subcutaneous nodules (pseudobuboes) and scarring
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Crush preparation/biopsy: Donovan bodies - safety-pin intracellular bacilli within macrophage vacuoles - pathognomonic
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Beefy-red painless ulcers plus pathognomonic Donovan bodies.

Infectious Diseases.name: Myiasis
clinical_manifestations: Furuncular lesion with a central punctum through which the larva's posterior spiracles breathe
Serous or serosanguineous discharge with intermittent stinging pain
Extraction photographs showing the larva are iconic
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound may show the moving larva within the cavity ('live' finding)
pathology_manifestations: Botfly (Dermatobia, Cordylobia) larvae in a cavity lined by granulation tissue; species identification on extracted specimen
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The breathing-larva punctum and extraction photographs are definitional.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tungiasis
clinical_manifestations: Periungual or plantar white-yellow nodule with a central black dot - pathognomonic lesion
Intense pruritus and pain; usually on the feet
Secondary infection from manual extraction is common
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Embedded female Tunga flea; black posterior discs visible at the punctum; eggs extruded from the abdomen
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: White-yellow periungual nodule with black dot is a pathognomonic photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Lobomycosis (Keloidal Blastomycosis)
clinical_manifestations: Slow-growing keloidal, shiny, indurated nodules on the ears and extremities
Keloid-like plaques that may ulcerate or form verrucous surfaces
Localized to cooler skin areas
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Long chains of uniform round yeast cells (Lacazia loboi) in 'string-of-pearls' arrangement on GMS - noncultivatable fungus
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Keloidal shiny ear nodules plus chains of yeast cells complete the implantation-mycosis set.

Infectious Diseases.name: Lymphogranuloma Venereum
clinical_manifestations: Transient painless genital ulcer followed by large painful inguinal buboes
Pathognomonic 'groove sign': matted nodes above and below the inguinal ligament
Late elephantiasis and anorectal strictures
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic/rectal imaging for the proctocolitis/stricture complications
pathology_manifestations: Chlamydia trachomatis L1-L3; suppurative lymphadenitis with stellate abscesses on histology
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The groove sign plus inguinal buboes is a classic named STI presentation.

Infectious Diseases.name: Sparganosis
clinical_manifestations: Slowly migratory subcutaneous nodule, sometimes painful or pruritic
Ocular and visceral forms in endemic regions
Worm recovered from the nodule on surgery
radiological_manifestations: MRI: 'tunnel sign' - a serpiginous elongated lesion with peripheral enhancement tracking worm migration
pathology_manifestations: Plerocercoid (sparganum) larvae in tissue; unsegmented white ribbon worms up to 35 cm on extraction
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Migrating nodule plus MRI tunnel sign is a distinctive parasitic disease.

Infectious Diseases.name: Carrión Disease (Oroya Fever / Verruga Peruana)
clinical_manifestations: Verruga peruana: miliary or nodular blood-red vascular skin eruptions, often facial
Oroya fever phase: acute febrile hemolytic anemia
Angiomatous lesions that bleed easily
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Bartonella bacilliformis parasitizing erythrocytes on blood smear (Oroya phase); verruga histology shows vascular proliferation like bacillary angiomatosis
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Blood-red verruga nodules complete the Bartonella disease set.

Infectious Diseases.name: African Tick-Bite Fever / Boutonneuse Fever
clinical_manifestations: Inoculation eschar ('tache noire') at the tick-bite site with regional lymphadenitis
Multiple eschars in African tick-bite fever (R. africae); single eschar plus maculopapular rash in boutonneuse fever (R. conorii)
Mild fever and headache; less severe than RMSF
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Eschar swab/biopsy PCR or immunohistochemistry for spotted-fever rickettsiae
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The tache-noire eschar plus maculopapular rash is a named spotted-fever presentation distinct from covered RMSF and scrub typhus.

Infectious Diseases.name: Ascariasis
clinical_manifestations: Emergence of adult worms from mouth, nose, or anus - the definitive photograph
Abdominal discomfort; biliary migration causes biliary colic
Loeffler pneumonitis during larval migration
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound/ERCP: 'spaghetti' filling defects in bile/pancreatic ducts in biliary ascariasis; barium: worm outlines in bowel loops
pathology_manifestations: Fertilized/decorticated eggs in stool; adult worms identified on passage
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Worm-emergence photos plus ductal 'spaghetti' filling defects are disease-specific.

Infectious Diseases.name: Anisakiasis
clinical_manifestations: Endoscopic photograph of the larva embedded in gastric mucosa - how the disease is recognized
Severe epigastric pain within hours of raw-fish ingestion
Urticaria or anaphylaxis as a hypersensitivity form
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging beyond the endoscopic photograph
pathology_manifestations: Coiled larva in gastric/intestinal mucosa with eosinophilic granuloma; Anisakis species on recovery
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The endoscopic embedded-larva image is the diagnostic photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Gnathostomiasis
clinical_manifestations: Intermittent migratory creeping swellings (cutaneous larva migrans profundus) lasting days
Deep nodular migratory panniculitis under the skin
Eosinophilic meningomyelitis in CNS involvement
radiological_manifestations: MRI: serpiginous tracks and hemorrhagic foci in the spinal cord/brain in the neuro form
pathology_manifestations: Gnathostoma larvae in subcutaneous tissues; eosinophilia; serology confirms
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Migratory deep swellings plus eosinophilic myeloradiculitis is a distinct parasite entity.

Infectious Diseases.name: Dirofilariasis
clinical_manifestations: Subconjunctival or eyelid live worm visible crawling under the conjunctiva - striking photograph
Subcutaneous nodule containing the coiled worm
Pulmonary 'coin lesion' in D. immitis on chest imaging
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph: well-circumscribed coin lesion when D. immitis embolizes; ultrasound may show the moving worm
pathology_manifestations: Dirofilaria species on extraction and morphologic identification
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Subconjunctival live-worm extraction photographs are striking and disease-defining.

Infectious Diseases.name: Malaria
clinical_manifestations: Cerebral malaria retinopathy: vessel whitening, orange discoloration, and white-centered hemorrhages on fundoscopy
Periodic fever paroxysms; splenomegaly
Severe anemia and blackwater fever in falciparum
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific clinical imaging beyond the pathognomonic retinopathy
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral thin film: ring-form trophozoites, banana-shaped gametocytes (P. falciparum); thick-film parasite density; pathology-recognized diagnosis
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Admitted under the pathology-recognition clause plus the distinct cerebral-malaria retinal findings.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rabies
clinical_manifestations: Hydrophobic and aerophagic spasms with terror on attempted swallowing
Hypersalivation and characteristic agitation
Bat-bite or dog-bite history; paralytic 'dumb' form less recognizable
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: nonspecific T2 hyperintensity of basal ganglia, brainstem, and limbic system in encephalitic form
pathology_manifestations: Negri bodies - eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in Purkinje cells and hippocampal neurons - pathognomonic on histology
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Pathology-recognition clause (Negri bodies) supports inclusion; limited clinical photo base.

Infectious Diseases.name: Mycobacterium marinum Infection (Fish-Tank Granuloma)
clinical_manifestations: Sporotrichoid nodular lymphangitis ascending the hand and forearm after aquarium or fish exposure
Violaceous verrucous papule at the inoculation site
Deep tenosynovitis in neglected cases
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Acid-fast bacilli in granulomatous infiltrate; culture at 30-32C; histology suppurative granulomas
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Sporotrichoid hand nodular pattern after fish-tank exposure is a classic photo.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rhinofacial Entomophthoromycosis
clinical_manifestations: Fixed, painless, firm swelling of the nose and perinasal face distorting features
Rhinofacial involvement: inferior turbinates through upper lip
Slow progression with normal overlying skin
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI of the soft-tissue rhinofacial mass
pathology_manifestations: Broad pauciseptate hyphae in granulomas with Splendore-Hoeppli eosinophilic cuffs
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Remaining implantation-mycosis gap; distinct fixed rhinofacial swelling.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tinea Imbricata (Tokelau)
clinical_manifestations: Concentric lamellar rings of scale resembling fish scales or wood-grain patterns
Large body-surface coverage without central clearing
Chronic lifelong infection in endemic Pacific/South Asian populations
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Trichophyton concentricum on microscopy/culture; autosomal-recessive predisposition in some families
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Concentric wood-grain rings are a pathognomonic dermatophyte morphology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tinea Nigra
clinical_manifestations: Painless brown-black macule on the palm or sole resembling a melanocytic lesion
Single irregular slowly enlarging stain-like lesion
No scale or inflammation
radiological_manifestations: Dermoscopy: fine spicules/filaments in a pigment network - differentiates from melanocytic nevus
pathology_manifestations: Dematiaceous (pigmented) Hortaea werneckii hyphae in stratum corneum on KOH
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Brown palmoplantar macule is a defined entity.

Infectious Diseases.name: Milker's Nodule (Paravaccinia)
clinical_manifestations: Red-purple 'target' nodule on the hands of dairy workers
Stages: red-blue target, weeping, papillomatous, and crusted
Single or few lesions on fingers
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Parapoxvirus (pseudocowpox) infection; histology similar to orf with ballooning degeneration
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Same class as covered orf but a distinct virus and target-nodule phenotype.

Infectious Diseases.name: Scabies
clinical_manifestations: Thin, grayish-white, serpiginous burrow tracks with a small dark papule or vesicle at one end, most often in finger webs and on the wrists
Papular, vesicular and excoriated lesions in the axillae, periumbilical area, genitalia and buttocks
Firm, pruritic nodules on the genitals or groin that persist for weeks
Thick hyperkeratotic crusts on the palms, soles and nails in crusted (Norwegian) scabies
pathology_manifestations: KOH mount of skin scraping: Sarcoptes scabiei mites, eggs and scybala (fecal pellets)
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Burrows in the finger webs and wrists and crusted disease in severe cases are recognizable on clinical and dermoscopic images.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tinea Pedis
clinical_manifestations: Interdigital maceration, scaling and fissuring, especially of the third and fourth web spaces
Diffuse plantar and lateral foot scaling with hyperkeratosis in the moccasin pattern
Vesicular or bullous lesions with erythema on the soles and instep
Erythema and fissuring at the heel margins in some patients
pathology_manifestations: KOH mount of skin scale: Septate, branching hyphae and arthroconidia
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Interdigital maceration and plantar scaling are visible on clinical photographs of the feet, and dermoscopy shows the scale pattern.

Infectious Diseases.name: Hand-Foot-and-Mouth Disease
clinical_manifestations: Grayish-white or clear oval vesicles on an erythematous base on the palms, soles, fingers and toes
Painful vesicles and ulcers on the tongue, buccal mucosa, gingiva and palate
Oval vesicular or papular eruption on the buttocks and perianal or genital skin
Peeling of the skin of the fingertips and toes during convalescence
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Oval vesicles on the palms, soles and buttocks with oral ulcers are visually distinctive on clinical photographs and oral examination images.

Infectious Diseases.name: Infectious Mononucleosis (Epstein-Barr Virus)
clinical_manifestations: Enlarged, erythematous tonsils with white-gray membranous exudate in the pharynx
Petechiae on the soft palate
Generalized lymphadenopathy, most prominent in the posterior cervical chain
Periorbital edema and a maculopapular rash, particularly after amoxicillin or ampicillin exposure
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal ultrasonography: Splenomegaly, sometimes with hepatomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral blood smear/Wright-Giemsa stain: Atypical lymphocytes with abundant cytoplasm and indented nuclei
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Tonsillar exudate, palatal petechiae and cervical lymphadenopathy are visible on clinical photographs of the oropharynx and neck, and atypical lymphocytes appear on blood smear.

Infectious Diseases.name: Chancroid
synonyms: genital ulcer due to Haemophilus ducreyi
clinical_manifestations: Ragged, undermined-edged genital ulcer with a soft, necrotic base
Thick, yellow-gray purulent exudate covering the ulcer floor
Multiple ulcers with satellite lesions, often on the penile shaft, foreskin or labia
Suppurating unilateral inguinal lymph node enlargement (bubo) with overlying erythema
pathology_manifestations: Ulcer exudate/Gram stain: Small Gram-negative coccobacilli in chains or parallel rows ('school of fish' pattern)
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Ragged genital ulcers with a purulent base and suppurating inguinal buboes are distinctive clinical photographs in STI and dermatology atlases.

Infectious Diseases.name: Vibrio vulnificus Infection
synonyms: necrotizing fasciitis due to Vibrio vulnificus
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly spreading erythema and edema of a limb, often starting at a wound exposed to seawater
Hemorrhagic bullae with dark or violaceous centers on the affected skin
Dusky, violaceous discoloration of skin extending beyond the margin of visible erythema
Necrotic ulcers with black eschar and sanguineous or serous drainage
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Hemorrhagic bullae and rapidly spreading necrotic cellulitis after seawater exposure are highly characteristic photographic findings.

Infectious Diseases.name: Disseminated Fusariosis
clinical_manifestations: Multiple firm, erythematous to violaceous papules and nodules, many with central necrosis
Target-like or annular lesions with a violaceous halo around a necrotic center
Black eschar and ulceration over necrotic skin lesions
Skin lesions distributed over the trunk and extremities in prolonged neutropenia
radiological_manifestations: CT chest: Multiple pulmonary nodules, some with a halo sign or cavitation
pathology_manifestations: Skin biopsy/GMS stain: Septate, branching hyphae invading blood vessels with ischemic necrosis
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Disseminated Fusarium produces widely recognized target-like necrotic skin lesions in immunosuppressed patients.

Infectious Diseases.name: Babesiosis
clinical_manifestations: Scleral icterus (yellow sclerae) from hemolysis
Jaundiced skin and mucous membranes from hyperbilirubinemia
Pallor of conjunctivae and skin from hemolytic anemia
Dark, cola-colored urine from hemoglobinuria in severe disease
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral blood smear/Giemsa or Wright stain: Intraerythrocytic ring-form trophozoites, some in pairs or tetrads forming a Maltese cross
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The visible signs are limited to hemolytic jaundice and pallor, so the diagnostic image is the Giemsa-stained intraerythrocytic parasites on blood smear.

Infectious Diseases.name: Relapsing Fever (Borrelia)
clinical_manifestations: Conjunctival suffusion or injection
Maculopapular rash on the trunk and limbs
Petechial hemorrhages on the trunk and limbs, mainly in severe louse-borne disease
Scleral icterus or jaundice in severe disease with hepatic involvement
pathology_manifestations: Thick and thin peripheral blood smears (Giemsa stain): Motile spirochetes among and on erythrocytes, most numerous during febrile episodes
Thick blood film (Giemsa): Coiled, corkscrew-shaped spirochetes with several undulating turns
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The diagnosis is made from visible spirochetes on Giemsa-stained blood smears, so the key image type is a blood film, supported by conjunctival and skin photographs.

Infectious Diseases.name: Dengue
clinical_manifestations: Morbilliform maculopapular rash with blanching 'islands of white' surrounded by erythema during defervescence
Petechiae on the lower limbs and forearms, and tourniquet-test petechiae at the antecubital fossa
Facial flushing and conjunctival injection
Mucosal bleeding with gingival oozing, epistaxis and oral petechiae
Purpuric ecchymoses and bruising in dengue hemorrhagic fever
Scleral icterus and jaundice in severe hepatitis
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal ultrasound: Gallbladder wall thickening, ascites and hepatomegaly in severe dengue
Chest radiograph: Pleural effusions in dengue shock syndrome
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral blood smear: Reactive atypical lymphocytes with thrombocytopenia
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Dengue has recognizable skin and mucosal signs (convalescent white-island rash, petechiae, bleeding) and ultrasound plasma-leakage findings, so clinical photographs, ultrasound and smear images all exist.
