Nephrology.name: Alport Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Anterior lenticonus: conical protrusion of the anterior pole of the lens into the anterior chamber on slit-lamp examination (pathognomonic hallmark)
Macular and mid-peripheral dot-and-fleck retinopathy (innumerable pale yellow or whitish flecks sparing the fovea)
Posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy
Bilateral progressive high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss
Persistent microscopic or gross recurrent hematuria from childhood
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasound: Progressive bilateral increase in renal cortical echogenicity, loss of normal corticomedullary differentiation, and symmetric reduction in kidney size in late-stage renal failure
Temporal Bone CT / Audiometry: Sensorineural cochlear hearing loss documentation
pathology_manifestations: Renal biopsy electron microscopy (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'basket-weave' appearance of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) characterized by irregular alternating areas of thinning and thickening, multi-layering, and longitudinal splitting of the lamina densa; immunohistochemistry demonstrates complete absence of collagen alpha-3, alpha-4, and alpha-5 (IV) chains in X-linked disease
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Unmistakable syndromic nephropathy pairing ocular anterior lenticonus and dot-and-fleck retinopathy on slit lamp with bilateral shrunken echogenic kidneys on ultrasound and basket-weave GBM on electron microscopy.

Nephrology.name: Atheroembolic Renal Disease
clinical_manifestations:
Classic cutaneous triad following recent vascular instrumentation, angiography, cardiac catheterization, aortic surgery, or anticoagulation:
1) Livedo reticularis: prominent, mottled, violaceous, lace-like or reticular net-like erythema over the thighs, abdomen, and buttocks that does not blanch completely
2) 'Blue toe syndrome' (purple toe syndrome): exquisitely painful, cold, cyanotic or purplish discoloration and ulceration of the toes and forefeet, in the presence of intact, palpable, bounding peripheral pedal (dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial) pulses (hallmark of microvascular embolic occlusion)
3) Digital gangrene, cutaneous infarction, and tender subcutaneous purpuric nodules

Ophthalmoscopic pathognomonic sign: Hollenhorst plaques: bright, highly refractile, glistening orange-yellow, copper-hued cholesterol crystals lodged at the arterial bifurcations of retinal arterioles on funduscopy
Subacute, stuttering, stepwise deterioration in renal function with oliguria, marked refractory hypertension, fever, and weight loss
Abdominal signs: severe ischemic abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, and pancreatitis from concurrent visceral mesenteric atheroembolization
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT Angiography (CTA) / MR Angiography (MRA) of the Aorta: Pathognomonic 'shaggy aorta' sign: extensive, severe, diffuse, protruding, ulcerated, irregular atheromatous plaques (>4 mm thickness) and mobile, pedunculated thrombi lining the thoracic and abdominal aorta, particularly at and proximal to the origins of the renal arteries

Renal Doppler Ultrasound: Symmetrically normal or mildly reduced renal size with elevated renal arterial resistive indices (RI >0.75-0.80), patchy cortical perfusion defects, and absence of main renal artery occlusion
Fundus Photography: High-resolution photographic documentation of glistening, yellow refractile intravascular crystals at branching bifurcations of the retinal arterial tree
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'cholesterol clefts': biconvex, needle-shaped, or spindle-shaped optically clear ghost clefts inside the lumens of medium- and small-sized arcuate and interlobular renal arteries and arterioles (formed by the chemical dissolution of cholesterol crystals during routine alcohol and paraffin histological processing)

Associated Vascular Inflammatory Reaction: Acute stage reveals occlusive luminal thrombi containing fibrin, platelets, and entrapped cholesterol crystals; followed rapidly by a vigorous foreign-body giant cell reaction, surrounding histiocytes, endothelial proliferation, concentric 'onion-skin' intimal fibrous hyperplasia, and perivascular mononuclear and eosinophilic inflammation leading to complete luminal obliteration and downstream ischemic glomerulosclerosis and tubular atrophy
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive systemic vascular nephropathy linking recent endovascular manipulation to livedo reticularis, blue toe syndrome with bounding pulses, and retinal Hollenhorst plaques, alongside a 'shaggy aorta' on CTA and pathognomonic biconvex biconcave needle-shaped cholesterol clefts on renal biopsy.

Nephrology.name: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
clinical_manifestations: Massively enlarged, palpable, nodular, ballotable bilateral flank masses extending into the lower abdomen
Protruding, distended abdomen with flank fullness
Gross macroscopic hematuria and acute flank pain from cyst rupture or hemorrhage
Signs of intracranial aneurysm (severe sudden headache / third nerve palsy)
Mitral valve prolapse click and murmur
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasound / CT / MRI: Bilateral, massively enlarged kidneys completely filled with innumerable, round, thin-walled fluid-filled cysts; high attenuation/hyperintensity in cysts with recent hemorrhage or infection; total kidney volume (TKV) calculation for Mayo prognostic classification; concurrent hepatic polycystic disease (cysts scattered throughout liver parenchyma) and pancreatic cysts
Brain MRA: Screening detection of unruptured intracranial saccular (berry) aneurysms in the Circle of Willis
pathology_manifestations: Nephrectomy gross and histology: Gigantic kidneys weighing up to several kilograms each; external surface resembles a bunch of grapes; cysts lined by flattened or cuboidal tubular epithelium; intervening normal renal parenchyma completely atrophied and compressed by progressive cystic expansion
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield genetic renal disorder with gigantic ballotable abdominal masses and distension, matched with unmistakable innumerable bilateral renal and hepatic cysts on ultrasound, CT, and MRI.

Nephrology.name: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
clinical_manifestations: Classic Potter sequence physical phenotype at birth: flattened, compressed facial features (flattened nose, prominent infraorbital folds, micrognathia), low-set and flattened floppy ears, clubbed feet (talipes equinovarus), and severe pulmonary hypoplasia leading to neonatal respiratory failure
Enormous, bilateral, symmetrical, ballotable flank masses palpated in the newborn, producing a dramatically distended, protuberant abdomen that may impede spontaneous vaginal delivery
Early severe systemic arterial hypertension appearing in the first weeks of life, often refractory to multi-drug therapy

Manifestations of progressive congenital hepatic fibrosis in older children: massive, firm, non-tender hepatosplenomegaly, bleeding esophageal varices (hematemesis/melena), hypersplenism (thrombocytopenia, leukopenia), and caput medusae from portal hypertension
Failure to thrive and oliguria/anuria in the immediate perinatal period
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Neonatal / Prenatal Renal Ultrasound (Diagnostic Hallmark): Bilateral, symmetrically enlarged, kidney silhouettes (often 4 to 10 times normal volume) that retain their reniform shape, exhibiting diffuse, homogeneous hyperechogenicity ('white kidneys') with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation; the bright echogenicity is caused by sound reflection from millions of microscopic acoustic interfaces between tiny, cylindrical (1-2 mm) radially arranged microcysts and fluid

Abdominal CT / MRI: Massively enlarged kidneys packed with radial microcysts, displaying high T2 signal intensity throughout the entire parenchyma; liver imaging demonstrates congenital hepatic fibrosis with periportal cuffing, dilation of intrahepatic biliary ducts (Caroli disease pattern), and prominent signs of portal hypertension (dilated portal vein, splenomegaly, gastroesophageal collateral veins)

High-Resolution Contrast Urography (Historical Classic): 'Sunburst' or 'spoke-wheel' striated nephrogram resulting from linear puddling and retention of contrast agent within elongated, fusiform dilated collecting ducts extending from the papillae outwards to the capsule
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology: Symmetrically gigantic kidneys retaining a smooth external surface (unlike the bosselated 'bunch-of-grapes' appearance of ADPKD); cut surface reveals countless uniform, tiny cylindrical, radially arranged fusiform cysts oriented perpendicular to the renal capsule, extending uninterrupted through the cortex and medulla

Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Diffuse, non-branching, uniform fusiform or cylindrical dilatation of 100% of the collecting ducts lined by simple cuboidal or columnar epithelium; normal intervening glomeruli and proximal tubules are compressed into spaces between the dilated ducts; liver histology invariably demonstrates ductal plate malformation characterized by extensive concentric periportal fibrosis and bizarrely branching, dilated intrahepatic bile ductules (congenital hepatic fibrosis)

Genetics / Molecular: Biallelic pathogenic loss-of-function variants in the *PKHD1* gene on chromosome 6p21, encoding fibrocystin/polyductin, an integral membrane protein essential for primary cilia/basal body signaling in renal collecting tubules and biliary epithelial cells
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Premier recessive ciliopathy presenting with neonatal Potter facies, massive symmetric flank masses, and hepatosplenomegaly, corroborated by pathognomonic echogenic 'white kidneys' packed with radial microcysts on ultrasound and diffuse cylindrical collecting duct ectasia with congenital hepatic fibrosis on pathology.

Nephrology.name: Dense Deposit Disease
synonyms: complement factor H-related dense deposit disease
clinical_manifestations: Barraquer-Simons syndrome (acquired partial lipodystrophy): striking, symmetrical, progressive, irreversible loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue beginning in the face ('gaunt, hollow-cheeked, aged facies'), neck, shoulders, thoracic cage, and arms, with absolute sparing or compensatory hypertrophy of hips, buttocks, and lower extremities

Juvenile Ocular Drusen: Bilateral, symmetrical, yellow-white nodular subretinal deposits densely clustered across the macula and posterior pole on slit-lamp fundoscopy (identical to age-related macular degeneration but manifesting in adolescents and young adults), complicated by choroidal neovascular membranes and visual blurring
Nephritic-nephrotic syndrome: macroscopic cola-colored hematuria, heavy proteinuria, periorbital and peripheral pitting edema, and accelerated hypertension in children or young adults

Persistent profound hypocomplementemia: marked depression of serum C3 with characteristically normal C4 levels, driven by circulating C3 nephritic factor (C3NeF—an IgG autoantibody stabilizing the alternative pathway C3 convertase C3bBb)
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasonography: Bilaterally enlarged, echogenic kidneys with increased cortical reflectivity that matches or exceeds adjacent liver parenchyma; prominent accentuation of corticomedullary contrast during acute phases, followed by progressive parenchymal thinning and symmetric cortical atrophy in chronic stages

Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Distinct dome-shaped, hyperreflective nodular elevations located between the basal lamina of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and the inner collagenous layer of Bruch's membrane, with focal RPE atrophy and subretinal fluid accumulation

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) & Fluorescein Angiography: Confluent areas of focal hypo-autofluorescence surrounded by hyper-autofluorescent halos at drusen sites, with early hyperfluorescence ('starry sky' appearance) on fluorescein angiography
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Electron Microscopy (Pathognomonic Gold Standard): Continuous, ribbon-like, extremely osmiophilic, electron-dense transformation of the lamina densa of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), creating a wavy, sausage-like, dark, highly electron-dense band replacing the normal lamina densa; identical dense transformation frequently involves Bowman's capsule and tubular basement membranes

Immunofluorescence Microscopy: Intense, dominant, bright staining for C3 alone along the glomerular capillary loops in a distinctive pseudolinear, patchy, or granular 'double-contour' / 'ring-and-saucer' pattern, along with bright mesangial C3 rings; characteristically negative for IgG, IgM, IgA, C1q, and C4

Light Microscopy: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) pattern with marked lobular accentuation of the glomerular tuft, mesangial and endocapillary hypercellularity, and basement membrane duplication ('tram-track' or double-contour appearance on Jones silver and PAS stains)
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Benchmark complement alternative pathway disorder linking Barraquer-Simons partial lipodystrophy (facial wasting) and juvenile ocular drusen to pathognomonic ribbon-like osmiophilic GBM transformation on EM and isolated bright C3 immunofluorescence.

Nephrology.name: Malakoplakia of the Urinary Tract
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, relentless, recurrent urinary tract infections refractory to conventional antibiotic regimens, classically occurring in immunocompromised, diabetic, or renal transplant patients
Gross painless hematuria, foul-smelling urine, and chronic dysuria
Palpable, tender, firm unilateral or bilateral flank mass mimicking a renal neoplasm, frequently accompanied by low-grade fever and weight loss
Acute or subacute obstructive renal failure (hydronephrosis) from ureteral or bladder neck lesions

Cystoscopic / Endoscopic Photographic Hallmark: Pathognomonic direct visualization of soft, friable, yellowish to yellowish-brown, umbilicated plaques or raised nodules (ranging from millimeters to several centimeters) surrounded by an intensely erythematous, hyperemic mucosal halo lining the urinary bladder (trigone) and ureter
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal/Pelvic CT: Multiple, poorly circumscribed, solid, hypoattenuating (20-40 HU) cortical and corticomedullary renal masses or diffuse enlargement of the entire kidney ('pseudotumor' pattern) with patchy, heterogeneous enhancement; pronounced perinephric fat stranding; thickened bladder wall with multiple discrete, intraluminal enhancing nodular mucosal plaques
Renal Ultrasound: Solitary or multifocal ill-defined, hypoechoic or heterogeneous parenchymal masses with distortion of the central renal sinus complex, accompanied by hydroureteronephrosis
Fluoroscopic Retrograde / Antegrade Ureteropyelography: Irregular filling defects, strictures, and luminal nodularity in the distal ureters mimicking multifocal urothelial carcinoma
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Dense, confluent, chronic histiocytic infiltrate composed of sheets of large, polygonal macrophages with abundant, eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm known as von Hansemann cells

Pathognomonic Pathologic Structure: Michaelis-Gutmann bodies: round to oval, targetoid, basophilic, concentrically laminated, calcified intracytoplasmic (or extracellular) inclusion bodies; they represent defective phagolysosomes containing incompletely digested, calcified bacterial fragments (Escherichia coli)

Special Stains: Michaelis-Gutmann bodies are strongly positive for von Kossa stain (black, demonstrating calcium phosphate), Prussian blue stain (bright blue, demonstrating ferric iron), and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) with diastase resistance; CD68 positive, confirming histiocytic lineage
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive chronic granulomatous infection featuring cystoscopic yellowish-brown mucosal plaques with hyperemic halos, CT renal pseudotumors with hydronephrosis, and pathognomonic basophilic targetoid Michaelis-Gutmann bodies within von Hansemann histiocytes on pathology.

Nephrology.name: Nail-Patella Syndrome
clinical_manifestations:
Tetrad of classic physical examination dysmorphic findings:
1) Dystrophic fingernails (pathognomonic bedside hallmark): Bilateral, symmetrical nail hypoplasia, aplasia, longitudinal ridging, spooning (koilonychia), triangular lunulae (pathognomonic sign where lunulae point distally like an arrowhead), most severe on the thumbs and progressively milder towards the fifth digit
2) Absent, hypoplastic, or dislocated patellae: easily palpated small, rudimentary, or absent kneecaps, associated with habitual recurrent patellar dislocations, genu valgum, and gait disturbances
3) Elbow dysplasias: prominent limitation of full extension, pronation, and supination of the forearms, with visible antecubital pterygia (webbing) and prominence of the radial head
4) Palpable posterior iliac horns: symmetric, firm, bony prominences palpated along the posterolateral surface of the iliac crests
Lester's sign: cloverleaf-shaped or irregular dark hyperpigmentation of the inner pupillary margin of the iris on slit-lamp ophthalmic examination

Renal manifestations: early asymptomatic microscopic hematuria and persistent, progressive non-nephrotic or nephrotic proteinuria developing in childhood or adolescence, progressing to end-stage kidney disease in 30-50%
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic Radiography (Pathognomonic Skeletal Hallmark): Pathognomonic bilateral, symmetrical, horn-like bony spurs or exostoses projecting posterolaterally from the posterior aspect of the iliac bones, known as iliac horns or Fong's sign (present in >80% of patients and pathognomonic for the syndrome)
Knee Radiography / MRI: Hypoplastic, small, asymmetrical, or completely absent patellae; lateral displacement/subluxation of the patella; hypoplastic lateral femoral condyle
Elbow Radiography: Hypoplasia of the capitellum, asymmetric enlargement of the medial epicondyle, and posterolateral subluxation or dislocation of the radial head
Renal Ultrasound: Non-specific findings of progressive glomerulopathy: bilateral normal-to-small kidneys with increased cortical echogenicity and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Electron Microscopy (Diagnostic Gold Standard & Pathognomonic Hallmark): Pathognomonic 'moth-eaten' appearance of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) with diffuse irregular lucent areas throughout the lamina densa, containing embedded bundles of banded collagen fibrils showing characteristic 64 nm periodic striations (Type III collagen fibers, which are normally entirely absent from the glomerular basement membrane); accompanied by podocyte foot process effacement
Light Microscopy: Variable, non-specific changes ranging from mild mesangial matrix expansion to progressive focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and tubular atrophy

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous pathogenic loss-of-function mutations in the *LMX1B* gene on chromosome 9q34.1, encoding the LIM homeobox transcription factor 1-beta, critical for dorsoventral limb patterning, podocyte differentiation, and glomerular basement membrane collagen regulation
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Premier hereditary pleiotropic nephropathy combining bedside triangular fingernail lunulae and absent patellae with pathognomonic bilateral iliac horns on pelvic radiography and pathognomonic banded collagen fibrils within a 'moth-eaten' GBM on electron microscopy.

Nephrology.name: Nephropathic Cystinosis
clinical_manifestations: Onset in early infancy (6-12 months) with complete renal Fanconi syndrome: extreme polyuria, polydipsia, recurrent episodes of severe dehydration, vomiting, failure to thrive, and growth arrest below the 3rd percentile

Hypophosphatemic Fanconi rickets: prominent rachitic rosary (beading of costochondral junctions), widening of wrists and ankles, severe lower limb bowing (genu varum/valgum), and craniotabes resistant to physiologic vitamin D

Pathognomonic ocular findings: severe photophobia, chronic blepharospasm, and eye rubbing; slit-lamp biomicroscopy reveals innumerable glistening, tinsel-like, needle-shaped and hexagonal cystine crystals deposited throughout the corneal stroma (appearing after 1 year of age, 100% pathognomonic)
Cutaneous pigmentary dilution: characteristic fair complexion, blond hair, and blue eyes (distinct hypopigmentation compared to unaffected family members due to altered melanogenesis)

Extrarenal storage manifestations in late childhood/adolescence: primary hypothyroidism (thyroid follicular atrophy), distal vacuolar myopathy, pancreatic exocrine and endocrine insufficiency (diabetes mellitus), and swallowing dysfunction
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography: Severe, active hypophosphatemic rickets demonstrating pathognomonic cupping, widening, splaying, and ragged fraying of the metaphyseal margins at the distal radius, ulna, and tibia; wide, radiolucent growth plates (physes); severe generalized osteopenia and pseudofractures (Looser zones)

Renal Ultrasonography: Progressive bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis characterized by intensely hyperechoic renal pyramids with acoustic shadowing, loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and progressive symmetric renal volume loss leading to small, shrunken, echogenic kidneys
In Vivo Corneal Confocal Microscopy: Quantitative visualization of high-density hyperreflective, needle-shaped and fusiform crystal deposits in the anterior, middle, and posterior corneal stroma
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Light Microscopy & Microdissection: Pathognomonic 'swan-neck' deformity of the proximal convoluted tubule (extreme atrophy and narrowing of the initial proximal tubule segment directly originating from the glomerulus, lined by flattened, atrophic epithelium); marked multinucleated podocytes; progressive focal segmental and global glomerulosclerosis with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy

Polarized Light Microscopy (Alcohol-Fixed Tissue): Innumerable iridescent, birefringent, hexagonal, rectangular, and needle-shaped cystine crystals packed within the lysosomes of interstitial histiocytes, mesangial cells, and proximal tubular cells (crystals dissolve in routine aqueous formalin fixation and require absolute ethanol fixation)

Electron Microscopy & Genetics: Intralysosomal crystalline voids within podocytes and interstitial macrophages; molecular testing demonstrates biallelic pathogenic loss-of-function variants in CTNS (such as the common 57-kb European founder deletion), resulting in defective lysosomal cystinosin transporter
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic lysosomal storage ciliopathy pairing infantile Fanconi rickets, blond hypopigmentation, and slit-lamp corneal crystals with metaphyseal fraying on X-ray, medullary nephrocalcinosis, and pathognomonic proximal tubular 'swan-neck' deformity on histology.

Nephrology.name: Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Early infantile or childhood presentation with recurrent, refractory calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis and urolithiasis, passing gravel or large calculi, leading to obstructive uropathy, renal colic, and rapid progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD)
Oxalate osteopathy: severe bone pain, joint deformities, pathological fractures of long bones, and painful swollen metaphyses mimicking intractable rickets

Cutaneous oxalosis (calciphylaxis-like ischemic necrosis): livedo reticularis, painful violaceous plaques, peripheral digital gangrene, Raynaud phenomenon, and ischemic acral ulcerations from systemic microvascular oxalate precipitation

Ocular oxalosis: pathognomonic 'crystalline retinopathy' characterized by white-to-yellow glistening birefringent flecks and crystalline deposits densely scattered across the posterior pole, macula, and retinal pigment epithelium on fundoscopy

Cardiac oxalosis: high-grade atrioventricular conduction blocks, bundle branch blocks, intractable ventricular arrhythmias, and restrictive cardiomyopathy resulting from diffuse myocardial oxalate crystal infiltration
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Abdominal CT / KUB Plain Radiography: Dense, diffuse, bilateral medullary and cortical nephrocalcinosis ('chalky-white kidneys') accompanied by bilateral radiopaque staghorn or multiple branched dendritic renal calculi (pure calcium oxalate monohydrate, >1200-1500 HU)

Renal Ultrasonography: Strikingly hyperechoic kidneys ('bright kidneys') with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation and dense posterior acoustic shadowing caused by diffuse parenchymal crystal aggregation

Skeletal Radiographs (Pathognomonic Oxalate Osteopathy): Sclerotic transverse metaphyseal bands ('dense bone bands'), generalized axial osteosclerosis alternating with radiolucent submetaphyseal bands, Looser zones, cortical thinning, and pathological metaphyseal fractures

Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): Distinct hyperreflective punctate foci throughout the inner and outer retinal layers, with retinal pigment epithelial disruptions corresponding to crystalline deposits
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy (Diagnostic Polarized Light Microscopy): Innumerable birefringent, prismatic, wheatsheaf-shaped and radial rosette-shaped calcium oxalate monohydrate (whewellite) crystals packing tubular lumens, tubular epithelial cells, and the renal interstitium; under polarized light microscopy, crystals exhibit intense, bright polychromatic birefringence (multicolored glistening crystals)

Renal Biopsy Histopathology (H&E): Extensive foreign-body giant cell granulomatous reaction surrounding ruptured tubules with extruded crystals, marked interstitial fibrosis, profound tubular atrophy, and glomerulosclerosis

Hepatic Biopsy / Molecular Testing: Absent or markedly deficient alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase (AGT) catalytic activity in liver homogenates; biallelic pathogenic mutations in the AGXT gene (chromosome 2q37.3) confirming peroxisomal enzyme deficiency or mitochondrial mistargeting
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Hallmark inborn error of glyoxylate metabolism causing childhood nephrocalcinosis, livedoid digital gangrene, crystalline retinopathy, dense metaphyseal bone bands, and intensely birefringent wheatsheaf calcium oxalate crystals on polarized microscopy.

Nephrology.name: Renal Angiomyolipoma and Wunderlich Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Classic Lenk's triad of Wunderlich syndrome (spontaneous, non-traumatic acute retroperitoneal hemorrhage from ruptured AML): sudden severe unilateral flank/loin pain, palpable tender flank mass, and acute hypovolemic hemorrhagic shock (pallor, diaphoresis, tachycardia, and profound hypotension)

Cutaneous ecchymoses: delayed development (24-48 hours) of Grey Turner's sign (blue-red discoloration of the flank) and Cullen's sign (periumbilical ecchymosis) due to massive retroperitoneal blood tracking along fascial planes

Cutaneous stigmata of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (present in up to 80% of bilateral/multifocal AML cases): facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum—erythematous papules in a butterfly distribution across cheeks and nose), ungual/periungual fibromas (Koenen tumors), shagreen patches (leathery lumbosacral plaques), and hypomelanotic macules (ash-leaf spots under Wood's lamp)
Macroscopic gross hematuria, dull aching flank heaviness, and palpable ballotable flank mass in unruptured large lesions (>4 cm in diameter)
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Imaging Gold Standard): Pathognomonic identification of macroscopic intratumoral fat—well-demarcated exophytic cortical renal mass demonstrating regions of measurable negative attenuation values (typically -20 to -100 Hounsfield Units [HU]) intermixed with soft-tissue attenuation vascular and muscular components

Abdominal CT in Wunderlich Syndrome: Massive, hyperdense retroperitoneal hematoma (40-70 HU) dissecting into the perinephric and paranephric spaces, displacing the kidney and colon anteriorly, with active contrast extravasation ('contrast blush') on early arterial CTA phases

Abdominal MRI: Chemical shift imaging demonstrates the pathognomonic 'india-ink' boundary artifact (black etching line at fat-water interfaces) on out-of-phase T1-weighted gradient echo images; bright T1 and T2 signal with characteristic complete loss of signal on fat-saturated sequences

Catheter Renal Angiography: Hypervascular renal mass supplied by dilated, tortuous, dysplastic arterial branches displaying a 'sunburst' neovascular pattern with characteristic saccular or fusiform pseudoaneurysms (spontaneous rupture risk increases exponentially when pseudoaneurysms exceed 5 mm)
pathology_manifestations: Gross Nephrectomy / Embolization Specimen: Well-circumscribed, non-encapsulated, lobulated mass bulging from the renal parenchyma, displaying a variegated bright-yellow (adipose tissue), reddish-brown (hemorrhage), and grayish-white (smooth muscle) cut surface

Histopathology (Triphasic PEComa Architecture): Pathognomonic intermingling of three distinct tissue components: mature adipose tissue (adipocytes with variable lipid droplets), dysplastic, thick-walled, hyalinized, tortuous blood vessels completely lacking an internal elastic lamina, and sheets/fascicles of spindled and epithelioid smooth muscle cells radiating outward from vessel walls

Immunohistochemistry: Characteristic co-expression of melanocytic markers (diffuse positivity for HMB-45 and Melan-A) and myogenic markers (smooth muscle actin [SMA], Calponin); negative for epithelial markers (Cytokeratin AE1/AE3, Epithelial Membrane Antigen [EMA]), differentiating AML from clear cell RCC
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Paramount renal mesenchymal neoplasm featuring TSC cutaneous stigmata and Lenk's triad in Wunderlich syndrome, confirmed by pathognomonic negative CT attenuation (<-20 HU) and triphasic HMB-45-positive histology.

Nephrology.name: Renal Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Classic Guyon's triad of locally advanced disease: palpable, firm, non-tender abdominal/flank mass, macroscopic gross hematuria (often with worm-like ureteral clot casts), and dull, persistent loin/flank pain (fully present in ~10% of cases)

Acute non-reducing left-sided scrotal varicocele ('bag of worms') that fails to decompress or empty in the supine/recumbent position, caused by left renal vein occlusion by tumor thrombus impeding left gonadal vein drainage

Bilateral lower extremity pitting edema, ascites, and dilated, tortuous superficial collateral veins on the anterior abdominal wall (caput medusae / IVC syndrome) resulting from inferior vena cava tumor thrombus extension

Paraneoplastic systemic signs: Stauffer syndrome (non-metastatic hepatic dysfunction presenting with hepatomegaly, jaundice, elevated serum alkaline phosphatase, and prolonged prothrombin time), severe erythrocytosis (plethoric facies from ectopic tumor erythropoietin production), and symptomatic hypercalcemia (PTHrP release)
Cachexia, marked unintentional weight loss, and prolonged fever of unknown origin (IL-6 mediated)
radiological_manifestations: Multiphase Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI of Abdomen (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Heterogeneous, solid, exophytic cortical renal mass showing intense, vivid early arterial phase enhancement (>80-100 HU increase over unenhanced baseline) with rapid washout in the nephrographic/excretory phase; prominent areas of central non-enhancing necrosis, internal cystic degeneration, and coarse dystrophic calcifications

CT Venography / Abdominal MRI with Gadolinium: Precise delineation and staging of intravenous tumor thrombus: non-enhancing filling defect expanding the main renal vein and advancing into the inferior vena cava (IVC) up to the retrohepatic space or right atrium (Neves/Zincke classification Levels I-IV)

Renal Doppler Ultrasound: Hypoechoic or heterogeneous vascular mass displaying disordered high-velocity internal vascularity, along with absent or reversed flow in the main renal vein indicating invasive tumor thrombus
pathology_manifestations: Gross Nephrectomy Specimen: Well-circumscribed, fleshy, golden-yellow to orange-tan lobulated cortical mass bulging from the renal contour, punctuated by geographic areas of red hemorrhage, grayish-white necrosis, and central cystic liquefaction

Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Clear cell RCC (75-80%): Sheets, alveolar nests, and cords of uniform polygonal cells with abundant optical clear cytoplasm (secondary to dissolved cytoplasmic glycogen and neutral lipids during processing); bordered by an exquisite, delicate, arborizing network of thin-walled sinusoidal capillaries ('chicken-wire' vasculature); nucleolar prominence graded by the WHO/ISUP 4-tier grading system

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong, circumferential 'box-like' membranous staining for Carbonic Anhydrase IX (CA-IX), along with positivity for CD10, Vimentin, and PAX8; typically negative for CK7, CD117, and AMACR (differentiating from chromophobe RCC, oncocytoma, and papillary RCC)
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal primary renal neoplasm exhibiting Guyon's triad, an irreducible left-sided varicocele, and IVC syndrome, corroborated by multiphase CT/MRI showing a hypervascular necrotic cortical mass with venous thrombus and pathognomonic clear cells with 'chicken-wire' vascularity on histology.

Nephrology.name: Retroperitoneal Fibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Deep-seated, dull, non-colicky, persistent lower back, lumbar, flank, or lower abdominal pain radiating into the groins, testicles, or thighs, worse at night and poorly responsive to position changes

Progressive bilateral lower extremity edema, scrotal swelling, and secondary deep vein thrombosis (DVT) resulting from extrinsic compression of the inferior vena cava and iliac veins by the retroperitoneal fibrous mass
Lower extremity claudication and diminished lower extremity pulses caused by encasement and constriction of the abdominal aorta and common iliac arteries
Oliguria, anuria, or fluctuating urine output secondary to extrinsic ureteral obstruction and progressive obstructive uropathy (post-renal acute kidney injury)
Constitutional symptoms: low-grade fever, anorexia, involuntary weight loss, and fatigue
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT / MRI (Diagnostic Imaging Gold Standard): Pathognomonic well-demarcated fibrous retroperitoneal plaque or soft-tissue mass centered over the anterior and lateral surface of the infrarenal abdominal aorta and common iliac vessels (between the renal arteries and the aortic bifurcation), characteristically entrapping both ureters and the IVC

Classic Urographic / CT Hallmark: Pathognomonic 'medial deviation of the middle third of both ureters' with proximal ureterohydronephrosis, smooth tapering of the obstructed ureteral segments, without displacement of the abdominal aorta anteriorly away from the spine (a vital imaging differentiator from retroperitoneal lymphoma or sarcoma, which elevate the aorta)

Contrast Enhancement / PET-CT: Active inflammatory phase demonstrates vivid contrast enhancement on CT/MRI and intense hypermetabolism on 18F-FDG PET-CT; late inactive fibrous phase shows low T1 and low T2 signal intensity on MRI with minimal contrast enhancement
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Biopsy Histopathology (Diagnostic Hallmark): Dense, hypocellular, collagenous connective tissue characterized by whorled, fascicular, or storiform fibrosis; prominent perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate composed of mature B and T lymphocytes, plasma cells, and eosinophils; obliterative phlebitis (fibrotic occlusion and transmural inflammatory destruction of retroperitoneal veins)

Immunohistochemistry (IgG4-Related RPF): Abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells with >10 to 30 IgG4+ plasma cells per high-power field (HPF) and an elevated IgG4/IgG ratio exceeding 40%; negative for cytokeratins and sarcoma markers, confirming benign fibro-inflammatory proliferation
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic periaortitis and fibroinflammatory obstructive uropathy featuring lower back pain, lower limb edema/DVT, and pathognomonic CT/IVU medial deviation of ureters with an infrarenal periaortic fibrotic plaque, and storiform fibrosis with IgG4+ plasma cells and obliterative phlebitis on biopsy.

Nephrology.name: Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis
clinical_manifestations: Large, firm, tender, ballotable unilateral flank mass that can mimic a huge malignant retroperitoneal neoplasm
Profound chronic constitutional wasting: marked unintentional weight loss, anorexia, severe cachexia, low-grade daily swinging fevers, and dull unilateral flank or abdominal pain
Draining nephrocutaneous fistula: discharging purulent or yellowish sinus tracts through the lumbar flank skin, buttock, or groin
Severe flank erythema, induration, and tenderness over the costovertebral angle, occasionally with psoas sign (pain on hip extension due to retroperitoneal and psoas abscess extension)
Recurrent recalcitrant urinary tract infections and urosepsis, predominantly caused by Proteus mirabilis or Escherichia coli
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'Bear's Paw Sign': massively enlarged, non-functioning kidney wherein normal renal parenchyma is completely replaced by multiple rounded, low-attenuation (-10 to +30 Hounsfield Units) fluid- and lipid-filled cavities (dilated calyces filled with pus and xanthomatous debris) radiating outward in a paw-like distribution around a central obstructing, contracted renal pelvis containing a large, dense staghorn calculus

CT Pelvis / Retroperitoneum: Marked inflammatory infiltration and thick stranding of the perirenal space, thickening of Gerota's fascia, and extrarenal invasion into the psoas muscle, retroperitoneal fat, colon, and lateral abdominal wall forming nephrocutaneous and nephrocolic fistulae

Renal Ultrasound: Massive renal enlargement with complete distortion of normal corticomedullary architecture, multiple hypoechoic fluid-debris filled calyces radiating outwards, and a brightly echogenic central staghorn stone producing sharp acoustic shadowing
pathology_manifestations: Gross Nephrectomy Specimen: Massively enlarged, distorted kidney, the parenchyma of which is obliterated and replaced by multiple nodular, circumscribed, bright golden-yellow, orange-tan, and yellow-brown lipid-rich masses surrounding the necrotic pelvicalyceal system and the central obstructive staghorn stone, frequently with extension through the renal capsule into perinephric adipose tissue

Histopathology (Diagnostic Hallmark): Extensive destruction of normal renal architecture by a dense, destructive granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate dominated by sheets of lipid-laden foamy histiocytes (xanthoma cells) with round vesicular nuclei and abundant pale granular vacuolated cytoplasm; interspersed with multinucleated Touton giant cells (lipid ring surrounding a central wreath of nuclei), plasma cells, lymphocytes, and neutrophils, bordered by extensive cholesterol clefts and dense fibrous encapsulation

Immunohistochemistry: Foamy xanthoma cells are strongly and diffusely positive for CD68 and CD163 (histiocytic markers), while negative for cytokeratin (AE1/AE3), EMA, and CD10, clearly distinguishing XGP from clear cell renal cell carcinoma
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic destructive chronic infection featuring chronic cachexia, draining cutaneous flank fistulae, and a ballotable flank mass, accompanied by the pathognomonic 'bear's paw sign' with staghorn calculus on CT and sheets of lipid-laden CD68+ xanthoma cells and Touton giant cells on pathology.

Nephrology.name: Anti-GBM Disease
clinical_manifestations: Hemoptysis and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage in a young adult
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis is laboratory and urinary, not photographic
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph and CT: bilateral alveolar hemorrhage that clears faster than pneumonia
pathology_manifestations: Linear IgG along the glomerular basement membrane on immunofluorescence; lung biopsy shows the same linear pattern
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Pulmonary-renal disease whose hemorrhage films and linear immunofluorescence are the images.

Nephrology.name: Prune Belly Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Wrinkled, prune-like abdominal wall in a newborn boy
Bilateral cryptorchidism
Potter-like facies only if severe oligohydramnios occurred
radiological_manifestations: Voiding cystourethrogram and ultrasound: massively dilated ureters, a large bladder, and dysplastic kidneys
pathology_manifestations: Deficient abdominal-wall muscle on resection; renal dysplasia on nephrectomy specimens
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Congenital syndrome with an immediate clinical photograph and a dilated-tract imaging set.

Nephrology.name: Bladder Exstrophy
clinical_manifestations: Exposed bladder plate on the lower abdominal wall of a newborn
Divergent rectus muscles and a low-set umbilicus
Epispadias in boys
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic radiograph: wide pubic diastasis
pathology_manifestations: The exposed urothelium is the operative photograph; histology is normal urothelium rather than a tumor
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Open-bladder malformation with a delivery-room photograph and pelvic diastasis.

Nephrology.name: Branchio-Oto-Renal Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Preauricular pits, branchial cleft cysts, and a cupped ear
Hearing loss is not the photograph
radiological_manifestations: Renal ultrasound: hypoplasia, agenesis, or collecting-system duplication
pathology_manifestations: EYA1 or SIX1 confirms; the branchial cyst lining is not specific
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Syndrome with ear and neck photographs plus a renal ultrasound.

Nephrology.name: Lowe Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Infantile cataracts and glaucoma
Hypotonia and areflexia
radiological_manifestations: Renal ultrasound is often bland early; rickets films appear with phosphate wasting
pathology_manifestations: OCRL enzyme or sequencing; lens histology is rarely obtained
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Oculocerebrorenal disease with cataract photographs and later rachitic films.

Nephrology.name: Bardet-Biedl Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Postaxial polydactyly, retinal dystrophy, and truncal obesity
Hypogonadism
radiological_manifestations: Renal ultrasound: cystic dysplasia or calyceal clubbing
Fundus photographs of the rod-cone dystrophy
pathology_manifestations: Ciliary gene panel; renal histology is cystic dysplasia
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Ciliopathy with polydactyly, fundus photographs, and cystic-kidney imaging.

Nephrology.name: Congenital Nephrotic Syndrome, Finnish Type
clinical_manifestations: Edema from birth and a large placenta
No hematuria requirement
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: enlarged echogenic kidneys
pathology_manifestations: Foot-process effacement and pseudotubular microcystic dilatation; NPHS1 confirms
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Neonatal nephrotic disease with edema photographs and enlarged kidneys.

Nephrology.name: Townes-Brocks Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Satyr ear, imperforate anus, and triphalangeal or bifid thumbs
radiological_manifestations: Renal ultrasound: hypoplasia or multicystic dysplasia
Hand radiograph of the thumb malformation
pathology_manifestations: SALL1 confirms; anal and ear photographs are the clinical gallery
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Syndrome with ear, thumb, and anal photographs plus renal imaging.

Nephrology.name: Denys-Drash Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Ambiguous genitalia or a streak of male undervirilization
Early nephrotic syndrome
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: nephromegaly and a Wilms tumor
pathology_manifestations: Diffuse mesangial sclerosis; WT1 exon 8 or 9 mutation
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: WT1 syndrome with genital photographs, nephrotic onset, and a Wilms-tumor ultrasound.

Nephrology.name: WAGR Syndrome
synonyms: Wilms tumor, aniridia, genitourinary anomalies, range of developmental delay
clinical_manifestations: Aniridia and a genital anomaly
A flank mass if Wilms tumor presents clinically
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal ultrasound or MRI of the Wilms tumor
Orbital photograph of aniridia
pathology_manifestations: 11p13 deletion including WT1 and PAX6; Wilms histology if resected
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Contiguous-gene syndrome with an aniridia photograph and a Wilms imaging set.

Nephrology.name: Senior-Loken Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Childhood polyuria and later blindness
Fundus: retinitis pigmentosa or Leber amaurosis
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: normal-size or small echogenic kidneys with cysts at the corticomedullary junction
pathology_manifestations: Nephronophthisis histology: tubular basement-membrane disruption
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Renal-retinal ciliopathy with fundus photographs and corticomedullary cysts.

Nephrology.name: Familial LCAT Deficiency
clinical_manifestations: Corneal opacities described as fish-eye
Proteinuria progressing to kidney failure
radiological_manifestations: No specific radiology; the slit-lamp cornea is the image
pathology_manifestations: Renal foam cells and serologic very-low HDL; LCAT sequencing confirms
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Lipid disorder with a slit-lamp corneal photograph and renal foam-cell histology.

Nephrology.name: Nephrogenic Systemic Fibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Striking clinical photographs of thick, indurated, brawny, woody skin plaques with a coarse 'peau d'orange' or cobblestone surface on the extremities and trunk
Severe, disabling flexion contractures of the fingers, wrists, elbows, knees, and ankles ('wooden doll' or 'frozen joints' appearance)
Yellow, discrete, scleral plaques or papules near the limbus (distinct from pingueculae) visible on direct ocular inspection in end-stage renal disease patients
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography and CT: Extensive, dense periarticular soft tissue calcification, fascial thickening, and joint contracture deformities in patients with renal failure
Extremity MRI: Diffuse thickening of the skin, deep subcutaneous fat stranding, and marked thickening and hyperintensity of the deep fascia on T2-weighted STIR images
Prior Imaging History: Documented prior exposure to linear gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) in the setting of acute kidney injury or stage 4-5 chronic kidney disease
pathology_manifestations: Full-Thickness Deep Incisional Skin Biopsy (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Marked expansion and thickening of the dermis extending into the subcutaneous septa, packed with proliferating CD34+/procollagen I+ spindle-shaped circulating fibrocytes

Dermal Matrix Pathology: Coarse, haphazard collagen bundles surrounded by abundant mucin (colloidal iron positive), thickened elastic fibers, and multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells containing gadolinium deposits (detectable by mass spectrometry)
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Classic iatrogenic dermatologic nephrology disease where GBCA exposure in severe renal failure triggers dramatic, woody skin plaques, frozen flexion contractures, and pathognomonic CD34+ dermal fibrocyte proliferation.

Nephrology.name: Urofacial Syndrome
synonyms: partial facial palsy with urinary tract abnormalities
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic 'inverted smile' on clinical facial photographs: whenever the child attempts to smile or laugh, the facial muscles contract paradoxically to produce an appearance of crying, frowning, or grimacing
Daytime and nighttime severe urinary incontinence, enuresis, and recurrent febrile urinary tract infections in early childhood
Palpable distended urinary bladder, failure to thrive, and progressive signs of uremic renal insufficiency
radiological_manifestations: Voiding Cystourethrography (VCUG): Severe neurogenic bladder with a thick-walled trabeculated 'Christmas tree' or pine-cone bladder, massive bilateral vesicoureteral reflux (grades IV-V), and bladder diverticula
Renal and Bladder Ultrasonography: Bilateral severe hydroureteronephrosis, renal parenchymal thinning, and persistent post-void residual urine volume
Renal Cortical Scintigraphy (DMSA): Extensive multifocal photopenic renal cortical scarring from recurrent pyelonephritis, with progressive loss of differential renal function
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Etiology: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in HPSE2 (heparanase 2) or LRIG2, affecting neural circuitry co-regulating pontine micturition center and facial motor nuclei
Renal Histopathology: Severe chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis, tubular atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis from reflux nephropathy
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield neuro-nephrologic condition featuring the unmistakable photographic clinical sign of an 'inverted smile' (crying grimace upon smiling) that points directly to severe neurogenic bladder and reflux nephropathy.

Nephrology.name: Papillorenal Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic optic nerve coloboma on direct funduscopic photographs: large, excavated optic nerve head with multiple cilioretinal vessels emerging from the periphery of the optic disc ('morning glory' appearance)
Visual impairment: decreased visual acuity, visual field defects, and sensory nystagmus
Progressive chronic kidney disease presenting with proteinuria, microscopic hematuria, hypertension, and early progression to end-stage renal disease
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasonography: Bilateral hypoplastic, small, echogenic kidneys with reduced corticomedullary differentiation, loss of renal parenchyma, and small cortical cysts
CT Urography: Bilateral small kidneys with caliceal blunting and hypoplastic caliceal systems without urinary tract obstruction
Orbital MRI / Ocular Coherence Tomography (OCT): Deep posterior excavation of the optic papilla with discontinuity of the neurosensory retina and retinal pigment epithelium
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the PAX2 transcription factor essential for metanephric mesenchyme and optic cup organogenesis
Renal Biopsy: Marked oligomeganephronia (reduced number of glomeruli with marked compensatory glomerular enlargement) with secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and tubular atrophy
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal syndromic renal disease pairing high-yield fundus photographs of optic nerve colobomas with cilioretinal vessels directly to bilateral renal hypodysplasia (oligomeganephronia) and early ESRD.

Nephrology.name: Alström Syndrome
synonyms: ciliopathy with renal disease and cone-rod dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Visual manifestations on clinical examination: infantile nystagmus, photophobia, and early childhood loss of vision due to progressive cone-rod dystrophy (optic atrophy and attenuated retinal vessels on fundus photos)
Prominent truncal childhood obesity with florid flexural acanthosis nigricans and severe insulin resistance visible in clinical photographs
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss, short stature in adulthood, and progressive chronic renal insufficiency with uremic symptoms
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasonography: Bilateral small or normal-sized kidneys with marked cortical hyperechogenicity, loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and multiple small cortical and medullary cysts
Transthoracic Echocardiography: Infantile dilated cardiomyopathy with severely reduced ejection fraction, or adult-onset restrictive cardiomyopathy with marked interstitial fibrosis
Abdominal Ultrasound / MRI: Marked hepatic steatosis, hepatosplenomegaly, and portal hypertension
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Etiology: Biallelic mutations in ALMS1 localized to basal bodies and primary cilia, disrupting cellular ciliary signaling and trafficking
Renal Histopathology: Severe chronic tubulointerstitial fibrosis out of proportion to glomerular changes, tubular atrophy, thickened tubular basement membranes, and secondary glomerulosclerosis
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Multi-organ ciliopathy characterized by progressive tubulointerstitial nephropathy and renal failure, accompanied by recognizable clinical photographs of early-onset obesity, acanthosis nigricans, and cone-rod retinopathy.

Nephrology.name: Schimke Immuno-Osseous Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Striking cutaneous signs in clinical photographs: multiple, diffuse, hyperpigmented macules and lentigines (freckle-like pigmented lesions) distributed over the face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism with accentuated lumbar lordosis, barrel chest, and characteristic triangular facies with broad depressed nasal bridge and bulbous nasal tip
Severe steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (massive proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, generalized anasarca) progressing rapidly to end-stage renal disease in childhood
radiological_manifestations: Spinal Radiography (Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia): Ovoid, flattened vertebral bodies (platyspondyly) with anterior beaking, irregular endplates, and thoracic kyphoscoliosis
Pelvic Radiography: Hypoplastic, small, fragmented capital femoral epiphyses with shallow, dysplastic acetabular roofs and coxa vara
Renal Ultrasonography: Bilateral echogenic kidneys with loss of corticomedullary differentiation and progressive volume reduction
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy (Light & Electron Microscopy): Classic focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) with extensive podocyte foot process effacement, mesangial expansion, and progressive global glomerulosclerosis
Molecular Etiology: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in SMARCAL1 (encoding a DNA annealing helicase required for stalled replication fork restart)
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield pediatric nephrology entity where aggressive FSGS nephrotic syndrome is directly recognizable by the unique bedside phenotype of widespread pigmented lentigines and spondyloepiphyseal dwarfism.

Nephrology.name: Mainzer-Saldino Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Early progressive vision loss with tapetoretinal degeneration / pigmentary retinopathy (salt-and-pepper fundus and bone-spicule retinal pigmentation visible on fundus photography)
Chronic tubulointerstitial nephropathy / nephronophthisis presenting with polyuria, polydipsia, anemia, and progression to end-stage renal disease in childhood or adolescence
Cerebellar ataxia with unsteady wide-based gait, intention tremor, and dysarthria
radiological_manifestations: Hand Radiography (Pathognomonic Gold Standard): Characteristic cone-shaped epiphyses of the middle and distal phalanges of the fingers, with premature fusion of phalangeal growth plates

Renal Ultrasonography: Small-to-normal sized kidneys with increased cortical echogenicity, loss of corticomedullary boundary, and multiple corticomedullary junction cysts characteristic of nephronophthisis
Chest and Long Bone Radiography: Narrow thorax with shortened ribs and mildly shortened tubular bones with flared metaphyses
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Pathogenesis: Biallelic mutations in IFT140 (encoding intraflagellar transport protein 140), disrupting retrograde primary ciliary transport

Renal Biopsy: Histopathology of nephronophthisis showing extensive tubular basement membrane thickening, tubular atrophy with diverticula, chronic interstitial fibrosis, and secondary glomerular sclerosis
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Classic 'conorenal' ciliopathy linking juvenile nephronophthisis leading to ESRD with pathognomonic radiological cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses on hand X-rays and pigmentary retinopathy on fundoscopy.

Nephrology.name: Medullary Sponge Kidney
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent, exquisitely painful nephrolithiasis and ureteral colic in young adults (typically 20s to 30s), frequently passing small calcium oxalate or calcium phosphate calculi
Recurrent complicated urinary tract infections, pyelonephritis, and dysuria secondary to urinary stasis within ectatic collecting ducts
Persistent gross or microscopic hematuria provoked by stone passage, gravel voiding, or hypercalciuria
Distal renal tubular acidosis (incomplete type 1 dRTA) with impaired urinary acidification and hypocitraturia
radiological_manifestations: Intravenous Urography (IVU) / CT Urography: Pathognomonic 'bouquet of flowers', 'paintbrush', or 'fan-like' appearance caused by contrast pooling within ectatic, cystic precaliceal collecting ducts of Bellini
Non-Contrast Helical CT: Diffuse, bilateral, clustered pyramidal medullary nephrocalcinosis characterized by punctate calcifications strictly confined to the renal pyramids surrounding the calyces
Renal Ultrasonography: Prominent, hyperechoic renal pyramids with or without acoustic shadowing, representing medullary nephrocalcinosis within ectatic papillary ducts
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology: Spongy, porous appearance of the renal papillae and medullae studded with multiple small spherical or fusiform cysts measuring 1 to 7 mm

Histopathology: Ectasia and cystic dilatation of terminal collecting ducts in the renal pyramids lined by cuboidal or transitional epithelium, frequently containing laminated calcium phosphate (apatite) calculi and surrounded by mild periductal fibrosis; renal cortex remains normal
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield cystic kidney disease characterized by the iconic 'bouquet of flowers' and 'paintbrush' signs on CT urography and pyramidal medullary nephrocalcinosis.

Nephrology.name: Jeune Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Unmistakable clinical thoracic photography: severely constricted, bell-shaped, extremely narrow thorax with short horizontal ribs, causing severe neonatal respiratory insufficiency
Micromelic dwarfism with disproportionately shortened extremities, brachydactyly, and occasional postaxial polydactyly
Progressive renal involvement in childhood: polyuria, polydipsia, proteinuria, and progressive renal failure (nephronophthisis-like ciliopathy developing in 30-40% of long-term survivors)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Pathognomonic Gold Standard): Severely hypoplastic, bell-shaped thorax with markedly shortened, horizontal ribs that do not extend past the anterior axillary line, and flared anterior rib ends
Pelvic Radiography: Characteristic 'trident' pelvis with flared iliac crests, spur-like medial and lateral acetabular projections, and premature capital femoral ossification
Renal Ultrasonography: Hyperechoic, small-to-normal sized kidneys with progressive corticomedullary cyst formation, loss of differentiation, and tubular atrophy
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Etiology: Mutations in intraflagellar transport and dynein motor genes (DYNC2H1, IFT80, IFT140), leading to defective skeletal and renal ciliary function
Renal Histopathology: Juvenile nephronophthisis / cystic renal dysplasia with thickened, disrupted tubular basement membranes, extensive interstitial fibrosis, and tubular microcysts
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Severe ciliopathy combining a pathognomonic constricted bell-shaped chest and trident pelvis with progressive cystic renal dysplasia and nephronophthisis-type renal failure.

Nephrology.name: Galloway-Mowat Syndrome
synonyms: microcephaly with nephrotic syndrome and hiatal hernia
clinical_manifestations: Striking craniofacial photographs: severe secondary microcephaly with sloping forehead, large floppy ears, epicanthal folds, and micrognathia
Early-onset, treatment-resistant nephrotic syndrome (massive proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, severe generalized anasarca) presenting in early infancy or childhood
Severe neurodevelopmental delay, generalized axial hypotonia with peripheral hypertonia, and intractable epileptic encephalopathy
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Severe microcephaly with simplified gyral pattern, lissencephaly/pachygyria, marked cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, and prominent arachnoid spaces
Renal Ultrasonography: Bilaterally enlarged, echogenic kidneys with poor corticomedullary differentiation during early nephrotic phase, progressing to small shrunken kidneys
Upper Gastrointestinal Series: Frequent presence of a large congenital hiatal hernia with gastroesophageal reflux
pathology_manifestations: Renal Histopathology: Diffuse mesangial sclerosis (DMS) or aggressive focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) with severe foot process effacement and podocyte detachment on electron microscopy
Molecular Etiology: Mutations in the KEOPS complex genes (WDR73, OSGEP, TP53RK, TPRKB, LAGE3), required for universal tRNA modification in podocytes and neurons
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct clinicopathologic disease linking treatment-resistant nephrotic syndrome (diffuse mesangial sclerosis) directly to severe microcephaly, sloping forehead, large ears, and cerebellar hypoplasia.

Nephrology.name: Multicentric Carpotarsal Osteolysis Syndrome
synonyms: carpal and tarsal osteolysis with nephropathy
clinical_manifestations: Dramatic clinical photographs of hand and foot deformities: marked shortening of the wrists, ulnar deviation of the hands, subluxated carpal joints, and flat collapsed arches with foot contractures
Craniofacial features: triangular face, micrognathia, exophthalmos, and corneal clouding
Aggressive childhood-onset renal disease: asymptomatic proteinuria and microhematuria progressing rapidly to steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, severe hypertension, and early ESRD
radiological_manifestations: Serial Wrist and Ankle Radiographs (Pathognomonic 'Disappearing Bones'): Progressive osteolysis, bone resorption, and complete disappearance of carpal and tarsal bones, with tapering 'penciling' of metacarpal and metatarsal bases
Renal Ultrasonography: Bilaterally small, hyperechoic kidneys with parenchymal thinning and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
Elbow and Knee Radiography: Progressive resorption of radial heads and adjacent articular surfaces with secondary joint subluxation
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous de novo missense mutations in MAFB (transcription factor regulating podocyte gene expression and osteoclast differentiation)
Renal Biopsy: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) with marked podocyte foot process effacement, prominent interstitial fibrosis, and dense collagenous glomerular obsolescence
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Unique skeletal-nephrologic disease pairing rapid childhood progression to ESRD with pathognomonic clinical and radiological disappearance (osteolysis) of carpal and tarsal bones.

Nephrology.name: IgA nephropathy
clinical_manifestations: mesangial proliferation, dominant IgA on immunofluorescence.

clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic bilateral extreme congenital microcoria (fixed pinhole pupils <2 mm) with iris atrophy + neonatal nephrotic anasarca and enlarged hyperechoic kidneys on US

Nephrology.name: Frasier Syndrome (WT1 Splice-Site Nephropathy with Gonadal Dysgenesis)
synonyms: WT1 Splice-Site Nephropathy with Gonadal Dysgenesis
clinical_manifestations: 46,XY complete female external genitalia, nephrotic edema (FSGS), and pelvic streak gonads with calcified gonadoblastoma on pelvic MRI/US
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Nephrology.name: Cystinuria (Hereditary Dibasic Aminoaciduria and Cystine Urolithiasis)
synonyms: Hereditary Dibasic Aminoaciduria and Cystine Urolithiasis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic colorless, flat, 6-sided hexagonal "benzene-ring" cystine crystals on urine microscopy and waxy yellow radiopaque staghorn calculi on CT/KUB
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Nephrology.name: Cranioectodermal Dysplasia (Sensenbrenner Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Dolichocephaly (sagittal craniosynostosis), sparse hair, microdontia, narrow thorax, brachydactyly, and hyperechoic nephronophthisis kidneys on US
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Nephrology.name: Adenine Phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT) Deficiency (2,8-Dihydroxyadeninuria)
clinical_manifestations: Reddish-brown diaper stains, friable bluish-gray stones, and pathognomonic brown spherical crystals with a central "Maltese cross" under polarized urine microscopy
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Nephrology.name: Uromodulin-Associated Kidney Disease (ADTKD-UMOD / Familial Juvenile Hyperuricemic Nephropathy)
clinical_manifestations: Precocious teenage/young-adult gouty podagra and tophi + "punched-out" overhanging rat-bite erosions on X-ray and shrunken corticomedullary-cyst kidneys
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Nephrology.name: Bilateral renal agenesis (Potter sequence)
clinical_manifestations: Potter facies with absent kidneys and pulmonary hypoplasia.
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Nephrology.name: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney (MCDK)
clinical_manifestations: a non-reniform cluster of noncommunicating cysts.
Transilluminating neonatal flank mass with non-communicating anechoic cysts of varying sizes ("bunch of grapes") and no central renal pelvis on ultrasound.
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Neurology.name: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
clinical_manifestations: Acute monophasic encephalopathy: Abrupt onset of altered mental status (lethargy, confusion, delirium, stupor, or coma) occurring 1 to 3 weeks following a viral prodrome (e.g., exanthematous virus, upper respiratory infection) or immunization, primarily in children and young adults

Multifocal neurologic deficits: Bilateral optic neuritis, multiple cranial neuropathies (facial palsy, ocular dysmotility), ataxia, hemiparesis or quadriparesis, meningismus, and hyperreflexia with bilateral extensor plantar responses
Acute transverse myelitis signs: Rapidly ascending sensory deficits, paraplegia, and acute neurogenic urinary retention requiring catheterization
Fulminant variants (Acute Hemorrhagic Leukoencephalitis / Weston Hurst syndrome): Hyperacute deterioration with high fever, seizures, deep coma, signs of brain herniation, and decerebrate posturing
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial and Coronal T2/FLAIR and T1+Gd): Hallmark large, bilateral, asymmetrical, poorly marginated, fluffy or 'cloud-like' T2/FLAIR hyperintensities involving the subcortical and deep cerebral white matter, centrum semiovale, thalamus, and basal ganglia; deep gray matter involvement (thalamic/striatal) is frequent and helpful in distinguishing from classic MS; post-gadolinium T1 shows variable punctate, nodular, or incomplete ring enhancement; all lesions appear of the same chronological age
Spine MRI: Confluent, poorly demarcated, extensive intramedullary T2 hyperintensity spanning multiple vertebral segments with mild cord swelling and patchy enhancement
Head CT / MRI in Weston Hurst syndrome: Massive cerebral edema with focal petechial hemorrhages on CT and prominent gradient blooming on GRE/SWI sequences
pathology_manifestations: CNS histopathology / autopsy: Pathognomonic perivenular sleeves ('cuffs') of demyelination centered around small- and medium-sized parenchymal veins in cerebral and spinal white matter; dense infiltration of foamy lipid-laden macrophages engulfing myelin debris, accompanied by perivascular T-cell and B-cell infiltration; remarkable relative preservation of axons and absence of older, chronic astrogliotic plaques (monophasic single-age pathology)
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Hallmark pediatric/young adult demyelinating encephalopathy with florid post-infectious presentation, classic bilateral fluffy/cloud-like white matter and deep gray MRI lesions of uniform age, and perivenular demyelinating sleeves on histopathology.

Neurology.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
clinical_manifestations: Widespread visible muscle fasciculations (rippling and flickering twitches beneath skin of limbs and trunk)
Tongue muscle atrophy, wrinkling, and continuous visible tongue fasciculations
'Split-hand' syndrome (preferential, marked wasting of the thenar complex [APB/FDI] with relative sparing of the hypothenar muscle [ADM])
Simultaneous upper motor neuron signs (spasticity, brisk hyperreflexia, extensor plantar response) and lower motor neuron signs (profound wasting, flaccidity, weakness)
Claw hand, wrist drop, and foot drop with steppage gait
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Cervical Spine MRI: Bilateral, symmetrical, continuous T2/FLAIR hyperintensity tracking along the corticospinal tracts from the corona radiata through the internal capsule and brainstem; 'motor band sign' (hypointensity of the precentral motor cortex on T2*/SWI due to excessive iron/macrophage deposition); spinal cord anterior horn atrophy
High-Frequency Muscle Ultrasound: High sensitivity for detection of silent, widespread muscle fasciculations and progressive muscle architecture atrophy
pathology_manifestations: Autopsy / muscle biopsy: Marked loss and degeneration of anterior horn alpha-motor neurons in the spinal cord and cortical Betz cells; reactive astrogliosis; characteristic TDP-43-positive ubiquitinated cytoplasmic inclusions within remaining motor neurons; muscle biopsy shows classic neurogenic group atrophy with target fibers
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Combines striking physical signs (tongue fasciculations, 'split-hand' thenar wasting) with MRI corticospinal tract hyperintensity and muscle ultrasound fasciculation mapping.

Neurology.name: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
clinical_manifestations: Florid psychiatric prodrome: Acute-onset severe psychosis, agitation, paranoid delusions, visual and auditory hallucinations, mania, bizarre disinhibited behavior, and severe insomnia in previously healthy young females or children

Pathognomonic stereotypic dyskinesias: Continuous, involuntary, bizarre oro-facial-lingual dyskinesias (continuous lip-smacking, chewing, tongue protrusion, grimacing, teeth-grinding/bruxism), accompanied by choreoathetoid limb writhing, oculogyric crises, and pelvic thrusting
Catatonia, mutism, and memory collapse: Rapid progression to profound speech reduction, echolalia, complete mutism, waxy flexibility, catatonic posturing, and dense retrograde/anterograde amnesia

Autonomic instability and central hypoventilation: Life-threatening fluctuations in blood pressure, hyperpyrexia, sinus tachycardia, severe cardiac bradyarrhythmias/pauses, hypersalivation, and central respiratory hypoventilation requiring mechanical ventilation
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic Transvaginal Ultrasound and Contrast-Enhanced CT/MRI: High-sensitivity demonstration of an underlying mature cystic ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst) containing calcified tooth/bone components, acoustic shadowing, cystic fat-fluid levels, and Rokitansky nodules in ~40-50% of young female cases

Brain MRI (T2/FLAIR and T1+Gd): Often normal or showing subtle, transient, non-specific T2/FLAIR hyperintensities within the medial temporal lobes, hippocampus, frontobasal cortex, basal ganglia, and periventricular white matter; faint meningeal or cortical gyral enhancement in ~20-30%

Continuous Video-EEG: Highly characteristic, pathognomonic 'extreme delta brush' (EDB) electrographic pattern: continuous, rhythmic, symmetrical 1-3 Hz delta waves with superimposed bursts of fast 20-30 Hz beta activity predominantly in frontal derivations
pathology_manifestations: Ovarian teratoma and neural tissue pathology: Mature cystic teratoma containing dysplastic neuroglial tissue infiltrated by prominent CD20+ B lymphocytes, CD138+ plasma cells, and microglial activation; confirmation of CSF and serum IgG antibodies (subclass IgG1) directed against the GluN1 (NR1) subunit of the NMDA receptor; immunofluorescence shows antibody-induced cross-linking, capping, and selective internalization of cell-surface NMDA receptors into endosomes, causing reversible loss of synaptic NMDA receptor clusters without neuronal death
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic autoimmune synaptic encephalitis featuring pathognomonic oro-facial-lingual dyskinesias, electrographic 'extreme delta brush', pelvic ultrasound/CT ovarian teratoma, and anti-GluN1 receptor-internalizing pathology.

Neurology.name: Carotid-Cavernous Fistula
clinical_manifestations: Pulsatile exophthalmos (proptosis): Unilateral forward ocular protrusion that visibly and synchronously pulsates with the arterial cardiac pulse, accompanied by palpable orbital thrill on gentle digital palpation of the globe

Auscultated ocular and cephalic bruit: Loud, continuous, whooshing subjective and objective cranial bruit heard loudest over the ipsilateral orbit, forehead, and temple, characteristically diminishing or abolished upon digital compression of the ipsilateral common carotid artery in the neck

Chemosis and 'corkscrew' arterialized episcleral vessels: Dramatic conjunctival edema (chemosis) with beefy red prolapse of the conjunctiva beyond the palpebral fissure, accompanied by pathognomonic corkscrew-like, dilated, tortuous, brightly arterialized episcleral and conjunctival vessels radiating outward towards the limbus ('caput medusae' of the eye)

Cranial nerve ophthalmoplegia: Variable combinations of third (oculomotor), fourth (trochlear), and sixth (abducens) cranial nerve palsies due to compressive engorgement or ischemia within the cavernous sinus wall, most frequently presenting as an early, isolated sixth nerve palsy (horizontal diplopia in lateral gaze) because CN VI runs free within the cavernous sinus lumen adjacent to the carotid artery

Secondary glaucoma and ocular hypertension: Severely elevated intraocular pressure (frequently >30-40 mmHg) with ocular pain, corneal edema, and venous stasis retinopathy (dilated tortuous retinal veins, flame hemorrhages, and optic disc edema) due to chronically elevated vortex and episcleral venous pressure
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Orbit and Brain CT / CTA: Prominent, pathognomonic enlargement and asymmetric dilatation of the ipsilateral superior ophthalmic vein (SOV, often >3-4 mm in diameter); outward convex bulging and expansion of the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus; asymmetric proptosis and marked enlargement of the extraocular muscle bellies (especially the superior rectus and medial rectus complexes) with sparing of the tendinous insertions

Orbit and Brain MRI / MRV: Markedly dilated, tortuous tubular flow voids in the superior ophthalmic vein and cavernous sinus on T1- and T2-weighted sequences; asymmetric expansion of the cavernous sinus with early post-contrast enhancement identical in timing to internal carotid artery transit; engorgement of cortical and dural draining veins with T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in adjacent brain parenchyma in high-risk retrograde cortical venous drainage

Catheter Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA, Gold Standard): Unequivocal demonstration of an abnormal high-flow or low-flow arteriovenous communication between the internal or external carotid artery and the cavernous sinus; Barrow classification: Type A (direct, high-flow shunt between the intracavernous internal carotid artery and cavernous sinus, classic post-traumatic or ruptured aneurysm), Type B (dural shunt from meningeal branches of the ICA), Type C (dural shunt from meningeal branches of the ECA), and Type D (dural shunt from meningeal branches of both ICA and ECA); immediate filling of the cavernous sinus during early arterial phase with retrograde opacification of the superior ophthalmic vein, inferior ophthalmic vein, and inferior petrosal sinus
pathology_manifestations: Vascular and Fistulous Histopathology: Direct laceration or defect in the muscularis and internal elastic lamina of the cavernous segment of the internal carotid artery connecting directly with the thin-walled, endothelially lined venous channels of the cavernous sinus; or complex plexiform nidus of microscopic arteriovenous communications within the dural wall of the sinus supplied by the meningohypophyseal trunk or inferolateral trunk; marked arterialization of the draining veins characterized by fibromuscular intimal hyperplasia, medial hypertrophy, fragmented elastic lamina, and microthrombosis
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive neurovascular and neuro-ophthalmic entity presenting with the unmistakable photographic triad of pulsatile proptosis, auscultable orbital bruit, and corkscrew arterialized conjunctival vessels, definitively staged on catheter DSA and orbit CT/MRI via superior ophthalmic vein enlargement.

Neurology.name: Cerebral Cavernous Malformation
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent unprovoked epileptic seizures: The most common initial presentation (50-70% of supratentorial cases), manifesting as focal seizures with or without impaired awareness or progression to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures, driven by recurrent microscopic subclinical hemorrhages that deposit epileptogenic hemosiderin into the surrounding perilesional cerebral cortex

Focal neurological deficits: Subacute or sudden motor weakness, sensory loss, cranial nerve palsies, dysmetria, or visual field deficits occurring in a 'stepwise' or episodic relapsing-remitting course caused by recurrent intralesional microhemorrhages, local mass effect, and perilesional edema

Brainstem cavernoma apoplexy: Severe acute headache, diplopia, internuclear ophthalmoplegia, facial numbness, dysarthria, dysphagia, ataxia, and quadriparesis resulting from acute hemorrhage within a brainstem cavernoma (pons, midbrain, medulla) causing catastrophic compression of compact cranial nerve nuclei and long tracts

Chronic intractable headaches: Persistent throbbing or dull localized head pain resulting from microvascular expansion, dural irritation, or intermittent microbleeding into neighboring parenchymal tissue

Familial multiple cavernoma cutaneous lesions: In patients with hereditary CCM (autosomal dominant loss-of-function mutations in CCM1/KRIT1, CCM2/MGC4607, or CCM3/PDCD10), presence of hyperkeratotic cutaneous capillary-venous malformations, facial angiofibromas, or vertebral hemangiomas accompanied by dozens of asymptomatic or symptomatic intracranial lesions
radiological_manifestations: Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI, Pathognomonic Popcorn Appearance): T2-weighted and FLAIR imaging unequivocally demonstrates the pathognomonic well-circumscribed 'popcorn' or 'mulberry' lesion characterized by a central heterogeneous core of reticulated mixed hyperintense and hypointense signal intensities representing hemorrhage of varying chronological stages (methemoglobin, intracellular and extracellular, and hemosiderin), completely enveloped by a continuous, well-defined hypointense rim of hemosiderin deposition

Gradient-Echo (GRE) T2* and Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI): Dramatic, exquisite 'blooming' artifact with intense signal drop-out resulting from magnetic susceptibility effects of perilesional hemosiderin; SWI is hypersensitive and detects dozens to hundreds of occult punctate micro-cavernomas in familial forms that are entirely invisible on conventional spin-echo T1/T2 imaging
