clinical_manifestations: Retinal capillary hemangioblastomas (von Hippel angiomas): Direct fundoscopy and color fundus photography demonstrate bright reddish-orange or pink spherical vascular lesions located in the peripheral or peripapillary retina, supplied by a conspicuously dilated, tortuous retinal feeder artery and drained by an engorged, tortuous vein, frequently surrounded by hard lipid exudates and macular star formation

Polycythemic ruddy cyanosis / plethora: Striking facial rubor, flushing, and conjunctival suffusion caused by secondary polycythemia resulting from tumor-driven ectopic erythropoietin (EPO) secretion by renal cell carcinomas or cerebellar hemangioblastomas

Pheochromocytoma paroxysms: Episodic severe hypertension accompanied by the classic symptomatic triad of profuse diaphoresis, headache, and episodic pallor/flushing, with postural orthostatic hypotension

Cerebellar and vestibular signs: Subacute truncal ataxia, appendicular intention tremor, dysmetria, past-pointing, and coarse horizontal/gaze-evoked nystagmus resulting from posterior fossa hemangioblastomas and obstructive hydrocephalus
Palpable scrotal or epididymal masses: Painless, firm, nodular scrotal swellings due to papillary cystadenomas of the epididymis in males or broad ligament cystadenomas in females
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Spinal Cord Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Pathognomonic hemangioblastomas appearing as well-demarcated cystic lesions with an intensely enhancing, vascular mural nodule abutting the pial surface; prominent serpiginous flow voids from dilated feeding vessels; characteristic predilection for the cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, medulla, and dorsal spinal cord; avid nodular enhancement on post-gadolinium T1-weighted images with high T2 signal in surrounding cystic fluid

Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT and MRI: Multicentric bilateral clear cell renal cell carcinomas (RCC) manifesting as heterogeneous enhancing cortical lesions with necrotic cystic components; innumerable simple pancreatic cysts, serous microcystic cystadenomas, and hypervascular pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET); bilateral adrenal pheochromocytomas with intense arterial phase enhancement, heterogeneous central necrosis, and delayed wash-out

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Immediate, intense hyperfluorescence of retinal capillary hemangioblastomas in the early arterial phase with late profuse fluorescein leakage into the vitreous and surrounding subretinal exudation
pathology_manifestations: Hemangioblastoma histopathology: Highly vascular neoplasm composed of an intricate meshwork of thin-walled, arborizing capillary blood vessels lined by normal endothelial cells, interspersed with abundant, distinctive vacuolated stromal cells containing lipid-rich, clear, lipid-laden cytoplasm; immunohistochemistry shows positive staining for inhibin-A, S100, neuron-specific enolase (NSE), and carbonic anhydrase IX (CA-IX); genetic confirmation demonstrates germline loss-of-function mutation or deletion of the VHL tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 3p25-26
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic multi-system phakomatosis combining unmistakable fundoscopic retinal angiomas and polycythemic facies with pathognomonic MRI cystic lesions with enhancing mural nodules, abdominal CT renal cell carcinomas and pheochromocytomas, and characteristic lipid-laden stromal pathology.

Neurology.name: Wilson's Disease
clinical_manifestations: Kayser-Fleischer (KF) rings: golden-brown or greenish copper rings at the periphery of the cornea in Descemet's membrane on slit-lamp biomicroscopy
Sunflower cataracts (anterior subcapsular copper deposition)
Facial dystonia creating an involuntary fixed vacant smile ('risus sardonicus')
'Wing-beating' tremor (coarse, slow, high-amplitude postural tremor upon arm abduction)
Dysarthria, dystonia, choreoathetosis, and parkinsonian rigidity
Stigmata of chronic liver disease (spider angiomas, palmar erythema, jaundice)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Pathognomonic 'face of the giant panda' sign in the midbrain (normal red nuclei as 'eyes', normal substantia nigra as 'ears', and hypointense superior colliculus as 'chin' set against hyperintense tegmentum on T2); 'face of the miniature panda' in the pons; bilateral symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in lentiform and caudate nuclei, thalami, and brainstem
Abdominal Ultrasound / MRI: Micronodular or macronodular cirrhosis, splenomegaly, ascites
pathology_manifestations: Liver needle biopsy: Steatosis, glycogenated nuclei, chronic active hepatitis progressing to micronodular cirrhosis; marked elevation of hepatic copper concentration (>250 ug/g dry weight); rhodanine or rubeanic acid staining demonstrates coarse copper granules in periportal hepatocytes
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield neuro-metabolic entity with the unmistakable corneal Kayser-Fleischer ring paired with the textbook 'face of the giant panda' sign on brain MRI.

Neurology.name: X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Bronze hyperpigmentation when adrenal failure accompanies the cerebral disease
Behavioral change and school failure are not images; the photograph is the pigment plus the MRI
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: posterior white-matter demyelination with a leading edge of contrast enhancement, scored by the Loes pattern
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal cortical atrophy; very-long-chain fatty acids and ABCD1 sequencing confirm
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Leukodystrophy with a named MRI pattern and, often, Addisonian photographs.

Neurology.name: Melkersson-Rosenthal Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent non-pitting lip or facial swelling
Fissured lingua plicata
Recurrent facial palsy, photographed during an attack
radiological_manifestations: MRI may show facial-nerve enhancement during palsy; it is supportive, not defining
pathology_manifestations: Non-caseating granulomas in the lip, overlapping orofacial granulomatosis
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Triad with three photographable findings: lip edema, fissured tongue, and facial palsy.

Neurology.name: Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy
clinical_manifestations: Acute painless central vision loss in a young adult, often sequential
Fundus in the acute phase: disc hyperemia and peripapillary telangiectatic microangiopathy
radiological_manifestations: Optical coherence tomography: early retinal-nerve-fiber swelling, then atrophy; MRI excludes compressive and demyelinating mimics
pathology_manifestations: Mitochondrial DNA mutation, most often m.11778G>A; there is no useful nerve biopsy
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Mitochondrial optic neuropathy with an acute fundus photograph and OCT, distinct from demyelinating optic neuritis.

Neurology.name: Cockayne Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cachectic dwarfism, sunken eyes, and photosensitivity
Disproportionately small head
radiological_manifestations: CT or MRI: basal-ganglia calcification and white-matter hypomyelination
pathology_manifestations: Transcription-coupled repair defect; a skin biopsy is not routinely diagnostic
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: DNA-repair progeria with a face photograph and basal-ganglia calcification.

Neurology.name: Niemann-Pick Disease Type C
clinical_manifestations: Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy
Gelastic cataplexy and school-age cognitive loss
Neonatal cholestasis in the early-onset form
radiological_manifestations: MRI is often normal early, then shows cerebellar atrophy
pathology_manifestations: Filipin staining of unesterified cholesterol in fibroblasts; NPC1 or NPC2 confirms
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Neurovisceral lipid disease whose gaze palsy and, in infants, cholestasis are the clinical images.

Neurology.name: LGI1-Antibody Encephalitis
clinical_manifestations: Very brief ipsilateral face and arm dystonic spasms, often filmed
Later memory loss
radiological_manifestations: MRI: temporal T2 hyperintensity or a normal scan
Hyponatremia is laboratory, not an image
pathology_manifestations: LGI1 antibodies; brain biopsy is not required
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Autoimmune encephalitis identified by a filmed faciobrachial seizure and antibody testing.

Neurology.name: Canavan Disease
clinical_manifestations: Macrocephaly and hypotonia in early infancy
radiological_manifestations: MRI: diffuse white-matter T2 hyperintensity including the subcortical U fibers, with an elevated NAA peak on spectroscopy
pathology_manifestations: Spongy myelin vacuolization; elevated urine NAA
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Leukodystrophy with macrocephaly photographs and a spectroscopy-confirmed MRI pattern.

Neurology.name: Zellweger Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: High forehead, large fontanelle, and severe hypotonia
Hepatomegaly and neonatal seizures
radiological_manifestations: MRI: germinolytic cysts and neuronal-migration abnormalities
Patellar and acetabular stippling on radiographs
pathology_manifestations: Absent peroxisomes and elevated very-long-chain fatty acids
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Peroxisomal syndrome with a face photograph, stippled epiphyses, and a neuronal-migration MRI.

Neurology.name: Parry-Romberg Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Progressive unilateral atrophy of the skin, subcutaneous adipose tissue, underlying facial musculature, and osteocartilaginous structures of the face, typically starting in the first or second decade of life

Characteristic sharply demarcated linear vertical furrow or scar-like depression on the frontoparietal paramedian scalp and forehead ("en coup de sabre" depression) accompanied by focal cicatricial alopecia
Severe enophthalmos and dystopia from atrophy of the retrobulbar and periorbital adipose tissue, accompanied by eyelid retraction, lagophthalmos, or Horner syndrome
Deviation of the mouth, philtrum, and nose toward the affected atrophic side with hemiatrophy of the tongue, gingiva, and unilateral jaw malocclusion
Neurological sequelae including intractable focal motor or sensory seizures (epilepsia partialis continua), migraine-like hemiplegic headaches, and trigeminal neuralgia
radiological_manifestations: Brain & Orbital MRI: Striking asymmetry of extracranial soft tissues with marked loss of facial and orbital fat; ipsilateral cerebral white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, subcortical leukoencephalopathy, focal ipsilateral cerebral cortical atrophy, ventricular dilatation, and leptomeningeal gadolinium enhancement

Non-Contrast Head & Maxillofacial CT: Marked bony hypoplasia and thinning of the ipsilateral mandible, maxilla, zygoma, and frontal bone with prominent intracranial intraparenchymal or cortical calcifications

Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) / CTA: Intracranial vascular dysplasias, aneurysmal dilatation, focal vessel caliber stenosis, and vascular malformations involving ipsilateral internal carotid or middle cerebral artery branches
pathology_manifestations: Skin and soft tissue biopsy: Severe dermal sclerosis and hyalinization with progressive disappearance of the subcutaneous fat architecture; atrophy of hair follicles and sweat glands; perivascular and perineural chronic lymphocytic infiltrates
Histopathology: Endothelial swelling and perivascular elastosis in the reticular dermis with condensation and homogenization of collagen bundles resembling localized scleroderma/morphea
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic neurocutaneous entity featuring profound unilateral facial and craniofacial atrophy, en coup de sabre deformity, and enophthalmos paired with ipsilateral cerebral white matter lesions and cortical calcifications.

Neurology.name: Kearns-Sayre Syndrome
synonyms: Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia with ragged red fibers
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad presenting before age 20: progressive external ophthalmoplegia (PEO), atypical pigmentary retinopathy, and cardiac conduction block
Bilateral, symmetric, slowly progressive severe ptosis with compensatory contraction of the frontalis muscle and backward head tilt (retroflexion of neck) to visualize objects in the field of view
Progressive ophthalmoparesis culminating in complete bilateral external ophthalmoplegia with fixed globes, sparing pupillary light and near reflexes

Ophthalmoscopic fundus examination demonstrating diffuse "salt-and-pepper" pigmentary retinopathy and chorioretinal atrophy, most prominent at the posterior pole and mid-periphery (unlike bone-spicule deposits in retinitis pigmentosa)
Systemic manifestations: progressive cerebellar ataxia, sensorineural hearing loss, proximal limb myopathy, endocrine abnormalities (diabetes mellitus, hypoparathyroidism), and short stature
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Symmetric T2-weighted and FLAIR hyperintensities within the subcortical cerebral white matter, globus pallidus, caudate nuclei, thalami, brainstem tegmentum, and cerebellar dentate nuclei, with sparing of deep cerebral white matter
Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (1H-MRS): Prominent lactate resonance doublet peak at 1.33 ppm in affected brain parenchyma and CSF, indicative of defective mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
Electrocardiogram / Transthoracic Echocardiogram: High-grade atrioventricular block (bifascicular or complete third-degree AV block) requiring urgent pacemaker placement; progressive cardiomyopathy
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy (Diagnostic Hallmark): Modified Gomori trichrome staining reveals pathognomonic "ragged-red fibers" (RRFs) caused by massive subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormal mitochondria; cytochrome c oxidase (COX) histochemistry displays mosaic pattern of COX-negative muscle fibers
Electron Microscopy: Disorganized myofibrillar architecture with dramatically enlarged mitochondria containing paracrystalline "parking-lot" inclusions and disrupted cristae
Molecular Genetics: Large-scale single heteroplasmic deletions of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), commonly a 4.97-kb "common deletion" spanning multiple tRNA and respiratory chain genes
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic visual mitochondrial disorder combining striking bedside facial photographs (extreme bilateral ptosis and compensatory chin-up posture), salt-and-pepper pigmentary fundus photography, and pathognomonic Gomori trichrome ragged-red fibers.

Neurology.name: Rasmussen Encephalitis
clinical_manifestations: Triphasic clinical progression in children or young adults: prodromal non-specific phase, acute progressive phase, and late residual stable phase characterized by severe neurological deficits

Epilepsia partialis continua (EPC): pathognomonic relentless, continuous, focal rhythmic clonic muscle jerks confined to one side of the body (typically face, hand, or thumb) persisting for days, months, or years without impairment of consciousness
Progressive unilateral motor loss resulting in dense hemiparesis and hemiplegia on the side affected by focal motor seizures
Progressive cognitive decline, homonymous hemianopia, and prominent receptive/expressive aphasia when the dominant cerebral hemisphere is affected
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Pathognomonic Progressive Unilateral Atrophy): Serial imaging demonstrates progressive, irreversible unilateral cortical atrophy with enlargement of the ipsilateral lateral ventricle (especially frontal and temporal horns) and widening of hemispheric sulci/Sylvian fissure; contralateral hemisphere remains completely unaffected

T2-weighted and FLAIR MRI: Hyperintense signal abnormality in the cortex and subcortical white matter of the affected hemisphere during active inflammatory stages, with focal caudate and putaminal atrophy

Fluorodeoxyglucose PET (18F-FDG-PET): Marked unilateral hemispheric hypometabolism during interictal phases, contrasting with hypermetabolic focal seizure foci during active epilepsia partialis continua
pathology_manifestations: Brain Biopsy / Hemispherectomy Neuropathology: Patchy multifocal chronic cortical inflammation driven by cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes forming perivascular cuffs and infiltrating the neuropil in close apposition to apoptotic neurons

Microglial activation: Prominent microglial nodules (babès nodules) throughout cerebral cortex and white matter, accompanied by reactive astrogliosis, neuronal loss, and spongiosis confined entirely to the affected hemisphere
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Exceptional clinical-radiological neurological entity featuring continuous bedside focal motor twitches (epilepsia partialis continua) and dramatic, unmistakable progressive unilateral hemispheric cortical atrophy on serial brain MRI.

Neurology.name: Miller Fisher Syndrome
synonyms: Acute ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and areflexia syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Classic acute post-infectious clinical triad (often preceded 1-3 weeks by Campylobacter jejuni or viral gastroenteritis/URI): acute external ophthalmoplegia, sensory ataxia, and generalized areflexia

Acute bilateral external ophthalmoparesis: dramatic limitation of conjugate eye movements starting in vertical or lateral gaze and rapidly progressing to complete symmetric or asymmetric bilateral external ophthalmoplegia
Bilateral ptosis, pupillary sluggishness or light-near dissociation, and fixed dilated pupils (internal ophthalmoplegia in severe cases)
Profound sensory ataxia with broad-based unsteadiness of gait and prominent dysmetria disproportionate to any motor weakness; preserved limb strength is a core feature
Loss of all deep tendon reflexes (universal generalized areflexia or hyporeflexia) with preserved sensation or minimal distal paresthesias
radiological_manifestations: Brain & Spine MRI with Gadolinium: High-resolution contrast-enhanced T1 sequences frequently show smooth enhancement of cranial nerves (CN III, IV, and VI) and dorsal spinal roots/cauda equina due to autoimmune disruption of the blood-nerve barrier
Orbital MRI: Excludes structural mass lesions, orbital apex syndrome, thyroid eye disease, or cavernous sinus thrombosis

Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS / EMG): Sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude reduction or absence with normal or minimally slowed motor conduction velocities; absent H-reflexes confirming sensory afferent pathway disruption
pathology_manifestations: Serology (Diagnostic Hallmark): Exceptionally high titers (>90-95% sensitivity and specificity) of serum IgG antibodies directed against GQ1b ganglioside, which is highly enriched in the paranodal myelin of human oculomotor, trochlear, abducens cranial nerves and muscle spindle primary afferents
CSF Analysis: Albuminocytologic dissociation (markedly elevated CSF protein with normal white blood cell count, <5 WBC/mcL)
Nerve Pathology: Acute antibody- and complement-mediated attack on the nodes of Ranvier of cranial and peripheral nerves with localized paranodal demyelination and microvascular inflammation
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic acute neuro-ophthalmologic disease entity with distinct visual ocular motility signs (bilateral external ophthalmoplegia and ptosis), gait ataxia, pathognomonic anti-GQ1b ganglioside serology, and cranial nerve enhancement on MRI.

Neurology.name: Wernicke Encephalopathy
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad caused by acute thiamine (vitamin B1) depletion (seen in chronic alcoholism, hyperemesis gravidarum, prolonged fasting, bariatric surgery, or TPN without vitamins): acute encephalopathy, gait ataxia, and prominent ocular motor signs

Ocular motor abnormalities: pathognomonic bilateral abducens (CN VI) nerve palsies causing horizontal diplopia; prominent horizontal, vertical, and rotary nystagmus (especially gaze-evoked horizontal nystagmus); bilateral conjugate gaze palsies progressing to complete external ophthalmoplegia in advanced stages
Truncal and gait ataxia: broad-based, unsteady, cerebellar gait with prominent postural instability and inability to perform tandem gait, often necessitating wheelchair assistance

Acute confusional state: profound apathy, spatial disorientation, drowsiness, inattention, progressing without thiamine repletion to stupor, coma, or permanent anterograde Korsakoff amnesic confabulatory psychosis
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Pathognomonic Pattern): Highly characteristic symmetric hyperintensity on T2-weighted, FLAIR, and DWI sequences localized to the mammillary bodies, periaqueductal gray matter of the midbrain, medial thalami, tectal plate, and third ventricle margins
Post-Contrast T1 MRI: Intense avid enhancement of the mammillary bodies (virtually pathognomonic sign of active thiamine deficiency)
Gradient Recalled Echo (GRE) / Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI): Petechial microhemorrhages and hemosiderin staining within the mammillary bodies and paraventricular thalamic regions
pathology_manifestations: Gross Brain Pathology: Petechial hemorrhages, discoloration, and softening specifically confined to the mammillary bodies, periaqueductal gray, and floor of the fourth ventricle; chronic atrophy of the mammillary bodies

Histopathology: Endothelial swelling and capillary proliferation with microvascular remodeling; localized petechial extravasation of erythrocytes, microglial proliferation, and spongiform neuropil vacuolation with relative preservation of neuronal perikarya (non-infarctive cytotoxic edema)
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Critical neurological emergency featuring overt physical ocular motor signs (bilateral lateral rectus palsies and multidirectional nystagmus) combined with pathognomonic symmetrical mammillary body and periaqueductal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and enhancement on MRI.

Neurology.name: Stiff-Person Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Insidious progressive fluctuating symmetric rigidity and stiffness of axial, paraspinal, abdominal, and proximal limb muscles, causing a rigid, robotic, "tin soldier" or "statue-like" gait

Pathognomonic fixed hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine caused by persistent simultaneous contraction of the thoracolumbar paraspinal and abdominal rectus muscles, persisting even when the patient lies recumbent or attempts relaxation

Violent, excruciating, episodic reflex muscle spasms triggered by unexpected acoustic stimuli (doorbell, loud noise), light emotional stress, cold temperature, or sudden touch, causing catastrophic stiff falls ("like a felled log") without protective outstretched arms
Severe task-specific phobias (agoraphobia, task-freeze when crossing open unassisted spaces), muscle hypertrophy, and board-like palpably rock-hard abdominal and paraspinal musculature
radiological_manifestations: Spine Radiography & CT: Exaggerated lumbar hyperlordosis with rigid paraspinal alignment without intrinsic destructive vertebral lesions or primary ankylosing spinal disease
Brain & Spinal Cord MRI: Usually normal or non-specific; essential for excluding compressive cervical or thoracic myelopathy, structural tumors, and demyelinating lesions

Electromyography (EMG - Diagnostic Hallmark): Pathognomonic continuous motor unit action potential (CMUAP) activity firing at rest in agonist and antagonist muscles simultaneously, which completely abolishes following intravenous diazepam administration
pathology_manifestations: Serology and CSF Biomarkers: Extremely high titers of autoantibodies targeting glutamic acid decarboxylase (anti-GAD65) in serum and CSF (>10,000 IU/mL; >80% of patients), or anti-amphiphysin antibodies in paraneoplastic cases associated with breast or small-cell lung cancer

Pathophysiology: Autoimmune loss of GABAergic inhibition in the spinal cord and motor cortex leading to unchecked tonic motor neuron firing and lack of reciprocal inhibition between opposing muscle groups
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Visually striking neurological condition featuring unforgettable bedside physical exam postures (rigid robot-like gait, rock-hard abdomen, persistent hyperlordosis) and pathognomonic continuous motor unit activity on EMG confirmed by anti-GAD65 autoantibodies.

Neurology.name: Möbius Syndrome
synonyms: Congenital facial diplegia and abducens nerve palsy
clinical_manifestations: Congenital non-progressive bilateral facial (CN VII) and abducens (CN VI) nerve palsies resulting in a completely mask-like, unexpressive, impassive facies ("frozen face") with complete inability to smile, frown, puff the cheeks, or whistle

Bilateral lagophthalmos: incomplete eyelid closure during blinking and sleep, leading to exposure keratitis and nocturnal corneal dryness; upward deviation of the eyes during attempts to close lids (intact Bell phenomenon)

Complete or near-complete inability to abduct either eye past midline with preservation of vertical gaze (supranuclear and third-nerve vertical pathways spared); cross-eyed appearance (convergent strabismus / esotropia)
Feeding difficulties and drooling in neonates due to weak orbicularis oris and hypoglossal (CN XII) nerve involvement, causing a furrowed, atrophic, or microglossic tongue

Associated musculoskeletal anomalies in 50-60%: clubfoot (talipes equinovarus), syndactyly, brachydactyly, or Poland syndrome (unilateral absence of the pectoralis major muscle and ipsilateral symbrachydactyly)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Brainstem MRI (3D CISS / FIESTA): Complete absence or profound hypoplasia of the facial (CN VII) and abducens (CN VI) cranial nerve rootlets as they exit the pons; hypoplasia of the facial colliculus and dorsal brainstem tegmentum
Brainstem CT: Focal punctate calcifications within the dorsal pontine tegmentum at the floor of the fourth ventricle corresponding to the abducens nuclei
Orbital MRI: Marked muscular atrophy or hypoplasia of the lateral rectus muscles bilaterally with normal superior, inferior, and medial recti
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology: Agenesis, hypoplasia, or degeneration of the motor nuclei of the sixth and seventh cranial nerves within the pontine tegmentum; absence of motor rootlet axons in the peripheral facial and abducens nerve trunks

Etiology: Disruption of early embryonic vascular supply to the subclavian artery branches and basilar vertebral arterial arcade (subclavian artery supply disruption sequence) during weeks 4-7 of gestation
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Congenital neuro-ophthalmologic entity defined by an instantly recognizable facial photographic phenotype (expressionless mask-like face, bilateral lagophthalmos, abducens palsy) coupled with brainstem cranial nerve agenesis on high-resolution MRI.

Neurology.name: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Severe, excruciating, deep, boring, lancinating retro-orbital and periorbital unilateral head pain centered around the brow and temple

Ipsilateral painful ophthalmoplegia developing within days of pain onset: paresis or paralysis of the oculomotor (CN III), trochlear (CN IV), and/or abducens (CN VI) nerves, manifesting with diplopia and limitation of ocular excursion in multiple directions
Ptosis and pupillary abnormalities (dilated non-reactive pupil due to parasympathetic CN III involvement or Horner syndrome due to sympathetic plexus involvement around the internal carotid artery)
Sensory loss and hyperesthesia over the ipsilateral forehead, brow, and cornea (involvement of the ophthalmic V1 division, and occasionally maxillary V2 division, of the trigeminal nerve)
Dramatic, rapid relief of severe pain within 24-72 hours following systemic high-dose corticosteroid administration (diagnostic criterion)
radiological_manifestations: Brain & Orbital MRI with Contrast (Diagnostic Modality of Choice): Pathognomonic focal soft-tissue thickening, enlargement, and avid homogeneous gadolinium enhancement filling the ipsilateral cavernous sinus, superior orbital fissure, and/or orbital apex, with isointense to hypointense signal on T1/T2-weighted images
Contrast MRA / CTA: Smooth focal narrowing or concentric caliber reduction of the cavernous and supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery as it traverses the inflamed cavernous sinus
Serial Post-Treatment MRI: Complete or near-complete resolution and normalization of the cavernous sinus mass and contrast enhancement following a taper of systemic corticosteroid therapy
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Biopsy of Cavernous Sinus / Orbital Apex: Non-specific, non-caseating granulomatous inflammatory tissue characterized by a dense proliferation of fibroblasts and collagen bundles densely infiltrated with lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and multinucleated giant cells; absence of fungal elements, acid-fast bacilli, or malignant neoplastic cells
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct neuro-ophthalmological emergency presenting with painful unilateral ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, and proptosis, diagnosed by pathognomonic cavernous sinus granulomatous soft tissue filling on contrast MRI and rapid steroid responsiveness.

Neurology.name: Neurocutaneous Melanosis with Giant Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
clinical_manifestations: Large 'bathing-trunk' or garment distribution congenital melanocytic nevus covering lumbosacral back/scalp
Numerous satellite melanocytic nevi of varying size
Hydrocephalus, seizures, or melanoma arising within the nevus or CNS
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: T1-hyperintense leptomeningeal and amygdala/cerebellar parenchymal melanosis (stable, nonenhancing foci) in symptomatic children with large GCMN
pathology_manifestations: Congenital nevomelanocytes throughout leptomeninges and brain parenchyma; NRAS mutation shared between nevus and CNS deposits
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Dual signature: giant garment nevus photograph plus pathognomonic T1-hyperintense leptomeningeal melanosis.

Neurology.name: Aicardi Syndrome
synonyms: agenesis of corpus callosum with chorioretinal lacunae
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic fundus: round, depigmented chorioretinal lacunae clustered around the optic disc
Infantile spasms in females (X-linked dominant, male-lethal)
Microphthalmia, optic-nerve coloboma, and severe developmental delay
radiological_manifestations: MRI: complete or partial corpus-callosum agenesis with polymicrogyria, periventricular nodular heterotopia, and posterior fossa/choroid-plexus cysts - the classic triad partner to the lacunae
pathology_manifestations: Chorioretinal lacunae histologically are well-circumscribed RPE/choroidal defects; X-linked dominant inheritance
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Pathognomonic chorioretinal lacunae plus callosal-agenesis/polymicrogyria triad.

Neurology.name: Menkes Disease (Kinky Hair Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Sparse, steel-gray, depigmented hair that is kinky and easily broken
Pili torti (flat twisted hair shafts) as the pathognomonic microscopic finding
Hypotonia, seizures, failure to thrive, sagging facies, and high-arched palate in the infantile course
radiological_manifestations: MR angiography/DSA: tortuous 'corkscrew' intracranial and systemic vessels; skeletal: wormian bones, metaphyseal flaring, and occipital exostoses (occipital horn)
pathology_manifestations: ATP7A copper-transporter defect: low serum copper/ceruloplasmin; microscopic pili torti/trichorrhexis nodosa/trichoptilosis
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Pathognomonic pili torti hair shafts plus corkscrew vessels - a dual signature in one disease.

Neurology.name: Tay-Sachs Disease
clinical_manifestations: Cherry-red macular spot on fundoscopy - the most reproduced fundus in metabolic disease
Exaggerated startle response (hyperacusis) in the first months
Progressive hypotonia, blindness, seizures, and macrocephaly in infancy
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI: characteristic bilateral thalamic hyperdensity on CT with later caudate/thalamic changes and diffuse white-matter disease on MRI
pathology_manifestations: Hexosaminidase A deficiency; GM2 ganglioside accumulates as membranous cytoplasmic bodies (whorled lysosomes) in neurons
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Cherry-red spot plus thalamic hyperdensity - the classic metabolic-neurodegenerative imaging pair.

Neurology.name: Leigh Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Infantile or early-childhood psychomotor regression with hypotonia, nystagmus, and dystonia
Feeding and respiratory rhythm abnormalities during crises
Optic atrophy and pigmentary retinopathy in subsets
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: bilateral symmetric T2 hyperintensity of the basal ganglia (especially putamen), periaqueductal gray, and brainstem - the archetypal mitochondrial MRI signature
pathology_manifestations: Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defects (SURF1, mtDNA mutations); spongiform necrotizing lesions of deep gray matter
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Admitted under the named-imaging-signature precedent (like covered X-ALD/Canavan): symmetric basal-ganglia lesions are definitional.

Neurology.name: Glutaric Aciduria Type I
clinical_manifestations: Progressive macrocephaly in a previously well infant
Acute striatal necrosis after intercurrent illness producing sudden irreversible dystonia
Bilateral subdural fluid collections and retinal hemorrhages frequently mistaken for nonaccidental trauma
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: pathognomonic bilateral widened Sylvian fissures ('bat-wing' appearance) with frontotemporal atrophy and post-crisis putaminal necrosis
pathology_manifestations: Glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency; accumulation of glutaric/3-hydroxyglutaric acids
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Bat-wing widened Sylvian fissures are a named pathognomonic sign; classic case mistaken for abuse.

Neurology.name: Cerebrotendinous Xanthomatosis
clinical_manifestations: Large bilateral Achilles-tendon xanthomas - dramatic photographs
Juvenile cataracts preceding neurologic disease
Progressive ataxia, pyramidal signs, and neuropsychiatric disease
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: bilateral dentate-nuclei and deep-cerebellar T2 hyperintensity; tendon MRI confirms xanthomatous infiltration
pathology_manifestations: CYP27A1 sterol-27-hydroxylase deficiency; cholestanol deposits forming tendon and CNS xanthomas
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Double signature: Achilles xanthoma photos plus dentate-nuclei MRI lesions.

Neurology.name: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Self-mutilation: chewed lips, fingers, and tongue producing unmistakable photographs
Dystonia with choreoathetosis and severe developmental delay
Hyperuricemia with orange crystalluria and gouty arthropathy
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; brain MRI largely normal distinguishing the self-mutilation from structural disease
pathology_manifestations: HPRT1 deficiency of purine salvage; uric-acid overproduction; striatal dopamine deficiency on imaging-pathway studies
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The self-mutilation photographs are the most reproduced behavioral phenotype in medicine.

Neurology.name: Aicardi-Goutières Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Early-onset encephalopathy with acral 'chilblain' violaceous skin lesions on digits and ears
Microcephaly, dystonia, and feeding difficulties
Sterile cerebrospinal pleocytosis with elevated interferon-alpha
radiological_manifestations: Brain CT/MRI: pathognomonic basal-ganglia and periventricular calcification with white-matter disease and cerebral atrophy - the 'pseudo-TORCH' imaging signature
pathology_manifestations: Type-I interferonopathy (TREX1, RNASEH2A/B/C, SAMHD1, ADAR, and others) mimicking congenital infection
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Chilblain skin lesions plus TORCH-like basal-ganglia calcification - a dual signature.

Neurology.name: Metachromatic Leukodystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Gait regression in toddlers (late-infantile form) evolving to spastic quadriplegia
Peripheral neuropathy masking upper-motor signs
Psychiatric and cognitive decline in juvenile/adult forms
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: diffuse periventricular leukodystrophy with 'tigroid' sparing of perivascular myelin and early U-fiber sparing - the characteristic pattern
pathology_manifestations: ARSA deficiency; sulfatide deposits stain metachromatically (brown) on cresyl violet in nerve biopsies; globoid cells absent (vs. Krabbe)
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Tigroid periventricular pattern is a named imaging signature in the leukodystrophy set.

Neurology.name: Alexander Disease
clinical_manifestations: Progressive macrocephaly in infants (infantile form) with psychomotor regression
Bulbar and pyramidal signs later in the course
Adult form: palatal tremor and ataxia with frontal predominance
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: frontal-predominant leukodystrophy with contrast enhancement, periventricular rim, and basal-ganglia/brainstem signal - the diagnostic I-IV MRI criteria
pathology_manifestations: GFAP mutation; Rosenthal fibers - eosinophilic protein aggregates - in astrocyte foot processes
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Frontal leukodystrophy with enhancement is a formal MRI-criteria diagnosis.

Neurology.name: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher Disease
clinical_manifestations: Infantile nystagmus ('dancing eyes') and hypotonia progressing to spasticity and choreoathetosis
Absent or minimal myelin formation; males affected via PLP1
Titubation and ataxia
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: near-total absence of normal myelination producing a reversed (dark-T1, bright-T2) 'tigroid' or diffuse hypomyelinating pattern persisting into childhood
pathology_manifestations: PLP1 duplication/mutation; oligodendrocyte maturation arrest; 'islands' of preserved myelin give the tigroid pattern
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Infant nystagmus plus the classic hypomyelination MRI pattern.

Neurology.name: Vanishing White Matter Disease
clinical_manifestations: Chronic progressive ataxia and spasticity with stress/fever-triggered acute deterioration
Ovarian failure (ovarioleukodystrophy) in adolescent girls
Coma after minor head trauma or infection
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI FLAIR: white matter that rarefies and becomes CSF-isointense (cavitation) with preserved cortex and characteristic sparing of U-fibers, corpus callosum, and anterior commissure - pathognomonic
pathology_manifestations: EIF2B1-5 mutations (eIF2B translation initiation); cystic cavitating white-matter degeneration
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The CSF-isointense vanishing-white-matter pattern is uniquely diagnostic.

Neurology.name: MELAS Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Stroke-like episodes in childhood/young adults with hemianopia, aphasia, or hemiparesis
Short stature, sensorineural hearing loss, and diabetes
Lactic acidosis during episodes
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: posterior-predominant stroke-like cortical lesions crossing vascular territories that migrate over serial scans; MR spectroscopy: lactate peak
pathology_manifestations: mtDNA m.3243A>G tRNA-Leu mutation; ragged-red fibers on modified Gomori trichrome; SDH 'strongly SDH-reactive' vessels
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Posterior, territory-crossing stroke-like lesions are a textbook imaging signature.

Neurology.name: Maple Syrup Urine Disease
clinical_manifestations: Maple-syrup odor of urine, cerumen, and skin in the first week
Neonatal encephalopathy: lethargy, alternating hyper/hypotonia, opisthotonos, and feeding failure
Burnt-sugar odor on ear examination
radiological_manifestations: Neonatal brain MRI/DWI: characteristic symmetric edema (restricted diffusion) of cerebellar white matter, brainstem, globi pallidi, and internal capsules - 'MSUD edema'
pathology_manifestations: Branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase deficiency; leucine/isoleucine/valine accumulation
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Maple-syrup cerumen odor plus the named neonatal DWI edema distribution.

Neurology.name: Krabbe Disease
clinical_manifestations: Extreme irritability and hypertonia in infants with fisting and arching
Blindness, deafness, and rapid deterioration to decerebrate state
Peripheral neuropathy with absent reflexes
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: parieto-occipital leukodystrophy; CT/MRI: enlarged optic nerves and chiasm - a relatively specific early sign; deep-gray and cerebellar-dentate hyperdensity on CT
pathology_manifestations: GALC deficiency; globoid multinucleated macrophages stuffed with galactocerebroside in white matter
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Enlarged optic nerves plus posterior leukodystrophy; weakest of the imaging-signature set but defensible.

Neurology.name: Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis (CLN3, Batten Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Progressive visual loss with bull's-eye maculopathy on fundoscopy
Seizures, myoclonus, and cognitive regression in school-age children
Parkinsonism in the later course
radiological_manifestations: Fundus photograph: bull's-eye maculopathy and attenuated retinal vessels; brain MRI: cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
pathology_manifestations: CLN3 mutation; lipofuscin 'fingerprint' profiles on electron microscopy; vacuolated lymphocytes
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Bull's-eye maculopathy plus retinal degeneration gives a fundus-recognizable lysosomal disease.

Neurology.name: Sialidosis Type I
clinical_manifestations: Cherry-red macular spot on fundoscopy
Progressive intention/action myoclonus - the famous combination
Preserved intellect and normal somatic features
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging beyond the fundus photograph
pathology_manifestations: Alpha-neuraminidase (NEU1) deficiency; lysosomal sialyl-oligosaccharide storage
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Cherry-red spot plus action myoclonus is one of neurology's most famous sign combinations.

Neurology.name: Giant Axonal Neuropathy
clinical_manifestations: Tightly curled, kinky hair - the signature photograph
Progressive sensorimotor neuropathy with gait failure
Central white-matter involvement in advanced disease
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: cerebellar and cerebral white-matter disease; nerve conduction studies show severe axonal neuropathy
pathology_manifestations: GAN (gigaxonin) mutation; giant axonal swellings packed with intermediate filaments on nerve biopsy
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Kinky-hair photo plus axonal-spheroid nerve biopsy is a distinct phenotype.

Neurology.name: Refsum Disease
clinical_manifestations: Retinitis pigmentosa night blindness with constricted fields
Ichthyosis scaling on the trunk and limbs
Chronic polyneuropathy with ataxia; anosmia and sensorineural hearing loss
radiological_manifestations: Fundus photograph: bone-spicule retinitis pigmentosa; brain MRI may show cerebellar atrophy
pathology_manifestations: PHYH deficiency impairing phytanic-acid alpha-oxidation; massively elevated plasma phytanic acid
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The RP-plus-ichthyosis-plus-neuropathy triad is a named classic tetrad disease.

Neurology.name: Emery-Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Early elbow-flexion contractures forming a fixed bent-arm posture
Achilles-tendon contractures with toe-walking
Humeroperoneal wasting (biceps/triceps then peroneal) and rigid spine
radiological_manifestations: Muscle MRI: selective involvement of soleus/medial gastrocnemius; cervical-films for rigid-spine contractures; cardiac Holter for conduction disease
pathology_manifestations: EMD (emerin) or LMNA mutation; X-linked and dominant forms; absent emerin nuclear staining on biopsy
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The early contracture-habitus photographs complete the covered dystrophy set (Duchenne, FSHD, OPMD).

Neurology.name: Tethered Cord Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous stigmata over the lower spine: faun-tail hair tuft, dermal sinus, or subcutaneous lipoma
Progressive leg weakness, gait abnormality, and bladder dysfunction
Orthopedic foot deformities and scoliosis
radiological_manifestations: Spinal MRI: low-lying conus with a thickened fatty filum terminale - the diagnostic signature; lipomyelomeningocele forms
pathology_manifestations: Occult spinal dysraphism; the caudal cutaneous markers signal underlying tethering
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Sacral hair-tuft/dermal-sinus photographs plus pathognomonic low-conus MRI.

Neurology.name: Bell Palsy (Idiopathic Facial Paralysis)
clinical_manifestations: Acute unilateral facial droop with inability to close the eye or smile
Flattened nasolabial fold and drooping mouth corner on the affected side
Bell phenomenon: visible globe rotation upward on attempted eye closure
radiological_manifestations: MRI shows enhancement of the facial nerve within the facial canal in some cases; diagnosis is clinical photograph
pathology_manifestations: Idiopathic facial-nerve inflammation (probable viral reactivation); lower motor neuron facial paralysis
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Unilateral facial-droop photograph is one of the most reproduced clinical signs.

Neurology.name: Hirayama Disease (Juvenile Monomelic Amyotrophy)
synonyms: juvenile muscular atrophy of unilateral upper extremity
clinical_manifestations: Insidious unilateral (or asymmetric) wasting of distal forearm and hand in young males
'Cold paresis' weakness worsened by cold; oblique forearm atrophy sparing brachioradialis
Arrest after 3-5 years of progression
radiological_manifestations: Flexion cervical MRI: anterior displacement of the posterior dural sac compressing the cord against the vertebra - the named diagnostic sign; asymmetric cord flattening
pathology_manifestations: Dynamic cervical-flexion anterior horn ischemia; no sensory involvement
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Dramatic unilateral distal wasting photo plus flexion-MRI dural shift is a dual signature.

Neurology.name: Schwartz-Jampel Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Mask-like 'staring' facies with blepharophimosis, puckered mouth, and fixed sad expression
Visible continuous muscle stiffness/myotonia
Short stature with joint contractures
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: epiphyseal dysplasia, platyspondyly, and hip dysplasia
pathology_manifestations: HSPG2 (perlecan) mutation; abnormal muscle-fiber excitability and cartilage matrix defect
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Staring mask-facies photo plus visible myotonia; proposed by two audits.

Neurology.name: Congenital Insensitivity to Pain with Anhidrosis (CIPA/HSAN IV)
clinical_manifestations: Self-mutilation: chewed tongue, lips, and fingertips producing ulcers and tissue loss
Painless fractures, joint destruction (Charcot joints), and oral ulcers
Anhidrosis causing recurrent unexplained fevers
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal radiographs: repeated painless fractures and neuropathic joint destruction in children
pathology_manifestations: NTRK1 mutation; absent small unmyelinated fibers and absent sweating
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Self-mutilation photos plus Charcot-joint films - Lesch-Nyhan precedent.

Neurology.name: Neuroferritinopathy
clinical_manifestations: Adult-onset chorea and dystonia with orofacial dyskinesia
Cognitive decline in later stages
Progressive gait dysfunction
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: pathognomonic basal-ganglia cavitation with iron deposition - hypointense lesions with T2 hyperintense rims on T2*/SWI
pathology_manifestations: FTL mutation; ferritin aggregates in neurons forming inclusion bodies
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Basal-ganglia cavitation plus iron deposition is near-pathognomonic.

Neurology.name: Aceruloplasminemia
clinical_manifestations: Retinal degeneration with peripheral vision loss
Anemia with diabetes and neurologic disease (ataxia, dystonia, cognitive decline)
Subtle systemic iron-overload findings
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: iron deposition in basal ganglia and dentate nucleus; abdominal MRI: hepatic and pancreatic iron loading - the multi-organ signature
pathology_manifestations: CP mutation abolishing ferroxidase activity; undetectable serum ceruloplasmin with high ferritin
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Multi-organ iron signature including retinal degeneration.

Neurology.name: FXTAS (Fragile X Tremor/Ataxia Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Intention tremor and cerebellar ataxia in older males
Executive decline, parkinsonism, and peripheral neuropathy
Family history of fragile X
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: symmetric middle cerebellar peduncle T2 hyperintensity - the 'MCP sign', plus generalized atrophy and white-matter disease
pathology_manifestations: FMR1 premutation (55-200 CGG repeats) producing toxic RNA; intranuclear inclusions
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Named MRI sign admitted under the imaging-signature precedent; maintainer to decide vs. prior fragile-X rejection.

Neurology.name: Neuroacanthocytosis (Chorea-Acanthocytosis)
clinical_manifestations: Self-mutilating lip and tongue biting with oral ulcers
Huntington-like chorea and dystonia
Feeding dystonia causing tongue expulsion of food
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: caudate-head atrophy; peripheral smear: acanthocytes (spiky erythrocytes)
pathology_manifestations: VPS13A mutation; acanthocytes on smear plus chorein reduction on Western blot
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Lip-biting self-mutilation plus acanthocytes plus caudate atrophy - Lesch-Nyhan class.

Neurology.name: Brain Arteriovenous Malformation
clinical_manifestations: Dilated, tortuous scalp veins with arterialized pulsation in infants with large high-flow lesions
radiological_manifestations: CT angiography: Tangle of enlarged feeding arteries and draining veins around a central nidus
MRI with SWI or T2: Serpiginous flow voids and hemosiderin rim from prior hemorrhage
Digital subtraction angiography: Arterial feeders converging on a nidus with early venous drainage, used for Spetzler-Martin grading
Non-contrast CT: Intraparenchymal or subarachnoid hemorrhage from the malformation, with possible calcification within the nidus
pathology_manifestations: Resected specimen (H&E): Dilated thin-walled veins and thick-walled arteries interspersed with gliotic brain tissue
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Diagnosis rests on angiographic and cross-sectional images rather than surface features, and these images are widely published.

Neurology.name: Vein of Galen Aneurysmal Malformation
clinical_manifestations: Dilated, prominent scalp veins with visible pulsation in neonates
Macrocephaly with rapid head circumference growth
Tense, bulging anterior fontanelle
radiological_manifestations: Cranial ultrasound (transfontanellar Doppler): Midline cystic mass with high-velocity arterialized flow in the vein of Galen
CT angiography or MRI: Dilated vein of Galen aneurysmal sac posterior to the third ventricle
MRI T2: Hydrocephalus or periventricular white matter changes from venous congestion
Digital subtraction angiography: Multiple choroidal and thalamoperforator feeding arteries draining into the aneurysmal sac
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Diagnosis relies on cranial ultrasound, CT and angiographic images, while the scalp and fontanelle changes are visible in neonates.

Neurology.name: Chiari Malformation and Syringomyelia
clinical_manifestations: Scoliosis, often cervicothoracic, visible on standing back photograph or spinal radiograph
Pes cavus or neuropathic foot deformity in long-standing syringomyelia
Wasting of the intrinsic hand muscles with clawing of the fingers in cervical syrinx
radiological_manifestations: MRI brain and craniocervical junction (sagittal T1/T2): Cerebellar tonsils descending 5 mm or more below the foramen magnum
MRI spine (sagittal T2): Intramedullary fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) in the cervical or thoracic cord, often with cord expansion
Phase-contrast cine MRI: Reduced or absent CSF flow across the foramen magnum in symptomatic patients
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Tonsillar descent and syrinx are defined on sagittal craniocervical and spinal MRI, with visible scoliosis and hand wasting as supporting bedside images.

Neurology.name: Spinal Dural Arteriovenous Fistula
clinical_manifestations: Progressive spastic paraparesis with brisk reflexes and extensor plantar responses on examination
Lower-limb sensory level on bedside examination
radiological_manifestations: MRI spine with gadolinium (T2 and post-contrast T1): Enlarged, serpentine perimedullary flow voids and dorsal subarachnoid vessels
MRI spine (T2): Longitudinally extensive intramedullary T2 hyperintensity with cord swelling, most often thoracolumbar
Digital subtraction spinal angiography: Single arterialized draining vein from a dural fistula at the nerve root sleeve, with retrograde flow into the perimedullary veins
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The lesion is recognized mainly on spinal MRI and angiography, showing dilated perimedullary vessels and cord edema.

Neurology.name: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent lobar intracerebral hemorrhage, most often in patients over 60, seen on serial head CT
Cognitive decline in the setting of multiple lobar hemorrhages on serial imaging
radiological_manifestations: MRI brain SWI or GRE: Multiple lobar cortical and corticosubcortical microbleeds, predominantly occipital and parietal
MRI brain FLAIR: Cortical superficial siderosis as linear hypointensity along the cortical sulci
MRI brain FLAIR/T2: Asymmetric vasogenic edema with lobar hemorrhage in CAA-related inflammation
Amyloid PET (PiB or florbetapir): Diffuse cortical tracer retention in a lobar pattern
pathology_manifestations: Brain biopsy or autopsy, Congo red stain: Amyloid-beta deposition in cortical and leptomeningeal arteriole walls with apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Lobar microbleeds, cortical siderosis and superficial hemorrhage are characteristic MRI patterns that are readily recognized on susceptibility-weighted and FLAIR imaging.

Neurology.name: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis
clinical_manifestations: Papilledema on fundoscopy from raised intracranial pressure, with engorged retinal veins
Peripapillary or retinal hemorrhages on fundus examination in severe cases
Periorbital edema, chemosis and proptosis when the cavernous sinus is involved
radiological_manifestations: Non-contrast CT: Hyperdense cord sign in the thrombosed sinus or cortical vein
CT venography or MR venography: Filling defect or absent flow in the superior sagittal, transverse or sigmoid sinus
Contrast-enhanced CT: Empty delta sign in the superior sagittal sinus
MRI with SWI: Cortical venous infarct with hemorrhagic transformation over the convexity
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The thrombosed sinus is identified on CT and MR venography, with the hyperdense cord and empty delta signs as classic imaging signatures.

Neurology.name: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES)
clinical_manifestations: Hypertensive retinopathy with cotton-wool spots and flame hemorrhages on fundoscopy in severe hypertension
Optic disc swelling in some patients with severe hypertension
radiological_manifestations: MRI brain FLAIR/T2: Symmetric bilateral parieto-occipital subcortical vasogenic edema, often extending into frontal regions
MRI brain DWI/ADC: Usually no restricted diffusion, with restriction only in a minority of patients
CT head: Bilateral symmetric hypodense white matter lesions in the parieto-occipital regions
MRI brain SWI: Scattered microhemorrhages or petechial hemorrhage in some patients
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The symmetric parieto-occipital vasogenic edema pattern on FLAIR MRI is the defining image, with fundal hypertensive changes as a supporting image.

Neurology.name: Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syndrome (RCVS)
synonyms: benign angiopathy of the central nervous system
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent thunderclap headache episodes that resolve over weeks
Exposure to vasoactive drugs such as SSRIs, cannabis or triptans, or the postpartum state, documented in the history
radiological_manifestations: MR angiography or CT angiography: Multifocal segmental constriction of cerebral arteries giving a string-of-beads appearance
Digital subtraction angiography: Multifocal vasoconstriction that resolves on repeat angiography within about 12 weeks
Transcranial Doppler: Elevated middle cerebral artery flow velocities
CT head: Subarachnoid hemorrhage or small cortical infarct in a subset of patients
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Multifocal segmental arterial narrowing with a string-of-beads pattern on angiography, which resolves on follow-up, is the defining image.

Neurology.name: Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension
clinical_manifestations: Orthostatic headache that worsens upright and eases on lying flat, elicited on history
Low CSF opening pressure on lumbar puncture, typically below 6 cm H2O
radiological_manifestations: MRI brain with gadolinium: Diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement from dural thickening
MRI brain: Brain sagging with a reduced pontomesencephalic angle and descended cerebellar tonsils
MRI brain: Bilateral subdural fluid collections, sometimes with engorged venous sinuses
Heavily T2-weighted spinal MRI: Epidural CSF collection at the level of the dural tear
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement and brain sagging on MRI are the characteristic images, and the spinal dural leak is shown on heavily T2-weighted MRI.

Neurology.name: Colloid Cyst of the Third Ventricle
clinical_manifestations: Papilledema on fundoscopy from obstructive hydrocephalus and raised intracranial pressure
Gait instability with sudden positional change on bedside examination
radiological_manifestations: CT head: Round, well-circumscribed hyperdense lesion in the anterior third ventricle near the foramen of Monro
MRI brain T1: Hyperintense signal within the cyst in most cases, with variable T2 signal
MRI brain or CT: Dilated lateral and third ventricles from obstructive hydrocephalus
pathology_manifestations: Cyst wall, H&E: Single layer of cuboidal or columnar epithelium surrounding gelatinous, eosinophilic colloid content
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The cyst is a well-defined anterior third ventricular mass on CT and MRI, with obstructive hydrocephalus as the characteristic image.

Neurology.name: Split Cord Malformation (Diastematomyelia)
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous stigmata over the lumbosacral midline such as hemangioma, hypertrichosis, dimple or skin tag
Pes cavus or clubfoot from neurological involvement, visible on examination
radiological_manifestations: Plain radiography (AP and lateral lumbar spine): Bifid spinal canal or sagittal bony spur splitting the lamina or vertebral body
CT lumbar spine: Bony or fibrocartilaginous septum dividing the canal into two hemicords
MRI spine (sagittal T2): Two separate hemicords with a midline septum, often with tethered cord
Ultrasound in infants: Two hemicords separated by a midline echogenic septum
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The split is shown on spinal radiographs, CT and MRI, and the overlying lumbosacral skin stigmata are visible on photographs.

Neurology.name: Cervical Artery Dissection
clinical_manifestations: Ipsilateral Horner syndrome with miosis, partial ptosis and facial anhidrosis on examination
Ipsilateral lower cranial nerve palsy with hoarseness or tongue deviation on examination
radiological_manifestations: CT angiography of the neck: Tapered, string-sign luminal narrowing of the cervical internal carotid or vertebral artery
MRI neck with fat-saturated T1: Crescent-shaped T1-hyperintense intramural hematoma around the vessel lumen
Digital subtraction angiography: Intimal flap with a double lumen or pseudoaneurysm in the dissected segment
MRI brain DWI: Acute ischemic infarct in the territory of the dissected artery
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: The string sign and crescent-shaped intramural hematoma on neck CTA and fat-saturated MRI are the characteristic images.

Neurology.name: Acute Ischemic Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack
clinical_manifestations: hyperdense MCA, DWI restriction, CTA occlusion.
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Neurology.name: Intracerebral hemorrhage
clinical_manifestations: hyperdense parenchymal hematoma, edema, mass effect.
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Added from Topics.docx (2026-10-21).

Neurology.name: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage and saccular aneurysm

Ophthalmology.name: Age-Related Macular Degeneration
clinical_manifestations: Progressive distortion of central vision (metamorphopsia, best detected on Amsler grid), central scotoma, and loss of reading vision in elderly patients

Dry (Non-neovascular) AMD: Funduscopy reveals soft, confluent, yellowish-white drusen at the macula, pigmentary changes, progressing to sharply demarcated, scalloped patches of geographic atrophy of the RPE exposing underlying large choroidal vessels

Wet (Neovascular) AMD: Sudden, rapid deterioration of central vision; funduscopic exam reveals a grayish-green elevated choroidal neovascular membrane (CNVM), subretinal or intraretinal hemorrhage, lipid/hard exudates, and exudative retinal elevation progressing to a dense, elevated fibrotic disciform scar
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain OCT (SD-OCT): Subretinal fluid (SRF) and intraretinal cystoid fluid (IRF); pigment epithelial detachment (PED: serous, drusenoid, or fibrovascular); hyperreflective material in subretinal or sub-RPE spaces corresponding to CNVM; in geographic atrophy: complete loss of RPE and outer retinal layers with pathognomonic hypertransmission ('choroidal light show') into deep choroid

OCT Angiography (OCTA): High-resolution depth-resolved flow visualization of the abnormal choroidal vascular network in the choriocapillaris or outer retina (Type 1 sub-RPE 'sea-fan' or Type 2 subretinal 'glomerular/medusa' CNVM)

Fluorescein Angiography (FA) and Indocyanine Green Angiography (ICGA): Classic lacy early hyperfluorescence with progressive, intense late fluorescein leakage; occult CNVM with ill-defined stippled leakage; ICGA highlights polypoidal lesions and feeder vessels
pathology_manifestations: Macular Histopathology: Thickening and calcification of Bruch membrane with basal laminar and basal linear deposits; drusen composed of lipids, complement components (C3, C5b-9), amyloid-beta, and vitronectin; choriocapillaris atrophy; in neovascular AMD, capillary ingrowth from choriocapillaris breaks through Bruch membrane into sub-RPE/subretinal spaces with fibrovascular proliferation, myofibroblastic transformation, and dense disciform collagen scarring
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Leading cause of blindness in elderly populations displaying unmistakable funduscopic soft drusen and subretinal hemorrhages, paired with multi-modal SD-OCT/OCTA choroidal neovascular network mapping.

Ophthalmology.name: Aniridia
clinical_manifestations: Near-total or complete bilateral absence of the iris, appearing clinically as a massive, fully dilated black pupil occupying the entire anterior chamber diameter
Congenital pendular nystagmus, marked photophobia, and reduced visual acuity (typically 20/100 to 20/200) from foveal hypoplasia
Progressive Aniridic Keratopathy: Corneal limbal stem cell deficiency (LSCD) causing conjunctivalization, superficial corneal vascular pannus, chronic epithelial defects, and corneal opacification
Secondary Glaucoma (in 50-75% of patients) developing in late childhood/adolescence; early developmental cataract and ectopia lentis
WAGR Syndrome: Wilms tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary anomalies, and intellectual disability
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Ultrasound Biomicroscopy (UBM) and Anterior Segment OCT (AS-OCT): Demonstrates the hidden, rudimentary, hypoplastic iris stump situated behind the corneoscleral limbus; progressive anterior rotation and synechial adherence of the rudimentary iris stump to the trabecular meshwork, causing secondary angle closure glaucoma

Spectral-Domain OCT (SD-OCT): Pathognomonic foveal hypoplasia: complete absence of the normal foveal pit/depression, persistent continuity of inner retinal layers across the center of the macula, and absence of photoreceptor outer segment elongation
Surveillance Abdominal Ultrasound and MRI (in WAGR / 11p13 deletion): Routine Q3-month screening for pediatric Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) and genitourinary anomalies
pathology_manifestations: Ocular Histopathology: Arrest of neuroectodermal optic cup and neural crest mesenchymal migration during week 12 of embryogenesis; hypoplastic iris root remnant containing rudimentary stromal collagen and sparse sphincter muscle fibers; fovea reveals multi-layered ganglion cells across the foveola with absent rod-free zone

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous mutations or haploinsufficiency of the master ocular transcription factor PAX6 on chromosome 11p13; contiguous gene deletion involving PAX6 and adjacent WT1 causes WAGR syndrome
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Cardinal ocular genetic disorder featuring bedside black-iris absence, aniridic keratopathy, AS-OCT visualization of the hidden iris stump, and SD-OCT foveal hypoplasia.

Ophthalmology.name: Central Serous Chorioretinopathy
clinical_manifestations: Idiopathic retinal disease characterized by serous detachment of the neurosensory retina at the macula, representing the prototypical pachychoroid spectrum disease; strongly predisposed to young and middle-aged adults (20-50 years, male-to-female ratio 6:1)

Strong clinical triggers: Exogenous corticosteroid use (any route: systemic, topical, inhaled, nasal spray, or intra-articular), elevated endogenous glucocorticoids (Cushing syndrome, pregnancy), intense emotional stress, type A personality traits, obstructive sleep apnea, and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor use

Patients present with sudden, painless, unilateral central visual blurring, micropsia (perceiving objects as smaller than actual size due to photoreceptor separation), metamorphopsia (straight lines appearing distorted on Amsler grid testing), central relative scotoma, delayed dark adaptation/recovery after photostress, and washed-out color saturation (dyschromatopsia)

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Hallmark: A well-demarcated, smooth, transparent, dome-shaped, blister-like circular or oval elevation of the neurosensory retina over the fovea/macular region, with loss of the crisp foveal light reflex

Associated Funduscopic Signs: Tiny yellowish-white subretinal fibrin deposits or subretinal lipid precipitants at the base of the detachment; one or more small, discreet, yellowish-orange elevations corresponding to focal pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs); in chronic cases, gravitation tracks ('guttering' or drip tracks) of RPE atrophic depigmentation extending downward from the macula toward the inferior retinal periphery
radiological_manifestations: Fluorescein Angiography (FA) Classic Pathognomonic Patterns: 1) 'Smoke-Stack' Phenomenon (~10-15% of cases): in early phases, a focal pinpoint hyperfluorescent leak at the RPE level appears, and as transit progresses, fluorescein ascends vertically in a thin stream (due to convection currents from protein gradients) before expanding laterally at the superior border of the detachment into an umbrella or mushroom shape; 2) 'Ink-Blot' / Expansile Dot Pattern (~80-90% of cases): focal pinpoint hyperfluorescent leak in early arteriovenous phases that gradually increases in size and intensity, symmetrically expanding radially to fill the entire serous subretinal space in late phases

Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Gold-standard cross-sectional diagnostic imaging: shows an optically clear, hypo-reflective space separating the elevated neurosensory retina from the underlying flat or minimally irregular RPE; elongation, swelling, and granular hyperreflectivity of outer photoreceptor segments ('shaggy' photoreceptors / photoreceptor outer segment elongation) due to lack of physiologic phagocytosis by detached RPE; small focal dome-shaped pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs) and hyperreflective subretinal fibrinous clumps

Enhanced-Depth Imaging OCT (EDI-OCT) & Swept-Source OCT (SS-OCT) Pachychoroid Features: Marked, diffuse thickening of the choroid beneath the detachment (subfoveal choroidal thickness often > 400-500 µm, compared to normal ~250 µm), accompanied by pathognomonic 'pachyvessels' (abnormally dilated, engorged outer choroidal venous channels in Haller's layer) with mechanical compression and thinning of the overlying Sattler's layer and choriocapillaris

Indocyanine Green Angiography (ICGA): Visualizes the primary choroidal pathophysiologic locus: early hypercyanescence with multifocal choroidal vascular hyperpermeability and delayed choroidal filling, mid-phase diffuse hyperfluorescent choroidal flush ('plumes' of leakage), and late hypofluorescent washout

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Acute subretinal fluid produces a masking effect with hypoautofluorescence, but as photoreceptors shed outer segments, accumulating fluorophores yield punctate hyperautofluorescence; chronic gravitation tracks display linear tracts of hypoautofluorescence with hyperautofluorescent margins
pathology_manifestations: Cellular and Hemodynamic Pathophysiology: Primary choroidal vascular hyperperfusion and choriocapillaris endothelial hyperpermeability mediated by excessive mineralocorticoid and glucocorticoid receptor activation; hydrostatic choroidal overload leads to focal breakdown and rupture of the tight junctions (zonula occludens) of the retinal pigment epithelium (the outer blood-retinal barrier), allowing proteinaceous choroidal fluid to escape into the subretinal space

Histopathology: Serous neurosensory retinal detachment without full-thickness retinal tears; accumulation of eosinophilic, protein-rich exudative fluid between the photoreceptor outer segments and the RPE; degenerative swelling, vacuolization, and elongation of photoreceptor outer segments; localized areas of RPE cell atrophy, RPE hyperplasia, and focal micro-dehiscences in the basement membrane of the RPE / Bruch's membrane; absent choroidal or retinal inflammatory cellular infiltrates (distinguishing it from inflammatory uveitis)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential pachychoroid retinal condition in young/middle-aged adults triggered by corticosteroids, displaying pathognomonic 'smoke-stack' leakage on FA, pachychoroid pachyvessels on EDI-OCT, and outer blood-retinal barrier breach.

Ophthalmology.name: Coats' Disease
clinical_manifestations: Idiopathic, non-familial condition occurring predominantly in young males (peak presentation 6-8 years of age), presenting with unilateral leukocoria (white pupillary reflex), strabismus, or failing vision

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Findings: Massive yellowish-golden intraretinal and subretinal lipoprotein exudation ('exudative retinitis'), frequently forming a dense circinate lipid ring around the macula
Striking retinal vascular abnormalities: localized telangiectasias, aneurysmal tortuosity, and saccular dilatations ('lightbulb' aneurysms) located primarily in the retinal periphery and midperiphery
Bullous exudative (serous) retinal detachment without retinal breaks; cholesterol crystal deposits glittering within subretinal fluid
radiological_manifestations: Orbit Contrast-Enhanced CT: Subretinal exudate appears hyperdense relative to vitreous, with ABSENCE of intraocular calcification (the critical radiological feature differentiating Coats' disease from retinoblastoma!)

Orbit MRI: Subretinal fluid/exudate is hyperintense on both T1- and T2-weighted images (due to high protein and cholesterol content); linear contrast enhancement of the detached retina and abnormal telangiectatic retinal vessels; absence of solid enhancing tumor mass

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Immediate hyperfluorescence of telangiectasias and aneurysmal saccular dilatations ('lightbulbs') in early phases, widespread capillary nonperfusion (ischemic zones), and massive progressive dye leakage in late phases
pathology_manifestations: Retinal Histopathology: Breakdown of the inner blood-retinal barrier due to loss of endothelial tight junctions and pericyte degeneration; dilated, thin-walled, aneurysmal retinal vessels with mural hyalinization and thrombosis; massive subretinal accumulation of proteinaceous fluid containing bipyramidal cholesterol crystals, lipid-laden foamy histiocytes (macrophages), and hemosiderin; complete absence of malignant neuroblastic cells
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Essential pediatric ocular condition presenting with leukocoria and lightbulb aneurysms, where lack of CT calcification distinguishes it from retinoblastoma.

Ophthalmology.name: Cytomegalovirus Retinitis
clinical_manifestations: Severe, sight-threatening opportunistic ocular infection occurring almost exclusively in profoundly immunocompromised individuals (HIV/AIDS with CD4+ T-cell count < 50 cells/uL, allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell or solid organ transplant recipients, or patients receiving potent immunosuppressive therapy)

Patients present with painless progressive visual blurring, expanding dark scotomas, sudden showers of floaters, and photopsias; may be asymptomatic initially if the peripheral retina is involved before extending into the macula or optic nerve

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Appearance: Classic 'pizza-pie' or 'cottage cheese and ketchup' retinopathy: extensive, dense, granular, yellowish-white full-thickness necrotizing retinal infiltrate with confluent, jagged superficial retinal flame hemorrhages and intraretinal blot hemorrhages distributed along retinal vascular arcades

Distinct clinical morphologic variants: 1) Fulminant / edematous / hemorrhagic pattern (classic pizza-pie appearance along arcades with massive hemorrhage and retinal edema); 2) Granular / indolent / brushfire pattern (peripherally located granular white infiltrate with minimal hemorrhage, expanding centrifugally with an active leading border leaving behind a thin, atrophic, scarred, hypocellular retina with granular RPE hyperpigmentation); 3) Frosted branch angiitis variant (severe perivascular sheathing resembling frosted tree branches)

Minimal to mild vitreous inflammation (vitritis) and anterior uveitis due to profound host immunosuppression ('quiet vitreous' compared to the intense vitritis seen in toxoplasmosis or acute retinal necrosis); late-stage complication of high-incidence rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) occurring through ragged necrotic atrophic retinal breaks (up to 30-50% of untreated eyes)
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Acute active phase reveals marked full-thickness retinal hyperreflectivity and architectural disorganization, prominent inner and outer retinal edema, hyperreflective intraretinal dots, and optical shadowing of the underlying choroid; chronic resolving phase reveals dramatic full-thickness retinal thinning, loss of all normal retinal laminae, necrotic retinal cavitations, and vitreoretinal traction bands predisposing to rhegmatogenous tears

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Early phases show hypofluorescence corresponding to blockage from retinal hemorrhages and dense opaque necrotic retina; late phases demonstrate striking granular hyperfluorescence along the active advancing 'brushfire' border due to vascular leakage and capillary breakdown; retinal vascular staining and extensive capillary non-perfusion in ischemic necrotic zones

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Active leading edge exhibits prominent hyperautofluorescence reflecting intense lipofuscin accumulation from damaged photoreceptors and RPE cell stress; burned-out necrotic atrophic zones exhibit profound hypoautofluorescence due to complete RPE and photoreceptor cell death

B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Indicated when media opacities or severe vitritis/cataract obscure direct visualization; demonstrates low-to-medium amplitude vitreous mobile echoes, focal retinochoroidal thickening at necrotizing sites, posterior vitreous detachment, and evaluates for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
pathology_manifestations: Retinal Histopathology: Coagulative, full-thickness cytolytic retinal necrosis with abrupt transition between completely necrotic retina and adjacent structurally preserved retina; extensive disruption of the internal limiting membrane, photoreceptor layer, and retinal pigment epithelium

Pathognomonic Cytomegalic Cells: Marked cytomegaly (cells enlarged up to 2-4 times normal size) with prominent, large, basophilic or amphophilic intranuclear inclusion bodies surrounded by a clear halo, imparting the classic 'owl's eye' appearance; granular, small, basophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions within retinal neurons, glial cells, and retinal vascular endothelial cells

Immunohistochemistry and Molecular Diagnostics: Strong cytoplasmic and nuclear immunoreactivity for CMV immediate-early (IE-1) and tegument (pp65) antigens; quantitative real-time PCR of aqueous humor or vitreous biopsy fluid demonstrates high viral copy loads of CMV DNA
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential opportunistic ocular infection in profound AIDS/immunosuppression characterized by pathognomonic 'pizza-pie' funduscopic retinopathy, full-thickness necrosis on SD-OCT, and pathognomonic cytomegalic 'owl's eye' viral inclusion pathology.

Ophthalmology.name: Duane Retraction Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic retraction of the globe into the orbit on attempted adduction, accompanied by immediate narrowing of the palpebral fissure (pseudoptosis)
Widening of the palpebral fissure on attempted abduction
Frequent dramatic 'upshoot' or 'downshoot' of the adducted eye during vertical movement (bridle phenomenon / leaping eye)

Motility subtypes: Type 1 (most common, ~70%): marked limitation or complete absence of abduction with normal or slightly restricted adduction; Type 2: marked limitation of adduction with normal or slightly restricted abduction; Type 3: marked limitation of both abduction and adduction
Compensatory head turn (face turn) toward the side of the affected eye to maintain binocular single vision and prevent diplopia
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Contrast-Enhanced 3T Orbit and Brainstem MRI (thin-slice heavily T2-weighted CISS / FIESTA sequences): Pathognomonic complete absence (aplasia) or severe hypoplasia of the abducens nerve (CN VI) within the prepontine cistern and Dorello canal on the affected side

Paradoxical Innervation Imaging: Aberrant branches arising from the inferior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III) entering the lateral rectus muscle belly; asymmetric hypoplasia and mild fibrous volume loss of the lateral rectus muscle compared to the contralateral normal eye
pathology_manifestations: Congenital Cranial Dysinnervation Disorder (CCDD): Primary developmental failure of abducens motor neurons in the abducens nucleus in the pons; secondary aberrant miswiring of oculomotor nerve axons to the lateral rectus muscle
Co-contraction phenomenon: Simultaneous firing of both the medial rectus and lateral rectus muscles during attempted adduction causes massive mechanical retraction of the globe into the orbital apex
Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous mutations in CHN1 (chimerin 1) in familial DRS, or SALL4 in Duane-radial ray syndrome (Okihiro syndrome)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential CCDD where globe retraction and palpebral fissure narrowing on adduction provide an immediate photographic exam finding matched with high-resolution 3T MRI demonstration of absent CN VI and paradoxical CN III innervation.

Ophthalmology.name: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Papilledema)
synonyms: papilledema secondary to raised intracranial pressure
