clinical_manifestations: Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP > 25 cm H2O on lumbar puncture in adults) of unknown etiology, overwhelmingly occurring in obese women of childbearing age (female-to-male ratio 8:1); strongly associated with rapid weight gain, hypervitaminosis A/retinoids, tetracycline antibiotics, and sleep apnea

Patients present with daily, severe, throbbing or holocephalic headaches (often worse in the morning or with Valsalva), pulse-synchronous tinnitus (rhythmic 'whooshing' sound in ears), and transient visual obscurations (TVOs: fleeting episodes of monocular or binocular vision graying out lasting seconds, typically triggered by bending or standing)

False-localizing Sixth Cranial Nerve (Abducens / CN VI) Palsy: Horizontal binocular diplopia worsening on lateral gaze due to mechanical stretching of the long, angulated intracranial course of the abducens nerve over Dorello's canal / petrous ridge

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Hallmark: Bilateral, symmetrical, severe optic disc swelling (Papilledema, Frisen staging grades 1 to 5): hyperemic swollen optic nerve heads with indistinct blurred margins, obliteration of the optic cup, elevation of the disc surface into the vitreous, and obscuration of major retinal vessels as they cross the disc margin

Specific Peripapillary Funduscopic Signs: Paton's lines (circumferential concentric retinal nerve fiber wrinkles and choroidal folds curving around the temporal disc border), radial retinal lines, flame-shaped peripapillary splinter hemorrhages, cotton-wool spots, and complete absence of spontaneous venous pulsations (SVP); central visual acuity remains preserved early, while perimetry reveals blind spot enlargement and progressive inferonasal visual field loss
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Brain and Orbit MRI (with Fat Suppression & Contrast) Pathognomonic Imaging Tetrad: 1) Partially empty or empty sella turcica (downward herniation of the suprasellar arachnoid space flattening the pituitary gland against the sellar floor); 2) Flattening of the posterior ocular globe / posterior sclera; 3) Prominent enlargement and distension of the perioptic subarachnoid space (increased optic nerve sheath diameter > 5.5-6.0 mm) with vertical tortuosity and kinking of the intraorbital optic nerve; 4) Intraocular protrusion / elevation of the optic nerve head into the vitreous cavity; lack of intracranial mass, ventricular enlargement, or dural enhancement
Magnetic Resonance Venography (MRV) / CT Venography (CTV): Demonstrates bilateral smooth, focal stenoses of the distal transverse cerebral venous sinuses (transverse sinus stenosis / TSS)

Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Quantitatively tracks papilledema: demonstrates marked, circumferential thickening of the peripapillary Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (pRNFL) and total retinal volume, dome-shaped elevated contour of the optic disc, inward protrusion of Bruch's membrane / lamina cribrosa angle, and peripapillary subretinal fluid; in chronic untreated stages, progression to profound pRNFL thinning reflects optic nerve atrophy

B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Demonstrates optic disc elevation, optic nerve sheath enlargement, and a positive '30-degree test' (decrease in optic nerve sheath diameter by >10% when gaze shifts 30 degrees away from primary position, confirming fluid distension within the subarachnoid sheath), with absence of optic disc calcification (ruling out optic disc drusen)
pathology_manifestations: Optic Nerve Pathophysiology: Transmission of markedly elevated cerebrospinal fluid hydrostatic pressure along the continuous subarachnoid space of the optic nerve sheath to the retrobulbar optic nerve; elevated pressure at the rigid scleral lamina cribrosa mechanically blocks both fast and slow axoplasmic transport in unmyelinated axons of retinal ganglion cells

Histopathology of Papilledema: Marked intracellular axoplasmic stasis and swelling of unmyelinated nerve fibers (cytoid bodies) in the prelaminar portion of the optic nerve head; compression of capillary microcirculation and peripapillary venous stasis with secondary extravasation of serous fluid and flame-shaped microhemorrhages; chronic pathology leads to irreversible loss of retinal ganglion cell axons, fibrous astrocytic proliferation (gliosis), and secondary optic disc pallor/atrophy

Sellar Histopathology: Herniation of the arachnoid membrane through an incompetent diaphragma sellae, leading to compression and thinning of the anterior pituitary parenchyma without adenomatous or neoplastic transformation
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential neuro-ophthalmic disorder in young overweight females featuring pathognomonic bilateral papilledema with Paton lines, MRI empty sella and perioptic nerve distension, and axoplasmic stasis pathology.

Ophthalmology.name: Keratoconus
clinical_manifestations: Progressive bilateral (often asymmetric) visual blurring, monocular polyopia, and rapid progression of irregular myopic astigmatism

Slit-Lamp Biomicroscopy Hallmark Signs: Fleischer Ring (partial or complete golden-brown ring of iron deposition in basal corneal epithelial cells encircling the cone base); Vogt Striae (fine, vertical stress lines in posterior stroma/Descemet membrane that disappear with gentle digital globe pressure)
Munson Sign: V-shaped conical indentation of the lower eyelid margin induced by the ectatic cornea on downgaze
Charleux Oil Droplet Sign on retroillumination; Acute Corneal Hydrops (sudden, painful profound stromal edema and visual drop due to spontaneous rupture of Descemet membrane)
radiological_manifestations: Scheimpflug Corneal Tomography (Pentacam / Sirius): Pathognomonic localized steepening with apex keratometry (Kmax >48-50 D), asymmetric bowtie pattern with skewed radial axes, elevation of anterior and posterior corneal elevation maps above best-fit sphere, and severe central/paracentral pachymetric thinning (<450 µm)

Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (AS-OCT): Epithelial thickness mapping showing epithelial thinning ('doughnut pattern' with surrounding hyperplastic ring over the cone apex), hyperreflective stromal scarring, and acute breaks/coiling of Descemet membrane in hydrops
pathology_manifestations: Corneal Histopathology: Progressive central/inferotemporal stromal thinning with loss and disorganization of collagen lamellae; fragmentation and multiple micro-dehiscences in Bowman layer; keratocyte apoptosis in anterior stroma; basal epithelial iron accumulation visualized with Prussian blue stain (Fleischer ring)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Premier corneal ectatic disease characterized by unmistakable photographic signs (Fleischer ring, Vogt striae, Munson sign) and definitive Scheimpflug tomography and AS-OCT pachymetric mapping.

Ophthalmology.name: Ocular Toxoplasmosis
clinical_manifestations: Most common cause of infectious posterior uveitis globally; caused by the obligate intracellular protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, typically representing late reactivation of encysted parasites from congenital or acquired systemic infection
Patients typically present in the 2nd to 4th decade of life with unilateral floaters, hazy blurred vision, scotoma, and ocular redness/photophobia

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Hallmark: The classic 'Headlight in the Fog' sign: a focal, intensely elevated, fluffy, creamy-white or yellowish-white area of active necrotizing retinochoroiditis with ill-defined borders, obscured by dense overlying vitreous haze and inflammatory exudate (vitritis)

Pathognomonic Satellite Lesion: Active creamy-white retinitis lesion typically arises immediately adjacent to an old, heavily hyperpigmented, punched-out, atrophic chorioretinal scar (the site of encysted reactivation); lesions preferentially involve the posterior pole and macular region

Associated Ocular Signs: Kyrieleis plaques (segmental, glistening, yellowish-white, non-occlusive periarteriolar exudates located away from the primary retinitis focus); secondary anterior uveitis with granulomatous 'mutton-fat' keratic precipitates on the corneal endothelium and elevated intraocular pressure (hypertensive uveitis)
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Highly specific cross-sectional findings: acute active lesion shows massive full-thickness hyperreflectivity and localized thickening of the neurosensory retina, disruption of retinal layered architecture, localized posterior optical shadowing of the underlying choroid, subretinal fluid accumulation, hyperreflective inflammatory cells within the vitreous and preretinal space, and thickened posterior hyaloid membrane with vitreomacular traction; adjacent inactive chorioretinal scars show profound full-thickness retinal excavation/atrophy, loss of the RPE layer, and hypertransmission of OCT signal into the sclera

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Early phases demonstrate pronounced hypofluorescence/blockage of choroidal and retinal background fluorescence caused by dense active retinal edema and infiltration; late phases show progressive, intense, fuzzy hyperfluorescence with extensive dye leakage along the margins of the active lesion; retinal vascular staining (periphlebitis and Kyrieleis arteriolitis); old adjacent inactive scars exhibit early window defects with late scleral staining

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Active retinochoroiditis exhibits patchy hypoautofluorescence surrounded by a hyperautofluorescent halo reflecting lipofuscin accumulation from dying RPE cells; old pigmented chorioretinal scars demonstrate deep hypoautofluorescence with rim hyperautofluorescence

B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Crucial when dense vitritis ('fog') precludes clear ophthalmoscopic visualization; shows dense vitreous clumped echoes/membranes, posterior vitreous detachment (PVD), localized retinochoroidal thickening, and rules out rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
pathology_manifestations: Retinochoroidal Histopathology: Severe, full-thickness coagulative retinal necrosis with destruction of neural elements and photoreceptors, surrounded by dense non-caseating granulomatous and lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory infiltrates in the adjacent retina and underlying choroid; secondary disruption, pigment liberation, and reactive hyperplasia of the retinal pigment epithelium

Identification of Toxoplasma gondii Organisms: Pathognomonic identification of crescentic, basophilic tachyzoites (rapidly dividing active vegetative form, 2-6 µm) in necrotic tissue borders, and spherical or oval tissue cysts (bradyzoites, 10-100 µm) containing hundreds of densely packed, slowly metabolizing organisms with a well-defined cyst wall that stains intensely positive with Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Gomori methenamine silver (GMS)

Molecular Confirmation: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of aqueous humor or vitreous biopsy fluid demonstrating Toxoplasma gondii B1 or SAG1 gene sequences, and positive Goldmann-Witmer coefficient (GWC > 3) confirming local intraocular antibody synthesis
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Foremost cause of infectious posterior uveitis worldwide, exhibiting the pathognomonic funduscopic 'headlight in the fog' sign adjacent to hyperpigmented scars, full-thickness hyperreflective necrosis on SD-OCT, and diagnostic PAS-positive bradyzoite tissue cysts.

Ophthalmology.name: Optic Nerve Sheath Meningioma
clinical_manifestations: Middle-aged female predilection (3:1 female-to-male ratio); presents with slowly progressive, painless, monocular vision loss and visual field defects

Classic Hoyt-Spencer Triad: 1) Painless, progressive, long-standing visual loss; 2) Optic disc pallor (atrophy) or chronic optic disc swelling; 3) Retinochoroidal collateral vessels (optociliary shunt vessels) on the optic disc: enlarged, tortuous pre-existing capillaries that shunt blood from obstructed retinal venous circulation to the peripapillary choroidal circulation
Mild, painless axial proptosis and limitation of ocular motility (especially upgaze)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Contrast-Enhanced Orbit MRI (with Fat Suppression): Pathognomonic 'Tram-Track' Sign on Axial T1 post-contrast images: Vivid, linear, homogeneous contrast enhancement of the expanded meningeal sheath surrounding the central, non-enhancing, hypointense optic nerve; Pathognomonic 'Doughnut' / 'Target' Sign on Coronal T1 post-contrast images: Circular ring of intensely enhancing meningeal tumor encasing the central non-enhancing circular optic nerve

Non-Contrast Orbit CT (Bone Window): Thickening of the optic nerve complex with pathognomonic fine, linear, punctate calcification along the optic nerve sheath (psammoma bodies), and apical expansion of the optic canal
pathology_manifestations: Meningioma Histopathology: Proliferation of uniform meningothelial cells arranged in tight syncytial lobules or concentric whorls with indistinct cell borders; abundant lamellated, concentric dystrophic calcifications (psammoma bodies); nuclear pseudoinclusions and longitudinal nuclear grooves
Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong positivity for Epithelial Membrane Antigen (EMA), Progesterone Receptor (PR), and Vimentin; negative for S100 (ruling out schwannoma)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield neuro-ophthalmic tumor displaying the Hoyt-Spencer triad of optic atrophy and optociliary shunt vessels, combined with pathognomonic MRI 'tram-track' sign and psammoma body pathology.

Ophthalmology.name: Orbital Cellulitis and Subperiosteal Abscess
clinical_manifestations: Marked, tense, painful unilateral eyelid edema and violaceous erythema
Severe proptosis (axial or non-axial globe protrusion)
Painful limitation of extraocular movements (ophthalmoplegia)
Chemosis (intense swelling of bulbar conjunctiva bulging past eyelids)
Decreased visual acuity, relative afferent pupillary defect, and optic disc edema
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT of Orbit and Paranasal Sinuses (Emergency Gold Standard): Opacification of adjacent ethmoid or maxillary sinuses with bone erosion (lamina papyracea); subperiosteal abscess (well-defined lenticular or crescent-shaped fluid collection adjacent to the orbital wall with peripheral rim enhancement); post-septal intraconal/extraconal fat stranding; superior ophthalmic vein thrombosis
Brain and Orbit MRI: High-sensitivity detection of intracranial complications: cavernous sinus thrombosis, epidural/subdural abscess, and cerebritis
pathology_manifestations: Surgical drainage aspirate: Abundant degenerate polymorphonuclear neutrophils, necrotic debris, and bacterial pathogens (S. aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, or fungal hyphae in immunocompromised hosts)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Emergency orbital condition featuring striking eyelid edema, chemosis, and proptosis paired with diagnostic subperiosteal fluid collections and ethmoid sinus opacification on contrast CT.

Ophthalmology.name: Persistent Fetal Vasculature
clinical_manifestations: Congenital developmental ocular malformation caused by the failure of the embryonic primary vitreous and hyaloid vascular system to undergo physiological programmed regression during the third trimester; typically sporadic and unilateral (>90% of cases)
Presents in full-term neonates or infants shortly after birth with leukocoria (white pupillary reflex), strabismus, microphthalmos, or failed red reflex screening

Pathognomonic Anterior PFV Hallmark on Slit-Lamp Biomicroscopy: Presence of a vascularized, dense, whitish-pink retrolental fibrovascular mass or membrane that adheres tightly to the posterior lens capsule; pathognomonic centripetal elongation and inward radial stretching of the ciliary processes visible through a dilated pupil around the margin of the small lens

Associated Anterior Segment Features: Microphthalmos (reduced corneal diameter and decreased axial length compared to contralateral eye), shallow anterior chamber, intumescent cataract due to posterior lens capsule dehiscence, and secondary angle-closure glaucoma

Pathognomonic Posterior PFV Features: Presence of a dense, opaque fibrovascular stalk or cord extending from the optic disc through the vitreous cavity to the posterior lens surface; associated with prominent falciform retinal folds, tractional retinal detachment, optic nerve hypoplasia, vitreous hemorrhage, and macular dragging
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Gold-standard first-line diagnostic modality; pathognomonically reveals a persistent, continuous, hyperechoic tubular or linear band/cord extending from the optic nerve head to the posterior surface of the lens (Cloquet's canal containing persistent hyaloid vessels); Color Doppler Ultrasonography detects persistent pulsatile arterial blood flow within the retrolental cord; demonstrates microphthalmia (shortened axial length); CRITICAL PATHOGNOMONIC NEGATIVE: absolute absence of intraocular calcification (the vital radiological sign distinguishing PFV from retinoblastoma!)

Contrast-Enhanced Orbit and Brain MRI: On T1- and T2-weighted sequences, demonstrates microphthalmic globe; retrolental soft tissue mass that shows moderate-to-marked enhancement following gadolinium administration; linear, enhancing tubular structure connecting the optic nerve to the posterior lens; subretinal exudate or fluid (often hyperintense on T1 due to proteinaceous or hemorrhagic content); no calcified intraocular tumor

Orbit Non-Contrast CT: Shows decreased globe dimensions (microphthalmia), hyperdense retrolental soft tissue, and definitively confirms the complete absence of intraocular calcifications (excluding calcifying retinoblastoma)

Fluorescein Angiography (FA) / RetCam Angiography: Visualizes abnormal radial branching of persistent vessels on the posterior lens surface, leaky fibrovascular tissue, and stretching of retinal vessels toward the central stalk
pathology_manifestations: Embryopathologic Basis: Disruption of regulated macrophage-mediated apoptosis and physiological regression of the embryonic hyaloid artery, vasa hyaloidea propria, and tunica vasculosa lentis between gestational weeks 8 and 34

Histopathology: Dense, vascularized fibrocollagenous retrolental plaque composed of proliferating spindle-shaped fibroblasts, myofibroblasts, and patent capillary/arteriolar vascular channels lined by endothelial cells containing persistent embryonic blood vessels; heterotopic mesenchymal elements (adipose tissue, smooth muscle, cartilage, or glial tissue) are identified within the plaque in up to 15-20% of cases

Lenticular Histopathology: Dehiscence, rupture, or thinning of the central posterior lens capsule, with invasion of the fibrovascular tissue into the posterior cortex producing posterior cortical cataract, Morgagnian globular degeneration of lens fibers, and foreign-body giant cell reaction to lens proteins; elongated ciliary processes drawn into the fibrovascular membrane
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential congenital cause of infant leukocoria and microphthalmos displaying inwardly stretched ciliary processes, ultrasound/MRI persistent hyaloid stalk without calcification (ruling out retinoblastoma), and hyaloid vascular remnant pathology.

Ophthalmology.name: Retinitis Pigmentosa
clinical_manifestations: Presenting symptom: Progressive night blindness (nyctalopia) in adolescence, followed by gradual concentric peripheral visual field constriction ('tunnel vision')

Pathognomonic Classic Funduscopic Triad: 1) Bone-Spicule Pigmentation: Dark black/brown melanophoric pigment deposits in a branching, reticular pattern aggregating predominantly in the mid-peripheral retina along retinal vessels; 2) Waxy Pallor of the Optic Nerve Head: Characteristic yellowish-white waxy appearance of the optic disc; 3) Severe Retinal Arteriolar Attenuation: Markedly thread-like, narrowed, attenuated retinal arterioles
Associated ocular findings: Posterior subcapsular cataract, cystoid macular edema (CME), vitreous cells, and epiretinal membrane
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Progressive loss and truncation of the photoreceptor inner segment/outer segment (IS/OS) junction (ellipsoid zone) advancing from the periphery toward the fovea; foveal sparing with preserved central island of outer retinal architecture; intraretinal cystoid fluid in CME

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Classic hyperautofluorescent perifoveal ring (Robson-Holder ring) demarcating viable, functioning central retina from metabolically stressed, degenerating outer retina; mottled mid-peripheral hypoautofluorescence corresponding to RPE atrophy and bone spicules

Full-Field Electroretinography (ffERG): Profound reduction or complete extinguishability of scotopic (rod-driven) responses, followed by progressive delay and attenuation of photopic (cone-driven) responses
pathology_manifestations: Retinal Histopathology: Primary apoptosis of rod photoreceptors followed by secondary death of cone photoreceptors; marked thinning and total loss of the outer nuclear layer and photoreceptor outer segments; detachment, hyperplasia, and transretinal migration of pigment-laden retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells into the perivascular spaces of inner retinal vessels, forming the histological bone-spicules
Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous, homozygous, or X-linked mutations in >80 genes (e.g., RHO, USH2A, RPGR, PRPF31, PDE6A)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Cardinal hereditary retinal degeneration featuring the classic funduscopic bone-spicule triad, Robson-Holder autofluorescent ring, ellipsoid zone collapse on OCT, and extinguished ERG.

Ophthalmology.name: Retinoblastoma
clinical_manifestations: Leukocoria: pathognomonic abnormal white pupillary reflex ('cat's-eye reflex') visible on photography or direct ophthalmoscopy
Strabismus (esotropia or exotropia from macular tumor involvement)
Buphthalmos, secondary neovascular glaucoma, and red, painful, inflamed eye
Hypopyon, hyphema, or orbital proptosis in advanced tumor extension
radiological_manifestations: Ocular B-Scan Ultrasound: High-attenuation intraocular retinal mass with high acoustic reflectivity and pathognomonic dense acoustic shadowing caused by intratumoral calcifications

Orbit and Brain MRI (Gold Standard for Staging): Delineation of tumor extent, optic nerve sheath invasion, transscleral extension, and screening for 'trilateral retinoblastoma' (associated pineoblastoma in the pineal gland); high T1 and low T2 signal relative to vitreous, with patchy calcifications
Orbit CT (if MRI unavailable): Highly calcified intraocular mass filling the posterior chamber
pathology_manifestations: Enucleation surgical histology: Densely packed sheets of small, round, malignant cells with hyperchromatic nuclei; pathognomonic Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (columnar cells arranged around a central lumen) and Homer-Wright pseudorosettes; widespread dystrophic calcification and necrosis
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Vivid pediatric ocular malignancy presenting with the unmistakable leukocoria ('cat's-eye') reflex, diagnosed by dense intraocular calcification on B-scan ultrasound and orbital MRI staging.

Ophthalmology.name: Retinopathy of Prematurity
clinical_manifestations: Premature neonates with low gestational age (<30 weeks) and extremely low birth weight (<1500 g) exposed to supplemental oxygen therapy

International Classification of ROP (ICROP3) Hallmark Stages: Stage 1: Demarcation line (thin, flat, white line separating vascular anterior retina from avascular posterior retina); Stage 2: Ridge (elevated pink-to-white mesenchymal ridge with volume arising from the demarcation line); Stage 3: Extraretinal fibrovascular proliferation (neovascular tufts growing from the ridge into the vitreous); Stage 4: Subtotal retinal detachment; Stage 5: Total retinal detachment presenting with leukocoria and funnel-shaped detachment
Pathognomonic 'Plus Disease': Marked tortuosity of retinal arterioles and engorgement/dilation of venules in the posterior pole, iris vascular engorgement, and pupillary rigidity
radiological_manifestations: Ocular B-Scan Ultrasonography: Funnel-shaped total retinal detachment (closed-funnel or open-funnel configuration); dense, hyperechoic retrolental fibrovascular membrane extending from optic disc to the posterior lens surface

Widefield Digital Pediatric Retinal Imaging (RetCam): High-resolution widefield photographic documentation of peripheral avascular retina, elevated fibrovascular ridge, arborizing neovascularization, vitreous hemorrhages, and posterior pole vascular tortuosity (plus disease)
pathology_manifestations: Two-Phase Pathogenesis Histology: Phase 1 (Hyperoxia/Vessel Loss): Supplemental oxygen suppresses retinal VEGF and IGF-1, causing endothelial apoptosis and cessation of normal centrifugal retinal vascular development; Phase 2 (Hypoxia/Neovascularization): Increasing metabolic demand of maturing avascular retina triggers massive hypoxic upregulation of VEGF; endothelial cell sprouting forms abnormal glomeruloid capillary tufts that breach the inner limiting membrane into cortical vitreous

Retrolental Fibroplasia: Proliferation of contractile alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblasts within the fibrovascular vitreous membrane creates severe anteroposterior and circumferential traction, causing tractional retinal detachment
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Core pediatric ophthalmic condition where RetCam fundus imaging of plus disease and B-scan ultrasound of funnel-shaped detachment match two-phase hypoxic-VEGF vascular pathology.

Ophthalmology.name: Stargardt Disease
clinical_manifestations: Most common inherited juvenile macular dystrophy; presents in childhood or adolescence with bilateral, progressive, symmetrical central vision loss, dyschromatopsia (color vision deficit), and central scotoma

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Appearance: Atrophic 'Beaten-Bronze' Maculopathy: Sharply demarcated, oval, shiny, metallic or 'snail-track' bull's-eye atrophy of the central retinal pigment epithelium at the fovea
Fundus Flavimaculatus Flecks: Innumerable yellowish-white, fish-tail shaped (pisciform) or triradiate flecks scattered throughout the posterior pole and midperiphery at the level of the RPE
radiological_manifestations: Fluorescein Angiography (FA) Pathognomonic Sign: 'Dark Choroid' / 'Silent Choroid' Sign (present in up to 85% of cases): Marked, widespread absence or blockage of the normal background choroidal flush/fluorescence throughout the entire angiogram, caused by massive accumulation of lipofuscin within the RPE absorbing blue-green excitation light; conspicuous hyperfluorescent transmission window defects at the macula revealing underlying RPE atrophy

Spectral-Domain OCT (SD-OCT): Focal disruption, attenuation, and progressive cavitation of the foveal photoreceptor ellipsoid zone (EZ) and external limiting membrane (ELM); thinning of the outer nuclear layer and loss of RPE with increased choroidal signal transmission

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Central macular hypoautofluorescence corresponding to RPE atrophy, surrounded by hyperautofluorescent pisciform flecks (representing intense bisretinoid/lipofuscin accumulation)
pathology_manifestations: Retinal Histopathology: Massive intracellular accumulation of toxic bisretinoid fluorophores (predominantly A2E and lipofuscin) within the phagolysosomes of retinal pigment epithelial cells; detergent-like lysis of lysosomal membranes leading to apoptosis of RPE cells; secondary loss and degeneration of overlying macular rod and cone photoreceptors

Molecular Genetics: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in ABCA4 on chromosome 1p22.1, encoding the ATP-binding cassette transporter operating as the flippase for N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine in photoreceptor outer segments
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Exemplary hereditary retinal disease exhibiting the pathognomonic 'beaten-bronze' maculopathy, FA 'dark choroid' sign, hyperautofluorescent flecks, and ABCA4 bisretinoid lipofuscin pathology.

Ophthalmology.name: Uveal Melanoma
clinical_manifestations: Most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults; often discovered incidentally or presenting with visual field loss, photopsia (flashes of light), metamorphopsia, or painless visual decline
Dilated Indirect Ophthalmoscopy Hallmark Findings: Elevated, dome-shaped, sessile, or collar-button/mushroom-shaped subretinal choroidal mass, typically dark brown/slate-gray (or amelanotic)
Conspicuous overlying patches of orange pigment (lipofuscin) clumps on the tumor surface
Associated secondary shifting exudative (serous) retinal detachment extending inferiorly from the tumor base; sentinel episcleral feeder vessels in anterior ciliary body tumors
radiological_manifestations: Ocular B-Scan Ultrasonography (Gold Standard Diagnostic Imaging): Pathognomonic collar-button / mushroom configuration representing rupture of the melanoma through Bruch membrane into the subretinal space; acoustic hollowing (low-to-medium internal reflectivity); choroidal excavation (depression of underlying choroidal echo); intrinsic vascular pulsations

Orbit MRI: Distinctive signal characteristics reflecting melanin paramagnetic properties: hyperintense on T1-weighted sequences and hypointense on T2-weighted sequences; avid contrast enhancement following intravenous gadolinium
Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Striking hyperautofluorescence of overlying orange lipofuscin pigment clumps; hypoautofluorescence over areas of tumor necrosis or dense melanin
pathology_manifestations: Modified Callender Classification Histopathology: Spindle A cells (slender with flattened nuclei and chromatin fold, low metastatic risk); Spindle B cells (plump with central nucleoli); Epithelioid cells (large, pleomorphic, dyscohesive with abundant cytoplasm and macronucleoli, high metastatic risk); closed extravascular matrix loops (PAS-positive loops)
Molecular Genetics: Mutually exclusive driver mutations in GNAQ or GNA11; high risk of distant hepatic metastasis associated with loss of BAP1 expression (chromosome 3 monosomy)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal ocular malignancy displaying pathognomonic mushroom configuration, acoustic hollowing on B-scan US, T1-hyperintensity on MRI, and Callender histopathology.

Ophthalmology.name: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease
clinical_manifestations: Severe, bilateral, systemic autoimmune granulomatous panuveitis with associated cutaneous, auditory, and central nervous system manifestations; strongly associated with HLA-DR4 and HLA-DRB1*0405 alleles; predilection for pigmented ethnicities (Asians, Hispanics, Native Americans, Middle Easterners) and females aged 20-50

Follows four classic clinical phases: 1) Prodromal Phase: flu-like syndrome, severe headache, stiff neck, orbital pain, tinnitus, dysacusis (sensorineural hearing loss), vertigo, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) lymphocytic pleocytosis; 2) Acute Uveitic Phase: sudden, catastrophic, bilateral painless vision loss presenting with severe granulomatous bilateral panuveitis, mutton-fat keratic precipitates, anterior chamber cells/flare, vitritis, and pathognomonic bilateral, multi-lobular, bullous exudative (serous) retinal detachments; 3) Convalescent (Chronic) Phase: occurring weeks to months later, marked by widespread depigmentation of melanocyte-containing tissues: pathognomonic 'Sunset Glow' fundus (striking bright orange-red or yellowish-red funduscopic discoloration due to profound choroidal depigmentation and melanocyte loss), Dalen-Fuchs nodules, Sugiura sign (perilimbal vitiligo), cutaneous vitiligo, poliosis (premature patchy whitening of eyebrows, eyelashes, and scalp hair), and alopecia; 4) Chronic Recurrent Phase: recurrent bouts of anterior granulomatous uveitis, subretinal fibrosis, choroidal neovascularization (CNV), and secondary glaucoma/cataract
Lack of preceding penetrating ocular trauma or ocular surgery (an absolute requirement to distinguish VKH from sympathetic ophthalmia)
radiological_manifestations: Fluorescein Angiography (FA) Classic Acute Findings: Early phases demonstrate multiple, discrete, pinpoint hyperfluorescent leaking foci at the level of the RPE ('starry night' or 'milky way' sign); late phases show progressive, dramatic pooling of fluorescein within multi-lobular subretinal spaces delineating the multi-lobular exudative retinal detachments ('flower-petal' or clover-leaf pattern); diffuse hyperfluorescent optic disc leakage/staining and delayed choroidal perfusion

Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Highly specific for acute VKH: demonstrates multi-lobular serous retinal detachments partitioned by membranous hyperreflective subretinal and intraretinal fibrinous septa; marked undulation, folding, and thickening of the RPE/Bruch's membrane layer (RPE corrugation / foldings); subretinal fluid containing hyperreflective inflammatory fibrinous aggregates; Enhanced Depth Imaging (EDI-OCT) reveals massive, diffuse, low-reflective choroidal thickening (>600-800 µm) during the acute phase that rapidly normalizes/compresses upon high-dose systemic corticosteroid therapy

Indocyanine Green Angiography (ICGA): Direct assessment of choroiditis: early-phase delay in choriocapillaris filling; intermediate-phase shows pathognomonic diffuse, evenly distributed hypofluorescent dark dots (HDDs) representing granulomatous choroidal infiltrates; late-phase diffuse hyperfluorescence and leakage of choroidal stromal vessels

B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Demonstrates diffuse, low-to-medium reflective choroidal thickening predominantly affecting the posterior pole (without scleral thickening, distinguishing it from posterior scleritis), serous exudative retinal detachments, vitreous opacities, and thickening of the posterior sclera
pathology_manifestations: Immunopathologic Basis: CD4+ T-cell-mediated autoimmune response against melanocyte-specific antigens (particularly tyrosinase-related proteins TRP-1 and TRP-2) expressed in the uvea, inner ear stria vascularis, meninges, and epidermis

Histopathology of Acute Phase: Diffuse, non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation almost entirely confined to the uveal tract (choroid, ciliary body, and iris), characterized by thick lymphocytic and epithelioid histiocytic infiltrates with multinucleated Langerhans-type giant cells and plasma cells; pathognomonic 'Dalen-Fuchs Nodules': discrete granulomatous cellular aggregates located between Bruch's membrane and the RPE, composed of transformed epithelioid RPE cells, histiocytes, and lymphocytes; preservation and sparing of the choriocapillaris in early stages

Histopathology of Convalescent Phase: Progressive, near-total loss of melanin pigment granules and destruction of uveal melanocytes throughout the choroidal stroma, with pigment clumping and clearance by melanophages, directly generating the gross orange-red 'sunset glow' fundus appearance
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Classic autoimmune melanocyte-directed panuveitis syndrome characterized by bilateral multi-lobular exudative detachments, FA pinpoint leaks, the pathognomonic 'sunset glow' fundus, Dalen-Fuchs nodules, and granulomatous choroiditis.

Ophthalmology.name: Primary Congenital Glaucoma
clinical_manifestations: Enlarged cloudy cornea and buphthalmos in an infant
Epiphora, photophobia, and blepharospasm
Haab striae once the cornea clears
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound biomicroscopy or axial-length ultrasound documents globe enlargement
pathology_manifestations: Trabecular meshwork dysgenesis on gonioscopy photographs; histology is rarely obtained
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Infantile glaucoma with a bedside corneal photograph.

Ophthalmology.name: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
clinical_manifestations: Red eye, mid-dilated oval pupil, and corneal edema
Shallow anterior chamber on slit lamp
The fellow eye often shows a closable angle
radiological_manifestations: Anterior-segment OCT or ultrasound biomicroscopy of iridotrabecular contact
pathology_manifestations: No routine histology; gonioscopy is the clinical image
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Acute glaucoma with a recognizable external and slit-lamp photograph, unlike chronic open-angle glaucoma which has no bedside image.

Ophthalmology.name: Trachoma
clinical_manifestations: Follicular conjunctivitis of the upper tarsus
Herbert pits and Arlt line in healed disease
Trichiasis and corneal opacity from cicatricial entropion
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Inclusion conjunctivitis with chlamydial inclusions; the WHO sign photographs are the usual gallery
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Chronic ocular infection with staged conjunctival and lid photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Onchocerciasis
clinical_manifestations: Sclerosing keratitis advancing from the limbus
Chorioretinal atrophy and optic atrophy in river blindness
Onchocercal nodules and leopard-skin depigmentation as the skin site of the same infection
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound of a nodule is optional; the slit-lamp microfilaria in the anterior chamber is the image
pathology_manifestations: Adult worms in a subcutaneous nodule and microfilariae in the cornea or skin snip
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Filarial disease whose corneal, nodule, and skin photographs belong together.

Ophthalmology.name: Ocular Coloboma
clinical_manifestations: Keyhole iris defect inferonasally
Fundus coloboma as a white inferonasal chorioretinal defect
Microphthalmos when the fissure closure defect is severe
radiological_manifestations: Orbital ultrasound or MRI for associated microphthalmos or cyst
pathology_manifestations: Failure of embryonic fissure closure; histology is not the usual image
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Congenital fissure defect with iris and fundus photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Peters Anomaly
clinical_manifestations: Central corneal opacity with iris strands to the posterior cornea
Shallow or absent anterior chamber in severe cases
radiological_manifestations: Anterior-segment OCT or ultrasound biomicroscopy of the lens-cornea adhesion
pathology_manifestations: Absent Descemet membrane and endothelium in the corneal leukoma
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Anterior-segment malformation with a corneal-opacity photograph.

Ophthalmology.name: Sympathetic Ophthalmia
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral granulomatous uveitis days to years after penetrating trauma or surgery in one eye
Dalen-Fuchs spots on the fundus
Mutton-fat keratic precipitates
radiological_manifestations: Fluorescein angiography and OCT of the multifocal choroiditis
pathology_manifestations: Diffuse granulomatous uveal inflammation if the exciting eye is enucleated
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Bilateral uveitis after trauma, with fundus and slit-lamp photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Morning Glory Disc Anomaly
clinical_manifestations: Enlarged funnel-shaped disc with a central glial tuft and radial vessels
Serous retinal detachment in some eyes
radiological_manifestations: MRI or MRA when a basal encephalocele or carotid narrowing is being excluded
pathology_manifestations: No routine histology
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Congenital disc anomaly with a named fundus photograph.

Ophthalmology.name: Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Painless morning blurriness and glare that gradually improves throughout the day as corneal surface evaporation reduces nighttime edema
Progressive decline in visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, and debilitating halo artifacts around light sources at night
Ocular pain, foreign body sensation, and photophobia when epithelial bullae rupture (bullous keratopathy stage)
radiological_manifestations: Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (AS-OCT): Confluent drop-like or dome-shaped excrescences arising from a thickened, hyperreflective Descemet membrane, accompanied by diffuse stromal thickening and cystic epithelial intraepithelial fluid pockets

Corneal Specular Microscopy / Confocal Microscopy: Severe pleomorphism and polymegathism with endothelial cell density depleted well below 1,000 cells/mm²; dark non-reflecting central holes surrounded by bright cellular halos corresponding to guttae
Pachymetry Mapping: Central corneal thickness markedly increased (>600–750 µm), demonstrating marked loss of the normal central-to-peripheral corneal thickness gradient
pathology_manifestations: Slit Lamp Biomicroscopy: Central corneal guttae displaying a pathognomonic 'beaten metal' or 'orange peel' reflection pattern on specular examination; stromal clouding; microcystic epithelial edema progressing to large bullae

Histopathology of Descemet Membrane / Cornea: Markedly thickened Descemet membrane exhibiting multiple mushroom- or anvil-shaped wart-like nodular excrescences (guttae) composed of abnormal cross-banded collagen, with a severely attenuated, flattened, and apoptotic endothelial monolayer
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic bilateral corneal dystrophy defined by pathognomonic 'beaten bronze' guttae on specular slit-lamp biomicroscopy and microcystic bullous keratopathy.

Ophthalmology.name: Best Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Insidious, painless deterioration of central visual acuity, reading difficulty, and metamorphopsia occurring in childhood or adolescence
Disproportionately preserved visual acuity during the intact vitelliform stage despite dramatic funduscopic appearance
Central scotoma with acute visual loss occurring during choroidal neovascularization (CNV) or final atrophic stages
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Striking dome-shaped homogeneous hyperreflective subretinal accumulation of lipofuscin-like vitelliform material uncoupling the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), progressing to a hyporeflective fluid fluid-level (pseudohypopyon stage) and subretinal fibrosis

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Intense, brilliant hyperautofluorescence corresponding exactly to the vitelliform 'egg-yolk' deposit, changing to gravity-dependent hyperautofluorescent layering in the pseudohypopyon stage and hypoautofluorescence in the atrophic stage
Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Early hypofluorescence (blockage of underlying choroidal flush by vitelliform material) followed by late hyperfluorescence; leakage seen if secondary CNV develops
pathology_manifestations: Fundus Photography: Classic multi-stage progression: Stage 1 (previtelliform: tiny yellow flecks), Stage 2 (vitelliform: homogeneous yellow, well-circumscribed, round 'sunny-side-up egg yolk' macular lesion), Stage 3 (pseudohypopyon: partial absorption with fluid-debris level), Stage 4 ('scrambled egg': fragmented lesion), Stage 5 (chorioretinal atrophy or scar)
Electro-oculogram (EOG): Markedly subnormal light peak with an Arden ratio consistently <1.5 (pathognomonic hallmark demonstrating generalized RPE bestrophin channel dysfunction despite normal ERG)
Histopathology: Massive accumulation of autofluorescent lipofuscin granules within RPE cells and in the subretinal space between the RPE and outer segments
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Classic macular dystrophy presenting with the unmistakable 'egg-yolk' to 'scrambled-egg' fundus lesion, brilliant hyperautofluorescence on FAF, and pathognomonic subnormal EOG Arden ratio.

Ophthalmology.name: Acanthamoeba Keratitis
clinical_manifestations: Severe, excruciating ocular pain notoriously disproportionate to early slit-lamp clinical findings
History of soft contact lens wear, contact lens rinsing with tap water, or swimming/hot tub exposure while wearing lenses
Intense photophobia, tearing, foreign body sensation, blepharospasm, and decreased vision
radiological_manifestations: In Vivo Confocal Microscopy (IVCM - Gold Standard Optical Imaging): High-contrast visualization of pathognomonic Acanthamoeba double-walled polygonal or round cysts (10–25 µm) with highly reflective walls, and bright, hyperreflective amoebic trophozoites infiltrating the corneal stroma alongside damaged keratocytes and disrupted subbasal nerve plexus
Anterior Segment OCT: Deep stromal hyperreflectivity corresponding to stromal ring infiltration, stromal edema, and descemetocele formation
pathology_manifestations: Slit Lamp Biomicroscopy: Early epithelial pseudo-dendritic or punctate lesions; pathognomonic radial keratoneuritis (linear, branching perineural infiltrates along corneal nerves); advanced stage featuring a complete stromal ring infiltrate (Wessely immune ring), dense central stromal suppuration, and hypopyon

Corneal Scraping Cytology / Histopathology: Giemsa, Calcofluor White (fluorescent), or Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS) stains highlighting double-walled polygonal cysts with outer wrinkled ectocyst and inner polygonal endocyst; non-nutrient agar culture with Escherichia coli lawn demonstrating classic amoebic trails (clearing tracks made by feeding trophozoites)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield sight-threatening corneal infection with unmistakable radial keratoneuritis, pathognomonic stromal ring infiltrates, and double-walled polygonal cysts visible on in vivo confocal microscopy.

Ophthalmology.name: Pigment Dispersion Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Typically asymptomatic in early stages; diagnosed in young, myopic males during routine ophthalmic examination
Episodic blurred vision, halos around lights, and ocular ache occurring after strenuous exercise or dark adaptation due to acute pigment shedding and intraocular pressure spikes
Insidious peripheral visual field loss when untreated pigmentary glaucoma develops
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound Biomicroscopy (UBM) / Anterior Segment OCT: Concave iris configuration with backward posterior bowing of the mid-peripheral iris into direct contact with the anterior lens zonules; wide anterior chamber angle and deepening of anterior chamber depth
Visual Field Testing (Humphrey Visual Field): Arcuate scotomas, nasal steps, and generalized depression characteristic of secondary open-angle glaucomatous optic neuropathy
pathology_manifestations: Slit Lamp Biomicroscopy: Krukenberg spindle (pathognomonic vertical, brown, spindle-shaped pigment deposit on the central corneal endothelium along convection currents); mid-peripheral radial spoke-like iris transillumination defects visible upon coaxial illumination; pigment dusting on the anterior lens surface (Zentmayer ring / Scheie stripe)
Gonioscopy: Deep wide anterior chamber angle with dense, homogeneous, chocolate-brown trabecular meshwork pigmentation throughout 360°; Sampaolesi line (wavy pigment line anterior to Schwalbe line)
Optic Disc Examination: Progressive glaucomatous optic disc cupping, neuroretinal rim thinning, and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) drop-out
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Classic ocular condition demonstrating the iconic Krukenberg endothelial spindle, radial iris transillumination spoke defects, and intense 360-degree trabecular meshwork hyperpigmentation on gonioscopy.

Ophthalmology.name: Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Often asymptomatic until severe elevated intraocular pressure or advanced secondary glaucoma causes irreversible peripheral visual field constriction
Poor pupillary dilation (pupillary rigidity) due to fibrovascular and fibrillar basement membrane infiltration of the iris stroma
Marked zonular instability causing phacodonesis (lens wobble), anterior chamber shallowing, lens subluxation, and high complication rates during cataract surgery
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound Biomicroscopy (UBM): Zonular elongation, thinning, or complete zonular dehiscence with asymmetric anterior chamber depth and tilting of the crystalline lens
Anterior Segment OCT: Hyperreflective fibrillar aggregates coating the pupillary margin, anterior lens capsule, and trabecular meshwork
Optic Nerve OCT / Visual Fields: Progressive optic nerve head cupping with marked retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) loss and deep glaucomatous scotomas
pathology_manifestations: Slit Lamp Biomicroscopy: Pathognomonic 'three-ring sign' on the anterior lens capsule consisting of a central translucent disc, a clear intermediate zone scraped clean by pupillary excursion, and a peripheral granular ring; dandruff-like flaky white-gray fibrillar deposits along the pupillary margin ('moth-eaten' pupillary border)

Gonioscopy: Irregular, heavily pigmented trabecular meshwork with pigment granules extending beyond Schwalbe line (Sampaolesi line), accompanied by dandruff-like white aggregates in the trabecular angles
Electron Microscopy: Cross-banded fibrillar microfibrillar amyloid-like basement membrane protein deposits associated with LOXL1 gene dysregulation
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield age-related systemic microfibrillopathy featuring the unmistakable anterior lens capsule 'three-ring sign', pupillary margin dandruff flakes, and high-risk zonular fragility.

Ophthalmology.name: Birdshot Chorioretinopathy
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral floaters, insidious painless decrease in visual acuity, and debilitating nyctalopia (night blindness)
Disturbances in color vision (dyschromatopsia), glare sensitivity, photopsias, and peripheral visual field constriction
Quiet anterior segment (minimal to no anterior chamber inflammation or synechiae) contrasting with chronic posterior segment inflammation
radiological_manifestations: Indocyanine Green Angiography (ICGA - Gold Standard): Numerous, well-demarcated hypofluorescent dark dots (hypofluorescent spots) in the early, intermediate, and late phases, representing active deep stromal choroidal granulomas that far exceed those visible on fundus photography
Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Retinal vasculitis with diffuse fern-like retinal vascular leakage, optic disc hyperfluorescence ('hot disc'), and cystoid macular edema (petaloid leakage)
Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): Loss of photoreceptor ellipsoid zone integrity, retinal thinning, and cystoid macular edema (CME)
pathology_manifestations: Fundus Photography: Multiple bilateral, creamy-orange, ovoid or round hypopigmented choroidal lesions (500–1500 µm) characteristically radiating outward from the optic nerve head toward the equator following choroidal vessels ('shotgun pellet pattern'), with prominent vitritis and vascular attenuation
Immunogenetics: Near-absolute association (>95%) with the human leukocyte antigen HLA-A29 allele
Histopathology: Non-necrotizing lymphohistiocytic choroidal infiltrates composed primarily of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells with melanocyte destruction and secondary retinal perivasculitis
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic posterior uveitis with unmistakable creamy-orange fundus lesions arranged in a shotgun pattern, HLA-A29 genetic restriction, and hypofluorescent dark spots on ICG angiography.

Ophthalmology.name: Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid
synonyms: mucous membrane pemphigoid with ocular involvement
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, insidious, bilateral progressive cicatrizing conjunctivitis manifesting with red eye, foreign body sensation, grittiness, and epiphora
Progressive conjunctival shrinkage with obliteration and foreshortening of the inferior and superior conjunctival fornices
Formation of symblepharon (fibrous bridges tethering the palpebral conjunctiva of the eyelids to the bulbar conjunctiva of the globe)

Trichiasis, distichiasis, and cicatricial entropion leading to mechanical corneal microtrauma, non-healing corneal epithelial defects, secondary infectious keratitis, and complete ocular surface keratinization (blindness)
radiological_manifestations: Slit Lamp Photographic Documentation / Staging: Foster Staging: Stage I (chronic conjunctivitis with subepithelial fibrosis), Stage II (fornix foreshortening), Stage III (symblepharon formation), Stage IV (ankyloblepharon, frozen globe, and keratinized ocular surface)
Anterior Segment OCT: Progressive subepithelial fibrosis, thinning of the fornices, and severe conjunctivalization of the cornea
pathology_manifestations: Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF - Gold Standard): Linear deposition of IgG, IgA, and/or complement C3 along the basement membrane zone (BMZ) of the conjunctival epithelium

Conjunctival Biopsy (Histopathology): Chronic subepithelial inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes, marked squamous metaplasia of conjunctival epithelium, loss of mucin-secreting goblet cells, and extensive dense stromal fibrosis
Autoantibody Targets: Autoantibodies targeting basement membrane components including BP180 (type XVII collagen), BP230, laminin 332 (epiligrin), and alpha-6-beta-4 integrin
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic autoimmune cicatrizing ocular disorder showcasing striking symblepharon bands, fornix obliteration, and direct immunofluorescence demonstrating linear BMZ antibody deposition.

Ophthalmology.name: Acute Endophthalmitis
clinical_manifestations: Sudden, catastrophic visual loss occurring within days of intraocular surgery (cataract extraction, intravitreal injection) or penetrating ocular trauma
Severe, throbbing ocular and periorbital pain accompanied by intense photophobia, lid edema, and chemosis
Profound loss of the red reflex on distant direct ophthalmoscopy
radiological_manifestations: Ophthalmic B-Scan Ultrasonography (Critical Imaging Modality): Dense mobile vitreous echogenic debris, sheets, and dense vitreous membranes ('white-out' vitreous chamber), choroidal thickening, and complete absence of posterior acoustic clarity with or without tractional/rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
pathology_manifestations: Slit Lamp Biomicroscopy: Dramatic hypopyon (layer of purulent white-yellow exudate in the inferior anterior chamber angle), intense conjunctival and ciliary injection, corneal haze/microcystic edema, fibrinous exudate across the pupil, and dense vitritis obscuring fundus details

Vitreous / Anterior Chamber Tap Microscopy: Gram stain demonstrating gram-positive cocci (Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species) or gram-negative bacilli (Pseudomonas aeruginosa); abundant degenerate polymorphonuclear leukocytes
Microbiological Culture: Positive bacterial or fungal growth on blood agar, chocolate agar, and thioglycollate broth confirmative of causative infectious organism
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield intraocular surgical emergency characterized by striking layered anterior chamber hypopyon, loss of red reflex, and dense vitreous opacification on B-scan ultrasonography.

Ophthalmology.name: Gyrate Atrophy of the Choroid and Retina
clinical_manifestations: Progressive nyctalopia and constricted visual fields from childhood
Pathognomonic fundus: sharply demarcated scalloped chorioretinal atrophy advancing from periphery toward macula
High myopia and posterior subcapsular cataracts
radiological_manifestations: Fundus photograph/OCT: characteristic scalloped-edge chorioretinal atrophic zones; electroretinography reduced
pathology_manifestations: OAT deficiency with massive hyperornithinemia; RPE and choroidal degeneration
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The scalloped gyrate fundus is a pathognomonic image.

Ophthalmology.name: X-Linked Juvenile Retinoschisis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic spoke-wheel/cartwheel foveal schisis - stellate radiating cysts at the macula
Peripheral retinoschisis with vitreous veils and schisis cavities
Reduced acuity in affected boys; vitreous hemorrhage complications
radiological_manifestations: OCT: splitting of the retinal nerve-fiber layer creating macular spoke-wheel cystoid spaces; ERG: electronegative b-wave
pathology_manifestations: RS1 mutation; Müller-cell defect splitting the nerve-fiber layer; no leakage on FA (unlike cystoid edema)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Cartwheel foveal schisis plus OCT layer-splitting is a pathognomonic fundus/OCT pairing.

Ophthalmology.name: Ocular Toxocariasis (Ocular Larva Migrans)
clinical_manifestations: Peripheral or posterior granuloma - a solitary elevated retinal/subretinal mass often dragging the macula into a fold
Leukocoria mimicking retinoblastoma in children
Unilateral painless vision loss
radiological_manifestations: Fundus photography documents the dragging granuloma; B-scan: elevated mass with vitreous traction; ELISA Toxocara serology
pathology_manifestations: Toxocara larva incites a fibrovascular eosinophilic granuloma; serum antibodies confirm
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct from covered ocular toxoplasmosis - the dragging macular granuloma is a different phenotype.

Ophthalmology.name: Choroidal Osteoma
clinical_manifestations: Orange-yellow, well-demarcated juxtapapillary or macular plaque with scalloped geographic borders on fundoscopy
Pseudopod-like margins distinguishing it from other choroidal lesions
Young women predominantly; bilateral in a minority
radiological_manifestations: B-scan ultrasound: high-amplitude calcified plaque with acoustic shadowing; CT: bone-density plaque in the choroid - disease-specific
pathology_manifestations: Mature bone formation within the choroid; decalcification causes RPE atrophy and CNV
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Orange-yellow scalloped plaque plus calcification on US/CT is disease-specific.

Ophthalmology.name: Wyburn-Mason Syndrome (Racemose Retinal Hemangioma)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic fundus: a tangled knot of markedly dilated retinal vessels forming a 'bag of worms' arteriovenous malformation
Associated ipsilateral midbrain and facial AVMs
Retinal hemorrhages or exudation threatening vision
radiological_manifestations: Fundus photograph and fluorescein angiography show the AV malformation without intervening capillary bed; cerebral MRI/angiography for associated brain AVMs
pathology_manifestations: Congenital retinal AVM; nonhereditary phakomatosis-like vascular anomaly
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The racemose 'bag-of-worms' fundus completes the phakomatosis set.

Ophthalmology.name: Septo-Optic Dysplasia (de Morsier Syndrome)
synonyms: optic nerve hypoplasia with absent septum pellucidum
clinical_manifestations: 'Double-ring' optic-disc hypoplasia on fundoscopy: small pale disc surrounded by a yellow ring of scleral pigment
Nystagmus and poor vision in infancy
Midline defects: absent septum pellucidum and hypothalamic-pituitary endocrinopathy
radiological_manifestations: MRI: absent septum pellucidum with 'squared' frontal horns and optic-nerve/chiasmal hypoplasia - the dual imaging signature
pathology_manifestations: Forebrain midline developmental defect; mutations in HESX1 and others in subsets
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Double-ring disc photo plus absent-septum MRI is a dual signature.

Ophthalmology.name: Familial Exudative Vitreoretinopathy
clinical_manifestations: Peripheral retinal avascular zone with temporal dragging of the macula and disc
Falciform retinal fold extending from disc to periphery
Neovascularization, exudation, and tractional detachment in severe cases
radiological_manifestations: Fluorescein angiography: peripheral avascular retina with a sharp V-shaped avascular-demarcation border - diagnostic; widefield FA in asymptomatic relatives shows mild avascularity
pathology_manifestations: Wnt-pathway mutations (FZD4, LRP5, NDP, TSPAN12); incomplete retinal vascularization
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The dragging-macular fold plus peripheral avascularity on FA is a distinct entity.

Ophthalmology.name: Axenfeld-Rieger Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Posterior embryotoxon: a prominent anteriorly displaced Schwalbe ring visible on slit-lamp
Iris strands stretching to the embryotoxon with corectopia and polycoria
Systemic: hypodontia, umbilical anomalies, facial dysmorphism; glaucoma in half
radiological_manifestations: Anterior-segment photography and OCT document the displaced ring, iris strands, and pupil anomalies; gonioscopy images the adhesion
pathology_manifestations: PITX2/FOXC1 mutations; anterior-chamber developmental arrest
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Anterior-segment photographs of embryotoxon plus iris strands are definitive.

Ophthalmology.name: Iridocorneal Endothelial (ICE) Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Unilateral progressive iris atrophy, hole formation, and pupil displacement (corectopia)
'Hammered-silver' beaten-bronze endothelial appearance on slit-lamp
Peripheral anterior synechiae closing the angle with secondary glaucoma
radiological_manifestations: Specular microscopy/slit-lamp photography: dark endothelial cells with loss of the hexagonal mosaic; anterior-segment OCT maps synechiae
pathology_manifestations: Abnormal corneal endothelium proliferates over angle and iris forming membranes that contract
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Iris-atrophy corectopia plus hammered-silver endothelium is disease-specific imagery.

Ophthalmology.name: Fuchs Heterochromic Iridocyclitis
clinical_manifestations: Iris heterochromia with atrophic lighter iris on the affected side
Stellate or medium-sized keratic precipitates scattered over the entire corneal endothelium
Insidious low-grade anterior-chamber inflammation without synechiae; cataract and glaucoma sequelae
radiological_manifestations: Slit-lamp photography documents heterochromia and the KP pattern
pathology_manifestations: Chronic anterior uveitis of uncertain etiology (rubella association in subsets); no granulomatous changes
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Heterochromia plus stellate KPs is a named uveitis entity.

Ophthalmology.name: Bietti Crystalline Corneoretinal Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Glistening yellow-white retinal crystals scattered in the posterior fundus on fundoscopy
Corneal limbal crystals visible on slit-lamp
Progressive nyctalopia and chorioretinal atrophy in adulthood
radiological_manifestations: Fundus photograph and autofluorescence document crystal distribution and atrophy; OCT shows intraretinal crystal hyperreflectivity
pathology_manifestations: CYP4V2 mutation; lipid-crystal deposits in retina and cornea; crystalline material in circulating lymphocytes
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The glistening retinal-crystal fundus is a unique photographic phenotype.

Ophthalmology.name: Corneal Stromal Dystrophies (Granular, Lattice, Macular)
clinical_manifestations: Granular: sharply demarcated white 'crumb/snowflake' anterior stromal opacities with clear intervals
Lattice: branching refractile lattice lines in the stroma
Macular: diffuse cloudy stroma with blurred-edge opacities and early visual loss
radiological_manifestations: Slit-lamp photography and anterior-segment OCT differentiate the three dystrophies by opacity morphology and depth
pathology_manifestations: TGFBI mutations in granular/lattice; Congo-red-positive amyloid in lattice; CHST6 mutation with keratan-sulfate deposits in macular
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The crumb/lattice/cloud slit-lamp morphologies are iconic corneal photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Anophthalmia and Microphthalmia
clinical_manifestations: Visible absent or severely reduced globe with small palpebral fissure
Sunken orbital appearance and ptosis on the affected side
Orbital hypoplasia in severe microphthalmia
radiological_manifestations: Orbital CT/MRI: absent or small malformed globe with disorganized orbital contents; quantifies axial length
pathology_manifestations: Developmental arrest of optic vesicle; SOX2, OTX2, PAX6 and other transcription-factor mutations
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive anterior-segment clinical photographs; a disease-level congenital entity.

Ophthalmology.name: Circumscribed Choroidal Hemangioma
clinical_manifestations: Orange-red, dome-shaped choroidal mass posterior to the equator on fundoscopy
Exudative retinal detachment overlying the mass
Blurred vision or metamorphopsia
radiological_manifestations: B-scan: acoustically solid dome; OCT/fluorescein/ICG angiography differentiates from amelanotic melanoma and choroidal metastasis
pathology_manifestations: Benign vascular choroidal tumor; distinct from the diffuse hemangioma of covered Sturge-Weber syndrome
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Orange-red fundus mass is a distinct solitary entity separate from diffuse SWS-associated hemangioma.

Ophthalmology.name: Ocular Surface Squamous Neoplasia (Conjunctival SCC)
clinical_manifestations: Gelatinous or leukoplakic limbal mass with prominent feeder vessels on slit-lamp
Interpalpebral limbal location typical
Cystic or pigmented variants
radiological_manifestations: Anterior-segment OCT/UBM: thickened hyperreflective epithelium with abrupt transition - disease-specific imaging sign
pathology_manifestations: Conjunctival intraepithelial neoplasia through invasive squamous carcinoma; HPV and UV-associated
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Feeder-vessel limbal mass photographs are how the disease is recognized.

Ophthalmology.name: Conjunctival Lymphoma
clinical_manifestations: 'Salmon-patch' fleshy pink infiltrate in the conjunctival fornix - named teaching sign
Painless swelling or ptosis
Bilateral in a minority; usually indolent MALT type
radiological_manifestations: Orbital MRI: enhancing molded lesion coating the globe without bone destruction; slit-lamp photo is the entry sign
pathology_manifestations: Dense monotonous marginal-zone (MALT) lymphoid infiltrate; CD20+ B-cells; often conjunctival-only presentation of systemic lymphoma
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The salmon-patch infiltrate is a pathognomonic ocular photograph.

Ophthalmology.name: Cataract (Age-Related and Pediatric)
clinical_manifestations: White pupillary reflex (leukocoria) from a dense lens opacity in pediatric cases
Brunescent yellow-brown discoloration of the lens nucleus (nuclear sclerosis) on slit-lamp examination
Cortical spokes: white, wedge-shaped opacities radiating from the lens periphery
Posterior subcapsular plaque: granular opacity beneath the posterior lens capsule
Mature cataract: diffuse milky-white lens opacity visible through the pupil
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Lens opacity patterns such as leukocoria, cortical spokes and mature milky lenses are standard slit-lamp and external eye photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
clinical_manifestations: Enlarged optic disc cup with increased cup-to-disc ratio on fundus photography
Focal notching or thinning of the neuroretinal rim, most often inferotemporal or superotemporal
Peripapillary atrophy surrounding the optic disc
Disc-edge hemorrhage (splinter hemorrhage) on the optic disc
Open anterior chamber angle on gonioscopy, distinguishing it from angle-closure
radiological_manifestations: OCT/retinal nerve fiber layer: Focal or diffuse thinning of the peripapillary nerve fiber layer
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Optic disc cupping, rim notching and nerve fiber layer thinning on fundus photography and OCT are core image classes for glaucoma.

Ophthalmology.name: Pterygium and Pinguecula
clinical_manifestations: Pterygium: triangular fibrovascular wing of bulbar conjunctiva growing onto the cornea, usually nasal
Pterygium: raised, thickened leading edge (head) advancing over the clear cornea
Pinguecula: yellow-white, elevated conjunctival nodule beside the limbus that does not invade the cornea
Engorged superficial conjunctival and episcleral vessels feeding the pterygium body
Surrounding hyperemia and inflammation during active disease
pathology_manifestations: Conjunctival specimen/H&E: Basophilic, degenerated (elastotic) collagen in the subepithelial stroma
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Wedge-shaped pterygia and limbal pingueculae are everyday slit-lamp and external photographs with distinctive morphology.

Ophthalmology.name: Bacterial Keratitis
clinical_manifestations: Focal dense stromal infiltrate with an overlying epithelial defect (corneal ulcer)
Hypopyon: layered white inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber
Ill-defined satellite infiltrates surrounding the main ulcer
Circumlimbal ciliary injection (red, flushed conjunctiva around the cornea)
Stromal melting or thinning with a crater-like ulcer in severe cases
pathology_manifestations: Corneal scraping/Gram stain: Gram-positive cocci or Gram-negative rods, depending on the organism (e.g., Pseudomonas aeruginosa)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Corneal ulcers with hypopyon and satellite infiltrates are routinely photographed on slit lamp and are visually distinct from fungal and viral keratitis.

Ophthalmology.name: Fungal Keratitis
clinical_manifestations: Dry, raised, gray-white stromal infiltrate with feathery or fluffy irregular margins
Satellite lesions adjacent to the main infiltrate
Endothelial plaque: grayish plaque on the posterior corneal surface
Hypopyon in the anterior chamber
Deep stromal ulcer with descemetocele in advanced disease
pathology_manifestations: Corneal scraping/KOH or calcofluor white stain: Septate or pauci-septate hyphae
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Dry, feathery stromal ulcers with endothelial plaques are visually distinctive and serve as standard slit-lamp comparison images against bacterial keratitis.

Ophthalmology.name: Allergic Conjunctivitis (Including Giant Papillary Conjunctivitis)
clinical_manifestations: Diffuse bilateral conjunctival hyperemia with chemosis (conjunctival swelling)
Enlarged papillae on the tarsal conjunctiva, visible after upper-lid eversion (giant papillae in GPC)
Stringy white mucus strands in the inferior fornix
Periocular eyelid edema and erythema, especially of the upper lids
pathology_manifestations: Conjunctival scraping/Giemsa stain: Increased eosinophils and mast cells
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Chemosis, giant tarsal papillae and mucoid discharge create characteristic external eye photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Vernal Keratoconjunctivitis
clinical_manifestations: Large, flat-topped cobblestone papillae on the upper tarsal conjunctiva, some with white gelatinous tops
Trantas dots: white-yellow, gelatinous limbal nodules
Shield ulcer: oval epithelial and stromal ulcer in the upper central cornea
Superficial punctate keratopathy highlighted with fluorescein
Ropy, stringy mucous discharge in the conjunctival fornices
pathology_manifestations: Conjunctival scraping/Giemsa stain: Eosinophils and eosinophilic granules
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Giant tarsal papillae, Trantas dots and shield ulcers are distinctive eversion and slit-lamp photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Ophthalmia Neonatorum
clinical_manifestations: Copious yellow-green purulent discharge from the eyes of a newborn
Marked conjunctival hyperemia with chemosis and eyelid swelling
Pseudomembrane on the tarsal or palpebral conjunctiva in severe gonococcal disease
Corneal infiltrate or ulceration in severe cases
Marked eyelid swelling that keeps the lids closed
pathology_manifestations: Conjunctival smear/Gram stain: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci within neutrophils (gonococcal)
Conjunctival scraping/Giemsa stain: Basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in epithelial cells (chlamydial)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Florid purulent neonatal conjunctivitis with lid edema is a highly recognizable, time-critical external eye photograph class.

Ophthalmology.name: Blepharitis
clinical_manifestations: Collarettes: cylindrical cuffs of scale encircling the base of the eyelashes
Erythematous, telangiectatic eyelid margins
Crusting and scale at the lash bases, with lash loss (madarosis) in chronic cases
Plugged or inspissated meibomian gland orifices with expressible secretion
Ulceration along the lid margin with misdirected lashes (trichiasis) in severe cases
pathology_manifestations: Eyelash epilation/microscopy: Demodex mites within lash follicles and cylindrical dandruff at lash bases
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Collarettes at the lash base and telangiectatic lid margins are well-recognized slit-lamp and external eye findings with distinctive photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Chalazion and Hordeolum
clinical_manifestations: Firm, round, well-circumscribed eyelid nodule within the tarsal plate (chalazion)
Red, granulomatous nodule on the palpebral conjunctiva after eversion (chalazion)
Yellow-tipped pustule at the lash base (external hordeolum)
Localized eyelid redness and swelling around an acute lid lesion
pathology_manifestations: Chalazion specimen/H&E: Lipogranulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells around lipid-filled meibomian acini
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Firm tarsal nodules, yellow-tipped lash pustules and red granulomatous conjunctival nodules are classic eyelid photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Dacryocystitis and Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction
clinical_manifestations: Erythematous, swollen mass at the medial canthus over the lacrimal sac
Mucopurulent discharge expressed from the puncta on pressure over the sac
Medial lower-lid and canthal cellulitis with eyelid edema in acute infection
Fluctuant, pointing abscess at the medial canthus in severe cases
Crusting at the lower lid margin and inner canthus
radiological_manifestations: CT orbit/nasolacrimal imaging: Dilated lacrimal sac with obstruction at the nasolacrimal duct
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Medial canthal swelling and regurgitant discharge on sac pressure are recognizable external photographs, with imaging showing the duct level.

Ophthalmology.name: Canaliculitis
clinical_manifestations: Swollen, inflamed lower punctum with mucopurulent discharge
Yellow-white concretions expressed from the lacrimal canaliculus
Crusting at the medial canthus and lower lid margin
Mild conjunctival injection near the lower punctum
pathology_manifestations: Canalicular concretion/Gram stain: Gram-positive, branching filamentous bacilli (Actinomyces)
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Yellow-white concretions expressed from the lower canaliculus are a specific external eye finding with distinctive photographs.

Ophthalmology.name: Scleritis and Episcleritis
clinical_manifestations: Episcleritis: sectoral salmon-pink episcleral injection, diffuse or nodular
Scleritis: deep violaceous or dusky-red scleral injection that does not move freely with the conjunctiva
Avascular, whitish scleral patches indicating necrosis in necrotizing scleritis
Scleral thinning with bluish-gray underlying uveal pigment visible
radiological_manifestations: B-scan ultrasound: Scleral thickening with fluid in Tenon space (T-sign) in posterior scleritis
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Salmon-pink episcleritis versus violaceous scleritis and avascular scleral necrosis are the key external eye photographic distinctions.

Ophthalmology.name: Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment
clinical_manifestations: Elevated, gray, undulating retina forming a visible detached sheet over the fundus
Horseshoe-shaped retinal tear visible at the margin of the detachment
Retinal folds and corrugations within the detached segment
Loss of the foveal reflex in macula-off detachments
Pigment cells in the vitreous ('tobacco dust') overlying the tear
radiological_manifestations: Ocular B-scan ultrasound: Hyperechoic, mobile retinal membrane separated from the globe wall, often in a V-shape
OCT macula: Subretinal fluid with retinal elevation
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Gray elevated retina with horseshoe tears and macula-off status are standard fundus image categories in retinal teaching.

Ophthalmology.name: Macular Hole
clinical_manifestations: Fundus photograph: Round, sharply demarcated full-thickness foveal defect, often with a yellow operculum sitting within or above the hole
Fundus photograph: Early stage shows a yellowish foveal spot with loss of the normal foveal reflex (pseudohole)
Fundus photograph: Gray-yellow crystalline or cuffed rim of subretinal fluid surrounding the hole in advanced stages
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy: Operculum visible as a floating yellow fragment above the foveal break
radiological_manifestations: Optical coherence tomography: Full-thickness break in the foveal neurosensory retina extending from the internal limiting membrane to the retinal pigment epithelium
Optical coherence tomography: Loss of the foveal pit with a foveal cyst or small cavity in early stages
Optical coherence tomography: Hyperreflective operculum fragment lying over the hole, with a surrounding cuff of subretinal fluid
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The full-thickness foveal defect and yellow operculum are visible on fundus and slit-lamp images, and OCT shows the characteristic cross-sectional break, so both image types are routinely used.

Ophthalmology.name: Epiretinal Membrane
clinical_manifestations: Fundus photograph: Translucent, cellophane-like sheen over the macula with a crinkled, wrinkled surface (macular pucker)
Fundus photograph: Retinal vessels appear tortuous and radially displaced toward the fovea in advanced disease
Fundus photograph: Central macular thickening with loss of the foveal reflex in advanced disease
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy: Wrinkled, pleated inner retinal surface seen with a contact lens
radiological_manifestations: Optical coherence tomography: Hyperreflective band of membrane on the inner retinal surface, with a corrugated or wrinkled inner limiting membrane
Optical coherence tomography: Thickened, lamellated inner retina with loss of the normal foveal pit in advanced disease
Optical coherence tomography: Tractional displacement or elevation of the foveal contour caused by membrane contraction
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology/H&E: Fibrocellular membrane of glial cells, myofibroblasts and collagen peeled from the internal limiting membrane at vitrectomy
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: The translucent, wrinkled macular surface is visible on fundus photographs, and the membrane is a discrete hyperreflective layer on OCT, both routinely imaged.

Ophthalmology.name: Macular Telangiectasia Type 2
clinical_manifestations: Fundus photograph: Subtle, bilateral, temporal parafoveal dilation of capillaries with a faint, grayish-green, crystalline deposit
Fundus photograph: Gray-green translucency or loss of macular transparency in the temporal parafoveal retina
Fundus photograph: Right-angle retinal venules and dilated, telangiectatic capillaries in the juxtafoveal region
Fundus photograph: Foveal atrophy with a flattened or absent foveal reflex in advanced disease
radiological_manifestations: Fluorescein angiography: Telangiectatic capillary dilation in the temporal parafoveal area with late leakage and staining
Optical coherence tomography: Hyporeflective intraretinal cavities in the temporal parafoveal retina with loss of the ellipsoid zone
Fundus autofluorescence: Hypo-autofluorescence of the temporal parafoveal zone reflecting loss of macular pigment and photoreceptors in advanced disease
Ophthalmology.inclusion_rationale: Subtle temporal parafoveal telangiectasia and crystalline deposits are visible on fundus photographs, and multimodal imaging (angiography, OCT, autofluorescence) is the main way the disease is documented.

Ophthalmology.name: Optic Disc Drusen
synonyms: hyaline bodies of the optic disc
clinical_manifestations: Fundus photograph: Elevated, lumpy, refractile yellow-white disc margins with a knobby, mulberry-like contour
Fundus photograph: Blurred, indistinct disc margins with a bumpy, nodular surface, often bilateral
Fundus photograph: Glistening, calcified-appearing bodies visible on the disc surface
Fundus photograph: Peripapillary hemorrhages near the disc margin in some eyes
