Severe sensory loss and intrinsic muscle wasting in median and ulnar nerve distributions
radiological_manifestations: Forearm / Wrist Radiographs: Malunited supracondylar humerus fracture or forearm shaft fracture, marked periarticular osteopenia, and joint flexion deformities
Forearm MRI: Extensive atrophy and low T1/T2 fibrofatty replacement of deep flexor compartment muscles (flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus, pronator teres) with nerve entrapment
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Pathology: Ellipsoid-shaped zone of dense ischemic muscular necrosis and dense cicatrix fibrosis replacing the deep forearm flexor muscle bellies; viable muscle fibers completely substituted by dense acellular collagenous scar tissue with perineural fibrotic constriction of median and ulnar nerves
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Classic orthopedic post-ischemic catastrophe defined by the iconic claw-like flexor contracture deformity and Volkmann sign following missed compartment syndrome.

Orthopedics.name: Campomelic Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic pretibial skin dimple over the apex of each bowed tibia
Tibial and femoral bowing with clubfeet
Flat facies, micrognathia, and XY sex reversal in most XY patients
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: anteriorly bowed long bones, hypoplastic scapulae, absent ossification of the lower thoracic pedicles, and trident acetabula
pathology_manifestations: SOX9 mutation; lethal perinatal skeletal dysplasia with campomelic (bent-bone) habitus
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Pretibial dimple plus bowed-limb phenotype is a named pathognomonic pairing.

Orthopedics.name: Larsen Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Multiple large-joint dislocations: bilateral knees, hips, and elbows at birth
Spatula (square-ended) thumbs and cylindrical fingers
Flat facies with prominent forehead and depressed nasal bridge
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: multiple joint dislocations plus the accessory calcaneal ossification center - the named radiographic sign
pathology_manifestations: FLNB filamin-B mutation; dislocation-predominant dysplasia
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Spatula thumbs plus multiple dislocations plus accessory calcaneal center is a classic composite.

Orthopedics.name: Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia Congenita
clinical_manifestations: Severe short-trunk dwarfism with barrel chest
Myopia and retinal detachment risk
Flat midface and short neck
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: pear-shaped or oval vertebral bodies, absent/minimal epiphyseal ossification, and odontoid hypoplasia
pathology_manifestations: COL2A1 type-II collagen mutation; completes the Stickler/Kniest COL2A1 cluster
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Pear-shaped vertebrae plus short-trunk dwarfism completes the covered Stickler COL2A1 family.

Orthopedics.name: Kniest Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Enlarged 'knobbly' joints with restricted motion
Flat facies with depressed nasal bridge and prominent eyes
Severe myopia with retinal detachment and hearing loss
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: dumbbell-shaped long bones, coronal vertebral clefts, and platyspondyly
pathology_manifestations: COL2A1 mutation; cartilage histology: 'Swiss-cheese' vacuolar appearance - pathognomonic
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Dumbbell bones plus Swiss-cheese cartilage histology is a dual signature.

Orthopedics.name: Pseudoachondroplasia
clinical_manifestations: Rhizomelic short stature with normal facies and skull - the diagnostic contrast to achondroplasia
Windswept knees (valgus one side, varus the other) and waddling gait
Ligamentous laxity and early osteoarthritis
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: anterior vertebral beaking, small irregular epiphyses, and metaphyseal flaring with normal skull
pathology_manifestations: COMP mutation; retention of mutant cartilage oligomeric matrix protein in chondrocyte rER (giant lamellar inclusions)
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Normal-facies rhizomelia plus beaked vertebrae - the classic achondroplasia contrast.

Orthopedics.name: Multiple Epiphyseal Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Stubby fingers and toes
Joint pain and early osteoarthritis of hips and knees
Mild short stature developing in childhood
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: delayed, small, irregular epiphyses at multiple sites; double-layered patella in the recessive form - near-pathognomonic sign
pathology_manifestations: COMP, MATN3, COL9A1-3, or recessive SLC26A2 mutations
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Double-layered patella plus stubby digits plus delayed epiphyses is a classic dysplasia.

Orthopedics.name: Cartilage-Hair Hypoplasia (McKusick)
clinical_manifestations: Fine, sparse, silky hair - the signature feature
Short-limbed dwarfism with bowed legs
Immunodeficiency and Hirschsprung/neutropenia associations
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: scalloped, sclerotic metaphyses with widened growth plates
pathology_manifestations: RMRP RNA mutation; defective chondrocyte proliferation; Amish and Finnish founder populations
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Fine hair plus metaphyseal scalloping is a classic composite.

Orthopedics.name: Trichorhinophalangeal Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Sparse, slow-growing scalp hair with high forehead
Bulbous pear-shaped nose with long philtrum
Short fingers and toes with deformity
radiological_manifestations: Hand radiographs: cone-shaped epiphyses of the phalanges - the named pathognomonic sign
pathology_manifestations: TRPS1 mutation (TRPS1); TRPS2 is a contiguous-gene deletion including EXT1 adding exostoses
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Pear nose plus cone-shaped epiphyses - a classic named sign.

Orthopedics.name: Hypophosphatasia
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic premature loss of deciduous teeth with intact roots
Skin-covered 'bone spurs' (Bowdler spurs) palpable on the shins
Craniosynostosis and bowed limbs in severe infantile form
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal radiographs: Bowdler spurs (fibular and ulnar spikes), craniosynostosis, and rickets-like metaphyseal defects
pathology_manifestations: ALPL loss-of-function; low alkaline phosphatase with elevated pyridoxal-5-phosphate
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Intact-root tooth loss plus Bowdler spurs is pathognomonic; proposed by two audits.

Orthopedics.name: Metatropic Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Progressive kyphoscoliosis that converts a long-trunk to a short-trunk infant
Pathognomonic coccygeal tail - a tail-like sacral appendage
Narrow chest with joint contractures
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: severe wafer platyspondyly, dumbbell metaphyses, and halberd-shaped ilia
pathology_manifestations: COL2A1 and TRPV4 mutations; changing ('metatropic') body proportions with age
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: The coccygeal tail appendage is a pathognomonic photograph.

Orthopedics.name: Spondylothoracic Dysostosis (Jarcho-Levin)
clinical_manifestations: Short-trunk dwarfism with a fan-shaped, crab-like thorax
Protuberant abdomen and restrictive lung disease
Cervical instability risk
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: 'fan-like' or 'crab' rib array with ribs radiating from a fused posterior origin - the named signature
pathology_manifestations: MESP2, DLL3, HES7 and other segmentation-gene mutations; severe vertebral/rib malformation
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Fan-like crab rib array is a named pathognomonic radiographic signature.

Orthopedics.name: Sclerosteosis
clinical_manifestations: Gigantism with massive progressive craniofacial hyperostosis
Syndactyly of the index and middle fingers - the distinguishing feature
Deafness, facial nerve palsy, and elevated intracranial pressure
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: massive diffuse skull and mandibular hyperostosis with sclerotic long bones and absent medullary cavities
pathology_manifestations: SOST (sclerostin) loss-of-function; dysregulated bone formation
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Gigantism plus syndactyly distinguishes it from covered osteopetrosis/van Buchem.

Orthopedics.name: Hajdu-Cheney Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Band-like acroosteolysis causing progressive shortening of fingers and toes
Premature tooth loss and periodontal disease
Coarse facies with low-set ears and joint laxity
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: transverse band-like distal phalangeal osteolysis, bathrocephaly, and wormian bones - a characteristic combination
pathology_manifestations: NOTCH2 activating mutation (truncating PEST domain); osteoclast-driven bone loss
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Band acroosteolysis plus wormian bones is a distinct osteolytic dysplasia.

Orthopedics.name: Freeman-Sheldon Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: 'Whistling face': microstomia with pursed lips, deep-set eyes, and H-shaped chin dimple
Windmill-blade hand: ulnar-deviation camptodactyly with thumb adduction
Clubfeet and scoliosis
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey for camptodactyly and foot deformity
pathology_manifestations: MYH3 mutation; most photogenic of the distal arthrogryposes
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Whistling face plus windmill-blade hand is the most photographed distal arthrogryposis.

Orthopedics.name: Progressive Osseous Heteroplasia
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous ossification plates beginning in infancy and deepening to subcutaneous and muscle planes
No congenital great-toe malformation - the contrast to covered FOP
Asymmetric heterotopic bone limiting joint motion
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey/CT: extensive dermal and subcutaneous ossification network progressing to deep tissues
pathology_manifestations: Inactivating GNAS mutation on the paternal allele; extra-skeletal ossification without FOP's malformation
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Dermal-onset ossification without the FOP great-toe defect is a distinct entity.

Orthopedics.name: Hypochondroplasia
clinical_manifestations: Mild rhizomelic short stature with stocky build
Normal-to-mild facial features (less marked than achondroplasia)
Lumbar lordosis and bowed legs
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: mild caudal interpediculate narrowing, short long bones, and squared ilia with small sciatic notches
pathology_manifestations: FGFR3 N540K mutation; milder allelic counterpart to achondroplasia and thanatophoric dysplasia
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Same FGFR3 family as covered achondroplasia but a distinct milder named entity.

Orthopedics.name: Hallux Valgus
clinical_manifestations: Lateral deviation of the great toe toward the second toe at the first metatarsophalangeal joint
Prominent bony medial eminence over the first metatarsal head, often with overlying callus or bursa
Overlapping or underlapping of the second toe by the deviated great toe
Splayed forefoot with a widened first web space between the great and second toes
Redness and thickening of the skin over the medial bunion
radiological_manifestations: Weight-bearing dorsoplantar radiograph: Hallux valgus angle above about 15 degrees
Weight-bearing dorsoplantar radiograph: First-second intermetatarsal angle above about 9 degrees
Dorsoplantar radiograph: Lateral displacement of the sesamoids beneath the first metatarsal head
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: The deviated great toe and medial bony bump are visually obvious on foot photographs and weight-bearing radiographs.

Orthopedics.name: Ganglion Cyst
clinical_manifestations: Smooth, round or lobulated cystic swelling over the dorsal wrist, typically at the scapholunate or radiocarpal joint
Firm to fluctuant, tense cyst with a translucent appearance that transilluminates
Overlying skin normal, without erythema, ulceration or sinus formation
Volar wrist swelling near the radial artery or flexor tendons
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: Anechoic or hypoechoic, thin-walled, lobulated cyst contiguous with the joint or tendon sheath
MRI: Well-defined T2-hyperintense cyst with a thin wall and no solid component
pathology_manifestations: Excised cyst wall (H&E): Fibrous wall lined by flattened or absent synovium with myxoid, mucinous degeneration of collagen
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Dorsal wrist swellings are recognizable on clinical photographs and on ultrasound images.

Orthopedics.name: Pyogenic Flexor Tenosynovitis
clinical_manifestations: Finger held in mild flexion at rest (Kanavel posture)
Fusiform, diffusely swollen finger (sausage digit) with tense, red skin
Erythema and swelling tracking along the volar flexor sheath into the palm
Puncture wound, pustule or abscess on the volar pad or flexor surface of the finger
Lymphangitic red streaks extending up the forearm in advanced infection
radiological_manifestations: Plain radiograph: Soft tissue swelling of the finger, with a retained radiopaque foreign body if present
MRI: Distended flexor tendon sheath with fluid and enhancing synovial lining on post-contrast images
pathology_manifestations: Sheath pus (Gram stain): Neutrophils with Gram-positive cocci in clusters, typically Staphylococcus aureus
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: Kanavel signs such as the flexed finger, fusiform swelling and volar tracking swelling are visible on clinical photographs and are characteristic.

Orthopedics.name: Adult Acquired Flatfoot Deformity (Posterior Tibial Tendon Dysfunction)
clinical_manifestations: Collapsed medial longitudinal arch with midfoot flattening on standing
Hindfoot valgus with the heel tilted outward
Too-many-toes sign: more toes visible from behind than normal because of forefoot abduction
Prominent medial midfoot bulge over the talonavicular region
radiological_manifestations: Weight-bearing AP radiograph: Talonavicular uncoverage with lateral displacement of the navicular on the talar head
Weight-bearing lateral radiograph: Increased talar-first metatarsal (Meary) angle and reduced calcaneal pitch
MRI: Posterior tibial tendon tenosynovitis with tendon degeneration or tear
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: The collapsed arch, hindfoot valgus and too-many-toes sign are visible on standing photographs, and weight-bearing radiographs and MRI document the deformity.

Orthopedics.name: High-Pressure Injection Injury of the Hand
clinical_manifestations: Pinhole puncture wound on the palm or finger with minimal external bleeding, a deceptively small entry site
Swelling of the hand and digit with pallor or bruising of the overlying skin
Finger held in slight flexion with tense swelling of the digit
Discolouration of the skin at the injection site from the injected material
Skin necrosis or ulceration over the injection site in established injuries
radiological_manifestations: Plain radiograph: Radiopaque injected material (for example metal-containing paint or grease) along the flexor tendon sheath
Ultrasound: Fluid or material collection along the flexor tendon sheath and palmar space
Orthopedics.inclusion_rationale: The deceptively small entry wound and digit swelling are visible on hand photographs, and radiographs can show the injected radiopaque material.

Pediatrics.name: Achondroplasia
clinical_manifestations: Disproportionate short stature with marked rhizomelic shortening of the limbs (humeri and femora shorter than forearms and shins)
Macrocephaly with frontal bossing, depressed nasal bridge (saddle nose), and midface hypoplasia
'Trident hand': short, broad fingers with an inability to approximate the third and fourth digits in extension
Exaggerated lumbar lordosis with prominent protruding buttocks and potbelly
Genu varum (bowing of legs) upon weight-bearing
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal Radiography of Spine: Pathognomonic progressive caudal narrowing of the interpedicular distances in the lumbar spine (L1 to L5); severe scalloping of posterior vertebral bodies; spinal canal stenosis
Pelvis Radiography: Pathognomonic square-shaped iliac wings with flat acetabular roofs ('tombstone ilia'), narrow sacro-sciatic notches, and 'champagne-glass' pelvic inlet
Extremity Radiography: Short, thick tubular bones with flared, cupped metaphyses; chevron deformity of distal femoral metaphysis
pathology_manifestations: Growth plate histology: Quantitative failure of endochondral ossification; disorganized, shortened, hypocellular chondrocyte columns in the hypertrophic and proliferative zones; normal periosteal intramembranous ossification leading to thick, broad bone collars
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Textbook dysmorphic syndrome with rhizomelic shortening, frontal bossing, and trident hands paired with pathognomonic narrowing of lumbar interpedicular distances and 'tombstone' pelvis on X-ray.

Pediatrics.name: Apert Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Severe turribrachycephaly ('tower skull') with flattened occiput, high bulging forehead, and wide gaping midline calvarial defect from glabella to posterior fontanelle
Severe ocular proptosis with downslanting palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, strabismus, and severe midface retrusion with flattened nasal bridge

Pathognomonic symmetric, complex bony and cutaneous syndactyly of hands ('mitten hands' / rosebud hands) and feet ('sock feet'), involving complete fusion of digits 2, 3, and 4 within a single cutaneous envelope and common nail bed (synonychia)
High-arched Byzantine-pattern palate with pseudocleft or frank cleft palate, severe maxillary dental crowding with delayed tooth eruption, and severe confluent nodulocystic acne vulgaris
radiological_manifestations: Craniofacial 3D CT: Bicoronal synostosis with a large, gaping, persistent midline calvarial defect; severe hypoplasia of maxilla, flat orbital roofs, and diminished orbital volume; 'beaten-copper' inner table markings

Plain Radiographs of Hands and Feet: Complex osseous syndactyly with side-to-side synostosis of the distal phalanges of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th digits ('mitten hand'); progressive synostosis of metacarpals, carpal bones, and tarsal bones; delta phalanx of the thumb causing radial deviation
Cervical Spine Radiographs: Progressive fusion of cervical vertebrae (C5-C6 in up to 70% of cases)
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology: Premature ossification of calvarial sutures and failure of interdigital blastemal apoptosis; skin biopsy of severe acne lesions shows diffuse sebaceous gland hypertrophy

Molecular Genetics: Gain-of-function heterozygous missense mutations in FGFR2 on chromosome 10q26, almost exclusively p.Ser252Trp (more severe craniofacial dysostosis) or p.Pro253Arg (more severe syndactyly)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Immediate photographic bedside diagnosis from 'mitten hands' / 'sock feet' syndactyly paired with bicoronal tower skull and 3D CT craniofacial synostosis.

Pediatrics.name: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad: 1) Severe macroglossia (large, scalloped protruding tongue); 2) Abdominal wall defects (omphalocele, large umbilical hernia, or diastasis recti); 3) Somatic gigantism / overgrowth at birth (macrosomia)
Lateralized overgrowth (hemihyperplasia) involving single limbs, half of the body, or face
Pathognomonic ear anomalies: linear indentation creases on the anterior earlobe and punctate circular pits on the posterior rim of the helix
Neonatal hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia secondary to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia; prominent facial capillary malformation (nevus flammeus) on glabella and forehead
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound and MRI: Nephromegaly (bilateral renomegaly with enlargement of renal pyramids and medullary dysplasia), hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and adrenomegaly

Surveillance Oncologic Imaging (Ultrasound Q3 months until age 8): Detection of embryonal malignancies, predominantly Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma - large, solid, heterogeneous intrarenal mass with pseudocapsule) and hepatoblastoma (well-circumscribed hepatic mass with microcalcifications)
Skeletal Scanograms: Quantitative measurement of asymmetric long bone overgrowth in patients with hemihyperplasia
pathology_manifestations: Pancreatic and Adrenal Pathology: Marked hyperplasia and hypertrophy of pancreatic islets of Langerhans; pathognomonic adrenal cytomegaly (enlarged cortical cells with massive, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic polyploid nuclei); persistent renal blastema / nephrogenic rests (precursors to Wilms tumor)

Molecular Genetics: Epigenetic and genomic alterations at chromosome 11p15.5 involving imprinted growth regulatory domains (IC2/KCNQ1OT1 hypomethylation in 50%, IC1/H19 hypermethylation in 5-10%, paternal uniparental disomy [UPD] in 20%, CDKN1C maternal mutations in 5%)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Landmark overgrowth condition featuring pathognomonic ear creases/pits, macroglossia, omphalocele, organomegaly on abdominal US, and adrenal cytomegaly histology.

Pediatrics.name: CHARGE Syndrome
synonyms: coloboma, heart defect, atresia choanae, retarded growth and development, genital hypoplasia, ear anomalies
clinical_manifestations: Cardinal diagnostic acronym features: C - Coloboma of the eye (typically bilateral chorioretinal and iris coloboma, 'keyhole pupil', microphthalmia); H - Heart defects in ~75-85% (tetralogy of Fallot, patent ductus arteriosus, VSD, AVSD, aberrant subclavian artery); A - Atresia of the choanae (unilateral or bilateral membranous and/or bony posterior choanal atresia causing neonatal respiratory distress relieved by crying); R - Retardation of growth and global development (postnatal growth deficiency, delayed motor milestones); G - Genital hypoplasia / anomalies (micropenis and cryptorchidism in males, hypoplastic labia in females, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism); E - Ear abnormalities and sensorineural/conductive deafness: Pathognomonic short, wide, cupped/floppy, low-set ears with hypoplastic lobes, deficient antihelix, and triangular concha
Cranial nerve dysfunction (especially CN VII, IX, X): Asymmetric lower motor neuron facial palsy (characteristic asymmetric crying facies) and severe pharyngeal/esophageal dysmotility with aspiration
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Temporal Bone CT: Pathognomonic complete aplasia or severe hypoplasia of the semicircular canals (particularly the lateral/horizontal and superior semicircular canals) with vestibulo-cochlear dysplasia (Mondini malformation) and hypoplasia or absence of the oval window and cochlear nerve canal; pathognomonic radiological marker present in >95% of CHD7 mutation-positive patients
Craniofacial / Paranasal Sinus CT: Demonstrates complete bony and/or membranous occlusion of the posterior choanae with medial bowing of the posterolateral maxillary wall and thickening of the vomer

Echocardiography: Conotruncal and aortic arch anomalies, notably interrupted aortic arch, tetralogy of Fallot, vascular rings (double aortic arch or right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery), and ventricular septal defects

Brain and Olfactory MRI: Bilateral aplasia or severe hypoplasia of the olfactory bulbs and olfactory sulci (arhinencephaly) explaining universal anosmia / hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (Kallmann-like phenotype)
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics / Epigenetics: Heterozygous de novo loss-of-function mutations (nonsense, frameshift, or splice-site) or deletions in the CHD7 gene on chromosome 8q12.2 in >90% of classic cases, encoding Chromodomain Helicase DNA-Binding Protein 7, an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler critical for neural crest cell migration, pharyngeal arch patterning, and inner ear organogenesis
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Premier multisystem pediatric genetic syndrome pairing classic bedside external ear dysmorphology, facial nerve palsy, and coloboma with pathognomonic temporal bone CT semicircular canal aplasia and choanal atresia, underpinned by CHD7 chromatin remodeling pathology.

Pediatrics.name: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia
clinical_manifestations: Acute severe respiratory distress immediately after delivery: tachypnea, grunting, prominent intercostal/subcostal retractions, nasal flaring, and central cyanosis refractory to bag-mask ventilation and supplemental oxygen

Pathognomonic asymmetric torso contour: markedly scaphoid (sunken, boat-shaped) abdomen due to displacement of abdominal viscera into the thoracic cavity, accompanied by an overinflated barrel-shaped chest

Auscultation abnormalities: markedly diminished or completely absent breath sounds over the affected hemithorax (85-90% left-sided Bochdalek defect) with audible bowel sounds (peristaltic gurgling) heard high in the thoracic cavity

Contralateral mediastinal and cardiac shift: heart sounds displaced to the contralateral hemithorax (dextroposition of the heart sounds to the right hemithorax in typical left-sided hernias) with shifted apical impulse

Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the neonate (PPHN): labile pre-ductal and post-ductal oxygen saturation gradients (delta SpO2 >10% between right upper extremity and lower extremities), single loud second heart sound (P2), right ventricular heave, and cardiogenic shock

Associated syndromic anomalies in 10-15% of cases: craniofacial dysmorphism, neural tube defects, or congenital heart disease (tetralogy of Fallot, coarctation of aorta, ventricular septal defect) seen in Fryns syndrome, Cornelia de Lange syndrome, or Pallister-Killian syndrome
radiological_manifestations: Neonatal Plain Chest and Abdominal Radiograph (Babygram): Pathognomonic appearance of multiple air-filled, cystic-appearing, radiolucent loops of bowel within the affected hemithorax (predominantly left) with complete loss of the distinct diaphragmatic contour; dramatic mediastinal, tracheal, and cardiac shift to the contralateral side; severe compressive hypoplasia of the ipsilateral and contralateral lungs; conspicuous paucity or total absence of intestinal gas within the scaphoid abdomen; radiopaque nasogastric tube tip arresting or curling within an intrathoracic stomach pouch

Antenatal Fetal Ultrasound: Demonstration of fluid-filled stomach bubble and peristalsing bowel loops at the level of the four-chamber cardiac view; mediastinal shift away from the lesion; calculation of the lung-to-head ratio (LHR) and observed-to-expected LHR (o/e LHR <25% predicts severe pulmonary hypoplasia and mortality); visualization of intrathoracic herniation of the left liver lobe ('liver-up' status signifying high surgical risk)

Fetal Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): Exquisite anatomical delineation without ionizing radiation; precise volumetric calculation of total fetal lung volume (TFLV) and percentage predicted lung volume (PPLV); accurate definition of liver, bowel, and spleen displacement relative to the diaphragm and thoracic cage

Neonatal Echocardiography: Flattening or leftward systolic bowing of the interventricular septum, severe tricuspid regurgitation jet velocity demonstrating suprasystemic pulmonary arterial pressures, right ventricular dilation/hypertrophy, and right-to-left or bidirectional shunting across the patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and patent foramen ovale (PFO)
pathology_manifestations: Macroscopic / Surgical Pathology: Posterolateral diaphragmatic muscular defect (foramen of Bochdalek, 85-90% left-sided, 10% right-sided; anterior retrosternal foramen of Morgagni in 2-5%) resulting from failure of closure of the embryonic pleuroperitoneal membranes with the septum transversum and esophageal mesentery at 8-10 weeks gestation; absence of a true peritoneal hernia sac in >80% of Bochdalek defects, resulting in direct herniation of stomach, jejunum, ileum, colon, spleen, and left liver lobe into the pleural space

Histopathology of Pulmonary Hypoplasia: Bilateral arrest of pulmonary acinar and vascular branching morphogenesis in the pseudoglandular and canalicular developmental stages (double-hit hypothesis combining primary genetic dysgenesis with mechanical compressive hypoplasia); profound reduction in total bronchial branch generations, alveolar surface area, and alveolar numbers; severe muscularization of intra-acinar precapillary arterioles with marked medial and adventitial smooth muscle hyperplasia extending into non-muscularized peripheral alveolar walls; diminished capillary bed density explaining fixed pulmonary vascular resistance

Embryological & Molecular Genetics: Disruption of the retinoid signaling pathway; mutations or copy number variants involving ZFPM2 (FOG2 on 8q23.1), GATA4 (8p23.1), STRA6, WT1, and 15q26 microdeletions; tetrasomy 12p (Pallister-Killian mosaic syndrome) and aneuploidies (trisomy 18)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic neonatal surgical emergency featuring the unmistakable bedside physical triad of scaphoid abdomen, barrel chest, and displaced heart sounds paired with the definitive babygram radiograph showing thoracic bowel loops and mediastinal shift.

Pediatrics.name: Cornelia de Lange Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic facial appearance: thick, highly arched, well-defined eyebrows that are confluent across the midline (synophrys), exceptionally long and curly eyelashes, and low anterior and posterior hairlines
Craniofacial anomalies: microbrachycephaly, depressed nasal bridge with short upturned nose and anteverted nares, long smooth flat philtrum, and thin down-turned upper lip vermilion ('carp mouth')

Upper limb reduction defects: varying from mild micromelia, severe oligodactyly (absent digits), to complete phocomelia (absent forearms with single digit projecting from elbow); pathognomonic proximally placed thumbs and fifth finger clinodactyly
Generalized hirsutism (hypertrichosis) prominent on forehead, ears, back, and arms; low-pitched, guttural, raspy cry in infancy; severe growth failure and developmental delay
radiological_manifestations: Upper Extremity Skeletal Radiographs: Severe longitudinal limb deficiency including hypoplasia or aplasia of radius and ulna, radio-ulnar synostosis, oligodactyly (absence of 2nd to 4th digits), hypoplastic first metacarpal with proximally placed thumb, and clinodactyly of 5th digit
Skull Radiographs and Brain MRI: Microbrachycephaly, thickened calvarium, delayed fontanelle closure, hypoplastic frontal lobes with simplified cortical gyration
Upper GI Fluoroscopy (Barium Swallow): High incidence of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with esophageal hiatus hernia and intestinal malrotation
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Pathology: Disruption of the multi-protein cohesin complex essential for sister chromatid cohesion and long-range transcriptional regulation; heterozygous mutations in NIPBL (50-60% of cases), SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21, or HDAC8
Tissue Histology: Hypoplastic embryonic limb bud mesenchyme; deficient cutaneous epidermal-dermal junction development with hyperplastic hair follicles
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Immediate photographic bedside recognition from arched confluent synophrys, long eyelashes, carp mouth, and upper extremity limb reduction on radiographs.

Pediatrics.name: Crouzon Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cranial dysmorphism due to bicoronal craniosynostosis: brachycephaly (short, widened calvarium), scaphocephaly, or oxycephaly/turricephaly (tower skull) with prominent frontal bossing
Severe ocular proptosis/exophthalmos resulting from shallow bony orbits, scleral show, lagophthalmos with corneal exposure keratitis, hypertelorism, and divergent strabismus
Midface hypoplasia with maxillary retrusion, depressed infraorbital rims, high-arched palate, and characteristic 'parrot-beak' (psittaciform) beaked nose

Severe Class III malocclusion with mandibular pseudoprognathism, anterior open bite, and crowded maxillary dentition; EXTREMITIES ARE ENTIRELY NORMAL (distinguishing from Apert, Pfeiffer, and Carpenter syndromes)
Obstructive sleep apnea due to severe midfacial retrusion and nasopharyngeal narrowing; chronic papilledema with optic nerve atrophy from raised intracranial pressure
radiological_manifestations: 3D Craniofacial CT with Bone Windows: Premature synostosis of bilateral coronal sutures, sagittal, and lambdoid sutures; extremely shallow, foreshortened bony orbits with markedly reduced orbital volume; severe hypoplasia of the maxilla and pterygoid plates; pathognomonic 'beaten-copper' appearance (digital markings / lacunar skull) of the inner calvarial table reflecting chronic elevated intracranial pressure

Brain and Cervical MRI: High prevalence of Chiari I malformation (tonsillar herniation through the foramen magnum in up to 70%), progressive obstructive ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalus, and jugular foramen stenosis causing cerebral venous hypertension
Skull Radiographs: Foreshortened anterior-posterior cranial diameter, absent coronal suture radiolucency, basilar kyphosis, and diffuse calvarial gyral impressions
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology: Complete osseous obliteration of the fibrous intersutural mesenchyme with accelerated osteoblast differentiation, disorganized collagen bundles, and premature osteoid deposition along sutural margins

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous gain-of-function missense mutations in FGFR2 (fibroblast growth factor receptor 2) on chromosome 10q26, concentrated in the third immunoglobulin-like (IgIII) domain (e.g., p.Cys342Arg, p.Cys342Tyr)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Cardinal craniosynostosis dysmorphic syndrome displaying dramatic ocular proptosis, parrot-beak facies, beaten-copper calvarium on 3D CT, and Chiari I tonsillar descent without limb anomalies.

Pediatrics.name: Down Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cardinal craniofacial and ocular dysmorphic features: Upward-slanting (upslanting) palpebral fissures, prominent medial epicanthal folds, flat facial profile with depressed nasal bridge and hypoplastic midface, small dysplastic low-set ears with overfolded superior helices, Brushfield spots (ring of small white or grayish-yellow speckles on the iris circumference), relative macroglossia protruding through an open mouth, and redundant posterior nuchal skin fold in neonates

Musculoskeletal and extremity stigmata: Generalized severe neonatal hypotonia ('rag doll' floppiness) with hyperflexible, hypermobile joints; single transverse palmar crease (simian crease), clinodactyly of the fifth digit (incurved little finger with hypoplasia of middle phalanx); wide gap between the first and second toes ('sandal gap') with a prominent deep longitudinal plantar crease

Cardiovascular and visceral malformations: Congenital heart disease in ~50% of patients, classically Complete Atrioventricular Septal Defect (AVSD / endocardial cushion defect) or ventricular septal defect (VSD); congenital duodenal atresia or annular pancreas; Hirschsprung disease; congenital hypothyroidism; transient myeloproliferative disorder (TMD / TAM) in the neonatal period
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic Radiograph (Caffey's signs): Markedly flattened, flared iliac wings ('elephant-ear' ilia) with decreased acetabular angles (<15 degrees) and decreased iliac angles, producing a characteristic broad, squared pelvic configuration

Cervical Spine Radiographs (Flexion-Extension Views) & CT: Atlantoaxial instability (AAI) defined by an increased anterior atlantodental interval (ADI >4-5 mm in children) due to transverse odontoid ligament laxity; hypoplasia or os odontoideum of the dens with danger of spinal cord compression
Abdominal Radiograph: Classic pathognomonic 'double bubble' sign (gas-distended stomach and proximal duodenum with complete absence of distal intestinal air) diagnostic of congenital duodenal atresia
Hand Radiograph: Hypoplastic, dysplastic, wedge-shaped middle phalanx of the fifth finger producing clinodactyly; shortened metacarpals and phalanges

Echocardiography: Diagnostic visualization of Complete Atrioventricular Septal Defect (AVSD) displaying a common atrioventricular valve, ostium primum atrial septal defect, and inlet ventricular septal defect with left-to-right or bidirectional shunting
pathology_manifestations: Cytogenetics / Karyotype & Microarray: Free full Trisomy 21 in ~95% of cases (47,XX,+21 or 47,XY,+21 resulting from maternal meiotic non-disjunction, predominantly meiosis I); Robertsonian translocation in ~3-4% (e.g., der(14;21)(q10;q10) or der(21;21)); mosaicism (46,XX/47,XX,+21) in ~1-2%

Hematopathology / Peripheral Blood: Transient Abnormal Myelopoiesis (TAM) / Transient Myeloproliferative Disorder in neonates showing circulating blast cells with megakaryoblastic differentiation and pathognomonic somatic GATA1 exon 2 mutations; heightened lifetime risk of acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL) and B-ALL

Neuropathology: Universally present Alzheimer disease neuropathological hallmarks (diffuse and neuritic beta-amyloid senile plaques, neurofibrillary tau tangles, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy) by age 40, driven by gene dosage triplication of the amyloid precursor protein (APP) gene on chromosome 21
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: The world's most prevalent chromosomal disorder, presenting an essential photographic physical exam constellation (Brushfield spots, sandal gap, simian crease) alongside iconic radiology (pelvic iliac flaring, double bubble sign, atlantoaxial subluxation) and universal genetic triplication.

Pediatrics.name: Duodenal Atresia
clinical_manifestations: Early, persistent, recurrent bilious (dark green) vomiting developing within the first 24 to 48 hours of life in >80-85% of cases (due to post-ampullary obstruction distal to the ampulla of Vater; non-bilious emesis in 15% with rare pre-ampullary atresia)

Scaphoid lower abdomen with localized epigastric fullness: Epigastrium is visibly full, prominent, or mildly distended due to the dilated stomach and duodenal bulb, while the remainder of the abdomen is flat or scaphoid (absence of generalized lower abdominal distension, differentiating upper from lower gastrointestinal obstruction)

Early passage of meconium: Neonates may pass one or two small, pale-gray, mucus-like or meconium stools consisting of sloughed cells and mucus produced distal to the atresia, followed by complete obstipation

Strong association with Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome): Present in ~30-40% of all infants with duodenal atresia; physical exam reveals hypotonia, upslanting palpebral fissures, epicanthal folds, flat nasal bridge, single transverse palmar crease (simian crease), and sandal-gap toes

Associated VACTERL features: Vertebral anomalies, anal atresia, cardiac defects (atrioventricular septal defect / AV canal in Down syndrome), tracheoesophageal fistula, renal anomalies, and limb anomalies
radiological_manifestations: Plain Abdominal Radiograph (Babygram; Supine and Upright): Pathognomonic 'Double-Bubble' sign: two large, distinct, gas-filled or air-fluid cavities in the upper abdomen—the first bubble on the left represents the dilated, air-filled stomach, and the second bubble to the right of the midline represents the blind-ending, dilated duodenal bulb; complete absence of gas throughout the remainder of the small bowel, colon, and rectum ('gasless lower abdomen'); confirms complete duodenal atresia without requiring contrast studies

Antenatal Fetal Ultrasound: Hallmark prenatal triad: polyhydramnios (amniotic fluid index >24 cm or deepest vertical pocket >8 cm due to failure of fetal swallowing and resorption of amniotic fluid) paired with fluid-filled fetal 'double-bubble' (simultaneously dilated stomach and proximal duodenum in the fetal upper abdomen) in the third trimester

Upper Gastrointestinal (UGI) Contrast Series: Indicated only in incomplete duodenal stenosis or duodenal web ('windsock sign') to exclude malrotation with midgut volvulus; demonstrates contrast pooling in the dilated stomach and duodenal bulb with a rounded blind pouch or web with a central pinhole aperture ('windsock deformity')
pathology_manifestations: Pathological Anatomy / Embryology: Results from failure of recanalization of the solid duodenal cord during weeks 8-10 of embryonic development (Tandler's recanalization hypothesis); classified into three Gray and Skandalakis anatomical types:
- Type I (most common, ~90%): Intraluminal mucosal diaphragm/web with an intact external muscular wall and mesentery ('windsock web')
- Type II (~1%): Blind ends connected by a fibrous cord with an intact mesentery
- Type III (~10%): Complete separation of the two blind ends with a V-shaped mesenteric defect

Annular Pancreas Association: A ring of pancreatic tissue encircles the second part of the duodenum in ~20-30% of cases, arising from abnormal migration of the ventral pancreatic bud (treated surgically via diamond-shaped duodenoduodenostomy without dividing the pancreatic tissue to avoid fistula)

Histopathology of Resected Web / Atresia Margin: Mucosal membrane lined by normal duodenal epithelium with submucosal core; muscular layer may be absent in the web; mucosal congestion and submucosal edema in the proximal dilated pouch with muscular hypertrophy; distal duodenum is hypoplastic and narrow from disuse ('microduodenum')
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic neonatal surgical disorder marked by early bilious vomiting and flat lower abdomen in a neonate frequently presenting with Down syndrome stigmas, paired with the diagnostic 'double-bubble' sign on plain babygram and prenatal polyhydramnios.

Pediatrics.name: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Marked cutaneous hyperextensibility (skin can be stretched >1.5-3 cm on volar forearm or neck and snaps back immediately)
Severe tissue fragility: 'cigarette-paper' (papyraceous) atrophic scars over bony prominences (knees, shins, elbows)
Generalized joint hypermobility assessed by Beighton score (>=5-6/9)
Molluscoid pseudotumors (fleshy calcified nodules over pressure points) and subcutaneous spheroids
In Vascular EDS (vEDS): thin, translucent skin with visible superficial venous network, pinched facial features (thin nose, lobeless ears, sunken eyes), easy bruising
radiological_manifestations: CT Angiography / MRA (Vascular EDS): Spontaneous dissection, aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, or rupture of medium and large muscular arteries (celiac, mesenteric, renal, carotid, iliac); carotid-cavernous fistulae; intestinal rupture with pneumoperitoneum
Joint Radiographs / MRI: Recurrent joint subluxations, chronic joint dislocations (shoulder, patella, temporomandibular), early secondary osteoarthritis
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy / electron microscopy: Dermal collagen bundles are loose, disorganized, and fragmented; transmission electron microscopy shows abnormal, irregular, composite 'flower-like' collagen fibrils with variable diameters; reduced total collagen density
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: High-impact visual connective tissue disease featuring extreme skin hyperextensibility and papyraceous scars, matched with vascular CTA/MRA showing spontaneous arterial aneurysms and dissections.

Pediatrics.name: Esophageal Atresia with Tracheoesophageal Fistula
clinical_manifestations: Excessive oral secretions immediately after birth: Continuous, frothy, white bubbling and drooling of saliva from the neonate's mouth and nostrils ('the infant blows bubbles')
The classic 'Three C's' on the first attempted feed: Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis triggered by aspiration of milk or secretions into the airway

Inability to pass a standard 8 or 10 French radiopaque nasogastric (NG) or orogastric (OG) feeding catheter into the stomach, with the tube meeting firm resistance at approximately 10-12 cm from the alveolar ridge (coiling in the blind upper esophageal pouch)

Progressive respiratory distress and tachypnea exacerbated by chemical pneumonitis and gastric acid reflux through the fistula into the lungs; marked abdominal distension in the commonest Type C (distal fistula), where crying forces air through the fistula into the stomach and bowel; conversely, a scaphoid abdomen in pure esophageal atresia (Type A, gasless GI tract)

VACTERL Association Anomalies (present in >50% of infants): Vertebral segmentation anomalies, Anal atresia (imperforate anus), Cardiac malformations (ventricular septal defect, tetralogy of Fallot), Renal dysgenesis / vesicoureteral reflux, and Limb anomalies (radial ray dysplasia, absent radius, hypoplastic thumb)
radiological_manifestations: Plain Babygram Radiograph (Chest and Abdomen, AP and Lateral):
- Pathognomonic coiling and arrest of the radiopaque feeding tube in the dilated, air-filled upper esophageal pouch at the level of T2-T4 vertebrae
- Abdominal gas pattern distinguishes anatomical subtypes:

* Presence of gastrointestinal gas (air in stomach and intestines): Pathognomonic for Esophageal Atresia with Distal Tracheoesophageal Fistula (Gross Type C / Vogt Type IIIb; accounts for 85-90% of all cases)

* Completely gasless abdomen (complete absence of any stomach or bowel air): Pathognomonic for Isolated / Pure Esophageal Atresia (Gross Type A; ~7-8% of cases) or EA with proximal fistula only (Gross Type B)
* Massive gastric distension: Severe distal fistula with potential gastric perforation
- Right-sided aortic arch in 5% (critical surgical finding dictating a left thoracotomy approach instead of the standard right extrapleural thoracotomy)
- Pulmonary infiltrates, atelectasis, and consolidation (predominantly right upper lobe) from salivary aspiration or chemical pneumonitis

Fluoroscopic Pouchography: Gentle instillation of 0.5-1 mL of non-ionic water-soluble contrast (e.g., Isovue) into the upper pouch under fluoroscopy outlines the blind pouch (strictly avoiding barium and large volumes to prevent fatal pulmonary aspiration)
Antenatal Fetal Ultrasound: Polyhydramnios in combination with an absent or persistently small fetal stomach bubble
Echocardiography: Routine mandatory pre-operative imaging to rule out CHD and confirm the branching pattern and sidedness of the aortic arch
pathology_manifestations: Embryological & Anatomical Classification: Failure of the primitive foregut to properly partition into the anterior respiratory primordium (trachea) and posterior digestive tube (esophagus) by the tracheoesophageal septum during weeks 4-6 of embryonic gestation
Anatomical Subtypes (Gross / Vogt Classification):
- Type C (85-90%): Blind proximal esophageal pouch with a distal tracheoesophageal fistula entering the membranous posterior trachea 0.5-1 cm above the carina
- Type A (7-8%): Isolated pure esophageal atresia without fistula ('long-gap' atresia)
- Type E / 'H-type' (4%): Tracheoesophageal fistula without atresia (patent esophagus; presents later in infancy with chronic coughing during feeds and recurrent right upper lobe pneumonias)
- Type B (1%): Proximal fistula with distal blind pouch
- Type D (1%): Double fistula (both proximal and distal)

Histopathology of Atretic Segment & Pouch: Proximal pouch shows hypertrophied muscularis externa with secondary subepithelial chronic inflammation and squamous epithelial hyperplasia; distal esophageal segment exhibits markedly thinned muscular walls with disorganized, hypoplastic circular and longitudinal muscle layers and deficient intramural neural plexuses, explaining lifelong postoperative esophageal dysmotility and severe gastroesophageal reflux
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal congenital foregut anomaly presenting with visible frothy drooling, feeding cyanosis, and catheter obstruction coiled in the upper pouch on babygram, paired with the gastric gas pattern establishing the TEF subtype and strong VACTERL syndromic ties.

Pediatrics.name: Gastroschisis
clinical_manifestations: Full-thickness congenital abdominal wall defect typically measuring 2-4 cm in diameter, located almost universally to the immediate right of a normally inserted umbilical cord, with an intact bridge of normal skin separating the defect from the umbilicus

Pathognomonic physical examination finding: Direct evisceration of naked, uncovered abdominal viscera (primarily small intestine and stomach, occasionally colon, bladder, or gonads; liver herniation is exceptionally rare, present in <1%)
Complete absence of any protective covering membrane: Herniated bowel loops are entirely devoid of an amnion or peritoneal sac, having floated directly in amniotic fluid throughout gestation

Bowel morphology at birth: Intestinal loops are markedly fore-shortened, edematous, thickened, stiff, and encased in a thick, dull, fibrous, yellowish-white inflammatory peel ('gelatinous pseudomembrane' resulting from chemical peritonitis caused by chronic exposure to amniotic fluid containing fetal urine and bile)

Severe hypothermia and rapid evaporative fluid loss: Marked third-spacing and convective heat/fluid loss through exposed viscera requiring emergent sterile plastic bowel bag wrapping and aggressive crystalloid resuscitation immediately in the delivery room

Extraintestinal anomalies are rare (<10%, unlike omphalocele); however, intestinal complications occur in 10-15% of cases ('complex gastroschisis': secondary intestinal atresia, stenosis, volvulus, infarction, or perforation resulting from constriction at the narrow abdominal wall ring); cryptorchidism present in up to 30% of affected males
radiological_manifestations: Antenatal Fetal Ultrasound: Pathognomonic appearance of multiple free-floating, unfurled loops of bowel waving freely in the amniotic fluid to the right of the umbilical cord insertion without a surrounding membrane sac ('cauliflower' or 'flower-like' appearance); normal insertion of the umbilical cord onto the anterior abdominal wall; maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP) markedly elevated (often 4 to 10 multiples of the median, significantly higher than in omphalocele); serial ultrasound monitors for intra-abdominal or extra-abdominal bowel dilation (>7-10 mm) and bowel wall thickening (>3 mm) as predictive markers of bowel atresia, ischemia, or postnatal complicated course

Postnatal Plain Radiograph (Babygram): Massive clustered, extracoelomic, gas-filled loops of bowel herniating outside the anatomical abdominal contour; small, hypoplastic, scaphoid abdominal cavity with diminished intracoelomic volume

Fetal Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): Confirms normal intra-abdominal location of the liver, details bowel caliber, rules out cloacal exstrophy, and differentiates gastroschisis from ruptured omphalocele without ionizing radiation
pathology_manifestations: Embryology & Pathological Anatomy: Full-thickness paraumbilical abdominal wall defect resulting from failure of mesodermal lateral body fold fusion, or localized vascular accident (thrombosis or premature involution of the right omphalomesenteric/vitelline vein or disruption of the right omphalomesenteric artery) at 4-6 weeks of embryonic gestation, creating a locus minoris resistentiae to the right of the umbilicus

Histopathology of Extruded Bowel: Severe subserosal and mural chemical peritonitis; dense fibrous serosal hyperplasia and transmural edema; marked hypertrophy of the muscularis propria; chronic perivascular inflammatory infiltrate; degenerative changes and hypoplasia of the interstitial cells of Cajal and myenteric (Auerbach) plexus explaining prolonged postnatal intestinal dysmotility, delayed transit, and prolonged reliance on parenteral nutrition

Epidemiology & Maternal Risk Factors: Strongly correlated with young maternal age (<20 years, up to 10-fold relative risk compared to mothers >30 years); maternal cigarette smoking, illicit drug use (methamphetamine, cocaine), maternal use of vasoconstrictive medications (pseudoephedrine), and low maternal body mass index (BMI)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential congenital abdominal wall defect instantly recognizable on bedside examination by naked, edematous, peel-encased bowel loops floating freely to the right of a normal umbilical cord, devoid of a membrane sac, and corroborated by antenatal ultrasound showing free-floating paraumbilical loops.

Pediatrics.name: Goldenhar Syndrome
synonyms: first and second branchial arch syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Marked hemifacial microsomia: severe unilateral underdevelopment of the facial skeleton and soft tissues, resulting in striking facial asymmetry

Pathognomonic ocular epibulbar choristoma: limbal dermoid appearing as a smooth, solid, dome-shaped, yellowish-white or pink tumor straddling the inferotemporal corneoscleral limbus; upper eyelid coloboma (notching at junction of middle and inner thirds)

Auricular anomalies: multiple preauricular skin tags (papillomas) and blind fistulae/pits arranged in a line from the tragus to the oral commissure; microtia, anotia, or severely dysplastic auricles with external auditory canal atresia
Macrostomia (transverse facial cleft extending from angle of mouth toward ear); asymmetric palatal elevation; conductive hearing loss
radiological_manifestations: 3D Craniofacial CT: Hypoplasia or complete aplasia of the mandibular condyle, coronoid process, and ascending ramus (Pruzansky classification); hypoplasia of the zygomatic arch, malar bone, and maxilla on the affected side

Cervical and Thoracic Spine Radiographs / CT: Hemivertebrae, block vertebrae (congenital cervical vertebral fusions), butterfly vertebrae, wedge vertebrae, and rib anomalies (bifid, fused, or missing ribs) causing congenital scoliosis
Temporal Bone CT: Dysplastic middle ear ossicles, atresia of the external auditory canal, and aberrant course of the facial nerve (CN VII)
pathology_manifestations: Epibulbar Limbal Dermoid Histopathology: Benign congenital choristoma composed of dense fibrous connective tissue covered by stratified squamous epithelium containing normal dermal skin appendages (hair follicles, sebaceous glands, adipose tissue, and sweat glands) abnormally situated on the cornea/sclera
Pathogenesis: Vascular disruption and embryonic hemorrhage involving the stapedial artery and branchial arch mesenchyme during weeks 4-8 of human development
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Immediate photographic bedside visual diagnosis from epibulbar limbal dermoids, preauricular tags, hemifacial microsomia, and cervical hemivertebrae on CT.

Pediatrics.name: Hallermann-Streiff Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic 'bird-like' craniofacial appearance: Facial gestalt characterized by a sharp, thin, beaked ('parrot-beak') nose with hypoplastic alae nasi; severe mandibular and malar hypoplasia with marked retrognathia ('micrognathic bird face'); small, narrow, pinched mouth (microstomia) and high-arched palate

Bilateral symmetrical ocular malformations: Congenital cataracts (often dense, pearly white, with spontaneous resorption or liquefaction of lens material), severe microphthalmia or microcornea, blue sclerae, nystagmus, strabismus, and high incidence of spontaneous retinal detachment

Cutaneous and hair abnormalities: Localized cutaneous atrophy tightly stretched over the scalp, nose, and central face with prominent superficial telangiectasias; hypotrichosis and localized alopecia affecting the scalp, eyebrows, and eyelashes, with pronounced frontal scalp baldness
Dental anomalies: Natal or neonatal teeth present at birth, severe hypodontia / oligodontia, malformed conical/peg-shaped teeth, enamel hypoplasia, and severe dental crowding/malocclusion

Severe upper airway vulnerability: Critical upper airway obstruction, severe microstomia, retroplaced tongue, and high-arched palate predisposing to neonatal asphyxia, obstructive sleep apnea, and catastrophic difficulty during endotracheal intubation
radiological_manifestations: 3D Craniofacial CT: Severe, symmetric hypoplasia of the mandibular body and ramus with absent or severely hypoplastic mandibular condyles (condylar aplasia/hypoplasia); anteriorly displaced or absent temporomandibular joint articulation; hypoplasia of the ascending ramus with an obtuse gonial angle; severely constricted bony oropharyngeal airway dimensions; delayed closure of cranial fontanelles with persistent wide cranial sutures and thin calvarium
Plain Skeletal Survey: Gracile, slender, thin long bones with narrow diaphyses; lordosis and scoliosis; hypoplastic or absent teeth in alveolar sockets; micrognathia on lateral skull radiographs
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous and Ocular Histopathology: Skin biopsy demonstrates marked epidermal thinning, flattening of the rete ridges, and dense sclerotic dermal collagen bundles with loss of hair follicles and sebaceous glands, resembling localized morphea; lens histology reveals capsular ruptures, morgagnian globule degeneration, and fibroblastic metaplasia with spontaneous cataractous liquefaction

Etiology and Molecular Genetics: Predominantly sporadic de novo occurrences; suspected postzygotic somatic mosaicism or mutations in genes controlling first and second branchial arch morphogenesis and ectodermal development (overlap with progeroid and laminopathy phenotypes)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Unmistakable photographic 'bird-like' facies with congenital cataracts, natal teeth, and cutis laxa/atrophy, matched to pathognomonic 3D craniofacial CT condylar hypoplasia/aplasia and high-risk upper airway skeletal stenosis.

Pediatrics.name: Hirschsprung Disease
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic failure to pass meconium within the first 24-48 hours of life in a term neonate (>90% of affected infants fail to pass meconium by 48 hours; normal full-term neonates pass meconium within 24 hours)
Progressive neonatal low intestinal obstruction: marked abdominal distension, feeding intolerance, bilious emesis, and prominent tympany over the entire abdomen

Pathognomonic bedside digital rectal examination (DRE) 'squirt sign' ('blast sign' / 'explosion sign'): a snug, tight anal canal with an empty rectal ampulla; upon withdrawal of the examining finger, an explosive, forceful release of trapped liquid, foul-smelling feces and gas occurs, resulting in immediate transient decompression of the abdomen

Chronic intractable constipation in older infants and children: ribbon-like, pencil-thin, or pellet-like stools, visible abdominal peristalsis, palpable fecal impaction in the left lower quadrant, severe failure to thrive, hypochromic anemia, and progressive abdominal protuberance with wasted limbs

Hirschsprung-Associated Enterocolitis (HAEC): Most catastrophic complication presenting with sudden-onset high fever, lethargy, severe explosive foul-smelling diarrhea, rapid massive abdominal distension, septic shock, and risk of bowel perforation
radiological_manifestations: Unprepared Fluoroscopic Contrast Enema (Barium Enema): Diagnostic imaging examination performed without prior colonic washouts or rectal prep; demonstrates the pathognomonic 'transition zone' characterized by a narrowed, spastic aganglionic rectosigmoid segment, an intermediate cone-shaped or funnel-shaped transition zone, and massive proximal colonic dilation (ganglionic megacolon); reversal of the normal rectosigmoid ratio (rectal diameter is narrower than the sigmoid colon diameter, rectosigmoid ratio <1.0); irregular, jagged, saw-tooth mucosal contractions ('fasciculations') in the aganglionic segment; delayed 24-hour post-evacuation radiograph demonstrates significant retention of barium contrast throughout the colon

Abdominal Plain Radiographs (Supine and Cross-Table Lateral): Multiple dilated loops of bowel with prominent air-fluid levels and a conspicuous, total absence of air in the rectum and deep pelvis; classic low mechanical bowel obstruction pattern

Anorectal Manometry: Complete absence of the normal rectoanal inhibitory reflex (RAIR)—inflation of a balloon within the rectal lumen fails to elicit reflexive transient relaxation of the internal anal sphincter, demonstrating persistent involuntary sphincter hypertonia (useful screening tool in older infants and children)
pathology_manifestations: Rectal Suction Biopsy (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Full-thickness submucosal suction biopsy obtained 2-3 cm above the pectinate (dentate) line; pathognomonic complete absence of ganglion cells in both the submucosal (Meissner) and myenteric (Auerbach) plexuses

Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) Histochemistry: Striking hypertrophy, hyperplasia, and dense dark-staining coarse meshwork of cholinergic nerve fiber bundles (>40 µm in caliber) extending through the muscularis mucosae and submucosa (representing compensatory extrinsic autonomic hyperinnervation)

Calretinin Immunohistochemistry: Complete absence of calretinin-immunoreactive fine granular nerve fibers and neuroganglion cells within the lamina propria and submucosa (calretinin negativity demonstrates >99% diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for aganglionosis)

Embryological & Molecular Genetics: Premature arrest in the craniocaudal migration of vagal neural crest cells along the enteric tract between weeks 5 and 12 of embryonic development; loss-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (chromosome 10q11.2) identified in ~50% of familial and 15-20% of sporadic cases; additional genes include EDNRB, EDN3, and SOX10; strongly associated with Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome, present in 10-15% of all Hirschsprung patients), Shah-Waardenburg syndrome, and congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (Haddad syndrome, PHOX2B)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Benchmark neonatal neurointestinal disorder with classic failure to pass meconium, diagnostic digital rectal 'squirt sign', fluoroscopic enema cone-shaped transition zone, and definitive aganglionic suction biopsy with calretinin-negative immunostaining.

Pediatrics.name: Holoprosencephaly
clinical_manifestations: Cardinal craniofacial spectrum ('the face predicts the brain'): Severe forms manifest with cyclopia (single median orbit with absent proboscis or supraorbital tubular proboscis), ethmocephaly (extreme hypotelorism with an interorbital blind proboscis), cebocephaly (hypotelorism with a rudimentary single-nostril nose without a cleft), or premaxillary agenesis (median cleft lip/palate, hypotelorism, absent nasal septum); mild microforms manifest with ocular hypotelorism, flat nasal bridge, midface hypoplasia, iris coloboma, anosmia, and a pathognomonic single central maxillary incisor (solitary median maxillary central incisor [SMMCI])

Severe neuroendocrine and hypothalamic dysfunction: Complete panhypopituitarism causing central diabetes insipidus (intractable polyuria and hypernatremic dehydration), adrenal crisis, secondary hypothyroidism, growth failure, micropenis, and cryptorchidism; severe poikilothermia with loss of central autonomic thermoregulation

Profound neurological impairment: Intractable neonatal and infantile seizures, profound global neurodevelopmental arrest, initial flaccid central hypotonia transitioning to severe spastic quadriplegia, dystonic posturing, and severe bulbar dysfunction with inability to coordinate swallowing
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial, Coronal, and Sagittal 3D T1, T2, and FIESTA/CISS): Pathognomonic spectrum of incomplete cleavage of the forebrain (prosencephalon): 1) Alobar HPE: Complete absence of the interhemispheric fissure and falx cerebri, single horseshoe-shaped monoventricle communicating with a large dorsal cyst, completely fused thalami across the midline, absent third ventricle, absent corpus callosum and septum pellucidum, and absent olfactory bulbs/tracts (arhinencephaly); 2) Semilobar HPE: Interhemispheric fissure and falx present only posteriorly in the occipital/parietal regions, anterior frontal lobes fused across midline, partial thalamic fusion, rudimentary third ventricle, and absent septum pellucidum; 3) Lobar HPE: Complete hemispheric cleavage except at the most rostral and ventral frontal neocortex, well-formed lateral ventricles with fused frontal horns and absence of the septum pellucidum; 4) Middle Interhemispheric Variant (Syntelencephaly): Selective failure of separation of the posterior frontal and parietal lobes with normal separation of the frontal and occipital poles

Fetal Neurosonography / Fetal MRI: Inability to visualize the normal midline 'butterfly' choroid plexus sign and cavum septi pellucidi in the second trimester; monoventricle with fused central grey nuclei and characteristic midline facial anomalies (hypotelorism, proboscis, median cleft lip)
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology / Autopsy: Macroscopic failure of diverticulation and cleavage of the primary prosencephalic vesicle into bilateral cerebral hemispheres; single, continuous cup-shaped neocortex over an undivided ventricular chamber; non-cleaved, globular, fused central diencephalic grey matter (thalamus and hypothalamus); total aplasia of olfactory nerves, bulbs, and tracts, and hypoplasia or fusion of optic chiasm

Molecular Genetics & Cytogenetics: Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations or deletions in the Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) signaling pathway: SHH (7q36.3), ZIC2 (13q32.3), SIX3 (2p21), and TGIF1 (18p11.3); chromosomal aneuploidies represent 25–50% of all cases, predominantly Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), followed by triploidy and Trisomy 18
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: The prototypical disorder of forebrain development demonstrating the inviolable rule that 'the face predicts the brain,' coupling photographic craniofacial midline malformations (cyclopia to single maxillary incisor) with definitive cross-sectional brain MRI monoventricle and thalamic fusion.

Pediatrics.name: Infantile Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis
clinical_manifestations: Presentation typically between 2 and 8 weeks of life (peak incidence at 3 to 5 weeks; 4:1 male-to-female predominance, often first-born males) with forceful, progressive non-bilious projectile vomiting occurring immediately after feeds; vomitus consists of curdled breast milk or formula ('coffee-ground' blood-tinged emesis occurs in protracted cases due to severe gastritis or Mallory-Weiss tears)
'Hungry vomiter' behavior: Infant remains alert, avidly feeds, and demands to re-feed immediately after an episode of projectile vomiting, exhibiting frantic rooting and vigorous suckling

Visible gastric peristalsis: Distinct left-to-right peristaltic waves visibly rippling across the epigastrium and upper abdomen from the left costal margin toward the right upper quadrant prior to projectile emesis

Pathognomonic 'Pyloric Olive' sign: Firm, hard, smooth, mobile, non-tender olive-shaped mass (1-2 cm in diameter) palpable in the right upper quadrant or transpyloric plane just lateral to the right rectus abdominis muscle, best palpated after vomiting or following stomach decompression with an orogastric tube during a quiet feed

Dehydration and metabolic derangement: Sunken anterior fontanelle, dry mucous membranes, decreased skin turgor, loss of buccal fat pads, depressed tearing, scaphoid lower abdomen with epigastric fullness, and pathognomonic hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with paradoxical aciduria
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Abdominal Ultrasonography (Diagnostic Modality of Choice / Imaging Gold Standard): Standard diagnostic criteria: pyloric muscle wall thickness >=3.0 mm (single-wall thickness of the circular muscle layer; sensitivity and specificity >98%), pyloric channel length >=14-15 mm, and transverse pyloric diameter >=10-14 mm; pathognomonic 'Target sign' or 'Doughnut sign' on transverse scanning (hypoechoic hypertrophied ring of circular smooth muscle encircling echogenic, compressed, crowded central mucosa); 'Cervix sign' on longitudinal scanning (the thickened pyloric muscle mass indenting into the fluid-filled gastric antrum, resembling the uterine cervix protruding into the vagina); 'Antral nipple sign' (redundant, crowded antral mucosa protruding retrograde into the gastric lumen); real-time dynamic failure of the pyloric channel to relax or open with absent passage of gastric fluid into the duodenal bulb

Upper Gastrointestinal (UGI) Barium Series: Indicated when ultrasound findings are equivocal; pathognomonic 'string sign' (thin, elongated, thread-like radiopaque streak of barium traversing the severely compressed, elongated pyloric channel); 'double track sign' (two parallel streaks of barium separated by redundant mucosal folds); 'shoulder sign' and 'beak sign' (mass effect of the hypertrophied pyloric muscle indentation on the distended gastric antrum); marked delay in gastric emptying (>4 hours)

Plain Abdominal Radiograph: Markedly dilated stomach containing abundant gas and fluid with the 'caterpillar sign' (prominent gastric contour undulations reflecting vigorous hyperperistaltic waves) and a conspicuous paucity or complete absence of gas throughout the distal small bowel and colon
pathology_manifestations: Macroscopic / Surgical Pathology: Striking hypertrophy and hyperplasia of the circular smooth muscle layer of the pylorus, producing an olive-sized, cartilaginous, hard, pale, avascular tumor-like mass that sharply terminates at the duodenum (where circular muscle fibers abruptly end, creating a mucosal fornix highly vulnerable to accidental intraoperative perforation during Fredet-Ramstedt extramucosal pyloromyotomy) and gradually attenuates into the gastric antral wall

Histopathology: Marked circular smooth muscle hypertrophy and hyperplasia with normal longitudinal muscle thickness; secondary mucosal congestion, submucosal edema, and chronic inflammatory infiltration of the lamina propria due to mechanical compression; deficient or absent neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) expression and diminished peptidergic innervation (vasoactive intestinal peptide, substance P) within the myenteric plexus of the hypertrophied circular muscle

Etiology & Risk Factors: Multifactorial polygenic inheritance; strong association with early neonatal oral macrolide antibiotic exposure (erythromycin or azithromycin within the first two weeks of life or maternal consumption during late pregnancy/lactation); male sex predilection; elevated circulating gastrin levels
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic pediatric surgical disorder marked by the observable triad of projectile non-bilious vomiting, visible left-to-right gastric peristalsis, and palpable RUQ 'olive', confirmed by pathognomonic ultrasound 'target' and 'cervix' signs with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis.

Pediatrics.name: Intestinal Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus
clinical_manifestations: Acute onset of sudden, bilious (bright yellow to dark emerald green) vomiting in a previously healthy, term neonate (classically within the first month of life; 30-50% present in the first week, 75-80% within the first month) - a true surgical emergency ('bilious vomiting in an infant is malrotation with volvulus until proven otherwise')

Progression of abdominal signs: Initially the abdomen may be soft and non-distended because the obstruction is high (duodenojejunal junction); with ongoing torsion, progressive severe epigastric distension, tenderness, voluntary guarding, and rigidity develop
Abdominal wall changes: Erythema, ecchymosis, or bluish discoloration of the anterior abdominal wall signaling full-thickness intestinal ischemia, gangrene, and peritonitis
Hematochezia / Melena: Passage of gross blood or occult blood in stools due to mucosal ischemia and mesenteric venous congestion

Hemodynamic shock: Rapid progression to hypovolemic and septic shock: extreme tachycardia, prolonged capillary refill (>3 seconds), mottled skin, cool extremities, hypothermia, metabolic lactic acidosis, and cardiovascular collapse
radiological_manifestations: Upper Gastrointestinal (UGI) Fluoroscopic Series (Imaging Gold Standard): Demonstrates pathognomonic 'Corkscrew sign': contrast opacifies the duodenum which fails to cross the midline to the left of the left pedicle of the L1 vertebra; instead, the duodenum and proximal jejunum spiral downward around the narrowed mesenteric pedicle in a tight corkscrew or helical configuration; Ligament of Treitz is abnormally positioned low and to the right of the vertebral column; in complete volvulus, obstruction manifests as a sharp tapered 'beak' or 'bird's beak' occlusion of the third part of the duodenum

Color Doppler Ultrasonography: Pathognomonic 'Whirlpool sign' (or 'Whirl sign'): clock-wise swirling of the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) and mesenteric branches tightly wrapped around the central superior mesenteric artery (SMA); inversion of the normal mesenteric vascular orientation: the SMV is positioned to the left of or anterior to the SMA (normal anatomy: SMV lies to the right of the SMA)

Plain Abdominal Radiograph: Variable; may show gastric and duodenal distension with diminished distal air (partial double-bubble); 'gasless abdomen' due to fluid-filled ischemic bowel; late findings show pneumatosis intestinalis, portal venous gas, or pneumoperitoneum
pathology_manifestations: Embryological & Surgical Pathology: Failure of normal 270-degree counterclockwise physiological rotation and retroperitoneal fixation of the midgut around the SMA axis during embryonic weeks 4 to 10; results in an abnormally narrow mesenteric root (pedicle) measuring only 1-2 cm (rather than the normal broad diagonal attachment from left upper quadrant to right lower quadrant) and fibrous peritoneal Ladd bands crossing from the cecum across the duodenum to the right abdominal wall, predisposing the entire midgut to clockwise torsion/volvulus

Intraoperative & Macroscopic Findings: Clockwise twisting (usually 360 to 720 degrees) of the small and large bowel around the narrow mesenteric axis; massive mesenteric venous occlusion causing intense cyanosis, hemorrhagic congestion, and progressing to irreversible transmural ischemic necrosis of the entire midgut from the duodenojejunal junction to the mid-transverse colon

Resection Histopathology (in non-viable bowel): Severe transmural coagulative necrosis, hemorrhagic infarction, microvascular thrombi within mesenteric vessels, mucosal sloughing, and secondary bacterial invasion
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Paramount pediatric surgical emergency where acute neonatal bilious emesis and rapid shock are matched by the pathognomonic UGI fluoroscopic 'corkscrew sign' and Doppler ultrasound 'whirlpool sign'.

Pediatrics.name: Joubert Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Neonatal respiratory and oculomotor hallmarks: Episodic alternating neonatal hyperpnea and central apnea (episodic rapid panting followed by prolonged apnea, prominent during wakefulness and abating in sleep); oculomotor apraxia (inability to initiate voluntary horizontal saccades, compensated by vigorous horizontal head thrusts), severe horizontal/rotatory nystagmus, and strabismus

Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism: Prominent broad forehead, high arched eyebrows, hypertelorism, epicanthal folds, ptosis, wide depressed nasal bridge with anteverted nares, and a classic open-mouth appearance with an inverted V-shaped or trapezoidal upper lip and tongue protrusion/rhythmic tongue movements
Neuromuscular manifestations: Profound generalized infantile hypotonia ('floppy infant'), severe truncal and appendicular ataxia, global developmental delay, and severe motor coordination impairment

Multi-organ ciliopathy phenotypes (in Joubert-related disorders): Retinal dystrophy / chorioretinal colobomas (Senior-Løken syndrome overlap), bilateral cystic kidney disease / juvenile nephronophthisis (leading to pediatric end-stage renal disease), congenital hepatic fibrosis, and postaxial polydactyly
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial T1/T2, Coronal, and Diffusion Tensor Imaging [DTI]): Pathognomonic 'Molar Tooth Sign' (MTS) on axial views through the midbrain-pontine junction, characterized by: 1) Marked hypoplasia or complete agenesis of the cerebellar vermis; 2) Abnormally thickened, horizontally oriented, and elongated superior cerebellar peduncles; 3) Abnormally deep, widened interpeduncular fossa; 4) 'Batwing' or umbrella-shaped fourth ventricle on coronal and axial sections
Diffusion Tensor Tractography (DTI): Pathognomonic total failure of decussation of the superior cerebellar peduncles and corticospinal tracts (non-decussating tract architecture)

Renal and Abdominal Ultrasonography: Demonstrates loss of corticomedullary differentiation, increased renal parenchymal echogenicity, and multiple small medullary and corticomedullary cysts characteristic of nephronophthisis; hepatomegaly with periportal echogenicity in hepatic fibrosis
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology / Autopsy: Macroscopic vermian hypoplasia/aplasia with mid-sagittal cleft separating the cerebellar hemispheres; microscopic absence of the deep cerebellar nuclei, severe fragmentation and heterotopia of the inferior olivary nuclei, and total absence of corticospinal and superior cerebellar decussations in the brainstem

Molecular Genetics / Ciliary Biology: Autosomal recessive (or rare X-linked) mutations in >35 primary cilia basal body and transition zone genes (e.g., AHI1, CEP290, CC2D2A, INPP5E, TMEM67, NPHP1, OFD1), disrupting ciliogenesis, Joubert-protein gating at the ciliary transition zone, and Sonic Hedgehog / Wnt signal transduction in embryonic neurogenesis
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic pediatric primary ciliopathy defined by the internationally revered neuroimaging 'molar tooth sign' on brain MRI, neonatal alternating hyperpnea-apnea, oculomotor apraxia, and molecular transition-zone ciliary biology.

Pediatrics.name: Klippel-Trénaunay Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic clinical triad: 1) Geographic capillary malformation (port-wine stain) with sharp demarcation, classically involving the lateral aspect of the affected limb and buttocks; 2) Bony and soft-tissue hypertrophy producing dramatic limb length and girth asymmetry; 3) Prominent, tortuous, persistent embryonic lateral superficial varicose veins (vein of Servelle)
Cutaneous lymphatic vesicles weeping clear or blood-tinged lymph fluid (lymphorrhea), secondary skin hyperkeratosis, and severe localized lymphedema with 'woody' induration
Pelvic and visceral vascular malformations manifesting as recurrent gross hematuria or severe rectal/gastrointestinal bleeding

Localized intravascular coagulopathy (LIC) with elevated D-dimer, consumption of fibrinogen, and frequent episodes of superficial thrombophlebitis or unprovoked deep vein thrombosis (DVT) with high risk of pulmonary embolism
radiological_manifestations: Color Doppler Ultrasonography: Demonstrates slow-flow, low-resistance venous and lymphatic malformations infiltrating subcutaneous fat and muscle; evaluates patency, hypoplasia, or complete agenesis of the deep femoral and popliteal veins; identifies the avalvular embryonic lateral marginal vein of Servelle

Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI and MR Venography): Extensive hyperintense T2/STIR lobulated vascular masses with multi-compartmental infiltration of the subcutis, intermuscular planes, and skeletal muscle; high-flow arteriovenous shunts (flow voids) are distinctly absent, differentiating KTS from Parkes Weber syndrome; scanograms quantify limb elongation and cortical thickening

Ascending Contrast Venography: Identifies hypoplastic or interrupted deep venous drainage with massive collateralization through avalvular superficial marginal channels draining toward the internal iliac or inferior vena cava
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology: Ectatic, thin-walled, irregular venous channels and dilated lymphatic spaces lined by single-layered CD31/ERG-positive endothelium in dermis, subcutis, and muscle; absence of internal elastic lamina, erratic smooth muscle bundling within vessel walls, and luminal organizing thrombi with phleboliths

Molecular Genetics: Somatic mosaic gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA (phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit alpha) on chromosome 3q26.3, placing KTS definitively within the PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS)
