Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal congenital vascular dysmorphic overgrowth syndrome featuring the visible triad of port-wine stain, limb hemihypertrophy, and lateral varicosities, corroborated by multi-compartmental low-flow MRI and PIK3CA somatic genetics.

Pediatrics.name: Marfan Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Tall, slender habitus with disproportionately long extremities (arm span exceeding height by >1.05)

Arachnodactyly ('spider fingers'): positive Steinberg thumb sign (distal phalanx projects beyond ulnar border of clenched fist) and positive Walker-Murdoch wrist sign (thumb overlaps fifth digit around contralateral wrist)
Pectus excavatum (funnel chest) or pectus carinatum (pigeon chest)
Ectopia lentis: upward and outward bilateral lens subluxation/dislocation on slit-lamp biomicroscopy
High-arched, narrow palate with severe dental crowding, hindfoot valgus, and stretch marks (striae distensae)
radiological_manifestations: Cardiovascular CTA / MRA / Echocardiography: Annuloaortic ectasia with dilatation of the aortic root at the sinuses of Valsalva (Z-score >=2), ascending aortic aneurysm, acute aortic dissection (Stanford Type A), mitral valve prolapse with regurgitation
Spine / Pelvis MRI: Dural ectasia (ballooning of the dural sac in the lumbosacral region, scalloping of anterior vertebral bodies)
Skeletal Radiography: Severe scoliosis (>20 degrees), acetabular protrusion (protrusio acetabuli)
pathology_manifestations: Aortic tissue histology: Cystic medial necrosis characterized by fragmentation, disruption, and loss of elastic fibers within the aortic media (Verhoeff-Van Gieson stain), accumulation of basophilic proteoglycan-rich ground substance, and lack of acute inflammatory infiltrates
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Renowned dysmorphic condition presenting with arachnodactyly, Steinberg thumb sign, and ectopia lentis paired with annuloaortic ectasia on echo/CTA and dural ectasia on spinal MRI.

Pediatrics.name: Necrotizing Enterocolitis
clinical_manifestations: Sudden clinical deterioration in premature, low-birth-weight infants (inversely related to gestational age: onset at 1 to 3 weeks of life in extremely low birth weight infants; earlier in late-preterm infants) following the initiation and advancement of enteral feeds (formula-fed infants have a 6-10 fold higher incidence than those fed exclusive maternal breast milk)

Gastrointestinal warning signs: Sudden feeding intolerance, large gastric residuals (>50% of prior feed, or bilious/coffee-ground aspirates), prominent abdominal distension, absent or markedly hypoactive bowel sounds, and visible dilated bowel loops mapped out through the thin abdominal wall

Abdominal wall cellulitis and tenderness: Pathognomonic shiny, taut, erythematous, edematous skin with induration, tenderness, and bluish-purple discoloration or duskiness of the anterior abdominal wall (indicating underlying transmural bowel necrosis, peritonitis, or impending perforation)
Hematochezia: Grossly bloody stools or heme-positive occult blood in stools

Systemic collapse: Temperature instability (hypothermia or hyperthermia), lethargy, recurrent severe apnea and bradycardia spells, hypotension, mottled skin, poor peripheral perfusion, mixed metabolic lactic acidosis, and profound thrombocytopenia with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
radiological_manifestations: Serial Plain Abdominal Radiographs (Babygram; Supine AP and Cross-Table Lateral or Left Lateral Decubitus): Diagnostic modality of choice for staging (Bell staging criteria):

- Pathognomonic Pneumatosis Intestinalis: Finely granular, bubbly, or curvilinear/linear radiolucent gas halos tracking within the subserosal and submucosal layers of the bowel wall (produced by hydrogen-producing gas-forming bacteria dissecting through disrupted mucosal barriers; Bell stage IIA/IIB)

- Branching Hepatic Portal Venous Gas (HPVG): Branching tubular radiolucent branching gas columns extending peripherally toward the hepatic capsule (distinguished from aerobilia which is central; carried by mesenteric venous drainage; Bell stage IIB)

- Persistent 'Fixed' Dilated Bowel Loop: A single dilated adynamic intestinal loop that remains identical in position, caliber, and configuration across sequential radiographs obtained 24 to 36 hours apart ('sentinel loop' indicating transmural full-thickness infarction)

- Pneumoperitoneum (Perforation / Bell Stage IIIB): Free extraluminal air; pathognomonic 'Football sign' on supine radiograph (massive oval radiolucency outlining the entire peritoneal cavity with the falciform ligament visualized as a sharp linear stripe resembling the laces of a football); 'Rigler sign' / double-wall sign (air outlining both luminal and serosal margins of bowel wall); subdiaphragmatic crescent of free air on cross-table lateral or left lateral decubitus radiographs

Bedside Abdominal Ultrasonography: Demonstrates dynamic microvascular flow; microbubble showers of portal venous gas moving through the portal trunk; echogenic intramural gas foci in bowel loops; focal bowel wall thinning (<1 mm) or thickening (>2.5 mm); absence of mural color Doppler flow ('colorless bowel' signifying transmural infarction); complex ascites with echogenic debris and peritoneal fibrin stranding
pathology_manifestations: Macroscopic Surgical Pathology: Patchy or confluent segments of transmural bowel infarction and gangrene with dark plum-colored, friable, paper-thin, dilated bowel loops (most commonly affecting the terminal ileum and ascending colon); palpable intramural crepitus due to gas bubbles; micro- and macro-perforations along the antimesenteric border; fibrinous purulent exudate coating the serosa

Histopathology: Pathognomonic coagulative (ischemic) necrosis of the bowel wall with ghost-like architecture of enterocytes; mucosal denudation, extensive submucosal and subserosal gas cysts (pneumatosis) surrounded by minimal or absent cellular inflammatory response; microvascular fibrin thrombi in submucosal arterioles and venules; secondary bacterial overgrowth and transmural bacterial invasion

Pathophysiology & Molecular Mechanisms: Multi-hit etiology: immature intestinal epithelial barrier and tight junctions, abnormal microbial colonization (gut dysbiosis with depletion of commensal Bifidobacteriaceae and overgrowth of inflammatory Gammaproteobacteria), toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) hyperactivation in immature enterocytes triggering microvascular endothelial vasoconstriction, loss of mucosal perfusion, and apoptosis, compounded by hyperosmolar formula feeds and hypoxic-ischemic stress
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Most catastrophic GI emergency of premature neonates, exhibiting recognizable abdominal wall erythema/bluish discoloration and distension, paired with pathognomonic babygram findings of pneumatosis intestinalis, branching portal venous gas, and the 'football sign' of pneumoperitoneum.

Pediatrics.name: Noonan Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic facial dysmorphism: broad forehead, hypertelorism with downslanting palpebral fissures, ptosis, epicanthal folds, low-set backward-rotated ears with thick folded helices, deeply grooved philtrum with high Cupid's bow, and micrognathia
Webbed neck (pterygium colli) with low posterior hairline and prominent trapezius muscle pads
Distinctive thoracic deformity: superior pectus carinatum with inferior pectus excavatum, accompanied by widely spaced, low-set nipples
Short stature, cryptorchidism in males (>70%), easy bruising/bleeding diathesis (coagulation factor deficiencies)
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic Echocardiography (Echo): Dysplastic pulmonary valve stenosis (50-60%) with thick, nodular, immobile valve cusps without commissural fusion; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, 20-30%), predominantly asymmetric septal hypertrophy with left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction
Chest Radiographs: Pectus deformity (carinatum-excavatum complex), cardiomegaly, and pulmonary oligemia or chylothorax
MR Lymphangiography / Lymphoscintigraphy: Generalized lymphatic dysplasia with hypoplasia or absence of the thoracic duct, retroperitoneal lymphatic ectasia, and lower extremity lymphedema
pathology_manifestations: Cardiac Histopathology: Excised pulmonary valves display severe myxomatous degeneration with disorganized collagen and proteoglycan accumulation; cardiac biopsy in HCM shows marked myocyte hypertrophy, extensive myofibrillar disarray, and interstitial fibrosis
Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous gain-of-function missense mutations in genes of the RAS-MAPK signaling pathway, most commonly PTPN11 (encoding SHP2, ~50%), SOS1 (10-15%), RAF1, RIT1, or KRAS
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Premier RASopathy with unforgettable bedside facial features, webbed neck, pectus carinatum/excavatum, dysplastic pulmonary valve stenosis on echo, and asymmetric septal hypertrophy.

Pediatrics.name: Omphalocele
clinical_manifestations: Midline anterior abdominal wall defect located directly at the base of the umbilicus, with the umbilical cord inserting directly onto the apex or center of the herniated mass

Pathognomonic physical examination finding: Herniated abdominal viscera encapsulated within a glistening, translucent, three-layered membranous sac consisting of an outer amnion layer, intermediate Wharton's jelly, and an inner peritoneum (sac may be intact or occasionally ruptured intrapartum)

Sac contents and size variation: Defect size ranges from small hernia into the umbilical cord (<4 cm) to giant omphalocele (>5 cm defect with >50% of the liver herniated); contents frequently include liver (herniated in >60-80% of cases), spleen, stomach, small intestine, and colon
High frequency of major co-existing anomalies (present in 50-70% of cases):

- Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome (BWS): Striking triad of omphalocele, macroglossia (large protruding tongue), and macrosomia, accompanied by earlobe creases and helical pits, organomegaly, and severe neonatal hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia secondary to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia

- Chromosomal Aneuploidies (in 30-40% of cases with normal liver location): Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome: clenched fists with overlapping index fingers, rocker-bottom feet, micrognathia), Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome: holoprosencephaly, microphthalmia, cleft lip/palate, polydactyly), and Trisomy 21

- Pentalogy of Cantrell: Midline epigastric omphalocele, lower sternal cleft, anterior diaphragmatic hernia, pericardial defect, and ectopia cordis (naked, pulsating heart visible outside the thoracic wall)
- OEIS Complex: Omphalocele, Exstrophy of the bladder, Imperforate anus, and Spinal defects
- Congenital Heart Defects (CHD): Present in 30-50% (tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, coarctation of aorta, atrial septal defect)
radiological_manifestations: Antenatal Fetal Ultrasound (Diagnostic Modality): Demonstration of a smooth, sharply demarcated, midline anterior abdominal wall mass encapsulated by a distinct, thin, echogenic membrane sac with the umbilical cord inserting into the sac apex; visualization of the liver, gallbladder, and bowel within the sac; Color Doppler verifies umbilical vessels traversing and branching along the membranous capsule; maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP) elevated (though generally lower than in gastroschisis); detects associated congenital heart defects, neural tube defects, and renal anomalies

Neonatal Plain Radiograph (Babygram): Smooth, rounded, well-circumscribed soft-tissue mass projecting from the midline anterior abdomen containing gas-filled bowel and uniform soft-tissue density of the herniated liver; small, hypoplastic abdominal cavity; associated skeletal anomalies (vertebral segmentation defects, hemivertebrae, sternal cleft)
Echocardiography: Routine, essential pre-operative imaging modality to rule out complex congenital heart defects (present in up to 50% of infants with omphalocele)
pathology_manifestations: Embryology & Pathological Anatomy: Midline defect resulting from failure of the lateral ectomesodermal embryonic body folds to migrate and fuse in the midline at the umbilical ring around 6-10 weeks of gestation, failing to complete physiological gut rotation and retraction from the extraembryonic celom

Histopathology of the Omphalocele Sac: Outer layer of avascular, single-to-pseudostratified amniotic epithelium; middle layer composed of myxoid, proteoglycan-rich Wharton's jelly containing sparse spindle cells; inner layer of single-layer cuboidal-to-flattened peritoneal mesothelium; umbilical vessels (two arteries and one vein) track circumferentially through the sac wall to insert at the apex

Visceral Histology: Viscera inside an intact sac show completely normal serosal surfaces with normal intestinal wall caliber, absence of the inflammatory fibrinous 'peel' characteristic of gastroschisis; however, persistent pulmonary hypoplasia is frequent in giant omphaloceles due to thoracic deformation
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal congenital midline abdominal wall anomaly featuring a glistening, membrane-covered sac with apex umbilical cord insertion, herniated liver, and frequent association with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, trisomies, and congenital heart disease.

Pediatrics.name: Osteogenesis Imperfecta
clinical_manifestations: Blue or slate-gray sclerae (due to thin scleral collagen allowing visualization of the underlying pigmented choroid)
Dentinogenesis imperfecta (translucent, yellowish-brown or opalescent teeth that fracture and wear rapidly)
Severe, multiple recurrent fractures from minimal or trivial trauma
Progressive limb bowing deformities (sabre shin, femoral bowing) and severe kyphoscoliosis
Triangular facies with broad forehead and pointed chin; conductive/sensorineural hearing loss
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal Radiography: Multiple fractures at various stages of healing (often with exuberant hyperplastic callus); profound generalized osteopenia with pencil-thin bone cortices; multiple wormian bones along cranial suture lines (>=10 mosaic bones in lambdoid suture); biconcave 'codfish' vertebral compression fractures; severe long bone bowing and 'accordion-like' crumpled femurs in severe OI
pathology_manifestations: Bone biopsy histology: Deficient synthesis of normal type I collagen resulting in thin, discontinuous trabeculae composed of immature woven bone with failure to convert into organized lamellar bone; hypercellularity of osteocytes
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield genetic syndrome with iconic blue sclerae and dentinogenesis imperfecta matched with multiple fractures at various stages of healing and wormian bones on skeletal X-rays.

Pediatrics.name: Pediatric Intussusception
clinical_manifestations: Sudden, paroxysmal, severe, colicky abdominal pain in a previously thriving infant (peak age 6 to 36 months; male-to-female ratio 3:2), presenting as dramatic bouts of inconsolable crying during which the infant flexes the hips and draws the knees tightly up to the chest

Characteristic pain-free intervals: Episodes recur every 15-20 minutes; between paroxysms, the infant initially appears completely well, but progressively becomes strikingly lethargic, somnolent, or stuporous (frequently misdiagnosed as sepsis, encephalitis, or narcotic ingestion due to endogenous opioid/endorphin release)

Palpable Abdominal Mass: Smooth, firm, tubular, sausage-shaped mass (4-8 cm long) palpable in the right upper quadrant or epigastrium (representing the invaginated intussusceptum), with an empty, hollow right lower quadrant on palpation (Dance sign or sign of Dance due to migration of the cecum and ascending colon)

Stool Changes: Early normal stools, followed by occult blood, progressing to pathognomonic 'currant jelly stool' (a dark red, gelatinous mixture of sloughed colonic mucosa, red blood cells, and inflammatory mucus passed spontaneously or seen on digital rectal examination; classic late finding indicating advanced mucosal ischemia)
Progressive bilious vomiting, tachycardia, abdominal distension, and signs of peritonitis/perforation as complete mechanical strangulation develops
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasonography (Diagnostic Gold Standard; sensitivity 98-100%, specificity 98-100%): Pathognomonic 'Target sign' or 'Doughnut sign' in transverse plane (concentric alternating hypoechoic rings of edematous bowel wall and hyperechoic mesenteric fat and mucosa, total outer diameter typically 2.5-4 cm); 'Pseudokidney sign' or 'Sandwich sign' in longitudinal plane (curvilinear, layered mass with a central echogenic mucosal/mesenteric core surrounded by hypoechoic bowel wall mimicking renal cortex and pelvis); Color Doppler interrogation evaluates perfusion—absence of mural blood flow within the intussusceptum correlates with bowel gangrene, irreducibility, and heightened perforation risk

Fluoroscopic Pneumatic (Air) or Hydrostatic (Contrast) Enema (Therapeutic & Diagnostic Modality): Demonstrates a sharply marginated, meniscus-shaped intraluminal filling defect at the leading edge of the intussusceptum; classic 'coiled-spring sign' as contrast outlines the space between the intussuscipiens and intussusceptum; under continuous fluoroscopy with controlled pressure (<120 mmHg for air), successfully reduces 80-90% of uncomplicated idiopathic intussusceptions, confirmed by free rush of air/contrast into multiple loops of terminal ileum

Plain Abdominal Radiographs: Soft-tissue mass in the right upper quadrant obscuring hepatic margins; absence of cecal gas in the right lower quadrant; small bowel obstruction pattern with dilated central loops and air-fluid levels; crescent-shaped gas shadow capping the intussusceptum ('crescent sign')
pathology_manifestations: Pathological Anatomy: Invagination (telescoping) of a proximal segment of the intestine (intussusceptum) into the lumen of the contiguous distal bowel (intussuscipiens); >90% of pediatric cases are ileocolic (terminal ileum prolapsing through the ileocecal valve into the cecum and ascending colon), followed by ileo-ileal and colocolic forms

Etiology & Lead Points: In infants and young children (<2 years), >90% of cases are idiopathic, triggered by marked lymphoid hyperplasia of the Peyer patches in the terminal ileum following viral infection (human adenovirus, rotavirus, or upper respiratory illness); in children >2-3 years or atypical presentations, a pathological lead point is found in 20-30% of cases: Meckel diverticulum (most common lead point), intestinal polyp (Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, juvenile polyp), intestinal duplication cyst, Henoch-Schönlein purpura (IgA vasculitis with intramural submucosal hematoma), celiac disease, or non-Hodgkin lymphoma (Burkitt lymphoma)

Histopathology of Resection Specimen (in gangrene or failed reduction): Intense ischemic venous congestion, extensive transmural hemorrhagic infarction, coagulative mucosal necrosis, fibrinous serositis, and massive reactive follicular hyperplasia of lymphoid tissue with enlarged germinal centers
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Paramount pediatric emergency with the classic clinical triad of colicky knee-chest cry, sausage mass with RLQ Dance sign, and 'currant jelly' stool, matched to the unmistakable ultrasound 'target/doughnut' and 'pseudokidney' signs and therapeutic fluoroscopic pneumatic/hydrostatic reduction.

Pediatrics.name: Pfeiffer Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Severe craniosynostosis and skull deformity: Type 1 (Classic): Turribrachycephaly (tall, tower-like skull with flattened occiput), high forehead, and midface hypoplasia; Type 2: Pathognomonic 'cloverleaf' skull deformity (Kleeblattschädel) caused by pan-synostosis (premature fusion of coronal, lambdoid, and sagittal sutures) with severe trilobate cranial bulge, extreme ocular proptosis (eyes bulging beyond orbital rim with danger of globe subluxation), and severe intracranial hypertension; Type 3: Severe turribrachycephaly and midface hypoplasia with extreme proptosis without cloverleaf deformity

Pathognomonic digital and limb malformations: Strikingly broad, short, medially or radially deviated thumbs and great toes (halluces); soft-tissue cutaneous syndactyly (variable webbing) of fingers and toes; radiohumeral synostosis (fixed elbow ankylosis)

Upper airway and systemic manifestations: Severe choanal stenosis or atresia, tracheal cartilaginous sleeve (continuous unsegmented tracheal cartilage ring) causing life-threatening respiratory distress; hydrocephalus, Chiari I malformation, and conductive hearing loss
radiological_manifestations: 3D Craniofacial CT: Exquisite visualization of premature fusion of cranial sutures (bicoronal, sagittal, and/or lambdoid synostosis; trilobate cloverleaf calvarial distortion in Type 2); marked shallowing of the bony orbits with reduced orbital volume causing severe exorbitism; midface retrusion with hypoplastic maxilla; copper-beaten / beaten-copper skull appearance on endocranial surface reflecting chronic high intracranial pressure

Hand and Foot Radiographs: Broad, short, trapezoidal or delta-shaped proximal phalanges of the thumbs and halluces with radial deviation; duplication or ankylosis of interphalangeal joints; soft-tissue syndactyly

Brain MRI: Communicating or obstructive hydrocephalus; low-lying cerebellar tonsils / Chiari type I herniation through a constricted foramen magnum; jugular foramen stenosis causing cerebral venous hypertension
Airway CT / Virtual Bronchoscopy: Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve (TCS) seen as a rigid, non-compliant, non-tapering tracheal cylinder lacking normal posterior membranous tracheal wall
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology of Cranial Sutures: Premature osteoblast hyper-proliferation and hyper-differentiation within the sutural osteogenic fronts leading to early osseous obliteration and bony bridging; respiratory pathology demonstrates complete absence of the dorsal membranous tracheal wall with full circular hyaline cartilage rings

Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant gain-of-function activating mutations in FGFR1 (predominantly c.755C>G, p.Pro252Arg in chromosome 8p11.23, primarily causing Type 1 Pfeiffer) or FGFR2 (mutations in IgIII domain, including p.Cys342Arg, p.Trp290Cys, and splice site mutations in chromosome 10q26.13, causing severe Type 2 and Type 3 Pfeiffer syndromes)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Cardinal syndromic craniosynostosis defined by broad deviated digits and kleeblattschädel skull deformity on bedside photographs, corroborated by 3D CT suture fusion, tracheal cartilaginous sleeves, and specific FGFR1/2 gain-of-function mutations.

Pediatrics.name: Pierre Robin Sequence
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic clinical triad: 1) Severe congenital micrognathia and retrognathia (severely receded, hypoplastic mandible with receding chin and bird-like profile); 2) Glossoptosis (posterior and superior retraction of the tongue base into the pharynx); 3) Wide, U-shaped cleft of the secondary palate (resulting from failure of horizontal palatal shelf fusion due to tongue interposition)

Upper airway obstruction and respiratory distress: Severe inspiratory stridor, suprasternal/subcostal retractions, stertor, cyanotic episodes, and life-threatening obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) that is characteristically aggravated in the supine position and relieved when placed prone

Severe feeding difficulties and failure to thrive: Disrupted suck-swallow-breathe coordination due to the posterior tongue occluding the oropharynx, leading to prolonged feeding sessions, fatigue, nasal regurgitation, recurrent microaspiration, and aspiration pneumonia

Secondary pectus excavatum: Progressive inward sternal depression resulting from chronic, severe intrathoracic negative pressure generated against the obstructed upper airway during inspiratory efforts in infancy

Associated syndromic features (in syndromic PRS): High myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration, and retinal detachment in Stickler syndrome (the most common syndromic cause, ~25-35%); conotruncal cardiac defects in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome; downward-slanting palpebral fissures and zygomatic hypoplasia in Treacher Collins syndrome
radiological_manifestations: 3D Reconstructed Craniofacial CT: Exquisite visualization of the hypoplastic, shortened mandibular body and ramus with acute mandibular angles; demonstrates severe posterior displacement of the genial tubercles and tongue base tightly abutted against the posterior pharyngeal wall, producing critical slit-like narrowing or complete obliteration of the retroglossal airway lumen; wide U-shaped cleft of the secondary palate with widely separated palatine shelves

Dynamic Airway Fluoroscopy / Cine MRI: Demonstrates dynamic inspiratory collapse of the tongue base into the hypopharynx (glossoptosis) acting as a ball-valve or piston-like total airway occlusion during tidal breathing; objectively demonstrates restoration of oropharyngeal airway dimensions during prone positioning, nasopharyngeal airway stenting, or surgical mandibular distraction osteogenesis (MDO)

Lateral Cephalometry / Skull Radiographs: Markedly decreased sella-nasion-B point (SNB) angle and increased ANB angle reflecting severe skeletal Class II retrognathia; foreshortened mandibular effective length (condylion to gnathion); hypoplasia of the mandibular symphysis
pathology_manifestations: Pathogenetic Sequence Mechanism: Primary intrauterine developmental arrest or mechanical hypoplasia of the mandible occurring prior to week 9 of gestation prevents the normal caudal descent of the embryonic tongue; the persistently high, interposed tongue mechanically prevents the bilateral lateral palatine shelves from elevating above the tongue dorsum and fusing in the midline, creating the pathognomonic rounded, wide U-shaped cleft palate (distinct from the typical V-shaped cleft palate resulting from intrinsic palatal shelf failure)

Molecular Genetics & Cytogenetics: Heterozygous disruption or translocation of non-coding upstream cis-regulatory enhancer elements of the SOX9 gene on chromosome 17q24.3 in isolated non-syndromic PRS; syndromic forms verified by targeted genetic testing: heterozygous mutations in COL2A1, COL11A1, or COL11A2 in Stickler syndrome; 22q11.2 microdeletion (TBX1) in velocardiofacial syndrome; TCOF1, POLR1D, or POLR1C mutations in Treacher Collins syndrome
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic textbook pediatric craniofacial malformation sequence where the bedside photographic finding of retrognathia and glossoptosis correlates with cross-sectional airway CT imaging demonstrating physical airway occlusion, and elucidates a fundamental paradigm of embryological mechanical cascades.

Pediatrics.name: Prader-Willi Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Biphasic clinical course: Phase 1 (neonatal/infancy) presents with severe central hypotonia ('floppy infant'), lethargy, weak cry, absent suck reflex, and failure to thrive requiring tube feeding
Phase 2 (early childhood): Insatiable voracious appetite (hyperphagia) due to lack of satiety leading to rapid development of massive central obesity

Characteristic dysmorphic craniofacial features: narrow bifrontal diameter (dolichocephaly), almond-shaped palpebral fissures, thin upper vermilion border with downturned corners of mouth ('fish-like' mouth), hypopigmentation of hair, skin, and irises
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: micropenis, cryptorchidism, and hypoplastic scrotal sac in males; hypoplastic labia minora/clitoris in females
Acromicria: disproportionately small hands and feet with straight ulnar borders
radiological_manifestations: Bone Age Radiographs (Left Hand/Wrist): Significant delay in skeletal maturation throughout childhood, followed by accelerated epiphyseal fusion and resultant adult short stature
Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA): Markedly elevated total body fat mass percentage with significant reduction in lean muscle mass and generalized osteopenia/osteoporosis
Spine Radiography: High prevalence of progressive scoliosis and kyphosis (>40-80% of adolescents)
Brain and Sella MRI: Hypoplasia of the pituitary gland, decreased pituitary height, or small sella turcica; normal posterior pituitary bright spot
pathology_manifestations: Hypothalamic Neurohistopathology: Marked reduction in the number and volume of oxytocinergic neurons within the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus; testicular biopsy reveals prepubertal seminiferous tubules with germ cell depletion and absent mature Leydig cells

Molecular Genetics: Absence of paternal expression in the 15q11.2-q13 imprinted region, caused by paternal 15q11-q13 deletion (65-75%), maternal uniparental disomy 15 (20-30%), or imprinting center defects (1-3%)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal biphasic pediatric syndrome evolving from the floppy infant to hyperphagic morbid obesity, small hands/feet, almond eyes, delayed bone age, and hypothalamic neuroendocrine disruption.

Pediatrics.name: Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic broad, spatulate thumbs and great toes (halluces), often with persistent radial deviation (angulation)

Highly characteristic facial dysmorphism: prominent beaked or aquiline nose with the nasal columella extending conspicuously below the lower margin of the alae nasi; heavy, arched eyebrows with long eyelashes; downslanting palpebral fissures; high-arched palate; talon cusps on incisors
Grimacing or 'pursing' smile with eyes closing almost completely during smiling
Microcephaly, post-natal growth retardation, severe intellectual disability, and excessive propensity to spontaneous keloid and hypertrophic scar formation
radiological_manifestations: Hand and Foot Radiographs: Broad, short, spatulate distal phalanges of the first digits (thumbs and great toes); pathognomonic abnormal triangular or trapezoidal proximal phalanx causing radial deviation (delta phalanx); partial or complete duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb
Cranial Radiographs and Brain MRI: Delayed closure of fontanelles, persistent parietal foramina, corpus callosum hypoplasia/agenesis, and Chiari I malformation
Pelvic and Spine Radiographs: Vertebral segmentation abnormalities, spina bifida occulta, and kyphoscoliosis
pathology_manifestations: Keloid and Skin Histopathology: Abundant haphazard bundles of thick, hyalinized, hypocellular collagen fibers (keloidal collagen) within the reticular dermis with absence of normal adnexal structures

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous mutations or microdeletions at 16p13.3 disrupting CREBBP (CREB-binding protein, ~60%) or at 22q13.2 disrupting EP300 (~10%), resulting in deficient histone acetyltransferase activity
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Immediate bedside visual recognition from broad deviated thumbs/toes, low-hanging columella, characteristic grimacing smile, delta phalanges on plain film, and CREBBP histone acetylation defect.

Pediatrics.name: Saethre-Chotzen Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Asymmetric craniosynostosis and cranial vault deformity: Coronal suture synostosis (frequently unicoronal, causing prominent anterior plagiocephaly with marked facial asymmetry, or bicoronal causing brachycephaly/turricephaly); low anterior hairline with prominent frontal bossing

Characteristic facial gestalt and ocular signs: Unilateral or bilateral eyelid ptosis (a major diagnostic hallmark differentiating it from other syndromic craniosynostoses); hypertelorism; tear-duct stenosis; prominent, sharp nasal bridge with beaked nasal tip; facial asymmetry

Pathognomonic ear anomalies: Small, low-set ears with a prominent horizontal crus of the helix extending across the concha (divided or prominent crus cymbae), folded upper helix, and narrow external auditory canals

Extremity and digital anomalies: Partial cutaneous soft-tissue syndactyly, classically involving the second and third fingers (syndactyly II-III) and third and fourth toes; broad, bifid, or duplicated hallux; clinodactyly of the fifth finger
radiological_manifestations: 3D Reconstructed Craniofacial CT: Demonstrates premature synostosis of the coronal suture (unilateral in anterior plagiocephaly or bilateral in brachycephaly); ipsilateral elevation of the superior orbital margin and sphenoid ridge ('harlequin eye' deformity on plain AP radiograph and CT scout view); contralateral compensatory frontal bossing; deviation of the nasal septum and chin point

Skeletal Radiographs of Hands and Feet: Soft-tissue syndactyly between digits 2 and 3; duplicated or bifid distal phalanx of the hallux; carpal/tarsal bone coalitions or radioulnar synostosis in severe variants

Cranial MRI: Parietal foramina (large symmetric calvarial defects in the parietal bones along the sagittal suture in cases with contiguous 7p21.1 microdeletions); low risk of Chiari I or hydrocephalus compared to FGFR-related craniosynostoses
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology of Sutures: Eburnation and premature bony bridging across coronal suture margins with fibrous disorganization of the pericranium and dura mater

Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant loss-of-function heterozygous mutations, intragenic deletions, or whole-gene microdeletions of TWIST1 on chromosome 7p21.1 (a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that acts as a negative regulator of osteogenic differentiation during calvarial development); haploinsufficiency of TWIST1 results in unrestrained RUNX2 and FGFR signaling, driving premature suture ossification
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: The leading basic helix-loop-helix craniosynostosis syndrome, recognized by bedside low hairline, eyelid ptosis, and ear crus crus cymbae alongside pathognomonic 3D CT unicoronal synostosis with 'harlequin eye' orbitopathy and TWIST1 haploinsufficiency.

Pediatrics.name: Sotos Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cardinal facial gestalt: Striking macrocephaly with dolichocephalic skull shape, prominent high forehead with frontotemporal bossing, receding frontotemporal hairline (parietotemporal alopecia/hair sparsity), downslanting palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, long narrow triangular face, and a prominent, pointed, square chin; prominent facial flushing across the cheeks

Pre- and postnatal somatic overgrowth: Height and head circumference typically >=2 standard deviations above the mean (>97th percentile) throughout infancy and childhood; disproportionately large hands and feet with broad digits, pes planus, and accelerated linear velocity that stabilizes toward normal adult height in late adolescence

Neurological and behavioral manifestations: Marked neonatal hypotonia with feeding difficulties, gross and fine motor coordination delay, severe expressive language delay, mild-to-severe intellectual disability, and characteristic behavioral features (autism spectrum traits, impulsivity, temper tantrums, and attention deficit)

Systemic associations: Neonatal jaundice, hypoglycemia, maternal/fetal polyhydramnios, congenital cardiac anomalies (ASD, VSD, patent ductus arteriosus), vesicoureteral reflux, and small increased risk of pediatric embryonal tumors (sacrococcygeal teratoma, neuroblastoma, Wilms tumor)
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Survey / Left Hand-Wrist Radiography: Marked advancement of bone age (carpal and epiphyseal ossification advanced by >=2 to 4 years ahead of chronological age) observed in 75–85% of affected pediatric patients; elongation of metacarpals and phalanges

Brain MRI: Prominent non-progressive cerebral ventriculomegaly (prominence of the lateral ventricles, especially trigones and occipital horns); persistence of cavum septum pellucidum and cavum vergae; hypoplasia of the corpus callosum; hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis and prominent cisterna magna; enlarged perivascular spaces and macrocrania

Abdominal Ultrasonography: Demonstrates renal structural anomalies (vesicoureteral reflux, hydronephrosis, duplex collecting systems, or unilateral renal agenesis) and screens for occult abdominal embryonal neoplasms
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics & Epigenetics: Heterozygous de novo loss-of-function mutation or 5q35 microdeletion spanning the NSD1 gene (Nuclear Receptor Binding SET Domain Protein 1), encoding a histone methyltransferase specific for histone H3 lysine 36 (H3K36me2); 5q35 microdeletions account for ~50% of Japanese cases and ~10-15% of European/American cases, whereas NSD1 intragenic truncating/missense mutations account for 75-80% of Western cohorts; pathognomonic peripheral blood genome-wide DNA hypomethylation episignature differentiates Sotos syndrome from other overgrowth conditions
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Premier pediatric overgrowth syndrome demonstrating pathognomonic photographic facial morphology (high prominent bossed forehead, inverted pear/triangular chin) corroborated by radiological advanced skeletal bone age and ventriculomegaly, governed by NSD1 epigenetic histone dysregulation.

Pediatrics.name: Thanatophoric Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Most common lethal neonatal skeletal dysplasia ('thanatophoric' = death-bearing); infants present at birth with severe, extreme micromelia (profound rhizomelic, mesomelic, and acromelic shortening of all four limbs)
Severe bell-shaped, narrow, constricted thorax with short ribs, leading to immediate respiratory failure at birth

Distinctive craniofacial features: prominent macrocephaly, heavy frontal bossing, depressed nasal bridge, marked hypertelorism, low-set ears; in Type 2 TD, severe cloverleaf skull deformity (kleeblattschädel)
Redundant skin folds ('doughy rolls') along all four shortened extremities; hypotonia and absent Moro reflex
radiological_manifestations: Infant Babygram (Whole-Body Skeletal Radiographs): Type 1 TD demonstrates extremely short, curved, bowed long bones with pathognomonic curved 'telephone-receiver' femora, flared irregular metaphyses, and prominent medial bone spurs; Type 2 TD demonstrates straight femora with pathognomonic cloverleaf skull (kleeblattschädel); axial skeleton reveals severe generalized platyspondyly with flattened 'H-shaped' or 'wafer-thin' vertebral bodies and wide intervertebral disc spaces; narrow thoracic cage with extremely short horizontal ribs
Brain CT/MRI: Severe foramen magnum stenosis, temporal lobe dysplasia with deep transverse fissuring and polymicrogyria, and obstructive hydrocephalus
pathology_manifestations: Growth Plate Chondro-osseous Histopathology: Disastrous disruption of endochondral ossification; growth plates display completely disorganized, short, hypocellular chondrocyte columns with loss of the normal proliferative and hypertrophic zones; abundant vascular mesenchyme and fibrous tissue encroaching into the physeal-metaphyseal junction

Molecular Genetics: Constitutively active gain-of-function missense mutations in FGFR3 (fibroblast growth factor receptor 3) on chromosome 4p16.3; Type 1 is caused by mutations such as p.Arg248Cys or p.Tyr373Cys, whereas Type 2 is universally caused by the specific p.Lys650Glu substitution
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Unforgettable neonatal presentation featuring extreme micromelia, telephone-receiver femora, wafer-thin platyspondyly, and cloverleaf skull driven by FGFR3 gain-of-function.

Pediatrics.name: Treacher Collins Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Striking downward-slanting (antimongoloid) palpebral fissures
Coloboma of the outer third of the lower eyelid (notching) with partial-to-complete absence of eyelashes medial to the coloboma
Severe hypoplasia of the zygomatic arches and malar bones resulting in hollow, sunken cheekbones
Micrognathia and retrognathia with steep mandibular angle and Class II malocclusion
External ear anomalies: microtia, anotia, or severely crumpled pinnae, meatal atresia, and preauricular hair displacement anterior to the ear
Bilateral conductive hearing loss due to middle ear ossicular chain dysgenesis; intact intellect
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Maxillofacial CT: Bilateral symmetrical hypoplasia or complete bony absence (cleft) of the zygomatic arches and malar complexes; hypoplasia of the mandibular ramus, condyle, and coronoid process; acute gonial angle; severely constricted pharyngeal airway

Temporal Bone High-Resolution CT: Complete bony atresia or stenosis of external auditory canals; malformed, hypoplastic, or ankylosed ossicular chains (malleus-incus fusion); hypoplastic middle ear cavities and mastoid pneumatization; normal inner ear (cochlea and vestibule typically preserved)
pathology_manifestations: Pathogenesis & Histopathology: Defective biogenesis of ribosomal RNA causing p53-dependent nucleolar stress and extensive apoptosis of migratory neural crest cells of the first and second pharyngeal arches; hypoplastic branchial bone architecture
Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant heterozygous mutations in TCOF1 (encoding Treacle, >90% of cases), POLR1D, or autosomal recessive mutations in POLR1C
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic bedside facial phenotype (antimongoloid slant, lower lid colobomas, sunken malar cheeks, microtia) with pathognomonic CT absence of zygomatic arches and middle ear atresia.

Pediatrics.name: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder
clinical_manifestations: Short palpebral fissures, smooth philtrum, and a thin upper lip
Growth restriction and microcephaly
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: corpus callosum hypoplasia or migration anomalies in the severe end
pathology_manifestations: No diagnostic biopsy; the lip-philtrum guide photograph is the clinical standard
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Teratogenic syndrome with a standardized facial photograph.

Pediatrics.name: 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Hooded eyelids, a bulbous nose tip, small ears, and a small mouth
Overt or submucous cleft palate and nasal regurgitation
Neonatal hypocalcemic tetany is not the image
radiological_manifestations: Echocardiography: conotruncal anomalies, especially tetralogy or interrupted aortic arch
Absent thymic shadow on the newborn chest radiograph when the T-cell defect is severe
pathology_manifestations: Thymic hypoplasia if tissue is examined; chromosomal microarray is the confirming test
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Microdeletion with a facial photograph, a palate photograph, and a conotruncal imaging set.

Pediatrics.name: Stickler Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Flat midface, Pierre Robin sequence, and a small jaw
High myopia and vitreous changes; retinal detachment is a complication, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: Spine and joint radiographs: mild epiphyseal dysplasia and platyspondyly
pathology_manifestations: Vitreous photography and COL2A1-spectrum testing; cleft-palate histology is not specific
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Collagenopathy with a midface photograph, vitreous findings, and mild skeletal films.

Pediatrics.name: Proteus Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Progressive, asymmetric, distorting overgrowth of a limb or digit after birth
Cerebriform connective-tissue nevus of the sole
Epidermal nevi and lipomas in the same mosaic distribution
radiological_manifestations: Radiographs of the affected limb: irregular bony overgrowth; MRI of soft-tissue asymmetry
pathology_manifestations: AKT1 activating mosaic variant; the sole nevus shows collagenous overgrowth
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Mosaic overgrowth with a progressive limb photograph and a cerebriform sole.

Pediatrics.name: Edwards Syndrome (Trisomy 18)
clinical_manifestations: Severe intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), microcephaly with a prominent, elongated occiput, and narrow bifrontal diameter
Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism: micrognathia, low-set, malformed 'faun-like' ears with pointed tops, short palpebral fissures, and high-arched palate
Pathognomonic clenched fists with overlapping digits: index finger overlapping the third finger, and fifth finger overlapping the fourth finger
Rocker-bottom feet (prominent calcaneus and convex rounded soles), hypoplastic or absent halluces, and hypoplastic fingernails
Severe congenital heart disease (VSD, PDA, ASD, polyvalvular dysplasia) and early infant lethality
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal Obstetric Ultrasound: Choroid plexus cysts, 'strawberry-shaped' cranium, clenched hands, persistent single umbilical artery, polyhydramnios, and severe growth restriction

Postnatal Skeletal Radiography: Hypoplastic thin ribs, short sternum with premature closure of sternal ossification centers, small pelvis with anteriorly rotated ilia, and rocker-bottom foot alignment (dorsiflexed talus with plantarflexed calcaneus)
Echocardiography: Ventricular septal defect (90%), patent ductus arteriosus, and coarctation of aorta
pathology_manifestations: Cytogenetics / Karyotype: Free trisomy 18 (47,XX,+18 or 47,XY,+18) in >95% of cases; mosaicism in remainder
Autopsy Pathology: Meckel diverticulum, horseshoe kidney, diaphragmatic hernia, malrotation, and polyvalvular cardiac dysplasia with nodular thickening of all four valves
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic chromosomal aneuploidy syndrome featuring the classic clenched hands with overlapping digits, rocker-bottom feet, and prominent occiput.

Pediatrics.name: Patau Syndrome (Trisomy 13)
clinical_manifestations: Prototypic triad: Holoprosencephaly with severe midline facial defects, microphthalmia/anophthalmia, and postaxial polydactyly of hands and feet
Midline craniofacial defects: Bilateral cleft lip and palate, cyclopia or ethmocephaly, hypotelorism, and low-set malformed ears
Cutis aplasia: Punched-out circular skin and scalp defects over the parieto-occipital vertex displaying glistening underlying dura or thin transparent membrane
Omphalocele, cryptorchidism, ambiguous genitalia, and profound neurodevelopmental arrest with high neonatal mortality
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal Ultrasound / Neuroimaging: Holoprosencephaly (alobar or semilobar failure of forebrain cleavage into hemispheres, monoventricle, fused thalami), facial clefts, and polycystic kidneys
Skeletal Radiography: Postaxial polydactyly with fully formed or pedunculated supernumerary digits, sloping forehead, and hypoplastic pelvic bones
Echocardiography: Complex cardiac malformations including hypoplastic left heart syndrome, double outlet right ventricle, and tetralogy of Fallot
pathology_manifestations: Cytogenetics / Karyotype: Full trisomy 13 (47,XX,+13 or 47,XY,+13) in 80%; Robertsonian translocation t(13;14) in 20%

Autopsy / Histopathology: Persistence of embryonic hemoglobin (Hb Gower), nuclear projections in circulating neutrophils (sessile nuclear tags), cystic renal dysplasia, and incomplete lobation of lungs and liver
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic chromosomal disorder presenting with the pathognomonic triad of holoprosencephaly, midline clefting, postaxial polydactyly, and scalp cutis aplasia.

Pediatrics.name: Wolf-Hirschhorn Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic 'Greek warrior helmet' facies: Broad, flat bridge of the nose continuing directly into a prominent glabella, high forehead, hypertelorism, and arched eyebrows
Microcephaly, micrognathia, downturned corners of the mouth ('carp mouth'), short philtrum, and prominent low-set ears with preauricular tags/pits
Iris coloboma, strabismus, and cleft lip/palate
Severe prenatal and postnatal growth retardation, intractable early-onset seizures (atypical absence and myoclonic seizures), profound intellectual disability, and hypotonia
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Diffuse microcephaly with corpus callosum hypogenesis or agenesis, delayed myelination, simplified gyral pattern, and cerebellar hypoplasia
Skeletal Radiography: Delayed bone age, kyphoscoliosis, asymmetric pelvic development, clubfoot, and supernumerary ribs
pathology_manifestations: Chromosomal Microarray / FISH: Terminal deletion of chromosome 4p16.3 (involving LETM1 and WHSC1/NSD2 genes); identified on standard high-resolution karyotyping or array CGH
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield deletion syndrome instantly identifiable by the striking pathognomonic 'Greek warrior helmet' facial profile.

Pediatrics.name: Cri-du-Chat Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic high-pitched, monochromatic, kitten-like crying (cri du chat) in infancy caused by structural laryngeal hypoplasia and abnormal vocal cord anatomy
Characteristic infant facies: Moon-shaped round face, hypertelorism, epicanthal folds, downward-slanting (antimongoloid) palpebral fissures, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Microcephaly, low-set ears, single transverse palmar creases (simian crease), severe hypotonia, and profound cognitive impairment
radiological_manifestations: Laryngoscopy: Small, narrow, diamond-shaped larynx with small, flaccid vocal cords and asymmetric epiglottis accounting for acoustic characteristics of the cat-like cry
Brain MRI: Brainstem hypoplasia with disproportionately small pontine and cerebellar vermian volume, enlarged lateral ventricles, and microcephaly
pathology_manifestations: Cytogenetics / FISH: Deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5 (terminal or interstitial deletion spanning 5p15.2-p15.3, the cri-du-chat critical region)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic cytogenetic deletion syndrome characterized by the unmistakable high-pitched cat-like cry and distinctive round moon-like facies with epicanthal folds.

Pediatrics.name: Angelman Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic behavioral phenotype: Inappropriately happy demeanor with frequent paroxysms of unprovoked laughter, smiling, and excitability, accompanied by hand-flapping movements
Severe motor delay and ataxia with jerky, puppet-like, stiff-legged uncoordinated gait
Severe speech impairment (complete absence of expressive speech or fewer than six words)

Dysmorphic craniofacial features: Microbrachycephaly, prominent pointed chin (prognathia), wide mouth (macrostomia) with widely spaced teeth, tongue protrusion, and fair skin with light eyes (hypopigmentation)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Generally structurally normal or mild non-specific white matter volume reduction and mild delayed myelination, ruling out destructive structural malformations

Electroencephalography (EEG - Diagnostic Hallmark): Striking, highly characteristic patterns including runs of high-amplitude rhythmic slow waves (2–3 Hz) with frontally dominant sharp waves, often appearing before clinical symptoms manifest
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics: Loss of maternal UBE3A expression at chromosome 15q11.2-q13 due to: (1) maternal deletion (70%), (2) paternal uniparental disomy 15 (2–5%), (3) imprinting defect (2–4%), or (4) maternal UBE3A point mutation (10%); confirmed via methylation-specific PCR (MS-PCR)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic genomic imprinting disorder characterized by the 'happy puppet' behavioral phenotype with joyful affect, ataxic hand-flapping gait, and prominent chin.

Pediatrics.name: Meckel-Gruber Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Lethal autosomal recessive ciliopathy defined by the classic triad: (1) Occipital encephalocele, (2) Large bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys, and (3) Postaxial polydactyly
Profound oligohydramnios resulting in severe Potter sequence: Pulmonary hypoplasia, compressed squashed facies, and talipes equinovarus deformities
Microcephaly, microphthalmia, cleft palate, and genital ambiguities
Uniformly fatal in the perinatal period or early neonatal hours
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal Ultrasonography / Fetal MRI: Large herniated occipital encephalocele containing brain parenchyma and meninges through an occipital skull defect; massive bilateral enlarged echogenic multicystic kidneys causing severe abdominal distension; postaxial polydactyly on hands and feet; severe anhydramnios
pathology_manifestations: Autopsy Pathology: Bilateral symmetrically enlarged kidneys replaced by sponge-like macroscopic cysts; pathognomonic hepatic ductal plate malformation characterized by profuse proliferation and dilation of intrahepatic bile ducts with portal fibrosis; complete pulmonary hypoplasia
Molecular Genetics: Biallelic pathogenic variants in cilia genes (MKS1, TMEM216, TMEM67/MKS3, RPGRIP1L, CC2D2A)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield lethal ciliopathy defined by the classic triad of occipital encephalocele, bilateral multicystic kidneys, and postaxial polydactyly on prenatal imaging and gross exam.

Pediatrics.name: Smith-Lemli-Opitz Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism: Microcephaly, ptosis, epicanthal folds, broad anteverted nostrils, and micrognathia
Pathognomonic skeletal anomaly: 2-3 toe syndactyly (Y-shaped cutaneous fusion of the second and third toes), postaxial polydactyly, and single palmar crease
Genital anomalies in 46,XY males ranging from hypospadias and cryptorchidism to complete sex reversal (female external genitalia)
Severe feeding intolerance, failure to thrive, photosensitivity, autistic behavioral stereotypies, and intellectual disability
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Hypoplasia or agenesis of the corpus callosum, frontotemporal atrophy, and ventriculomegaly
Echocardiography: Atrioventricular canal defects, anomalous pulmonary venous return, and coarctation of aorta
Skeletal Radiographs: 2nd and 3rd toe syndactyly with postaxial hexadactyly and osteopenia
pathology_manifestations: Biochemical Diagnostics: Elevated serum 7-dehydrocholesterol (7-DHC) and markedly decreased total cholesterol levels (pathognomonic hallmark reflecting defective conversion to cholesterol)
Molecular Genetics: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the DHCR7 (7-dehydrocholesterol reductase) gene
Pathology: Bilateral adrenal cortical hypoplasia, Hirschsprung disease, and renal cystic dysplasia on autopsy
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic inborn error of cholesterol synthesis featuring the pathognomonic Y-shaped 2-3 syndactyly of toes, ambiguous genitalia, and elevated 7-dehydrocholesterol.

Pediatrics.name: Kabuki Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic facial features resembling the makeup worn by actors in traditional Japanese Kabuki theatre: Elongated palpebral fissures with eversion of the lateral third of the lower eyelid, arched high eyebrows with lateral sparseness, broad depressed nasal tip, and prominent large earlobes
Persistent prominent fetal fingertip pads (fleshy pads on digital pulps persisting throughout life)
Skeletal anomalies including brachydactyly V, clinodactyly, scoliosis, and sagittal clefting of vertebrae
Congenital heart disease (coarctation of aorta, VSD, ASD), hypermobility of joints, frequent otitis media with hearing impairment, and mild-to-moderate intellectual disability
radiological_manifestations: Spinal Radiographs: Sagittal cleft vertebrae (butterfly vertebrae), scoliosis, rib anomalies, and hip dysplasia
Hand Radiographs: Short fourth and fifth metacarpals, brachydactyly, and pseudoepiphyses
Brain MRI: Non-specific enlargement of ventricles, Chiari I malformation, and microcephaly
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic variants in KMT2D (MLL2) in type 1 (~75%) or KDM6A in type 2 (~5%), encoding histone methyltransferases involved in chromatin remodeling
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Instantly recognizable dysmorphic syndrome named after traditional Japanese theatre makeup with everted lateral lower eyelids and persistent fetal fingertip pads.

Pediatrics.name: Neuroblastoma
clinical_manifestations: Periorbital ecchymoses ('raccoon eyes') from skull-base metastases
Blueberry-muffin subcutaneous nodules in stage 4S infants
Horner syndrome, opsoclonus-myoclonus 'dancing eyes' syndrome, and a fixed abdominal mass
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI: calcified suprarenal/paraspinal mass encasing (not displacing) the aorta and renal vessels; MIBG scintigraphy: avid skeletal and soft-tissue uptake
pathology_manifestations: Small round blue cells with Homer Wright rosettes and neuropil; urinary VMA/HVA elevated; MYCN amplification stratifies risk
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Commonest extracranial pediatric solid tumor with raccoon-eye and blueberry-muffin phenotypes plus vessel-encasing/MIBG imaging signature.

Pediatrics.name: Wilms Tumor (Nephroblastoma)
clinical_manifestations: Large, smooth, nontender flank mass in a well-appearing toddler
Hematuria, hypertension, and abdominal pain less commonly
Associations: aniridia (WAGR), hemihypertrophy, genitourinary anomalies
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI: large intrarenal mass with 'claw sign' of renal origin displacing (not encasing) vessels; tumor-thrombus extension into IVC; pulmonary metastases on chest CT
pathology_manifestations: Triphasic histology: blastema, epithelial tubules, and stroma; WT1 mutation in syndromic cases
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic pediatric renal mass recognized by claw-sign imaging and triphasic histology; covered WAGR is the predisposition syndrome, not the tumor.

Pediatrics.name: Rhabdomyosarcoma
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly progressive orbital proptosis or periorbital mass in a child
Sarcoma botryoides: polypoid 'bunch of grapes' mass protruding from vagina or bladder
Parameningeal (ear, sinus, nasopharyngeal) mass with cranial-nerve deficits
radiological_manifestations: MRI/CT: enhancing orbit/parameningeal mass with intracranial or bony extension; parameningeal tumors erode skull base
pathology_manifestations: Rhabdomyoblasts with cross-striations; desmin/myogenin (MyoD1) positive; PAX-FOXO1 fusion defines alveolar type
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Proptosis and pathognomonic botryoid 'grape cluster' gross morphology are iconic pediatric-tumor images.

Pediatrics.name: Sacrococcygeal Teratoma
clinical_manifestations: Huge midline mass projecting from the sacrum/buttocks of a newborn (Altman type I external; types II-IV increasingly intrapelvic)
Skin-covered or ulcerated vascular mass displacing the anus anteriorly
Prenatal polyhydramnios, hydrops, or high-output failure from tumor steal
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal ultrasound and fetal MRI: mixed cystic-solid, often calcified sacral mass with internal pelvic extension; postnatal CT/MRI maps the intraspinal/pelvic component
pathology_manifestations: Gross specimen with mature (skin, cartilage, gut) and immature neuroepithelial elements; graded by immature-tissue content
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic neonatal midline sacral mass; external photo is essentially the diagnosis.

Pediatrics.name: Hepatoblastoma
clinical_manifestations: Enlarging right-upper-quadrant mass in a child under three with weight loss and pallor
Isosexual precocity from beta-hCG secretion in some cases
Associations: Beckwith-Wiedemann spectrum, FAP
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI: large heterogeneous, often calcified hepatic mass; PRETEXT staging by sector; pulmonary metastases on chest CT
pathology_manifestations: Epithelial (fetal/embryonal) and mixed mesenchymal patterns; AFP markedly elevated and tracks disease
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Disease-level pediatric liver tumor recognized on imaging-plus-AFP; admitted at weaker end of the visual spectrum.

Pediatrics.name: Cervical Lymphatic Malformation (Cystic Hygroma)
clinical_manifestations: Huge, soft, translucent posterolateral neck mass in a newborn that transilluminates
Sudden enlargement with intralesional hemorrhage or infection
Airway compression or feeding difficulty from mass effect
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound/MRI: multiseptated cystic mass with fluid-fluid levels; prenatal US shows a septated nuchal cystic structure (distinct from simple increased nuchal translucency)
pathology_manifestations: Thin-walled lymphatic channels lined by flat D2-40-positive endothelium with lymphoid aggregates
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: The external photograph of a translucent posterolateral neck mass is the diagnosis.

Pediatrics.name: Anorectal Malformation (Imperforate Anus)
clinical_manifestations: Absent or anteriorly malpositioned anal opening on inspection of the newborn perineum
Perineal or vestibular fistula passing meconium in girls; cutaneous fistula in boys
Flat bottom (poor gluteal musculature) and sacral dimple suggesting associated anomalies
radiological_manifestations: Invertogram/prone cross-table lateral film classically measures gas-to-marker distance; distal colostogram delineates the recto-urinary/perineal fistula; spinal ultrasound/MRI for associated tethered cord
pathology_manifestations: Surgical classification by fistula anatomy (perineal, vestibular, bulbar/prostatic urethral, cloaca, no fistula); Krickenbeck classification
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Same anomaly-as-topic grain as covered esophageal atresia; perineal photographs and fistulogram are definitive.

Pediatrics.name: Myelomeningocele (Open Spina Bifida)
clinical_manifestations: Lumbosacral midline sac with exposed neural placode leaking CSF at birth
Hydrocephalus, clubfeet, and lower-limb paralysis/sensory level
Associated Chiari II features (bulbar dysfunction, apnea) in severe cases
radiological_manifestations: Fetal ultrasound: 'lemon' frontal-bone scalloping and 'banana' cerebellar signs with the sac itself; MRI: Chiari II hindbrain herniation and open posterior elements
pathology_manifestations: Open dysraphic neural tube with placode continuous with skin; folate-preventable spectrum
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Commonest major neural-tube defect; sac photograph plus pathognomonic fetal lemon/banana signs.

Pediatrics.name: Amniotic Band Sequence (Constriction Ring Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Circumferential constriction rings of digits or limbs, often with distal lymphedema
Fenestrated acrosyndactyly (fused digits with sinus tracts at the base) and in-utero amputations
Asymmetric non-embryologic clefts of face/body and clubfoot
radiological_manifestations: Radiographs: soft-tissue constriction grooves with distal osseous tapering or absent segments; prenatal US may show bands attached to the fetus
pathology_manifestations: Fibrous amniotic strands entangling fetal parts; malformation sequence rather than genetic disease
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Dramatic photographic phenotype (constriction rings, fenestrated syndactyly) as a defined disruption sequence.

Pediatrics.name: Encephalocele
clinical_manifestations: Skin-covered or ulcerated midline sac protruding through a skull defect at birth (occipital commonest in Western, frontoethmoidal in Southeast Asian populations)
Frontoethmoidal lesions produce hypertelorism and a nasal/dorsal mass widening the nasal bridge
Microcephaly or hydrocephalus depending on herniated content
radiological_manifestations: MRI/CT: meningeal sac with brain tissue herniating through a calvarial defect; fetal MRI defines contents for prognosis; CT shows the bony defect margins
pathology_manifestations: Herniated neural and meningeal tissue through the skull defect; classified by location (occipital, parietal, frontoethmoidal, basal)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Midline skull herniation sac is a definitive clinical photograph plus structural MRI diagnosis.

Pediatrics.name: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Persistent oxygen and ventilatory requirement in a premature infant beyond 28 days of life
Chronic tachypnea, retractions, and feeding difficulties in infancy
radiological_manifestations: Serial chest radiographs: classic Northway stage evolution from dense RDS to interstitial thickening, small cysts, and hyperinflation; CT: coarse interstitial bands and hyperinflated segments
pathology_manifestations: Simplified large alveoli with reduced septation and dysmorphic pulmonary microvasculature
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Named staged radiographic evolution (Northway) gives this a disease-specific imaging signature under the neonatal-imaging precedent.

Pediatrics.name: Waardenburg Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Brilliant sapphire-blue irides or complete/segmental heterochromia iridis
White forelock (poliosis) and premature graying
Dystopia canthorum (lateral displacement of inner canthi), synophrys, broad nasal root, and sensorineural deafness; piebald patches in some
radiological_manifestations: High-resolution temporal-bone CT only when indicated for associated inner-ear anomalies; the diagnosis is the composite external gestalt
pathology_manifestations: Neural-crest melanocyte migration defects; PAX3 (WS1/WS3), MITF (WS2), EDNRB/EDN3/SOX10 (WS4 with Hirschsprung)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Instantly diagnostic composite of white forelock, heterochromia, and dystopia canthorum; proposed by two audits.

Pediatrics.name: Silver-Russell Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Small triangular face with broad forehead tapering to a small pointed chin
Body and limb asymmetry (hemihypotrophy), fifth-finger clinodactyly, and relative macrocephaly
Severe intrauterine and postnatal growth restriction with feeding difficulties and low muscle mass
radiological_manifestations: Hand/wrist radiographs: clinodactyly and delayed bone age; asymmetry documented on growth/limb-length films
pathology_manifestations: ICR1 hypomethylation at 11p15 or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7; the epigenetic mirror image of covered Beckwith-Wiedemann
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic undergrowth gestalt (triangular face, asymmetry, clinodactyly) that mirrors the covered BWS overgrowth syndrome.

Pediatrics.name: PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (CLOVES)
clinical_manifestations: Truncal lipomatous overgrowth with sharply demarcated segmental fatty masses
Sandal-gap feet, macrodactyly, and acral overgrowth with a wide triangular foot
Vascular malformations (capillary, venous, lymphatic) and epidermal nevi; scoliosis in CLOVES
radiological_manifestations: MRI: infiltrative lipomatous overgrowth with venous/lymphatic malformations and neural fibrolipomas; spinal survey for paraspinal lipomatous disease
pathology_manifestations: Postzygotic activating PIK3CA mutation in affected tissue; AKT-pathway-driven segmental overgrowth
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Distinct PIK3CA mosaic overgrowth entity separate from covered Proteus (PTEN) and Klippel-Trenaunay.

Pediatrics.name: Simpson-Golabi-Behmel Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Coarse facies with macroglossia, wide mouth, upturned nose, and hypertelorism
Supernumerary nipples, postaxial polydactyly, and nail/hypoplastic-index anomalies
Macrosomia with organomegaly and neonatal hypoglycemia
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal/postnatal imaging for macrosomia, diaphragmatic hernia, and renal anomalies; skeletal survey for polydactyly
pathology_manifestations: Loss-of-function GPC3 (glypican-3) mutation; increased Wilms/hepatoblastoma risk warrants surveillance
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Distinct GPC3 overgrowth phenotype separate from covered Beckwith-Wiedemann and Sotos.

Pediatrics.name: EEC Syndrome (Ectrodactyly-Ectodermal Dysplasia-Clefting)
clinical_manifestations: Lobster-claw ectrodactyly: deep median cleft of hands and feet with central ray absence
Ectodermal defects: sparse hair, absent/hypoplastic nails, hypodontia, and absent sweat glands
Cleft lip with or without palate; lacrimal-duct anomalies and genitourinary defects
radiological_manifestations: Hand/foot radiographs: absent central rays with syndactyly of remaining digits; panorex: hypodontia
pathology_manifestations: Autosomal dominant TP63 mutation disrupting epithelial and limb-bud development
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Dramatic split-hand/foot photographs plus ectodermal dysplasia make a highly visual TP63 syndrome.

Pediatrics.name: Oral-Facial-Digital Syndrome Type 1 (OFD1)
clinical_manifestations: Hyperplastic oral frenulae, a lobulated/bifid tongue, midline upper-lip cleft, and alveolar clefts
Facial milia that resolve to pitted scars; sparse hair
Hand anomalies (brachydactyly, clinodactyly, occasional polydactyly) and polycystic kidneys
radiological_manifestations: Renal ultrasound: adult-onset polycystic kidney disease; brain MRI for associated CNS malformations
pathology_manifestations: X-linked dominant OFD1 mutation affecting a centrosomal/ciliary protein; typically lethal in males; X-inactivation pattern
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Frenula/tongue/hand photographs plus renal cystic imaging fill the ciliopathy gap (Joubert/Meckel/Bardet-Biedl covered).

Pediatrics.name: Coffin-Siris Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Hypoplastic or absent fifth fingernails and toenails with hypoplastic distal fifth phalanges
Coarse facies: thick eyebrows and lashes, broad nose and lips, sparse scalp hair
Developmental delay with feeding difficulty
radiological_manifestations: Hand radiographs: hypoplastic/absent distal fifth phalanx and nail aplasia
pathology_manifestations: Mutations in SWI/SNF (BAF) chromatin-remodeling genes (ARID1B commonest)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Completes the chromatinopathy set (Rubinstein-Taybi, Cornelia de Lange, Kabuki covered) with pathognomonic fifth-nail hypoplasia.

Pediatrics.name: Kleefstra Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Flat midface with synophrys, arched brows, and a fleshy everted lower lip with open-mouth posture
Childhood hypotonia and obesity; developmental delay
Brachy(micro)cephaly, short neck, and small hands/feet
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI may show white-matter abnormalities and ventriculomegaly; no pathognomonic sign - the gestalt is the image
pathology_manifestations: EHMT1 haploinsufficiency at 9q34.3 (deletion or point mutation)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Recognizable dysmorphic gestalt (everted lip, synophrys, flat midface) as a named microdeletion.

Pediatrics.name: Smith-Magenis Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Square face with broad nasal bridge, deep-set eyes, and a fleshy everted 'tented' upper lip
Self-hugging stereotypy and poliembolokoilamania (object insertion into body orifices)
Brachydactyly and hoarse voice; sleep inversion and self-injury
radiological_manifestations: No pathognomonic imaging; skeletal survey for brachydactyly and vertebral anomalies
pathology_manifestations: 17p11.2 microdeletion or RAI1 point mutation
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Distinct square-face/everted-lip gestalt plus iconic behavioral phenotype photographs.

Pediatrics.name: 1p36 Deletion Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Straight horizontal eyebrows, deep-set eyes, midface hypoplasia, and a small pointed chin
Large late-closing anterior fontanelle and brachycephaly
Orofacial clefting, hearing loss, and hypotonia
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: cortical dysplasia/polymicrogyria and white-matter anomalies in some; echocardiography for associated noncompaction cardiomyopathy
pathology_manifestations: Terminal microdeletion of 1p36 - the commonest terminal deletion syndrome
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Consistent recognizable gestalt of the commonest terminal-deletion syndrome.

Pediatrics.name: Weaver Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Advanced growth with broad forehead, large ears, hypertelorism, and micrognathia
Camptodactyly, broad thumbs, and deep-set nails
Hoarse voice and hypotonia
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: accelerated bone age, long-bone metaphyseal flaring, and camptodactyly
pathology_manifestations: EZH2 mutation; histone-methylation overgrowth pathway shared with Sotos (NSD1)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Distinct EZH2 overgrowth gestalt separate from covered Sotos.

Pediatrics.name: Nager Syndrome (Acrofacial Dysostosis)
clinical_manifestations: Treacher-Collins-like mandibulofacial dysostosis: malar hypoplasia, downslanting palpebral fissures, micrognathia, and ear anomalies
Radial-ray defects: hypoplastic or absent thumbs, radial hypoplasia/aplasia, and proximal radioulnar synostosis
Lower-limb and internal anomalies in a minority
radiological_manifestations: Upper-limb radiographs: radial aplasia and thumb absence/hypoplasia; temporal CT for middle/external ear malformation
pathology_manifestations: SF3B4 spliceosome mutation; preaxial (radial) limb involvement distinguishes it from postaxial Miller syndrome
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: TCS-like face plus radial aplasia is a classic dual photographic/radiographic phenotype.

Pediatrics.name: Adams-Oliver Syndrome
synonyms: aplasia cutis congenita with terminal transverse limb defects
clinical_manifestations: Vertex aplasia cutis congenita: a hairless scalp defect, sometimes with underlying calvarial bone loss
Terminal transverse limb defects: absent or hypoplastic fingers/toes and nail hypoplasia
Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita and cardiovascular anomalies in subsets
radiological_manifestations: Skull radiograph/CT: calvarial defect beneath scalp aplasia; limb films: transverse terminal reductions
pathology_manifestations: Heterogeneous (ARHGAP31, RBPJ, NOTCH1, DLL4, DOCK6, EOGT) dominant and recessive forms
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Scalp aplasia-cutis photograph plus transverse limb defects form a recognizable composite.

Pediatrics.name: Van der Woude Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral paramedian pits/fistulae on the lower lip - pathognomonic when combined with clefting
Cleft lip with or without cleft palate, or isolated cleft palate
Hypodontia in some cases
radiological_manifestations: No pathognomonic imaging; the lip pits are the image
pathology_manifestations: Autosomal dominant IRF6 mutation; commonest syndromic orofacial clefting
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Bilateral lower-lip pits are a pathognomonic sign and the commonest syndromic clefting.

Pediatrics.name: Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I (Hurler Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Coarse gargoyle-like facies: flattened nasal bridge, thick lips, macroglossia, and hirsutism
Corneal clouding, claw-hand contractures, and gibbus kyphosis
Hepatosplenomegaly, hernias, and cardiomegaly
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: dysostosis multiplex - bullet-shaped metacarpals, oar-shaped ribs, J-shaped sella, and beaked vertebrae - the named disease-specific skeletal pattern
pathology_manifestations: Alpha-L-iduronidase (IDUA) deficiency; dermatan/heparan sulfate accumulation; metachromatic storage material in tissues
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Dysostosis multiplex is a named pathognomonic skeletal-survey signature; coarse facies/corneal clouding are iconic photos.

Pediatrics.name: Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II (Hunter Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Coarse facies similar to Hurler but with clear corneas
Near-pathognomonic ivory pebbled papular skin nodules over the scapulae and posterior axillary lines
Claw hands, hernias, hepatosplenomegaly, and behavioral problems
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: dysostosis multiplex as in MPS I; brain MRI for white-matter changes in the severe form
pathology_manifestations: X-linked iduronate-2-sulfatase (IDS) deficiency; the only X-linked MPS
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Scapular pebbled papules plus cornea-clear coarse facies distinguish it from Hurler.

Pediatrics.name: Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata
clinical_manifestations: Rhizomelic (proximal) limb shortening with contractures and characteristic flat midface
Congenital bilateral cataracts
Severe growth and developmental failure
radiological_manifestations: Newborn skeletal survey: stippled epiphyseal calcification (the eponymous 'punctata' sign) with humeral/femoral shortening and coronal vertebral clefts
pathology_manifestations: PEX7 receptor defect of peroxisomal import; reduced plasmalogens and elevated phytanic acid
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Stippled-epiphysis newborn survey plus cataract/facies phenotype is a named signature.

Pediatrics.name: Classical Homocystinuria
clinical_manifestations: Marfanoid tall slender habitus with long limbs
Inferior (downward) ectopia lentis - the directional opposite of Marfan's superior dislocation
Livedo reticularis, malar flush, osteoporosis, and thromboembolic events
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal radiographs: marfanoid proportions and osteoporosis; slit-lamp: inferior lens dislocation; angiography for thrombosis as needed
pathology_manifestations: CBS deficiency accumulating homocysteine; nitroprusside urine test positive; methionine elevated on amino-acid analysis
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Marfanoid-habitus photo plus directional (inferior) ectopia lentis is a classic teaching distinction.

Pediatrics.name: Mucopolysaccharidosis Type IV (Morquio Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Severe short-trunk dwarfism with prominent pectus carinatum and knock-knees
Coarse facies milder than Hurler; normal intelligence
Odontoid hypoplasia with atlantoaxial instability and myelopathy risk
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: universal platyspondyly with anterior beaking, odontoid hypoplasia, and flared ilia; flexion-extension cervical films for atlantoaxial subluxation
pathology_manifestations: GALNS (type A) or beta-galactosidase GLB1 (type B) deficiency; keratan-sulfate accumulation
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Universal platyspondyly plus odontoid hypoplasia with short-trunk dwarfism is a classic dysplasia.

Pediatrics.name: I-Cell Disease (Mucolipidosis Type II)
clinical_manifestations: Severe Hurler-like coarse facies present in the newborn period
Striking gingival hyperplasia burying the teeth
Tight, firm, thickened skin; growth and motor failure without hepatosplenomegaly or corneal clouding early on
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey: severe dysostosis multiplex with periosteal cloaking of long bones in infancy
pathology_manifestations: GNPTAB GlcNAc-phosphotransferase defect; fibroblast 'inclusion' vacuoles on microscopy; massive lysosomal enzyme elevation in serum
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Coarse facies plus gingival hyperplasia plus periosteal cloaking is a distinct neonatal phenotype.

Pediatrics.name: PMM2-CDG (Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation Type Ia)
clinical_manifestations: Inverted nipples - pathognomonic sign
Abnormal suprapubic and periarticular fat pads (lipodystrophic pads)
Strabismus, axial hypotonia, and cerebellar hypoplasia with stroke-like episodes
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy, especially vermis; no other pathognomonic sign
pathology_manifestations: Phosphomannomutase-2 deficiency; abnormal transferrin glycosylation pattern on isoelectric focusing
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Inverted nipples plus pathognomonic fat pads are photographable disease-specific signs.

Pediatrics.name: Miller-Dieker Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic facies: bitemporal hollowing, short upturned nose, prominent upper lip, and small jaw
Lissencephaly ('smooth brain') with severe epilepsy
High forehead and microcephaly
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: classic four-layer lissencephaly with absent sulcation and figure-of-8 brain; grade severity by gyral pattern
pathology_manifestations: 17p13.3 microdeletion including PAFAH1B1 (LIS1); type-I lissencephaly
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Distinct facies plus lissencephaly is a recognizable composite; more than an MRI-only diagnosis.

Pediatrics.name: Farber Disease (Lipogranulomatosis)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic painful periarticular subcutaneous nodules over joints
Progressive hoarseness from laryngeal nodules
Cherry-red macular spot in some; contractures
radiological_manifestations: Joint radiographs: periarticular soft-tissue nodules; no pathognomonic sign
pathology_manifestations: ASAH1 deficiency; ceramide-laden foam cells and granulomatous inflammation in nodules
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Painful periarticular nodules plus hoarseness are pathognomonic; tiny but defined image base.

Pediatrics.name: Cleft Lip and Palate
