clinical_manifestations: anterior bony nasal narrowing in a newborn.

Otolaryngology.name: Nasal glial heterotopia
clinical_manifestations: a firm nasal glial mass with no open intracranial connection.

Otolaryngology.name: Microtia and Congenital Aural Atresia
clinical_manifestations: a small or absent pinna and a bony atretic plate. Goldenhar syndrome and Treacher Collins syndrome stay the craniofacial syndromes.

Otolaryngology.name: Preauricular sinus and cyst
clinical_manifestations: a pit anterior to the helix.

Otolaryngology.name: Reinke edema
clinical_manifestations: diffuse gelatinous swelling of both vocal folds.

Otolaryngology.name: Laryngocele
clinical_manifestations: an air-filled laryngeal saccule that enlarges with Valsalva.

Immunology.name: Hereditary Angioedema
clinical_manifestations: Dramatic recurrent facial, lip, and oropharyngeal swelling during attacks (no urticaria)
Nonpitting, nonpruritic edema of extremities
Life-threatening laryngeal edema requiring airway protection
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal CT during attacks: bowel-wall edema causing obstruction-like pain - disease-typical radiology
pathology_manifestations: C1-INH deficiency (type I low protein, type II dysfunctional, or normal-C1-INH forms); low C4 during attacks
Immunology.inclusion_rationale: Attack photographs (facial/airway edema) plus low C4 make a disease-level entity; agent disagreement resolved toward inclusion.

Immunology.name: Hyper-IgE Syndrome (Job Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Coarse facies: broad nose, prominent forehead, and rough skin texture
Recurrent 'cold' (noninflamed) staphylococcal skin and lung abscesses
Neonatal papulopustular/eczematoid rash; retained primary teeth and scoliosis
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT: pneumatoceles and bronchiectasis after recurrent pneumonia - characteristic; retained-primary-teeth dental films
pathology_manifestations: STAT3 loss-of-function (dominant form); elevated IgE >2000 IU/mL with eosinophilia
Immunology.inclusion_rationale: Coarse facies plus cold abscesses plus pneumatoceles fill the immunodeficiency-with-phenotype gap.

Immunology.name: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Eczematous dermatitis starting in infancy (often mislabeled atopic dermatitis)
Thrombocytopenic bleeding: petechiae, bloody diarrhea, and circumcision-site bleeding
Recurrent otitis and pneumonia; bloody-palmar photographs combine eczema and bleeding
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: WAS-protein mutation; microthrombocytopenia (small platelets) is pathognomonic on smear; increased malignancy and autoimmunity
Immunology.inclusion_rationale: Eczema-plus-petechiae photographs define a distinct X-linked immunodeficiency.

Immunology.name: Chronic Granulomatous Disease
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent purulent skin abscesses and granulomatous lesions
Perianal abscesses and fistulizing inflammation
Granulomatous obstruction of gastric outlet or urinary tract
radiological_manifestations: CT: multifocal liver abscesses with characteristic rim-enhancing granulomas; chest: recurrent pneumonia with aspergillosis 'halo' lesions
pathology_manifestations: Phagocyte NADPH-oxidase defect: negative nitroblue tetrazolium test; catalase-positive organisms (S. aureus, Serratia, Aspergillus, B. cepacia)
Immunology.inclusion_rationale: Abscess/granuloma photographs plus liver-abscess imaging make a recognizable phenotype.

Immunology.name: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency
clinical_manifestations: no thymic shadow, absent lymphoid tissue, and early opportunistic infection.

Immunology.name: Omenn Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: neonatal erythroderma, alopecia, hepatosplenomegaly, and enlarged nodes.

Immunology.name: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency
clinical_manifestations: delayed cord separation, omphalitis, necrotic skin ulcers.
a cord still attached after three weeks, infections without pus, and a very high neutrophil count.

Immunology.name: DOCK8 deficiency
clinical_manifestations: severe atopic dermatitis, recurrent cutaneous viral infections, warts/molluscum.
severe eczema with extensive cutaneous herpes, warts, and molluscum.

Immunology.name: GATA2 deficiency (MonoMAC)
clinical_manifestations: monocytopenia, NTM infections, HPV warts, lymphedema, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.
warts, lymphedema, monocytopenia, and atypical mycobacterial infection.

Immunology.name: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (Bruton)
clinical_manifestations: absent tonsils and nodes after maternal antibody wanes.

Immunology.name: Chronic Mucocutaneous Candidiasis
clinical_manifestations: persistent Candida of mouth, skin, and nails.

Immunology.name: IPEX Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: neonatal diarrhea, eczematous erythroderma, and early diabetes in a boy.

Immunology.name: WHIM Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: widespread warts with myelokathexis on the smear.

Immunology.name: Nijmegen breakage syndrome
clinical_manifestations: microcephaly, a sloping forehead, infections, and lymphoma.

Nutrition.name: Marasmus
clinical_manifestations: Extreme generalized wasting with visible ribs and muscle atrophy
'Old-man' wizened facies with sunken eyes
'Baggy-pants' loose skin folds on buttocks and thighs without edema
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Total calorie deprivation; subcutaneous fat and muscle consumed
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: The wizened, baggy-pants phenotype photographs complete the PEM pair with kwashiorkor.

Nutrition.name: Kwashiorkor
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral pitting edema masking the wasting, with protuberant belly
'Flaky-paint' or enamel dermatosis: desquamating hyperpigmented skin patches
Discolored sparse reddish-brown hair and apathetic affect; hepatomegaly
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; abdominal ultrasound shows fatty liver
pathology_manifestations: Protein deficiency predominant; hypoproteinemic edema; skin biopsy shows pallor and desquamation
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: The edematous flaky-paint phenotype is one of the most reproduced nutritional photographs; earlier-flagged topic endorsed.

Nutrition.name: Beriberi (Thiamine Deficiency)
clinical_manifestations: Wet beriberi: high-output edema and cardiac-failure habitus
Dry beriberi: wrist and foot drop from symmetric peripheral neuropathy
Infantile form: aphonia (silent cry) and cardiac failure in breastfed infants
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; echocardiography shows high-output failure in wet form
pathology_manifestations: Thiamine pyrophosphate deficiency; blood transketolase or thiamine levels confirm
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: Classic deficiency disease; signs not fully specific but photographic phenotype is teachable.

Nutrition.name: Vitamin A Deficiency (Xerophthalmia)
clinical_manifestations: Bitot spots: foamy triangular conjunctival plaques temporal to the cornea
Xerosis and keratomalacia - corneal softening and ulceration leading to blindness
Night blindness and follicular hyperkeratosis ('toadskin')
radiological_manifestations: Slit-lamp photographs document Bitot spots and keratomalacia
pathology_manifestations: Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency; squamous metaplasia of epithelium; low serum retinol
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: Bitot spots and keratomalacia are named pathognomonic photographs.

Nutrition.name: Kashin-Beck Disease
clinical_manifestations: Symmetric shortening and thickening of fingers producing a stubby-hand appearance
Enlarged interphalangeal joints in children
Endemic to selenium-deficient belt regions
radiological_manifestations: Hand radiographs: shortened, widened phalanges and metacarpals with early epiphyseal closure
pathology_manifestations: Chondrocyte necrosis of growth-plate cartilage; selenium deficiency with mycotoxin/cofactor hypotheses
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: Endemic osteoarthropathy with distinct hand photographs and films; partially imaging-dependent.

Nutrition.name: Bulimia Nervosa
clinical_manifestations: Russell sign: callused knuckles on the dorsal hand from self-induced vomiting
Parotid and submandibular gland enlargement ('chipmunk' face)
Perimylolysis: dental enamel erosion on the lingual surfaces of upper front teeth
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Criteria-defined psychiatric illness; hypokalemia from purging
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: Russell sign plus parotid swelling plus dental erosion are teachable photographic signs.

Nutrition.name: Scurvy (Vitamin C Deficiency)
clinical_manifestations: Corkscrew hairs: coiled broken hairs on inspection
Perifollicular hemorrhage and ecchymoses
Hemorrhagic gingivitis and tooth loosening; subperiosteal hemorrhage in infants (Barlow)
radiological_manifestations: Infant skeletal films: Wimberger ring sign (dense epiphyseal rim), Frankel metaphyseal line, and Pelkan spurs
pathology_manifestations: Ascorbic-acid deficiency of collagen hydroxylation; hemorrhagic tissue response
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: Corkscrew hairs plus perifollicular hemorrhage are classic photographic findings; same class as covered pellagra.

Nutrition.name: Lead Poisoning (Plumbism)
clinical_manifestations: Burton line: a blue-black gingival lead line at the tooth-gum margin
Wrist drop from peripheral motor neuropathy
Abdominal lead colic and pallor
radiological_manifestations: Long-bone radiographs in children: dense metaphyseal 'lead lines' at the growth plates - the named sign
pathology_manifestations: Basophilic stippling of erythrocytes on smear; blood-lead level confirms
Nutrition.inclusion_rationale: The gingival lead line plus metaphyseal lead lines plus basophilic stippling are classic toxidrome images.

Dentistry.name: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Indurated nonhealing ulcer of the lateral tongue or floor of mouth with rolled margins
Exophytic verrucous or endophytic variants
Leukoplakia or erythroplakia precursor fields
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI staging for depth and nodal disease; the clinical photo is the recognition image
pathology_manifestations: Invasive squamous-cell carcinoma; tobacco, alcohol, and betel-associated; HPV in a minority
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Most common oral malignancy with definitive external-photograph lesions.

Dentistry.name: Proliferative Verrucous Leukoplakia
clinical_manifestations: Multifocal, progressive verrucous white plaques that spread and recur after excision
Gingival and tongue predominance in older women
Near-obligate malignant transformation over years
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Hyperkeratotic verruciform surface progressing through dysplasia to verrucous or conventional SCC
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Defined precancerous entity - not the rejected generic 'leukoplakia' descriptor.

Dentistry.name: Acute Necrotizing Ulcerative Gingivitis
clinical_manifestations: 'Punched-out' necrotic interdental papillae with gray pseudomembrane - iconic photograph
Intense pain, metallic taste, and spontaneous gingival bleeding
Fetid breath and regional lymphadenopathy
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Fusospirochetal complex (Borrelia/Fusobacterium) with necrosis; immunosuppression, stress, and smoking predispose
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The punched-out papilla photograph is a single-entity diagnostic image; distinct from covered noma.

Dentistry.name: Oral Submucous Fibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Blanched, marble-like mucosa of the palate, buccal mucosa, and faucial pillars
Palpable vertical fibrous bands and progressive trismus
Burning sensation and restricted mouth opening in betel/areca users
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Dense collagen deposition with loss of vascularity; precancerous potential toward SCC
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Marble mucosa plus bands plus trismus is a defined precancerous photographic entity.

Dentistry.name: Hereditary Gingival Fibromatosis
clinical_manifestations: Massive generalized fibrous gingival overgrowth burying the tooth crowns
Slowly progressive firm pale enlargement
Impeded eruption, displacement, and malocclusion
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic film shows buried unerupted crowns; no pathognomonic sign
pathology_manifestations: Dense collagen and fibroblast proliferation; SON1/periodontin mutations in subsets
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The crown-burying gingival overgrowth is a dramatic disease-specific photograph.

Dentistry.name: Cherubism
clinical_manifestations: 'Cherub facies': bilateral symmetric mandibular/maxillary fullness producing a full-cheeked child
Lower-eyelid retraction exposing sclera in severe cases
Painless jaw swelling; remission at puberty
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic/CT: bilateral symmetric multilocular radiolucencies of the mandibular rami/angles - the dual signature with the facies
pathology_manifestations: SH3BP2 mutation; fibrous tissue with multinucleated giant cells
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Cherub facies plus symmetric multilocular jaw lucencies is a dual signature.

Dentistry.name: Ameloblastoma
clinical_manifestations: Painless expansile swelling of the posterior mandible and angle
'Soap-bubble' or multilocular radiolucency on panoramic film
Facial asymmetry in advanced cases
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic/CT: multilocular 'soap-bubble' radiolucency with cortical thinning or perforation; unicystic variant as a unilocular lesion
pathology_manifestations: Follicular or plexiform odontogenic epithelium with peripheral palisading and reverse-polarized nuclei; BRAF mutation commonest
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Soap-bubble multilocular mandibular lucency plus follicular histology - jaw analog of covered adamantinoma.

Dentistry.name: Amelogenesis Imperfecta
clinical_manifestations: Pitted, grooved, rough hypoplastic enamel or soft hypomineralized discolored teeth
Yellow-brown teeth that chip and wear rapidly
Anterior open bite in some forms
radiological_manifestations: Dental radiographs: thin or absent enamel layer, or enamel of dentin-like radiodensity depending on type
pathology_manifestations: ENAM/AMELX/others mutations; enamel matrix formation, mineralization, or maturation defect

Dentistry.name: Dentinogenesis Imperfecta
clinical_manifestations: Opalescent amber/blue-gray translucent teeth
Bulbous crowns with cervical constriction
Rapid wear exposing dentin and fracturing teeth
radiological_manifestations: Dental radiographs: bulbous crowns, cervical constriction, obliterated pulp chambers, and short slender roots
pathology_manifestations: DSPP mutation (isolated DGI-II); dentinal-tubule disorganization; standalone disease distinct from covered osteogenesis imperfecta
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Opalescent teeth plus obliterated-pulp films are pathognomonic.

Dentistry.name: Verrucous Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Broad-based exophytic warty white mass of the gingiva, buccal mucosa, or palate
Slow-growing 'church-spire' surface with minimal invasion
Often in smokeless-tobacco users
radiological_manifestations: CT/MRI for depth and bone involvement
pathology_manifestations: Bulbous pushing rete ridges with dense keratin; pushing (not infiltrating) margin; bland cytology despite size
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The warty church-spire mass plus pushing-margin histology is a defined entity.

Dentistry.name: Oral Mucosal Melanoma
clinical_manifestations: Pigmented palatal or maxillary gingival lesion with irregular borders
Often amelanotic or mixed color; late diagnosis
Satellite pigmentation spots
radiological_manifestations: CT/PET staging; the pigmented palatal photo is the recognition image
pathology_manifestations: Mucosal melanoma with radial and vertical growth; poorer prognosis than cutaneous melanoma
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Distinct mucosal-melanoma entity; covered cutaneous melanoma does not include mucosal.

Dentistry.name: Heck Disease (Focal Epithelial Hyperplasia)
clinical_manifestations: Multiple flat-topped flesh-colored papules and plaques of the labial, buccal, and lingual mucosa
Clustered 'cobblestone' appearance in children
Self-limited; HPV-13/32 driven
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Acanthosis with mitosoid (mitosis-like) cells - pathognomonic HPV cytopathic effect
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Multiple flat oral papules in children are a defined photographic entity.

Dentistry.name: White Sponge Nevus
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral thick, spongy, folded white plaques of the buccal mucosa
Symmetric involvement from childhood
Painless; plaques can be peeled off leaving normal mucosa
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: KRT4/KRT13 mutation; intracellular edema of spinous cells with eosinophilic condensation
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Bilateral spongy white plaques are a distinct hereditary oral entity.

Dentistry.name: Sialolithiasis
clinical_manifestations: Palpable stone in the submandibular Wharton duct or floor of mouth
Meal-time swelling and pain ('meal-time syndrome')
Purulent discharge from the duct orifice on massage
radiological_manifestations: Floor-of-mouth occlusal radiograph shows the radio-opaque stone; ultrasound/sialoendoscopy images the calculus and duct
pathology_manifestations: Calcium-phosphate salivary calculus obstructing the duct
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Stone in the duct plus meal-time swelling is a classic photographic sign.

Dentistry.name: Oral Hairy Leukoplakia
clinical_manifestations: Corrugated 'hairy' white plaques on the lateral tongue border that cannot be scraped off
Vertical folds and ridges along the tongue edge
In HIV and immunosuppressed patients
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Epstein-Barr virus replication in differentiated epithelial cells; koilocyte-like 'ballooned' cells with nuclear beading
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The most reproduced oral photo in medicine; named entity kept at High pending maintainer call.

Dentistry.name: Fluorosis (Dental and Skeletal)
clinical_manifestations: Dental: pathognomonic mottled, chalky-white to pitted-stained enamel in horizontal bands
Skeletal: joint stiffness and pain in severe endemic exposure
Bilateral symmetric mottling
radiological_manifestations: Dental photographs and films for mottled enamel; skeletal survey: osteosclerosis, ligament calcification, and interosseous membrane ossification in skeletal fluorosis
pathology_manifestations: Excess fluoride during amelogenesis; histology shows subsurface porosity of enamel
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The banded mottled enamel is pathognomonic; skeletal osteosclerosis is disease-specific.

Dentistry.name: Dental Caries
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Chalky white, demineralized enamel (white spot lesion), typically at the gingival third of the tooth, the earliest visible sign
Intraoral photograph: Brown or black staining within a pit or fissure with a visible enamel cavity
Intraoral photograph: Cavitated lesion with undermined, soft enamel margins and exposed dentin at the base
Intraoral photograph: Brown to black, rough root surface at the gumline in root caries of older adults
Intraoral photograph: Extensive crown destruction with exposed pulp in advanced caries
radiological_manifestations: Bitewing radiography: Radiolucent lesion in enamel or dentin, most often on the proximal surfaces between teeth
Periapical radiography: Radiolucency extending toward the pulp chamber in advanced lesions
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: White spot and cavitated lesions are visible on intraoral photographs, and bitewing radiographs reveal interproximal decay that is not visible clinically.

Dentistry.name: Periodontal Disease (Gingivitis and Periodontitis)
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Swollen, erythematous or bluish-red gingiva with a shiny, bulbous contour around the teeth
Intraoral photograph: Bleeding at the gingival margin, visible as blood on the gingiva or in the sulcus
Intraoral photograph: Gingival recession with exposed root surfaces and dark gaps between gum and tooth
Intraoral photograph: Plaque and calculus (tartar) accumulated at the gingival margin, often on the lingual surfaces of the lower incisors
Intraoral photograph: Tooth spacing or drifting from alveolar bone loss in advanced periodontitis
radiological_manifestations: Bitewing or periapical radiography: Horizontal alveolar bone loss with reduced alveolar bone height
Bitewing or periapical radiography: Vertical or angular bone defects between adjacent teeth
Cone-beam CT: Furcation involvement and three-dimensional bone loss
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Gingival inflammation, recession and calculus are visible on intraoral photographs, and radiographs show the alveolar bone loss that defines periodontitis.

Dentistry.name: Periapical (Dental) Abscess
clinical_manifestations: Extraoral photograph: Facial swelling over the affected tooth with overlying erythema of the cheek or lip
Intraoral photograph: Fluctuant gingival swelling or pustule (parulis, or gumboil) adjacent to the tooth apex
Intraoral photograph: Tooth with a deep carious or fractured crown, sometimes darkened from pulp necrosis
Intraoral photograph: Purulent discharge from the gingival sulcus near the involved tooth
radiological_manifestations: Periapical radiography: Well-defined radiolucency at the root apex from bone destruction
Panoramic radiography: Periapical radiolucency around the root with a widened periodontal ligament space
Cone-beam CT: Periapical lucent lesion with cortical expansion or perforation in larger abscesses
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Parulis, facial swelling and an affected tooth are visible clinically, and periapical radiolucency on radiographs confirms the diagnosis.

Dentistry.name: Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Round or oval shallow ulcer with a yellow-gray fibrinous base and a red halo on non-keratinized mucosa
Intraoral photograph: Painful ulcers on the labial and buccal mucosa, lateral tongue and soft palate, usually sparing the attached gingiva
Intraoral photograph: Clusters of small ulcers in recurrent crops, healing over one to two weeks
Intraoral photograph: Larger, deeper ulcers with raised, irregular margins in major aphthosis, sometimes with scarring
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy/H&E: Ulcer base with fibrinous pseudomembrane and a mixed lymphocytic and neutrophilic infiltrate at the margins
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Multiple painful shallow ulcers with a yellow-gray base and red halo are classic intraoral findings that are routinely photographed.

Dentistry.name: Geographic Tongue (Benign Migratory Glossitis)
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Multiple well-demarcated smooth red patches on the dorsum of the tongue where filiform papillae are absent
Intraoral photograph: Irregular map-like patches with white or yellow serpiginous borders
Intraoral photograph: Lesions often on the lateral tongue margins, sometimes with associated fissuring
Intraoral photograph: Smaller, scattered lesions on the ventral or lateral tongue in extensive disease
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The depapillated, map-like patches with serpiginous borders are a distinctive visual pattern on intraoral photographs.

Dentistry.name: Black Hairy Tongue
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Elongated, hair-like filiform papillae on the dorsal tongue, several millimeters long
Intraoral photograph: Black, brown or green discoloration of the elongated papillae, typically on the posterior dorsum
Intraoral photograph: Furry appearance of the dorsal tongue, with the anterior tongue often spared
Intraoral photograph: Otherwise intact tongue mucosa with no ulceration
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The elongated, dark-stained papillae give a distinctive furry dorsal tongue appearance on intraoral photographs.

Dentistry.name: Oral Leukoplakia and Erythroplakia
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Homogeneous white plaque with a smooth surface that cannot be scraped off
Intraoral photograph: Speckled leukoplakia with mixed red and white patches (erythroleukoplakia)
Intraoral photograph: Erythroplakia as a well-demarcated, velvety bright red patch, the highest-risk presentation
Intraoral photograph: Nodular or verrucous white lesion with an irregular, corrugated surface
Intraoral photograph: Ulceration or induration within a lesion, suggesting invasion or malignant transformation
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy/H&E: Epithelial dysplasia graded from mild to severe, with atypical keratinocytes and loss of stratification
Biopsy/H&E: Erythroplakia often shows severe dysplasia or carcinoma in situ
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: White and red oral plaques are visually recognizable, and biopsy grading of dysplasia is needed to assess malignant risk.

Dentistry.name: Oral Mucocele and Ranula
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Smooth, dome-shaped, translucent bluish swelling on the lower or inner lip mucosa
Intraoral photograph: Soft, fluctuant bluish sublingual swelling on the floor of the mouth, elevating the tongue
Intraoral photograph: Ruptured lesion with a crusted or ulcerated surface after drainage of clear saliva
Extraoral photograph: Submandibular swelling from a plunging ranula extending beneath the mylohyoid muscle
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasonography: Well-circumscribed anechoic cyst with posterior acoustic enhancement
MRI or CT: Fluid-filled cystic mass in the sublingual or submandibular space, extending through the mylohyoid in plunging ranula
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology/H&E: Cyst wall of granulation or fibrous tissue with extravasated mucin and foamy macrophages
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Translucent bluish swellings of the lip or floor of the mouth are recognizable on intraoral photographs, and MRI or CT delineates plunging ranulas.

Dentistry.name: Osteonecrosis of the Jaw (Medication-Related and Osteoradionecrosis)
clinical_manifestations: Intraoral photograph: Exposed necrotic bone visible through a non-healing extraction socket or gingival defect, typically white or yellow
Intraoral photograph: Exposed bone surrounded by erythema, swelling and purulent discharge in infected stages
Intraoral photograph: Fistula or sinus tract draining through the gingiva in advanced disease
Intraoral photograph: Mobile teeth within the affected bone segment with soft-tissue ulceration over the bony exposure
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic radiography: Mixed sclerotic and lytic bone changes with sequestra in the affected jaw
Cone-beam CT: Cortical erosion, sequestrum formation and sclerotic bone with periosteal reaction
Bone scintigraphy (99mTc-MDP): Increased radiotracer uptake in the necrotic jaw bone
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy/H&E: Avascular necrotic bone with empty osteocyte lacunae and inflamed, non-viable marrow
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: Exposed necrotic bone and draining fistulas are visible intraorally, and panoramic or cone-beam CT imaging shows sequestra and sclerosis.

Dentistry.name: Odontoma
clinical_manifestations: Unerupted or impacted tooth with delayed eruption or absence of the adjacent permanent tooth
Firm, painless bony expansion of the jaw in large lesions
radiological_manifestations: Panoramic radiograph: Well-circumscribed radiopaque mass in the tooth-bearing area with a thin radiolucent rim
Panoramic or periapical radiograph: Cluster of multiple small tooth-like denticles (compound type)
CBCT: Radiopaque mass displacing adjacent tooth roots
Panoramic radiograph: Displacement of an unerupted permanent tooth germ by the lesion
pathology_manifestations: Excisional biopsy (H&E): Enamel, dentin, cementum and pulp-like tissue arranged in a tooth-like pattern
Dentistry.inclusion_rationale: The lesion is defined radiographically by its tooth-like calcified masses, with clinical images showing the associated impacted tooth and bony expansion.

Dentistry.name: Actinic cheilitis
clinical_manifestations: lower-lip erythema/scaling, blurred vermilion border.

Dentistry.name: Pericoronitis
clinical_manifestations: operculum over impacted third molar, trismus.

Dentistry.name: Dentigerous Cyst
clinical_manifestations: a corticated lucency attached at the crown of an unerupted tooth.

Dentistry.name: Odontogenic Keratocyst
clinical_manifestations: a mandibular radiolucency along an impacted tooth, with little expansion. Multiple cysts stay inside Gorlin syndrome.

Dentistry.name: Central Giant Cell Granuloma
clinical_manifestations: an expansile anterior-jaw lucency that often crosses the midline.

Dentistry.name: Central ossifying fibroma of the jaws
clinical_manifestations: a boxed-in mixed lucent-opaque jaw mass.

Dentistry.name: Drug-Induced Gingival Overgrowth
clinical_manifestations: mulberry gingiva from phenytoin, cyclosporine, or a calcium-channel blocker.

Dentistry.name: Nasopalatine Duct Cyst
clinical_manifestations: a heart-shaped midline maxillary lucency between vital incisors.

Dentistry.name: Adenomatoid Odontogenic Tumor
clinical_manifestations: a pericoronal lucency around an unerupted canine, often with snowflake calcifications.

Dentistry.name: Odontogenic Myxoma
clinical_manifestations: a soap-bubble lucency that scallops between roots.

Dentistry.name: Cementoblastoma
clinical_manifestations: a painful radiopaque mass fused to a root, with a lucent rim.

Dentistry.name: Cemento-Osseous Dysplasia (Periapical and Florid)
clinical_manifestations: radiopacities at the apices of vital teeth.

Dentistry.name: Peripheral Giant Cell Granuloma
clinical_manifestations: a red-purple gingival nodule.

Dentistry.name: Regional odontodysplasia (ghost teeth)
clinical_manifestations: one quadrant of thin, large-pulp teeth.

Dentistry.name: Dentin Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: short or rootless teeth with obliterated pulps.

Dentistry.name: Tetracycline Tooth Discoloration
clinical_manifestations: intrinsic gray-brown bands that fluoresce.

Dentistry.name: Necrotizing Sialometaplasia
clinical_manifestations: a deep palatal crater that heals.

Dentistry.name: Median Rhomboid Glossitis
clinical_manifestations: a fixed red diamond on the midline posterior tongue.

Dentistry.name: Nicotinic Stomatitis
clinical_manifestations: a white palate with red puncta at the minor-salivary orifices.

Dentistry.name: Epulis Fissuratum
clinical_manifestations: fibrous folds under a denture flange.

Dentistry.name: Angina bullosa hemorrhagica
clinical_manifestations: a sudden blood blister on the soft palate.

Dentistry.name: Riga-Fede disease
clinical_manifestations: a granulomatous ulcer on the ventral tongue of an infant, cut by natal teeth.

Dentistry.name: Laugier-Hunziker syndrome
clinical_manifestations: adult lip macules with longitudinal melanonychia and no polyps.

Dentistry.name: Oral squamous papilloma
clinical_manifestations: a solitary cauliflower nodule on the palate or uvula.

Dentistry.name: Irritation fibroma
clinical_manifestations: a firm pink nodule on the bite line.

Dentistry.name: Congenital epulis
clinical_manifestations: a pedunculated mass on the maxillary alveolus of a newborn girl.

Dentistry.name: Acute bacterial sialadenitis
clinical_manifestations: unilateral salivary swelling with pus at the duct.

Dentistry.name: Juvenile recurrent parotitis
clinical_manifestations: repeated childhood parotid swelling with punctate sialectasis.

Dentistry.name: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: a parotid mass or a bluish palatal swelling.

Dentistry.name: Floor-of-mouth dermoid cyst
clinical_manifestations: a midline doughy swelling that lifts the tongue.

Dentistry.name: Peripheral ossifying fibroma
clinical_manifestations: a firm nodule on the interdental papilla.

Dentistry.name: Molar-incisor hypomineralization
clinical_manifestations: chalky yellow-brown opacities limited to first permanent molars and incisors.

Dentistry.name: Internal tooth resorption (pink tooth of Mummery)
clinical_manifestations: a pink crown with a ballooned pulp canal.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Cutaneous Endometriosis
clinical_manifestations: Cyclically bleeding tender nodule in a cesarean or surgical scar or the umbilicus
Blue-red-brown discoloration enlarging with menses
Villar nodule (umbilical) in nonscar form
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound/MRI: hypoechoic irregular subcutaneous nodule with hemosiderin signal
pathology_manifestations: Endometrial glands and stroma with hemosiderin in skin/subcutis
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Cyclical bleeding nodule is a definitive photograph.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Hydatidiform Mole
clinical_manifestations: Gross expelled 'bunch-of-grapes' vesicular tissue from the uterus
Vaginal bleeding, hyperemesis, and uterus large for dates
Pre-eclampsia in early gestation in complete moles
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: 'snowstorm' or vesicular intrauterine mass of grape-like cystic spaces without an embryo - pathognomonic; complete vs partial distinguished by fetal parts
pathology_manifestations: Diploid androgenetic (complete) or triploid diandric (partial) fertilization; diffuse villous edema and trophoblastic hyperplasia; p57 immunostain distinguishes
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Snowstorm ultrasound plus grape-vesicle tissue photograph is pathognomonic.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Pelvic Endometriosis
clinical_manifestations: Laparoscopy: 'powder-burn' black lesions, 'chocolate' endometrioma cysts, and peritoneal pockets
Cyclical dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility
Catamenial symptoms at extrapelvic sites
radiological_manifestations: MRI: T1-hyperintense endometrioma with T2 'shading'; ultrasound: ground-glass cyst contents
pathology_manifestations: Ectopic endometrial glands and stroma with hemosiderin; definitive diagnosis is surgical-visual
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Endometriomas and powder-burn lesions are definitive surgical photographs.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Laparoscopy: pathognomonic 'violin-string' adhesions between liver capsule and peritoneum
Right-upper-quadrant pain accompanying pelvic inflammatory disease
Pleuritic pain radiating to the shoulder
radiological_manifestations: CT: perihepatic enhancement; ultrasound for PID features; the violin-string laparoscopic image is the signature
pathology_manifestations: Chlamydial or gonococcal ascension causing capsular hepatic inflammation
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Violin-string adhesions are a pathognomonic laparoscopic photograph.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Endometrial Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Hysteroscopy: exophytic friable polypoid endometrial mass
Postmenopausal bleeding - the presenting sign
Gross specimen: fungating endometrial tumor
radiological_manifestations: Transvaginal ultrasound: thickened endometrial stripe; MRI for myometrial invasion
pathology_manifestations: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma; PTEN/p53/POLE molecular classes
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Postmenopausal-bleeding mass under the endoscopic-cancer precedent; maintainer call.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Ovarian Dermoid Cyst (Mature Cystic Teratoma)
clinical_manifestations: Gross specimen: sebum, hair, and teeth filling a unilocular cyst
Rokitansky protuberance containing differentiated tissues
Ovarian torsion as the acute presentation
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: dot-dash 'dermoid mesh' echogenic pattern with acoustic shadowing; CT/MRI: macroscopic fat and calcification (teeth/bone) in an adnexal mass - disease-specific
pathology_manifestations: Mature cystic teratoma with derivatives of all three germ layers; struma ovarii variant
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Dermoid-mesh ultrasound plus fat/teeth CT is a recognized entity.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Imperforate Hymen
clinical_manifestations: Pubertal bulging blue-violet membrane at the introitus under tension
Primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain
Palpable lower-abdominal hematocolpos mass
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: distended vagina filled with blood (hematocolpos); the blue bulging membrane is the clinical photograph
pathology_manifestations: Canalization failure of the caudal vaginal plate
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: The bulging blue membrane is a pathognomonic pubertal photograph.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Vulvar Squamous Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Ulcerated or exophytic vulvar mass usually on the labia
Chronic pruritus and bleeding
Groin lymphadenopathy in advanced cases
radiological_manifestations: Groin ultrasound/MRI for staging; the clinical photo is the recognition image
pathology_manifestations: Invasive squamous-cell carcinoma; HPV-associated (usual type) or lichen sclerosus-associated (differentiated type)
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Visible vulvar mass under the external-cancer photograph precedent.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Vulvar Intraepithelial Neoplasia (VIN)
clinical_manifestations: Multifocal pigmented or white multifocal vulvar plaques and papules
Pruritic verrucous lesions in the usual type
Erosive thin plaques in differentiated VIN against lichen sclerosus
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; vulvoscopy with acetic-acid staining maps lesions
pathology_manifestations: Full-thickness vulvar dysplasia; HPV-associated usual type vs p53-mutant differentiated type
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Multifocal vulvar plaque photographs of a defined precancerous entity.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Bartholin Gland Cyst and Abscess
clinical_manifestations: Unilateral swelling at the posterolateral 4-8 o'clock vestibular position
Non-tender cyst versus exquisitely painful abscess with erythema
Dyspareunia and sitting discomfort
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound of the cyst/abscess; the posterolateral bulge is the clinical photograph
pathology_manifestations: Duct obstruction with cystic dilation; abscess is usually polymicrobial
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: The 4-8 o'clock posterolateral vestibular swelling is a classic photograph.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: PUPPP (Pruritic Urticarial Papules and Plaques of Pregnancy)
clinical_manifestations: Urticarial papules and plaques beginning within abdominal striae
Periumbilical sparing - the named distribution sign
Spreads to thighs and buttocks in late third trimester
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Nonspecific lymphohistiocytic infiltrate; direct immunofluorescence negative (excludes covered pemphigoid gestationis)
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: The striae-sparing-umbilicus distribution is the named dermatosis of pregnancy.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy
clinical_manifestations: Palmoplantar-predominant pruritus without a primary rash
Secondary excoriations visible on examination
Mild jaundice and dark urine in a minority; resolves postpartum
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Elevated serum bile acids >10 umol/L with transaminitis; bile-acid handling defect
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Defined pregnancy disease; primary image base is limited (mostly excoriation photos) - maintainer call.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Vaginal Agenesis (MRKH Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Absent vaginal dimple with normal secondary sexual characteristics and normal karyotype
Primary amenorrhea in a well-estrogenized adolescent
Short blind vaginal pouch
radiological_manifestations: MRI/ultrasound: absent vagina and uterus with normal ovaries; the absent-dimple examination is the clinical sign
pathology_manifestations: Müllerian-duct developmental failure; renal, skeletal, and auditory anomalies in syndromic type II
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: External examination plus MRI defines a named syndrome.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Cervical Carcinoma
synonyms: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix
clinical_manifestations: Speculum examination: Exophytic, friable, cauliflower-like or papillary mass arising from the ectocervix
Speculum examination: Ulcerated, necrotic, bleeding cervical lesion with irregular tumor
Speculum examination: Barrel-shaped enlargement of the cervix in bulky, locally advanced disease
Colposcopy: Dense acetowhite epithelium with coarse mosaic, punctation and atypical vessels
radiological_manifestations: MRI pelvis: Intermediate T2-signal mass replacing the high-signal cervical stroma, with parametrial extension when advanced
PET/CT: FDG-avid cervical primary with metastatic pelvic or para-aortic nodes
pathology_manifestations: Cervical biopsy/H&E: Invasive nests of atypical squamous cells (keratinizing or nonkeratinizing) or glandular adenocarcinoma
p16 immunostain: Strong block-type nuclear and cytoplasmic staining in HPV-associated carcinoma
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Exophytic or ulcerated cervical masses and acetowhite lesions on colposcopy are visible in clinical photographs, and MRI and PET images show tumor extent.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Uterine Leiomyomas (Fibroids)
clinical_manifestations: Hysteroscopy: Smooth, round, pedunculated or sessile submucosal mass protruding into the uterine cavity with intact overlying mucosa
Laparoscopy/laparotomy: Firm, smooth, pale subserosal nodules bulging from the uterine surface
Gross specimen: Well-circumscribed, firm, whorled tan-white cut surface with a pseudocapsule
Gross specimen: Degenerated fibroid with hyaline, cystic, or red-necrotic areas
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic ultrasound: Well-defined, round, hypoechoic solid mass with posterior acoustic shadowing
MRI pelvis: Well-circumscribed, T2-dark solid mass, with heterogeneous high-signal areas in degenerated regions
pathology_manifestations: Myomectomy specimen/H&E: Well-circumscribed fascicles of bland smooth muscle cells with hyalinized collagen and no significant atypia
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Fibroids are seen directly on hysteroscopy, laparoscopy and gross specimens as whorled masses, and ultrasound and MRI show their characteristic appearance.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Labial Adhesions
clinical_manifestations: Vulvar inspection (prepubertal girls): Thin, translucent or whitish membrane fusing the labia minora in the midline
Vulvar inspection: Partial fusion leaving a small central pinhole opening over the introitus
Vulvar inspection: Complete fusion with a pale, avascular membrane covering the introitus
Vulvar inspection (postmenopausal): Atrophic, pale, thinned labia minora fused posteriorly with loss of labial architecture
Vulvar inspection: Erythematous or inflamed margins on the adhesion in infected or irritated cases
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Labial fusion is directly visible on vulvar examination and photographs, most often in prepubertal girls and in postmenopausal women with atrophy.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Asherman Syndrome (Intrauterine Adhesions)
clinical_manifestations: Hysteroscopy: Thin or dense fibrous bands (synechiae) spanning the uterine cavity
Hysteroscopy: Partial or complete obliteration of the cavity with loss of the normal triangular shape
Hysteroscopy: Narrowed or obliterated tubal ostia within the fundal adhesions
Hysteroscopy: Pale, thin, atrophic endometrium with patchy white scar tissue
radiological_manifestations: Hysterosalpingography: Irregular cavity outline with filling defects from intracavitary adhesions
Hysterosalpingography: Incomplete filling of the uterine cavity or failure of tubal spill
Saline-infusion or 3D ultrasound: Hyperechoic bands crossing the endometrial cavity
pathology_manifestations: Endometrial biopsy (H&E): Dense fibrous stroma with sparse or absent endometrial glands
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: The synechiae and cavity distortion are seen directly at hysteroscopy and on hysterosalpingography and 3D ultrasound.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Adnexal (Ovarian) Torsion
clinical_manifestations: Laparoscopy: Enlarged, dusky, blue-black or hemorrhagic ovary
Laparoscopy: Twisted utero-ovarian pedicle with the adnexa rotated around its axis, commonly 180 to 720 degrees
Laparoscopy: Edematous, pale or necrotic-appearing ovary after prolonged torsion
radiological_manifestations: Transvaginal ultrasound: Enlarged ovary with peripheral follicles in a string-of-pearls pattern and stromal edema
Grayscale ultrasound: Whirlpool sign of the twisted vascular pedicle
Color Doppler ultrasound: Absent or markedly reduced ovarian flow; normal flow does not exclude torsion
CT: Adnexal mass with twisted pedicle and ovarian enlargement, often with ascites
pathology_manifestations: Ovarian specimen (H&E): Hemorrhagic infarction with stromal edema and ischemic necrosis
Obstetrics & Gynecology.inclusion_rationale: Torsion is recognized on ultrasound and Doppler images and confirmed at laparoscopy, where the enlarged, twisted ovary is visible.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Ectopic pregnancy
clinical_manifestations: empty uterus, adnexal ring/mass, free fluid.
an empty uterus with a tubal ring or extrauterine sac. Tubal, interstitial, cervical, and cesarean-scar sites stay inside this topic.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Preeclampsia/eclampsia
clinical_manifestations: growth restriction, abnormal Doppler, PRES on MRI.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease and Tubo-Ovarian Abscess
clinical_manifestations: thickened tubes, hydrosalpinx/pyosalpinx, rim-enhancing adnexal mass.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Adenomyosis
clinical_manifestations: junctional-zone thickening, myometrial cysts, “venetian blind” shadowing.
a thickened junctional zone and myometrial cysts on MRI.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: complex cystic-solid mass, ascites, omental caking.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
clinical_manifestations: ≥20 follicles/ovary, ovarian volume >10 mL, “string of pearls.”

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Ovarian functional cysts
clinical_manifestations: simple/hemorrhagic cyst, “ring of fire” corpus luteum.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Placenta previa
clinical_manifestations: placenta covering the internal os.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Placenta accreta spectrum
clinical_manifestations: loss of the retroplacental clear zone, placental lacunae, and an interrupted bladder line.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Choriocarcinoma
clinical_manifestations: hypervascular uterine mass, “cannonball” lung metastases.
hemorrhagic vaginal nodules and cannonball lung metastases.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Trichomoniasis
clinical_manifestations: a strawberry cervix with frothy discharge.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Uterine inversion
clinical_manifestations: a red bleeding mass at the introitus with an absent abdominal fundus.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Pelvic Organ Prolapse (Uterine Procidentia)
clinical_manifestations: descent of the vaginal walls or cervix to the introitus.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN)
clinical_manifestations: acetowhite epithelium, mosaicism, and punctation on colposcopy.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: OHVIRA syndrome
clinical_manifestations: uterus didelphys, an obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal agenesis.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Persistent cloaca
clinical_manifestations: a single perineal opening for urethra, vagina, and rectum.

Obstetrics & Gynecology.name: Twin-twin transfusion syndrome
clinical_manifestations: the polyhydramnios–oligohydramnios stuck-twin pair.

Urology.name: Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Ulcerated or exophytic glans or foreskin mass
Foul discharge under a non-retractile foreskin
Inguinal lymphadenopathy in advanced disease
radiological_manifestations: Inguinal ultrasound and MRI staging; the external mass photo is the recognition image
pathology_manifestations: Invasive squamous-cell carcinoma; HPV-associated warty/basaloid or lichen sclerosus-associated usual type
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Visible external genital carcinoma like the bladder-cancer endoscopic precedent.

Urology.name: Peyronie Disease
clinical_manifestations: Palpable dorsal plaque producing curvature during erection
Painful erections in the acute phase
Hourglass deformity in severe cases
radiological_manifestations: Penile ultrasound: echogenic fibrotic plaque in the tunica albuginea, sometimes calcified
pathology_manifestations: Disordered wound-healing fibrosis (Dupuytren-analog) forming a tunica plaque
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Palpable curvature deformity is a defined disease entity.

Urology.name: Hypospadias
clinical_manifestations: Urethral meatus located on the ventral shaft rather than the tip
Ventral curvature (chordee) and dorsal hooded foreskin
Splayed urinary stream
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging; the external anomaly is the photograph
pathology_manifestations: Incomplete ventral urethral fold fusion; common male congenital anomaly
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Ventral meatus plus dorsal hood is a definitive anomaly photograph.

Urology.name: Interstitial Cystitis / Bladder Pain Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cystoscopy: Hunner lesions - red, ulcerated, mucosal bleeding patches after bladder distention
Glomerulations (submucosal petechiae) on hydrodistention
Suprapubic pain relieved by voiding
radiological_manifestations: Cystoscopy with hydrodistention is the recognition image
pathology_manifestations: Urothelial thinning and mucosal ulceration with mast-cell-rich inflammation
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Hunner-lesion cystoscopy photographs are how the disease is defined.

Urology.name: Posterior Urethral Valves
clinical_manifestations: Cystoscopy: obstructing membrane folds in the posterior urethra
Weak stream and distended bladder in newborn boys
Associated hydroureter and renal dysplasia
radiological_manifestations: Voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG): dilated posterior urethra above a membrane with abrupt distal cutoff - the diagnostic film
pathology_manifestations: Congenital obstructive urethral membrane; 'keyhole' bladder sign on prenatal ultrasound
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Valve-leaflet cystoscopy plus keyhole VCUG are dual images.

Urology.name: Primary Urethral Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Palpable periurethral mass with discharge or bleeding
Obstructive voiding symptoms
Urethroscopy shows an ulcerated mass
radiological_manifestations: MRI staging; urethroscopic photo is the recognition image
pathology_manifestations: Squamous-cell or urothelial carcinoma of the urethra; rare distinct entity

Urology.name: Zoon Balanitis (Plasma Cell Balanitis)
clinical_manifestations: Well-demarcated, shiny, moist 'cayenne-pepper' speckled orange-red plaque of the glans
Painless persistent lesion in uncircumcised men
Symmetric 'kissing' lesion on the prepuce contact surface
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Dense plasma-cell-rich dermal infiltrate with lozenge-shaped keratinocytes and erythrocyte extravasation
Urology.inclusion_rationale: The cayenne-pepper shiny plaque plus plasma-cell histology is a defined entity.

Urology.name: Urothelial Bladder Carcinoma
synonyms: transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
clinical_manifestations: Papillary exophytic tumor with slender fronds and fused papillae on the bladder wall at cystoscopy
Flat, velvety erythematous patches of carcinoma in situ at cystoscopy
Solid, nodular or ulcerated mass with a friable, hemorrhagic surface at cystoscopy
Multifocal tumors involving the trigone, bladder neck or a bladder diverticulum
Filling defects in the renal pelvis or ureter on retrograde pyelography or ureteroscopy
radiological_manifestations: CT urography: Enhancing intravesical mass or sessile filling defect along the bladder wall
CT urography: Upper-tract filling defect with hydronephrosis from ureteral obstruction
MRI pelvis: Bladder wall mass with disruption of the low-signal detrusor muscle on T2 indicating muscle invasion
pathology_manifestations: TURBT specimen (H&E): Papillary urothelial neoplasm with fibrovascular cores graded as low or high grade
TURBT specimen (H&E): Urothelial nests invading lamina propria or detrusor muscle
Biopsy (H&E): Flat urothelial carcinoma in situ with high-grade nuclear atypia and loss of polarity
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Papillary and flat mucosal lesions are directly seen at cystoscopy, and cystoscopy, urography and TURBT images are widely published.

Urology.name: Phimosis, Paraphimosis and Balanitis
clinical_manifestations: Phimosis: Narrow preputial orifice with a constricting ring that prevents foreskin retraction over the glans
Paraphimosis: Retracted foreskin trapped behind the glans by a tight constricting band
Paraphimosis: Marked edema of the glans with dusky, violaceous discoloration of the exposed glans
Balanitis: Erythematous, edematous glans with superficial moist white or yellow exudate
Balanoposthitis: Erosions, fissures or small ulcers on the glans or inner foreskin
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Foreskin constriction, glans swelling and surface exudate are visible on clinical photographs and in genitourinary atlases.

Urology.name: Hydrocele and Spermatocele
clinical_manifestations: Smooth, tense, uniformly enlarged scrotum from a fluid-filled swelling
Bright red transillumination glow through the scrotum when a light is applied (positive transillumination)
Scrotal skin stretched and thinned over the swelling
Non-tender, well-circumscribed cystic swelling above and separate from the testis (spermatocele)
radiological_manifestations: Scrotal ultrasound: Anechoic, thin-walled fluid collection surrounding the testis (hydrocele)
Scrotal ultrasound: Anechoic cyst in the epididymal head or tail with a normal testis (spermatocele)
Scrotal ultrasound: Thickened, calcified tunica vaginalis in chronic hydrocele
Urology.inclusion_rationale: Scrotal swellings are visible and transilluminate, and scrotal ultrasound images show the fluid collections clearly.

Urology.name: Testicular Torsion
clinical_manifestations: Swollen, high-riding testis with a horizontal (transverse) lie
Dusky, purple-black discoloration of the testis
Scrotal edema and erythema, sometimes with a reactive hydrocele
radiological_manifestations: Color Doppler ultrasound: Absent or markedly reduced intratesticular arterial flow with an enlarged testis
Color Doppler ultrasound: Whirlpool sign of the twisted spermatic cord above the testis
Grayscale ultrasound: Enlarged, hypoechoic testis with heterogeneous echotexture in delayed presentations
Tc-99m pertechnetate scintigraphy: Photopenic (absent uptake) testis
pathology_manifestations: Orchiectomy specimen (H&E): Hemorrhagic infarction with necrosis of seminiferous tubules
Urology.inclusion_rationale: The swollen, high-riding testis and the absent Doppler flow are the visible signs, with ultrasound and operative images as the main image types.

Urology.name: Varicocele
clinical_manifestations: Dilated, tortuous scrotal veins above the testis, described as a bag of worms, most often on the left
Visible enlargement of the veins on standing or with the Valsalva maneuver
Scrotal asymmetry with the affected hemiscrotum larger and lower-hanging
Reduced testicular size on the affected side in long-standing disease
radiological_manifestations: Color Doppler ultrasound: Dilated pampiniform plexus veins with retrograde flow on Valsalva
Grayscale ultrasound: Tortuous, serpiginous cluster of anechoic tubular structures in the spermatic cord region
Ultrasound: Ipsilateral testicular volume loss in chronic disease
Urology.inclusion_rationale: The dilated, tortuous scrotal veins are visible on examination and on Doppler ultrasound images.

Urology.name: Cryptorchidism (Undescended Testis)
clinical_manifestations: Empty hemiscrotum on the affected side with an absent testis
Smaller, hypoplastic hemiscrotum compared with the contralateral side
Testis located high in the inguinal canal or superficial inguinal pouch on examination
Inguinal hernia or hydrocele on the same side as the undescended testis
radiological_manifestations: Scrotal and inguinal ultrasound: Testis located in the inguinal canal or absent from the scrotum, with the spermatic cord visible in the canal
MRI pelvis: Intra-abdominal ovoid testis near the internal inguinal ring
pathology_manifestations: Orchidopexy testicular biopsy (H&E): Germ cell loss and hypospermatogenesis with Sertoli cell predominance in the tubules
Urology.inclusion_rationale: The empty hemiscrotum and the abnormal testicular position are visible on examination, with inguinal ultrasound and MRI used to localize the testis.

Urology.name: Penile Fracture
clinical_manifestations: Acute swelling and deformity of the penile shaft immediately after injury
Ecchymosis spreading to the scrotum and perineum (eggplant deformity)
Penile curvature or deviation away from the injured side
Blood at the urethral meatus suggesting associated urethral injury
radiological_manifestations: Retrograde urethrography: Extravasation of contrast from the urethra, suggesting urethral injury
Ultrasound: Disruption of the tunica albuginea with a hypoechoic hematoma and irregular corporal outline
Urology.inclusion_rationale: The bruising, deformity and hematoma are visible on examination photographs and at surgical exploration.

Urology.name: Testicular Germ Cell Tumor
clinical_manifestations: Enlarged, firm testis with loss of the normal oval contour
Reactive hydrocele or scrotal swelling overlying the tumor
Gynecomastia (breast enlargement) in patients with hCG-secreting germ cell tumors
radiological_manifestations: Scrotal ultrasound: Solitary, hypoechoic intratesticular mass with ill-defined margins
Scrotal ultrasound: Intratesticular microlithiasis as a risk marker
CT chest-abdomen-pelvis: Retroperitoneal para-aortic lymphadenopathy for staging
pathology_manifestations: Orchiectomy specimen (gross): Solid, homogeneous tan-white lobulated tumor (seminoma) or heterogeneous hemorrhagic cystic mass (non-seminomatous)
Immunohistochemistry (OCT3/4, PLAP): Nuclear and membranous positivity in seminoma cells
Urology.inclusion_rationale: The tumor is seen as a scrotal mass on ultrasound, and gross orchiectomy photographs distinguish seminoma from non-seminomatous patterns.

Urology.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
clinical_manifestations: enlarged transition zone, median lobe, post-void residual.

Urology.name: Prostate cancer
clinical_manifestations: PI-RADS lesion on mpMRI, diffusion restriction, bone/PSMA metastases.

Urology.name: Nephrolithiasis
clinical_manifestations: hyperdense stone, hydronephrosis, perinephric stranding on noncontrast CT.

Urology.name: Obstructive uropathy/hydronephrosis
clinical_manifestations: dilated pelvis/calyces, cortical thinning, transition point.

Urology.name: Urethral stricture
clinical_manifestations: retrograde urethrogram narrowing.

Urology.name: Epididymitis/epididymo-orchitis
clinical_manifestations: enlarged hyperemic epididymis, reactive hydrocele.

Urology.name: Priapism
clinical_manifestations: Doppler absent/reduced cavernosal flow (ischemic) or high flow (nonischemic).

Urology.name: Acute bacterial prostatitis/prostatic abscess
clinical_manifestations: tender prostate, rim-enhancing collection.

Urology.name: Testicular rupture
clinical_manifestations: disrupted tunica albuginea, heterogeneous testis, hematocele.

Urology.name: Torsion of the appendix testis
clinical_manifestations: avascular upper-pole nodule, blue-dot sign.
the blue-dot sign with preserved testicular flow.

Urology.name: Urethral prolapse
clinical_manifestations: a circumferential red-purple doughnut of mucosa at the meatus of a prepubertal girl.

Urology.name: Urethral caruncle
clinical_manifestations: a focal friable red lesion at the posterior meatus.

Urology.name: Urethral diverticulum
clinical_manifestations: an anterior vaginal mass, with a horseshoe fluid collection on MRI.
Anterior vaginal wall mass expressing purulent discharge with pathognomonic T2-hyperintense "saddlebag / horseshoe" cystic lesion wrapping around the mid-urethra on pelvic MRI

Urology.name: Staghorn calculus
clinical_manifestations: a branching cast of the renal pelvis and calyces.
Branched coral-like radiopaque staghorn calculus casting the renal pelvis/calyces on KUB/CT, "twinkling artifact" and absent ureteral jet on Doppler US, and rectangular "coffin-lid" struvite crystals

Urology.name: Primary obstructive megaureter
clinical_manifestations: a dilated ureter that narrows at an adynamic distal segment and does not reflux.

Urology.name: Urachal carcinoma
synonyms: Congenital Urachal Anomalies and Urachal Adenocarcinoma
clinical_manifestations: a midline, often calcified mass at the bladder dome.
Umbilical urine drainage in neonates or mucosuria in adults; midline bladder-dome mass extending along the space of Retzius with peripheral calcifications on sagittal CT/MRI

Urology.name: Patent urachus
clinical_manifestations: urine leaking from the umbilicus through a tract to the bladder dome.

Urology.name: Emphysematous cystitis
clinical_manifestations: gas outlining the bladder wall.

Urology.name: Epispadias
clinical_manifestations: Dorsal urethral cleft on a broad, flattened "spade-like" dorsally curved penis (or bifid clitoris) + wide pubic symphysis diastasis ("manta-ray pelvis") on pelvic X-ray

Urology.name: Penile Intraepithelial Neoplasia (Erythroplasia of Queyrat and Bowenoid Papulosis)
synonyms: Erythroplasia of Queyrat and Bowenoid Papulosis
clinical_manifestations: Velvety bright-red glistening plaque on the glans penis vs. multiple reddish-brown/violaceous papules on the penile shaft with glomerular vessels on dermoscopy

Urology.name: Giant Condyloma Acuminatum (Buschke-Löwenstein Tumor)
clinical_manifestations: Massive cauliflower-like exophytic verrucous penile/perianal mass with multiple urethrocutaneous fistulae and deep cavernosal invasion on pelvic MRI

Urology.name: Idiopathic Scrotal Calcinosis
clinical_manifestations: Numerous chalky yellowish-white intradermal nodules studding the scrotal skin with acoustic shadowing on ultrasound and normal serum calcium/phosphate

Urology.name: Angiokeratoma (Solitary, Fordyce and Mibelli)
clinical_manifestations: 1–5 mm dark-red to blue-black vascular papules along the scrotum/labia majora with pathognomonic "dark lacunae" and whitish veil on dermoscopy
a dark keratotic papule or clustered scrotal or vulvar papules. Fabry disease stays the widespread form.

Urology.name: Renal Oncocytoma
clinical_manifestations: Mahogany-brown renal cortical tumor with a central stellate scar and "spoke-wheel" vascular pattern on CT/MRI/angiography

Breast.name: Phyllodes Tumor of the Breast
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly growing large, well-circumscribed breast mass stretching overlying skin
Bulging veins over the mass
Can reach enormous size distorting breast contour
radiological_manifestations: Mammography: large round/lobulated circumscribed mass; ultrasound: heterogeneous solid mass with cystic clefts - the leaf-like internal architecture
pathology_manifestations: Leaf-like (phyllodes) intracanalicular stromal architecture with stromal hypercellularity; benign/borderline/malignant grading
Breast.inclusion_rationale: The rapidly-growing stretched-skin mass plus leaf-architecture histology is a defined entity.

Breast.name: Diabetic Mastopathy (Sclerosing Lymphocytic Lobulitis)
clinical_manifestations: Firm, irregular, ill-defined breast mass in long-standing type-1 diabetics
Mimics carcinoma clinically
Premenopausal women and men with diabetic complications
radiological_manifestations: Mammography: asymmetric dense mass; ultrasound: hypoechoic shadowing mass - a carcinoma mimic
pathology_manifestations: Lymphocytic lobulitis and ductitis with keloid-like sclerosis - the characteristic 'diabetic' stromal fibrosis
Breast.inclusion_rationale: A named autoimmune breast entity; imaging-dependent scope call.

Breast.name: Idiopathic Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis
clinical_manifestations: Tender peripheral breast mass with sinus tracts draining pus to the skin
Mimics inflammatory breast carcinoma
Recurrent ulcers and abscesses
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: hypoechoic tubular masses with sinus tracts to skin; mammography mimics carcinoma
pathology_manifestations: Noncaseating granulomas centered on lobules with neutrophilic microabscesses; exclusion of infection is required
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Sinus-forming breast mass is a defined clinical entity.

Breast.name: Mondor Disease
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic palpable subcutaneous cord along the lateral breast or thoracoepigastric region
Overlying skin may dimple along the cord
Self-limited superficial thrombophlebitis
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: noncompressible tubular hypoechoic structure without flow - the thrombosed superficial vein
pathology_manifestations: Superficial vein thrombosis of the breast/chest wall; occasionally associated with occult malignancy
Breast.inclusion_rationale: The palpable breast cord is a pathognomonic clinical photograph.

Breast.name: Gigantomastia (Gestational Macromastia)
clinical_manifestations: Extreme bilateral breast enlargement over weeks during pregnancy
Skin ulceration, infection, and venous congestion
Breasts disproportionate to body habitus with mechanical disability
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific imaging
pathology_manifestations: Massive hormone-driven stromal and glandular hyperplasia; PTEN-associated in subsets
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Extreme gestational breast overgrowth is a defined photographic entity.

Breast.name: Male Breast Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Hard, fixed, painless subareolar mass behind the nipple
Nipple retraction, ulceration, or bloody discharge
Often late-stage at diagnosis
radiological_manifestations: Mammography/ultrasound: eccentric subareolar spiculated mass (distinct from the flame-shaped gynecomastia pattern)
pathology_manifestations: Invasive ductal carcinoma; BRCA2 enrichment; ER-rich
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Distinct entity from covered female breast carcinoma with a subareolar-mass phenotype.

Breast.name: Breast Implant-Associated Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma
clinical_manifestations: Late-onset peri-implant seroma producing sudden unilateral breast swelling
Palpable capsular mass in some cases
9+ years post-implant typically
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound: peri-implant fluid collection; the seroma aspirate is the diagnostic material
pathology_manifestations: CD30-positive anaplastic large cells in seroma fluid; ALK-negative; indolent if capsule-confined
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Named implant-lymphoma entity with a seroma phenotype.

Breast.name: Tubular Breast Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Screening-detected small spiculated breast mass
Often occult clinically
Excellent prognosis
radiological_manifestations: Mammography: small spiculated irregular mass; architectural distortion
pathology_manifestations: >90% well-formed angulated open tubules infiltrating stroma; low-grade ER-rich
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Named carcinoma subtype under the invasive-breast-cancer precedent.

Breast.name: Mucinous (Colloid) Breast Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Soft, mobile, well-circumscribed breast mass
Older women typically
Good prognosis in pure form
radiological_manifestations: Mammography: circumscribed lobulated mass; MRI: very high T2 signal from extracellular mucin - characteristic
pathology_manifestations: Clusters of tumor cells floating in abundant extracellular mucin pools

Breast.name: Inflammatory Breast Cancer
clinical_manifestations: Breast inspection: Diffuse erythema involving at least one-third of the breast, often with peau d'orange skin
Breast inspection: Rapid-onset, warm, firm, swollen breast without a discrete mass
Breast skin: Ridging and thickening of the skin with dermal edema and pitting
Breast inspection: Nipple retraction or ulceration in advanced disease
radiological_manifestations: Mammography: Diffuse skin thickening and trabecular edema, often without a discrete mass
Breast MRI: Diffuse, non-mass enhancement of skin and parenchyma with skin thickening
Breast ultrasound: Diffuse hypoechoic stromal edema with skin thickening
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy/H&E: Tumor emboli within dermal lymphatic channels
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Diffuse erythema, edema and ridged skin are visible on breast photographs and clinical examination, and mammography shows the characteristic skin thickening.

Breast.name: Accessory Breast Tissue and Polythelia
clinical_manifestations: Inspection: Small, pigmented, round or oval papule or nodule along the milk line between the axilla and groin
Inspection: Supernumerary nipple with a surrounding darker pigmented areola, sometimes with hair
Inspection: Accessory breast as an ill-defined glandular mound in the axilla or along the milk line, with or without a nipple
Inspection: Lesions are frequently symmetric and bilateral along the milk line
radiological_manifestations: Breast ultrasound: Ectopic glandular tissue in the axilla or along the milk line with breast-type parenchymal echotexture
pathology_manifestations: Excision specimen/H&E: Mammary ducts and lobules in an ectopic dermal or subcutaneous location
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Supernumerary nipples and accessory breast tissue are visible on skin inspection along the milk line, and ultrasound shows ectopic glandular tissue.

Breast.name: Lactational Mastitis and Breast Abscess
clinical_manifestations: Breast inspection: Localized, wedge-shaped, erythematous, warm and swollen area, most often in the upper outer quadrant
Breast inspection: Fluctuant, tender, erythematous mass with overlying skin thinning in breast abscess
Nipple: Cracked or fissured nipple with purulent or milky-purulent discharge
Breast skin: Sinus tract or ulceration over a chronic or recurrent abscess
radiological_manifestations: Breast ultrasound: Hypoechoic, fluid-filled abscess cavity with thick irregular wall and internal debris
Breast ultrasound with Doppler: Hypoechoic stromal edema with hyperemia in the affected quadrant
pathology_manifestations: Abscess aspirate/Gram stain: Neutrophils with clusters of Gram-positive cocci, most often Staphylococcus aureus
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Wedge-shaped erythema, fluctuant abscesses and nipple discharge are visible on breast photographs, and ultrasound images of abscess cavities are common.

Breast.name: Gynecomastia
clinical_manifestations: Breast inspection: Symmetric or asymmetric, firm, rubbery subareolar enlargement in a male, often bilateral
Breast inspection: Disc-shaped subareolar fullness centered behind the nipple-areola complex
Breast inspection: Diffuse fatty fullness without a central disc in pseudogynecomastia
Breast inspection: Enlarged, slightly pigmented areola-nipple complex in some patients
radiological_manifestations: Mammography: Symmetric, dense subareolar fibroglandular tissue in a male breast without a suspicious mass
Breast ultrasound: Triangular or disc-shaped subareolar tissue with ductal structures, typically bilateral and symmetric
pathology_manifestations: Excision specimen/H&E: Proliferating ductal structures with stromal edema and fibrosis in florid gynecomastia
Breast.inclusion_rationale: Subareolar disc-shaped enlargement is recognizable on clinical photographs and inspection, and mammography and ultrasound show the symmetric glandular tissue.

Breast.name: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
clinical_manifestations: Unilateral serous or bloody nipple discharge from a single duct
Nipple retraction or areolar change in extensive comedo-type DCIS (uncommon)
radiological_manifestations: Mammography: Clustered fine pleomorphic or fine linear branching microcalcifications, often the only sign
Mammography: Segmental or linear distribution of microcalcifications following the ductal anatomy
Breast MRI: Non-mass enhancement in a segmental or ductal pattern
Ultrasound: Ill-defined hypoechoic duct-like lesion with ductal dilatation
pathology_manifestations: Core or excisional biopsy (H&E): Atypical epithelial cells filling and distending the duct lumen with an intact myoepithelial layer
Myoepithelial stain (p63 or calponin): Highlighted basal layer around the involved ducts
Specimen (H&E): Comedonecrosis with central necrotic debris and calcification within the ducts
Breast.inclusion_rationale: DCIS is detected mainly by mammographic microcalcification patterns, with histology images showing distended ducts.
